# Authentication

* API Key (clientId)
    - Parameter Name: **PLAID-CLIENT-ID**, in: header.

* API Key (secret)
    - Parameter Name: **PLAID-SECRET**, in: header.

* API Key (plaidVersion)
    - Parameter Name: **Plaid-Version**, in: header.

- oAuth2 authentication. The Plaid API supports client credentials, authorization code, and custom delegation flows.

    - Flow: clientCredentials
    - Token URL = [https://api.plaid.com/oauth2/apiv2/token](https://api.plaid.com/oauth2/apiv2/token)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|cra:read|Read CRA report data.|
|user:write|Write user data.|
|item:read|Read Item data.|
|link:write|Create Link tokens.|
|item:write|Exchange a public token for an access token.|
|auth:read|Read Auth data.|
|accounts:read|Read account data.|
|identity:read|Read Identity data.|
|transactions:read|Read Transactions data.|
|issues:read|Read institution issue data.|
|issues:write|Manage institution issue subscriptions.|

<h1 id="the-plaid-api-plaid">plaid</h1>

The Plaid API

## Create an Asset Report

<a id="opIdassetReportCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "access_tokens": [
      "string"
    ],
    "days_requested": 0,
    "options": {
      "client_report_id": "string",
      "webhook": "http://example.com",
      "include_fast_report": true,
      "products": [
        "string"
      ],
      "add_ons": [
        "investments"
      ],
      "user": {
        "client_user_id": "string",
        "first_name": "string",
        "middle_name": "string",
        "last_name": "string",
        "ssn": "string",
        "phone_number": "string",
        "email": "string"
      },
      "require_all_items": true
    }
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/create`

The `/asset_report/create` endpoint initiates the process of creating an Asset Report, which can then be retrieved by passing the `asset_report_token` return value to the `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get` endpoints.

The Asset Report takes some time to be created and is not available immediately after calling `/asset_report/create`. The exact amount of time to create the report will vary depending on how many days of history are requested and will typically range from a few seconds to about one minute. When the Asset Report is ready to be retrieved using `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get`, Plaid will fire a `PRODUCT_READY` webhook. For full details of the webhook schema, see [Asset Report webhooks](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/assets/#webhooks).

The `/asset_report/create` endpoint creates an Asset Report at a moment in time. Asset Reports are immutable. To get an updated Asset Report, use the `/asset_report/refresh` endpoint.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "access_tokens": [
    "string"
  ],
  "days_requested": 0,
  "options": {
    "client_report_id": "string",
    "webhook": "http://example.com",
    "include_fast_report": true,
    "products": [
      "string"
    ],
    "add_ons": [
      "investments"
    ],
    "user": {
      "client_user_id": "string",
      "first_name": "string",
      "middle_name": "string",
      "last_name": "string",
      "ssn": "string",
      "phone_number": "string",
      "email": "string"
    },
    "require_all_items": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-asset-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportCreateRequest](#schemaassetreportcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» access_tokens|body|[[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)]|false|An array of access tokens corresponding to the Items that will be included in the report. The `assets` product must have been initialized for the Items during Link; the Assets product cannot be added after initialization.|
|» days_requested|body|integer|true|The maximum integer number of days of history to include in the Asset Report. If using Fannie Mae Day 1 Certainty, `days_requested` must be at least 61 for new originations or at least 31 for refinancings.<br><br>An Asset Report requested with "Additional History" (that is, with more than 61 days of transaction history) will incur an Additional History fee.|
|» options|body|[AssetReportCreateRequestOptions](#schemaassetreportcreaterequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/asset_report/create` results. If provided, must be non-`null`. The optional `user` object is required for the report to be eligible for Fannie Mae's Day 1 Certainty program.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "asset_report_token": "assets-sandbox-6f12f5bb-22dd-4855-b918-f47ec439198a",
  "asset_report_id": "1f414183-220c-44f5-b0c8-bc0e6d4053bb",
  "request_id": "Iam3b"
}
```

```json
}
```

|default|Default|Error response|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & secret & plaidVersion

## Retrieve an Asset Report

<a id="opIdassetReportGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "asset_report_token": "string",
    "user_token": "string",
    "include_insights": false,
    "fast_report": false,
    "options": {
      "days_to_include": 0
    }
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/get`

The `/asset_report/get` endpoint retrieves the Asset Report in JSON format. Before calling `/asset_report/get`, you must first create the Asset Report using `/asset_report/create` (or filter an Asset Report using `/asset_report/filter`) and then wait for the [`PRODUCT_READY`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/assets/#product_ready) webhook to fire, indicating that the Report is ready to be retrieved.

By default, an Asset Report includes transaction descriptions as returned by the bank, as opposed to parsed and categorized by Plaid. You can also receive cleaned and categorized transactions, as well as additional insights like merchant name or location information. We call this an Asset Report with Insights. An Asset Report with Insights provides transaction category, location, and merchant information in addition to the transaction strings provided in a standard Asset Report. To retrieve an Asset Report with Insights, call the `/asset_report/get` endpoint with `include_insights` set to `true`.

For latency-sensitive applications, you can optionally call `/asset_report/create` with `options.add_ons` set to `["fast_assets"]`. This will cause Plaid to create two versions of the Asset Report: one with only current and available balance and identity information, and then later on the complete Asset Report. You will receive separate webhooks for each version of the Asset Report.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "asset_report_token": "string",
  "user_token": "string",
  "include_insights": false,
  "fast_report": false,
  "options": {
    "days_to_include": 0
  }
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-an-asset-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportGetRequest](#schemaassetreportgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» asset_report_token|body|[AssetReportTokenNullable](#schemaassetreporttokennullable)|false|A token that can be provided to endpoints such as `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get` to fetch or update an Asset Report.|
|» user_token|body|string|false|The user token associated with the User for which to create an asset report for. The latest asset report associated with the User will be returned|
|» include_insights|body|boolean|false|`true` if you would like to retrieve the Asset Report with Insights, `false` otherwise. This field defaults to `false` if omitted.|
|» fast_report|body|boolean|false|`true` to fetch "fast" version of asset report. Defaults to false if omitted. Can only be used if `/asset_report/create` was called with `options.add_ons` set to `["fast_assets"]`.|
|» options|body|[AssetReportGetRequestOptions](#schemaassetreportgetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter or add data to `/asset_report/get` results. If provided, must be non-`null`.|

## Retrieve a PDF Asset Report

<a id="opIdassetReportPdfGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/pdf/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "asset_report_token": "string",
    "options": {
      "days_to_include": 0
    }
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/pdf/get`

The `/asset_report/pdf/get` endpoint retrieves the Asset Report in PDF format. Before calling `/asset_report/pdf/get`, you must first create the Asset Report using `/asset_report/create` (or filter an Asset Report using `/asset_report/filter`) and then wait for the [`PRODUCT_READY`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/assets/#product_ready) webhook to fire, indicating that the Report is ready to be retrieved.

The response to `/asset_report/pdf/get` is the PDF binary data. The `request_id`  is returned in the `Plaid-Request-ID` header.

[View a sample PDF Asset Report](https://plaid.com/documents/sample-asset-report.pdf).

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportpdfget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "asset_report_token": "string",
  "options": {
    "days_to_include": 0
  }
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-pdf-asset-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportPDFGetRequest](#schemaassetreportpdfgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» asset_report_token|body|[AssetReportToken](#schemaassetreporttoken)|true|A token that can be provided to endpoints such as `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get` to fetch or update an Asset Report.|
|» options|body|[AssetReportPDFGetRequestOptions](#schemaassetreportpdfgetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter or add data to `/asset_report/get` results. If provided, must be non-`null`.|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
  "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
  "error_code": "string",
  "error_code_reason": "string",
  "error_message": "string",
```

## Refresh an Asset Report

<a id="opIdassetReportRefresh"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/refresh \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "asset_report_token": "string",
    "days_requested": 0,
    "options": {
      "client_report_id": "string",
      "webhook": "http://example.com",
      "user": {
        "client_user_id": "string",
        "first_name": "string",
        "middle_name": "string",
        "last_name": "string",
        "ssn": "string",
        "phone_number": "string",
        "email": "string"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/refresh`

An Asset Report is an immutable snapshot of a user's assets. In order to "refresh" an Asset Report you created previously, you can use the `/asset_report/refresh` endpoint to create a new Asset Report based on the old one, but with the most recent data available.

The new Asset Report will contain the same Items as the original Report, as well as the same filters applied by any call to `/asset_report/filter`. By default, the new Asset Report will also use the same parameters you submitted with your original `/asset_report/create` request, but the original `days_requested` value and the values of any parameters in the `options` object can be overridden with new values. To change these arguments, simply supply new values for them in your request to `/asset_report/refresh`. Submit an empty string ("") for any previously-populated fields you would like set as empty.

Note: Asset Report refresh is not supported in Canada.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportrefresh">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "asset_report_token": "string",
  "days_requested": 0,
  "options": {
    "client_report_id": "string",
    "webhook": "http://example.com",
    "user": {
      "client_user_id": "string",
      "first_name": "string",
      "middle_name": "string",
      "last_name": "string",
      "ssn": "string",
      "phone_number": "string",
      "email": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="refresh-an-asset-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportRefreshRequest](#schemaassetreportrefreshrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» asset_report_token|body|[AssetReportRefreshAssetReportToken](#schemaassetreportrefreshassetreporttoken)|true|The `asset_report_token` returned by the original call to `/asset_report/create`|
|» days_requested|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of days of history to include in the Asset Report. Must be an integer. If not specified, the value from the original call to `/asset_report/create` will be used.|
|» options|body|[AssetReportRefreshRequestOptions](#schemaassetreportrefreshrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/asset_report/refresh` results. If provided, cannot be `null`. If not specified, the `options` from the original call to `/asset_report/create` will be used.|

> Example responses

```json
  "asset_report_id": "c33ebe8b-6a63-4d74-a83d-d39791231ac0",
  "asset_report_token": "assets-sandbox-8218d5f8-6d6d-403d-92f5-13a9afaa4398",

}
```

## Filter Asset Report

<a id="opIdassetReportFilter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/filter \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "asset_report_token": "string",
    "account_ids_to_exclude": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/filter`

By default, an Asset Report will contain all of the accounts on a given Item. In some cases, you may not want the Asset Report to contain all accounts. For example, you might have the end user choose which accounts are relevant in Link using the Account Select view, which you can enable in the dashboard. Or, you might always exclude certain account types or subtypes, which you can identify by using the `/accounts/get` endpoint. To narrow an Asset Report to only a subset of accounts, use the `/asset_report/filter` endpoint.

To exclude certain Accounts from an Asset Report, first use the `/asset_report/create` endpoint to create the report, then send the `asset_report_token` along with a list of `account_ids` to exclude to the `/asset_report/filter` endpoint, to create a new Asset Report which contains only a subset of the original Asset Report's data.

Because Asset Reports are immutable, calling `/asset_report/filter` does not alter the original Asset Report in any way; rather, `/asset_report/filter` creates a new Asset Report with a new token and id. Asset Reports created via `/asset_report/filter` do not contain new Asset data, and are not billed.

Plaid will fire a [`PRODUCT_READY`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/assets/#product_ready) webhook once generation of the filtered Asset Report has completed.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportfilter">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "asset_report_token": "string",
  "account_ids_to_exclude": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="filter-asset-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportFilterRequest](#schemaassetreportfilterrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» asset_report_token|body|[AssetReportToken](#schemaassetreporttoken)|true|A token that can be provided to endpoints such as `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get` to fetch or update an Asset Report.|
|» account_ids_to_exclude|body|[string]|true|The accounts to exclude from the Asset Report, identified by `account_id`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "asset_report_token": "assets-sandbox-bc410c6a-4653-4c75-985c-e757c3497c5c",
  "asset_report_id": "fdc09207-0cef-4d88-b5eb-0d970758ebd9",

}
```

## Delete an Asset Report

<a id="opIdassetReportRemove"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/remove \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "asset_report_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/remove`

The `/item/remove` endpoint allows you to invalidate an `access_token`, meaning you will not be able to create new Asset Reports with it. Removing an Item does not affect any Asset Reports or Audit Copies you have already created, which will remain accessible until you remove them specifically.

The `/asset_report/remove` endpoint allows you to remove access to an Asset Report. Removing an Asset Report invalidates its `asset_report_token`, meaning you will no longer be able to use it to access Report data or create new Audit Copies. Removing an Asset Report does not affect the underlying Items, but does invalidate any `audit_copy_tokens` associated with the Asset Report.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportremove">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "asset_report_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-asset-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportRemoveRequest](#schemaassetreportremoverequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» asset_report_token|body|[AssetReportToken](#schemaassetreporttoken)|true|A token that can be provided to endpoints such as `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get` to fetch or update an Asset Report.|

## Create Asset Report Audit Copy

<a id="opIdassetReportAuditCopyCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/audit_copy/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "asset_report_token": "string",
    "auditor_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/audit_copy/create`

Plaid can provide an Audit Copy of any Asset Report directly to a participating third party on your behalf. For example, Plaid can supply an Audit Copy directly to the GSEs on your behalf if you participate in Fannie Mae's Day 1 Certainty™ program or utilize Freddie Mac's Loan Product Advisor® (LPA®) Asset and Income Modeler (AIM). An Audit Copy contains the same underlying data as the Asset Report.

To grant access to an Audit Copy, use the `/asset_report/audit_copy/create` endpoint to create an `audit_copy_token` and then pass that token to the third party who needs access. Each third party has its own `auditor_id`, for example `fannie_mae`. You'll need to create a separate Audit Copy for each third party to whom you want to grant access to the Report.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportaudit_copycreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "asset_report_token": "string",
  "auditor_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-asset-report-audit-copy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportAuditCopyCreateRequest](#schemaassetreportauditcopycreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» asset_report_token|body|[AssetReportToken](#schemaassetreporttoken)|true|A token that can be provided to endpoints such as `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get` to fetch or update an Asset Report.|
|» auditor_id|body|string|false|The `auditor_id` of the third party with whom you would like to share the Asset Report.|

## Retrieve an Asset Report Audit Copy

<a id="opIdassetReportAuditCopyGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/audit_copy/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "audit_copy_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/audit_copy/get`

`/asset_report/audit_copy/get` allows auditors to get a copy of an Asset Report that was previously shared via the `/asset_report/audit_copy/create` endpoint.  The caller of `/asset_report/audit_copy/create` must provide the `audit_copy_token` to the auditor.  This token can then be used to call `/asset_report/audit_copy/get`.

<a href="/none/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "audit_copy_token": "string"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportAuditCopyGetRequest](#schemaassetreportauditcopygetrequest)|true|none|

|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Retrieve a PDF Asset Report Audit Copy

<a id="opIdassetReportAuditCopyPdfGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/audit_copy/pdf/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "audit_copy_token": "string",
    "options": {
      "days_to_include": 0
    }
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/audit_copy/pdf/get`

The `/asset_report/audit_copy/pdf/get` endpoint retrieves an Asset Report Audit Copy in PDF format. The caller must provide the `audit_copy_token` that was shared via the `/asset_report/audit_copy/create` endpoint.

The response to `/asset_report/audit_copy/pdf/get` is the PDF binary data. The `request_id` is returned in the `Plaid-Request-ID` header.

[View a sample PDF Asset Report](https://plaid.com/documents/sample-asset-report.pdf).

<a href="/none/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "audit_copy_token": "string",
  "options": {
    "days_to_include": 0
  }
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-pdf-asset-report-audit-copy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportAuditCopyPdfGetRequest](#schemaassetreportauditcopypdfgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» audit_copy_token|body|string|true|The `audit_copy_token` granting access to the Audit Copy you would like to get as a PDF.|
|» options|body|[AssetReportPDFGetRequestOptions](#schemaassetreportpdfgetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter or add data to `/asset_report/get` results. If provided, must be non-`null`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response


## Remove Asset Report Audit Copy

<a id="opIdassetReportAuditCopyRemove"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asset_report/audit_copy/remove \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "audit_copy_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /asset_report/audit_copy/remove`

The `/asset_report/audit_copy/remove` endpoint allows you to remove an Audit Copy. Removing an Audit Copy invalidates the `audit_copy_token` associated with it, meaning both you and any third parties holding the token will no longer be able to use it to access Report data. Items associated with the Asset Report, the Asset Report itself and other Audit Copies of it are not affected and will remain accessible after removing the given Audit Copy.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#asset_reportaudit_copyremove">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "audit_copy_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="remove-asset-report-audit-copy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssetReportAuditCopyRemoveRequest](#schemaassetreportauditcopyremoverequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## (Legacy) Subscribe to Cash Flow Updates

<a id="opIdcraMonitoringInsightsSubscribe"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/cra/monitoring_insights/subscribe \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_id": "string",
    "item_id": "string",
    "webhook": "http://example.com",
    "income_categories": [
      "SALARY"
    ],
    "user_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /cra/monitoring_insights/subscribe`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

This endpoint allows you to subscribe to insights for a user's linked CRA Item, which are updated between one and four times per day (best-effort). Only one Item per user may be subscribed. This endpoint is part of the legacy Cash Flow Updates product and is available only to integrations already using it; other integrations should use `/cra/servicing/subscription/create` instead.

<a href="/api/products/check-legacy/#cramonitoring_insightssubscribe">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "item_id": "string",
  "webhook": "http://example.com",
  "income_categories": [
    "SALARY"
  ],
  "user_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="legacy-subscribe-to-cash-flow-updates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CraMonitoringInsightsSubscribeRequest](#schemacramonitoringinsightssubscriberequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» item_id|body|string|false|The Item ID to subscribe for Cash Flow Updates.|
|» webhook|body|string(url)|true|URL to which Plaid will send Cash Flow Updates webhooks, for example when the requested Cash Flow Updates report is ready.|
|» income_categories|body|[[CreditBankIncomeCategory](#schemacreditbankincomecategory)]|false|Income categories to include in Cash Flow Updates. If empty or `null`, this field will default to including all possible categories.|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|false|The user token associated with the user for which data is being requested. This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. ## (Legacy) Retrieve a Cash Flow Updates report

<a id="opIdcraMonitoringInsightsGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/cra/monitoring_insights/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_id": "string",
    "consumer_report_permissible_purpose": "ACCOUNT_REVIEW_CREDIT",
    "user_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /cra/monitoring_insights/get`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

This endpoint allows you to retrieve a Cash Flow Updates report by passing in the `user_id` referred to in the webhook you received. This endpoint is part of the legacy Cash Flow Updates product and is available only to integrations already using it. CRA Servicing has no direct equivalent; other integrations should handle the `CRA_REPORT_UPDATED` webhook and pass its `report_id` to the relevant product `/get` endpoint, such as `/cra/check_report/base_report/get`.

<a href="/api/products/check-legacy/#cramonitoring_insightsget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "consumer_report_permissible_purpose": "ACCOUNT_REVIEW_CREDIT",
  "user_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="legacy-retrieve-a-cash-flow-updates-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CraMonitoringInsightsGetRequest](#schemacramonitoringinsightsgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|body|[MonitoringConsumerReportPermissiblePurpose](#schemamonitoringconsumerreportpermissiblepurpose)|true|Describes the reason you are generating a Consumer Report for this user.<br><br>`ACCOUNT_REVIEW_CREDIT`: In connection with a consumer credit transaction for the review or collection of an account pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(A).<br><br>`WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION_OTHER`: In accordance with the written instructions of the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(2), such as when an individual agrees to act as a guarantor or assumes personal liability for a consumer, business, or commercial loan.|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|false|The user token associated with the user for which data is being requested. This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. ## Update an Audit Copy Token

<a id="opIdcreditAuditCopyTokenUpdate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/audit_copy_token/update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "audit_copy_token": "string",
    "report_tokens": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /credit/audit_copy_token/update`

The `/credit/audit_copy_token/update` endpoint updates an existing Audit Copy Token by adding the report tokens in the `report_tokens` field to the `audit_copy_token`. If the Audit Copy Token already contains a report of a certain type, it will be replaced with the token provided in the `report_tokens` field.

<a href="/none/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "audit_copy_token": "string",
  "report_tokens": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-audit-copy-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditAuditCopyTokenUpdateRequest](#schemacreditauditcopytokenupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» audit_copy_token|body|string|true|The `audit_copy_token` you would like to update.|
|» report_tokens|body|[[AssetReportToken](#schemaassetreporttoken)]|true|Array of tokens which the specified Audit Copy Token will be updated with. The types of token supported are asset report token and employment report token. There can be at most 1 of each token type in the array.|

<a id="opIdcraCheckReportIncomeInsightsGet"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.com/cra/check_report/income_insights/get \

        "excluded_categories": [

        ]
      },
      "income_insights_version": "II2"
    },

    "consumer_report_permissible_purpose": {}
  }'
```

`POST /cra/check_report/income_insights/get`

This endpoint allows you to retrieve the Income Insights report for your user. You should call this endpoint after you've received a `CHECK_REPORT_READY` or a `USER_CHECK_REPORT_READY` webhook, either after the Link session for the user or after calling `/cra/check_report/create`. If the most recent consumer report for the user doesn't have sufficient data to generate the report, or the consumer report has expired, you will receive an error indicating that you should create a new consumer report by calling `/cra/check_report/create`.

NOTE: The following schema was updated in April 2026 to reflect the response when the provided version is "II2". Please see [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kQkQ7FOgFaC4n-sUGUk74hoXZNY_L_nJeCuMe7Keip4/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.rudamzinus2i) for guidance on migrating to II2 if you are currently using the II1 version, and [this section](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kQkQ7FOgFaC4n-sUGUk74hoXZNY_L_nJeCuMe7Keip4/edit?tab=t.0#bookmark=id.tdcc2wpk0h60) for an example II1 response along with its [documentation](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kQkQ7FOgFaC4n-sUGUk74hoXZNY_L_nJeCuMe7Keip4/edit?tab=t.36c85n2ircqk#heading=h.79dwr5c1iszl).

<a href="/api/products/check-legacy/#cracheck_reportincome_insightsget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_token": "string",
  "third_party_user_token": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "income_insights_filter": {
      "included_categories": [
        "string"
      ],
      "excluded_categories": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "income_insights_version": "II2"
  },
  "report_id": "string",
  "consumer_report_permissible_purpose": {}
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-income-insights-from-your-users-banks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CraCheckReportIncomeInsightsGetRequest](#schemacracheckreportincomeinsightsgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|false|The user token associated with the user for which data is being requested. This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» third_party_user_token|body|[ThirdPartyUserToken](#schemathirdpartyusertoken)|false|The third-party user token associated with the requested User data.|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» options|body|[CraCheckReportIncomeInsightsGetOptions](#schemacracheckreportincomeinsightsgetoptions)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. This field is no longer accepted for new clients (created on or after 2026-07-01). New clients should specify required products when creating the Consumer Report. Existing integrations may continue to pass `options`.|
|» report_id|body|string|false|The CRA report token (formatted `cra-report-<env>-<uuid>`) identifying a specific consumer report. When provided alongside `consumer_report_permissible_purpose`, pins retrieval to that report and stamps its permissible purpose. If omitted, the most recently generated report for the user is returned.|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|body|object|false|The permissible purpose under which the consumer report is being retrieved.|

```bash
    "item_ids": [

    "user_tier": "free",

```

`POST /cra/check_report/base_report/get`

This endpoint allows you to retrieve the Base Report for your user, allowing you to receive comprehensive bank account and cash flow data. You should call this endpoint after you've received a `CHECK_REPORT_READY` or a `USER_CHECK_REPORT_READY` webhook, either after the Link session for the user or after calling `/cra/check_report/create`. If the most recent consumer report for the user doesn't have sufficient data to generate the base report, or the consumer report has expired, you will receive an error indicating that you should create a new consumer report by calling `/cra/check_report/create`.

<a href="/api/products/check-legacy/#cracheck_reportbase_reportget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "third_party_user_token": "string",
  "item_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "user_token": "string",
  "user_tier": "free",
  "report_id": "string",
  "consumer_report_permissible_purpose": {}
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-base-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CraCheckReportBaseReportGetRequest](#schemacracheckreportbasereportgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» third_party_user_token|body|[ThirdPartyUserToken](#schemathirdpartyusertoken)|false|The third-party user token associated with the requested User data.|
|» item_ids|body|[[ItemId](#schemaitemid)]|false|The Item IDs to include in the Base Report. If not provided, all Items associated with the user will be included.|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|false|The user token associated with the user for which data is being requested. This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» user_tier|body|[CraUserTier](#schemacrausertier)|false|The tier of the user.|
|» report_id|body|string|false|The CRA report token (formatted `cra-report-<env>-<uuid>`) identifying a specific consumer report. When provided alongside `consumer_report_permissible_purpose`, pins retrieval to that report and stamps its permissible purpose. If omitted, the most recently generated report for the user is returned.|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|body|object|false|The permissible purpose under which the consumer report is being retrieved.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» user_tier|free|
|» user_tier|paid|
|» user_tier|null|

## Retrieve a Consumer Report as a PDF

<a id="opIdcraCheckReportPdfGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/cra/check_report/pdf/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_id": "string",
    "third_party_user_token": "string",
    "add_ons": [
      "cra_income_insights"
    ],
    "user_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /cra/check_report/pdf/get`

`/cra/check_report/pdf/get` retrieves the most recent Consumer Report in PDF format. The most recent Base Report for the user is always included. Use the `add_ons` field to also include the most recent Income Insights, Partner Insights or LendScore report in the PDF.

<a href="/api/products/check-legacy/#cracheck_reportpdfget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "third_party_user_token": "string",
  "add_ons": [
    "cra_income_insights"
  ],
  "user_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-consumer-report-as-a-pdf-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CraCheckReportPDFGetRequest](#schemacracheckreportpdfgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» third_party_user_token|body|[ThirdPartyUserToken](#schemathirdpartyusertoken)|false|The third-party user token associated with the requested User data.|
|» add_ons|body|[[CraPDFAddOns](#schemacrapdfaddons)]|false|Use this field to include the most recent Income Insights, Partner Insights, or LendScore report in the PDF.|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|false|The user token associated with the user for which data is being requested. This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» add_ons|cra_income_insights|
|» add_ons|cra_partner_insights|
|» add_ons|cra_lend_score|

## Refresh or create a Consumer Report

<a id="opIdcraCheckReportCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/cra/check_report/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_id": "string",
    "user_token": "string",
    "webhook": "http://example.com",
    "days_requested": 0,
    "days_required": 0,
    "client_report_id": "string",
    "products": [
      "assets"
    ],
    "base_report": {
```

`POST /cra/check_report/create`

Use `/cra/check_report/create` to refresh data in an existing report. A Consumer Report will last for 24 hours before expiring; you should call any `/get` endpoints on the report before it expires. If a report expires, you can call `/cra/check_report/create` again to re-generate it and refresh the data in the report. The report is generated from all Items associated with the user, excluding [duplicate Items](https://plaid.com/docs/check/add-to-app/#duplicate-items) and Items that cannot supply data.

Each call to `/cra/check_report/create` creates a new, independent report. `/get` endpoints will retrieve the most recently created report for the requested user.

For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» webhook|body|string(url)|true|The destination URL to which webhooks will be sent<br>|
|» days_requested|body|integer|true|The number of days of data to request for the report. Maximum is 731; minimum is 180. If a value lower than 180 is provided, a minimum of 180 days of history will be requested.|

|» client_report_id|body|string \| null|false|Client-generated identifier, which can be used by lenders to track loan applications.|
|» products|body|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|Specifies a list of products to generate when creating the report (in addition to the Base Report, which is always generated except for requests for only `cra_network_insights` or for FICO-only Partner Insights). These products will be made available before a success webhook is sent. Note that specifying `cra_partner_insights` in this field will trigger a billable event. Other products are not billed until the respective reports are retrieved via their product-specific `/get` endpoints.|
|» base_report|body|[CraCheckReportCreateBaseReportOptions](#schemacracheckreportcreatebasereportoptions)|false|Defines configuration options to generate a Base Report|
|» cashflow_insights|body|[CraCheckReportCreateCashflowInsightsOptions](#schemacracheckreportcreatecashflowinsightsoptions)|false|Defines configuration options to generate Cashflow Insights|
|» partner_insights|body|[CraCheckReportCreatePartnerInsightsOptions](#schemacracheckreportcreatepartnerinsightsoptions)|false|Defines configuration to generate Partner Insights.|

|» include_investments|body|boolean \| null|false|Indicates that investment data should be extracted from the linked account(s).|
|» income_insights|body|[CraCheckReportCreateIncomeInsightsOptions](#schemacracheckreportcreateincomeinsightsoptions)|false|Defines configuration options to generate Income Insights.|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|body|[ConsumerReportPermissiblePurpose](#schemaconsumerreportpermissiblepurpose)|true|Describes the reason you are generating a Consumer Report for this user. When calling `/link/token/create`, this field is required when using Plaid Check (CRA) products; invalid if not using Plaid Check (CRA) products.<br><br>`ACCOUNT_REVIEW_CREDIT`: In connection with a consumer credit transaction for the review or collection of an account pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(A).<br><br>`ACCOUNT_REVIEW_NON_CREDIT`: For a legitimate business need of the information to review a non-credit account provided primarily for personal, family, or household purposes to determine whether the consumer continues to meet the terms of the account pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(F)(2).<br><br>`EXTENSION_OF_CREDIT`: In connection with a credit transaction initiated by and involving the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(A).<br><br>`LEGITIMATE_BUSINESS_NEED_TENANT_SCREENING`: For a legitimate business need in connection with a business transaction initiated by the consumer primarily for personal, family, or household purposes in connection with a property rental assessment pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(F)(i).<br><br>`LEGITIMATE_BUSINESS_NEED_OTHER`: For a legitimate business need in connection with a business transaction made primarily for personal, family, or household initiated by the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(F)(i).<br><br>`WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION_PREQUALIFICATION`: In accordance with the written instructions of the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(2), to evaluate an application's profile to make an offer to the consumer.<br><br>`WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION_OTHER`: In accordance with the written instructions of the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(2), such as when an individual agrees to act as a guarantor or assumes personal liability for a consumer, business, or commercial loan.<br><br>`ELIGIBILITY_FOR_GOVT_BENEFITS`:  In connection with an eligibility determination for a government benefit where the entity is required to consider an applicant's financial status pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(D).|

`POST /cra/check_report/partner_insights/get`

This endpoint allows you to retrieve the Partner Insights report for your user. You should call this endpoint after you've received a `CHECK_REPORT_READY` or a `USER_CHECK_REPORT_READY` webhook, either after the Link session for the user or after calling `/cra/check_report/create`. If the most recent consumer report for the user doesn't have sufficient data to generate the report, or the consumer report has expired, you will receive an error indicating that you should create a new consumer report by calling `/cra/check_report/create`.

## Retrieve the LendScore from your user's banking data

<a id="opIdcraCheckReportLendScoreGet"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.com/cra/check_report/lend_score/get \

    }

```

`POST /cra/check_report/lend_score/get`

This endpoint allows you to retrieve the LendScore report for your user. You should call this endpoint after you've received a `CHECK_REPORT_READY` or a `USER_CHECK_REPORT_READY` webhook, either after the Link session for the user or after calling `/cra/check_report/create`. If the most recent consumer report for the user doesn't have sufficient data to generate the report, or the consumer report has expired, you will receive an error indicating that you should create a new consumer report by calling `/cra/check_report/create`.

<a href="/api/products/check-legacy/#cracheck_reportlend_scoreget">External documentation</a>

```json
  "user_token": "string",

}
```

`POST /cra/check_report/verification/get`

This endpoint allows you to retrieve home lending reports for a user. To obtain a VoA or Employment Refresh report, you need to make sure that `cra_base_report` is included in the `products` parameter when calling `/link/token/create` or `/cra/check_report/create`.

You should call this endpoint after you've received a `CHECK_REPORT_READY` or a `USER_CHECK_REPORT_READY` webhook, either after the Link session for the user or after calling `/cra/check_report/create`.

If the most recent consumer report for the user doesn't have sufficient data to generate the report, or the consumer report has expired, you will receive an error indicating that you should create a new consumer report by calling `/cra/check_report/create`.

<a href="/api/products/check-legacy/#cracheck_reportverificationget">External documentation</a>

```json
  "secret": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "reports_requested": [
    "VOA"
  ],
  "employment_refresh_options": {
    "days_requested": 0
  },
  "user_token": "string"
}
```

## Retrieve a Consumer Report as a Verification PDF

<a id="opIdcraCheckReportVerificationPdfGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/cra/check_report/verification/pdf/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_id": "string",
    "third_party_user_token": "string",
    "report_requested": {},
    "reports_requested": [
      "voa"
    ],
    "hide_gse_details": true,
    "user_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /cra/check_report/verification/pdf/get`

The `/cra/check_report/verification/pdf/get` endpoint retrieves the most recent Consumer Report in PDF format, specifically formatted for Home Lending verification use cases. Before calling this endpoint, ensure that you've created a VOA report through Link or the `/cra/check_report/create` endpoint, and have received a `CHECK_REPORT_READY` or a `USER_CHECK_REPORT_READY` webhook.

The response to `/cra/check_report/verification/pdf/get` is the PDF binary data. The `request_id`  is returned in the `Plaid-Request-ID` header.

<a href="/api/products/check-legacy/#cracheck_reportverificationpdfget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "third_party_user_token": "string",
  "report_requested": {},
  "reports_requested": [
    "voa"
  ],
  "hide_gse_details": true,
  "user_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-consumer-report-as-a-verification-pdf-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CraCheckReportVerificationPdfGetRequest](#schemacracheckreportverificationpdfgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» third_party_user_token|body|[ThirdPartyUserToken](#schemathirdpartyusertoken)|false|The third-party user token associated with the requested User data.|
|» report_requested|body|object|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» reports_requested|body|[[CraCheckReportVerificationPdfReportType](#schemacracheckreportverificationpdfreporttype)]|false|Specifies which types of verification reports to include in the returned PDF. Supported combinations are: `[voa]`, `[employment_refresh]`, `[income]`, or `[voa, income]`. Other combinations are not supported.<br>|
|» hide_gse_details|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the GSE identifiers (the Report ID and `gse_reference_id`) are omitted from the returned Home Lending Report PDF. Defaults to `false`. These identifiers are always present in the `/cra/check_report/verification/get` JSON response regardless of this field.<br>|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|false|The user token associated with the user for which data is being requested. This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» reports_requested|voa|
|» reports_requested|employment_refresh|
|» reports_requested|income|

`POST /cra/servicing/subscription/update`

`/cra/servicing/subscription/update` modifies an existing CRA servicing subscription. Fields left blank are unchanged; provided fields overwrite the current value. Use `reset_fields` to clear fields.

<a href="/api/products/check-legacy/#craservicingsubscriptionupdate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",

  "webhook": "http://example.com",
  "products": [

      "version": "string"
    }
  ],
  "reset_fields": [

  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|body|body|[CraServicingSubscriptionUpdateRequest](#schemacraservicingsubscriptionupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|

|» webhook|body|string(url)|false|The URL to which the webhook should be sent. If provided, this will override the URL set in the dashboard.|
|» products|body|[[CraSubscriptionProductConfig](#schemacrasubscriptionproductconfig)]|false|The products included in this subscription. If provided, this replaces the subscription's entire product list.|
|» reset_fields|body|[CraServicingSubscriptionUpdateRequestResettableFieldList](#schemacraservicingsubscriptionupdaterequestresettablefieldlist)|false|A list of fields to reset back to their default value. ## Generate an updated Consumer Report for your user

<a id="opIdcraReportCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/cra/report/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_id": "string",
    "products": [
      {
        "product": "cra_base_report",
        "version": "string",
        "options": {
          "require_identity": true
        }
      }
    ],
    "scope": {},
    "decision_stage": "PREQUALIFICATION",
    "consumer_report_permissible_purpose": {},
    "client_report_id": "string",
    "days_requested": 0,
    "days_required": 0,
    "include_investments": true,
    "include_identity_match": true,
    "webhook": "http://example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /cra/report/create`

`/cra/report/create` generates a Consumer Report for a user. With `scope` set to `PLAID_NETWORK`, the report is generated from the Plaid Network view of the user's profile. With `CLIENT_USER`, the report is generated from only the Items the user linked to your client.

Each requested product is generated asynchronously. Use the returned `report_id` to retrieve the report once its products are ready.

<a href="/api/products/check/#crareportcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "products": [
    {
      "product": "cra_base_report",
      "version": "string",
      "options": {
        "require_identity": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "scope": {},
  "decision_stage": "PREQUALIFICATION",
  "consumer_report_permissible_purpose": {},
  "client_report_id": "string",
  "days_requested": 0,
  "days_required": 0,
  "include_investments": true,
  "include_identity_match": true,
  "webhook": "http://example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="generate-an-updated-consumer-report-for-your-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CraReportCreateRequest](#schemacrareportcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|true|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» products|body|[[CraReportProduct](#schemacrareportproduct)]|true|The Plaid Check products, versions, and options to generate for the report.|
|» scope|body|object|true|none|
|» decision_stage|body|[CraReportDecisionStage](#schemacrareportdecisionstage)|true|The stage in the credit or other eligibility decisioning lifecycle for which a given report will be utilized.<br><br>Allowable permissible purposes for `PREQUALIFICATION`:<br><br>- `WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION_PREQUALIFICATION`<br><br>Allowable permissible purposes for `DECISIONING`:<br><br>- `ELIGIBILITY_FOR_GOVT_BENEFITS`<br>- `EXTENSION_OF_CREDIT`<br>- `LEGITIMATE_BUSINESS_NEED_OTHER`<br>- `LEGITIMATE_BUSINESS_NEED_TENANT_SCREENING`<br>- `WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION_OTHER`<br><br>If an incompatible `decision_stage` and `consumer_report_permissible_purpose` pairing is requested, an `INVALID_FIELD` error is returned. If your client isn't yet enabled for a given `decision_stage` on a product, a `DECISION_STAGE_NOT_ENABLED` error is returned instead (contact your Plaid account manager to enable it).|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|body|object|true|none|
|» client_report_id|body|string \| null|false|Client-generated identifier, which can be used by lenders to track loan applications.|
|» days_requested|body|integer \| null|false|The number of days of history to include in Plaid Check products. Maximum is 731. If a value lower than 180 is provided, a minimum of 180 days of history will be requested.|
|» days_required|body|integer \| null|false|The minimum number of days of data required for the report to be successfully generated.|
|» include_investments|body|boolean \| null|false|Indicates that investment data should be extracted from the linked account(s).|
|» include_identity_match|body|boolean \| null|false|Indicates that identity match results should be included for all products in the report that contain identity information. Defaults to `false`.|
|» webhook|body|string(url)|false|The destination URL to which the report's webhooks will be sent.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» decision_stage|PREQUALIFICATION|
|» decision_stage|DECISIONING|
|» decision_stage|SERVICING|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "request_id": "eYupqX1mZkEuQRx",
  "report_id": "cra-report-production-3c9d2a71-5e4b-4f0a-8b6d-7a1e9f2c4b58"
}
```

```json
  "error_message": "string",
  "display_message": "string",

    null
  ],

  ],
```

## Retrieve the credit profile report for a user

<a id="opIdcraCreditProfileReportGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/cra/credit_profile/report/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_id": "string",
    "consumer_report_permissible_purpose": "ACCOUNT_REVIEW_CREDIT",
    "client_report_id": "string",
    "report_type": "QUALIFY",
    "inquiry_type": "SOFT_INQUIRY",
    "version": "v1"
  }'
```

`POST /cra/credit_profile/report/get`

`/cra/credit_profile/report/get` retrieves a credit profile report for a user.

<a href="/none/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "consumer_report_permissible_purpose": "ACCOUNT_REVIEW_CREDIT",
  "client_report_id": "string",
  "report_type": "QUALIFY",
  "inquiry_type": "SOFT_INQUIRY",
  "version": "v1"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-the-credit-profile-report-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CraCreditProfileReportGetRequest](#schemacracreditprofilereportgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|true|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|body|[ConsumerReportPermissiblePurpose](#schemaconsumerreportpermissiblepurpose)|true|Describes the reason you are generating a Consumer Report for this user. When calling `/link/token/create`, this field is required when using Plaid Check (CRA) products; invalid if not using Plaid Check (CRA) products.<br><br>`ACCOUNT_REVIEW_CREDIT`: In connection with a consumer credit transaction for the review or collection of an account pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(A).<br><br>`ACCOUNT_REVIEW_NON_CREDIT`: For a legitimate business need of the information to review a non-credit account provided primarily for personal, family, or household purposes to determine whether the consumer continues to meet the terms of the account pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(F)(2).<br><br>`EXTENSION_OF_CREDIT`: In connection with a credit transaction initiated by and involving the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(A).<br><br>`LEGITIMATE_BUSINESS_NEED_TENANT_SCREENING`: For a legitimate business need in connection with a business transaction initiated by the consumer primarily for personal, family, or household purposes in connection with a property rental assessment pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(F)(i).<br><br>`LEGITIMATE_BUSINESS_NEED_OTHER`: For a legitimate business need in connection with a business transaction made primarily for personal, family, or household initiated by the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(F)(i).<br><br>`WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION_PREQUALIFICATION`: In accordance with the written instructions of the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(2), to evaluate an application's profile to make an offer to the consumer.<br><br>`WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION_OTHER`: In accordance with the written instructions of the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(2), such as when an individual agrees to act as a guarantor or assumes personal liability for a consumer, business, or commercial loan.<br><br>`ELIGIBILITY_FOR_GOVT_BENEFITS`:  In connection with an eligibility determination for a government benefit where the entity is required to consider an applicant's financial status pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(D).|
|» client_report_id|body|string|true|Client-generated identifier, which can be used by lenders to track loan applications.|
|» report_type|body|[CraCreditProfileReportType](#schemacracreditprofilereporttype)|true|The product type for the credit profile report request.|
|» inquiry_type|body|[CraCreditProfileInquiryType](#schemacracreditprofileinquirytype)|true|The inquiry type of credit profile report.|
|» version|body|[CraCreditProfileReportVersion](#schemacracreditprofilereportversion)|true|The version of the credit profile report to retrieve.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|ACCOUNT_REVIEW_CREDIT|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|ACCOUNT_REVIEW_NON_CREDIT|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|EXTENSION_OF_CREDIT|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|LEGITIMATE_BUSINESS_NEED_TENANT_SCREENING|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|LEGITIMATE_BUSINESS_NEED_OTHER|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION_PREQUALIFICATION|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION_OTHER|
|» consumer_report_permissible_purpose|ELIGIBILITY_FOR_GOVT_BENEFITS|
|» report_type|QUALIFY|
|» inquiry_type|SOFT_INQUIRY|
|» inquiry_type|STANDARD_INQUIRY|
|» version|v1|

## Create or refresh an OAuth access token

<a id="opIdoauthToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/oauth/token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "grant_type": "refresh_token",
    "client_id": "string",
    "client_secret": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "scope": "user:read user:write exchange",
    "refresh_token": "string",
    "resource": "https://production.plaid.com",
    "audience": "68028ce48d2b0dec68747f6c",
    "subject_token": "user-sandbox-b0e2c4ee-a763-4df5-bfe9-46a46bce993d",
    "subject_token_type": "urn:plaid:params:tokens:user"
  }'
```

`POST /oauth/token`

`/oauth/token` issues an access token and refresh token depending on the `grant_type` provided. This endpoint supports `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` as well as JSON. The fields for the form are equivalent to the fields for JSON and conform to the OAuth 2.0 specification.

<a href="/api/oauth/#oauthtoken">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "grant_type": "refresh_token",
  "client_id": "string",
  "client_secret": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "scope": "user:read user:write exchange",
  "refresh_token": "string",
  "resource": "https://production.plaid.com",
  "audience": "68028ce48d2b0dec68747f6c",
  "subject_token": "user-sandbox-b0e2c4ee-a763-4df5-bfe9-46a46bce993d",
  "subject_token_type": "urn:plaid:params:tokens:user"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-refresh-an-oauth-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[OAuthTokenRequest](#schemaoauthtokenrequest)|true|none|
|» grant_type|body|[OAuthGrantType](#schemaoauthgranttype)|true|The type of OAuth grant being requested:<br><br>`client_credentials` allows exchanging a client id and client secret for a refresh and access token.<br><br>`refresh_token` allows refreshing an access token using a refresh token. When using this grant type, only the `refresh_token` field is required (along with the `client_id` and `client_secret`).<br><br>`urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` allows exchanging a subject token for an OAuth token. When using this grant type, the `audience`, `subject_token` and `subject_token_type` fields are required.<br><br>These grants are defined in their respective RFCs. `refresh_token` and `client_credentials` are defined in RFC 6749 and `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` is defined in RFC 8693.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» client_secret|body|[OauthAPISecret](#schemaoauthapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body as either `secret` or `client_secret`.|
|» secret|body|[OauthAPISecret](#schemaoauthapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body as either `secret` or `client_secret`.|
|» scope|body|[OAuthScope](#schemaoauthscope)|false|A space-separated list of scopes associated with this token, in the format described in [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.3). Currently accepted values are:<br><br>`user:read` allows reading user data.<br><br>`user:write` allows writing user data.<br><br>`exchange` allows exchanging a token using the `urn:plaid:params:oauth:user-token` subject token type.<br><br>`mcp:dashboard` allows access to the MCP dashboard server.|
|» refresh_token|body|[OAuthRefreshToken](#schemaoauthrefreshtoken)|false|Refresh token for OAuth|
|» resource|body|string|false|URI of the target resource server|
|» audience|body|string|false|Used when exchanging a token. The meaning depends on the `subject_token_type`:<br><br>- For `urn:plaid:params:tokens:user`: Must be the same as the `client_id`.<br>- For `urn:plaid:params:oauth:user-token`: The other `client_id` to exchange tokens to.<br>- For `urn:plaid:params:credit:multi-user`:  a `client_id` or one of the supported CRA partner URNs: `urn:plaid:params:cra-partner:experian`, `urn:plaid:params:cra-partner:fannie-mae`, or `urn:plaid:params:cra-partner:freddie-mac`.|
|» subject_token|body|string|false|Token representing the subject. The meaning depends on the `subject_token_type`. For `urn:plaid:params:tokens:user`, the `subject_token` must be a Plaid-issued user token from the `/user/create` endpoint. For `urn:plaid:params:oauth:user-token`, the `subject_token` must be an OAuth refresh token issued from the `/oauth/token` endpoint.|
|» subject_token_type|body|[OAuthSubjectTokenType](#schemaoauthsubjecttokentype)|false|The type of the subject token.<br><br>`urn:plaid:params:tokens:user` allows exchanging a Plaid-issued user token for an OAuth token. When using this token type, `audience` must be the same as the `client_id`. `subject_token` must be a Plaid-issued user token issued from the `/user/create` endpoint.<br><br>`urn:plaid:params:oauth:user-token` allows exchanging a refresh token for an OAuth token to another `client_id`. The other `client_id` is provided in `audience`. `subject_token` must be an OAuth refresh token issued from the `/oauth/token` endpoint.<br><br>`urn:plaid:params:credit:multi-user` allows exchanging a Plaid-issued user token for an OAuth token. When using this token type, `audience` may be a client id or a supported CRA partner URN. `audience` supports a comma-delimited list of clients. When multiple clients are specified in the `audience` a multi-party token is created which can be used by all parties in the audience in conjunction with their `client_id` and `client_secret`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» grant_type|refresh_token|
|» grant_type|urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange|
|» grant_type|client_credentials|
|» subject_token_type|urn:plaid:params:tokens:user|
|» subject_token_type|urn:plaid:params:oauth:user-token|
|» subject_token_type|urn:plaid:params:credit:multi-user|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "pda-RDdg0TUCB0FB25_UPIlnhA==",
  "refresh_token": "pdr--viXurkDg88d5zf8m6Wl0g==",
  "expires_in": 900,
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "request_id": "m8MDqcS6F3lzqvP"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": "invalid_request",
  "error_description": "string",
  "error_uri": "string",
  "request_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-refresh-an-oauth-access-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[OAuthTokenResponse](#schemaoauthtokenresponse)|
|default|Default|Error response.|[OAuthErrorResponse](#schemaoautherrorresponse)|
