## Report whether you initiated an ACH transaction

<a id="opIdprocessorSignalDecisionReport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/processor/signal/decision/report \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "processor_token": "string",
    "client_transaction_id": "string",
    "initiated": true,
    "days_funds_on_hold": 0,
    "decision_outcome": "APPROVE",
    "payment_method": "SAME_DAY_ACH",
    "amount_instantly_available": 0
  }'
```

`POST /processor/signal/decision/report`

After you call `/processor/signal/evaluate`, Plaid will normally infer the outcome from your Signal Rules. However, if you are not using Signal Rules, if the Signal Rules outcome was `REVIEW`, or if you take a different action than the one determined by the Signal Rules, you will need to call `/processor/signal/decision/report`. This helps improve Signal Transaction Score accuracy for your account and is necessary for proper functioning of the rule performance and rule tuning capabilities in the Dashboard. If your effective decision changes after calling `/processor/signal/decision/report` (for example, you indicated that you accepted a transaction, but later on, your payment processor rejected it, so it was never initiated), call `/processor/signal/decision/report` again for the transaction to correct Plaid's records.

If you are using Plaid Transfer as your payment processor, you also do not need to call `/processor/signal/decision/report`, as Plaid can infer outcomes from your Transfer activity.

If using a Balance-only ruleset, this endpoint will not impact scores (Balance does not use scores), but is necessary to view accurate transaction outcomes and tune rule logic in the Dashboard.

<a href="/api/processor-partners/#processorsignaldecisionreport">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "processor_token": "string",
  "client_transaction_id": "string",
  "initiated": true,
  "days_funds_on_hold": 0,
  "decision_outcome": "APPROVE",
  "payment_method": "SAME_DAY_ACH",
  "amount_instantly_available": 0
}
```

<h3 id="report-whether-you-initiated-an-ach-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ProcessorSignalDecisionReportRequest](#schemaprocessorsignaldecisionreportrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» processor_token|body|[ProcessorToken](#schemaprocessortoken)|true|The processor token obtained from the Plaid integration partner. Processor tokens are in the format: `processor-<environment>-<identifier>`|
|» client_transaction_id|body|string|true|Must be the same as the `client_transaction_id` supplied when calling `/processor/signal/evaluate`|
|» initiated|body|boolean|true|`true` if the ACH transaction was initiated, `false` otherwise.<br><br>This field must be returned as a boolean. If formatted incorrectly, this will result in an [`INVALID_FIELD`](https://plaid.com/docs/errors/invalid-request/#invalid_field) error.|
|» days_funds_on_hold|body|integer \| null|false|The actual number of days (hold time) since the ACH debit transaction that you wait before making funds available to your customers. The holding time could affect the ACH return rate.<br><br>For example, use 0 if you make funds available to your customers instantly or the same day following the debit transaction, or 1 if you make funds available the next day following the debit initialization.|
|» decision_outcome|body|[SignalDecisionOutcome](#schemasignaldecisionoutcome)|false|The payment decision from the risk assessment.<br><br>`APPROVE`: approve the transaction without requiring further actions from your customers. For example, use this field if you are placing a standard hold for all the approved transactions before making funds available to your customers. You should also use this field if you decide to accelerate the fund availability for your customers.<br><br>`REVIEW`: the transaction requires manual review<br><br>`REJECT`: reject the transaction<br><br>`TAKE_OTHER_RISK_MEASURES`: for example, placing a longer hold on funds than those approved transactions or introducing customer frictions such as step-up verification/authentication<br><br>`NOT_EVALUATED`: if only logging the results without using them<br>|
|» payment_method|body|[SignalPaymentMethod](#schemasignalpaymentmethod)|false|The payment method to complete the transaction after the risk assessment. It may be different from the default payment method.<br><br>`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH by Nacha. The debit transaction is processed and settled on the same day.<br><br>`STANDARD_ACH`: Standard ACH by Nacha.<br><br>`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: if there is no default debit rail or there are multiple payment methods.<br>|
|» amount_instantly_available|body|number(double) \| null|false|The amount (in USD) made available to your customers instantly following the debit transaction. It could be a partial amount of the requested transaction (example: 102.05).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

|» decision_outcome|APPROVE|
|» decision_outcome|REVIEW|
|» decision_outcome|REJECT|
|» decision_outcome|TAKE_OTHER_RISK_MEASURES|
|» decision_outcome|NOT_EVALUATED|
|» payment_method|SAME_DAY_ACH|
|» payment_method|NEXT_DAY_ACH|
|» payment_method|STANDARD_ACH|
|» payment_method|MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS|
|» payment_method|null|

## Report a return for an ACH transaction

<a id="opIdprocessorSignalReturnReport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/processor/signal/return/report \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \

  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{

    "secret": "string",
    "processor_token": "string",
    "client_transaction_id": "string",
    "return_code": "string",
    "returned_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /processor/signal/return/report`

Call the `/processor/signal/return/report` endpoint to report a returned transaction that was previously sent to the `/processor/signal/evaluate` endpoint. Your feedback will be used by the model to incorporate the latest risk trend in your portfolio.

If you are using the [Plaid Transfer product](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer) to create transfers, it is not necessary to use this endpoint, as Plaid already knows whether the transfer was returned.

<a href="/api/processor-partners/#processorsignalreturnreport">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "processor_token": "string",
  "client_transaction_id": "string",
  "return_code": "string",
  "returned_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

## Opt-in a processor token to Signal

<a id="opIdprocessorSignalPrepare"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/processor/signal/prepare \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "processor_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /processor/signal/prepare`

When a processor token is not initialized with `signal`, call `/processor/signal/prepare` to opt-in that processor token to the data collection process, which will improve the accuracy of the Signal Transaction Score.

If this endpoint is called with a processor token that is already initialized with `signal`, it will return a 200 response and will not modify the processor token.

<a href="/api/processor-partners/#processorsignalprepare">External documentation</a>

Maximum of 50 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create a bank transfer fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single bank transfer is created.|
|» processor_token|body|[ProcessorToken](#schemaprocessortoken)|true|The processor token obtained from the Plaid integration partner. Processor tokens are in the format: `processor-<environment>-<identifier>`|
|» type|body|[BankTransferType](#schemabanktransfertype)|true|The type of bank transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into the origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of the origination account.|

|» amount|body|[BankTransferAmount](#schemabanktransferamount)|true|The amount of the bank transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|» iso_currency_code|body|string|true|The currency of the transfer amount - should be set to "USD".|
|» description|body|string|true|The transfer description. Maximum of 10 characters.|
|» ach_class|body|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|false|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network. For more details, see [ACH SEC codes](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/creating-transfers/#ach-sec-codes).<br><br>Codes supported for credits: `ccd`, `ppd`<br>Codes supported for debits: `ccd`, `ppd`, `tel`, `web`<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - The transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer. Authorization was obtained in writing either in person or via an electronic document signing, e.g. Docusign, by the consumer. Can be used for credits or debits.<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry. The transfer debits a consumer's bank account. Authorization from the consumer is obtained over the Internet (e.g. a web or mobile application). Can be used for single debits or recurring debits.<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry. The transfer debits a consumer. Debit authorization has been received orally over the telephone via a recorded call.|
|» user|body|[BankTransferUser](#schemabanktransferuser)|true|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|
|» custom_tag|body|string \| null|false|An arbitrary string provided by the client for storage with the bank transfer. May be up to 100 characters.|
|» metadata|body|[BankTransferMetadata](#schemabanktransfermetadata)|false|The Metadata object is a mapping of client-provided string fields to any string value. The following limitations apply:<br>The JSON values must be Strings (no nested JSON objects allowed)<br>Only ASCII characters may be used<br>Maximum of 50 key/value pairs<br>Maximum key length of 40 characters<br>Maximum value length of 500 characters<br>|
|» origination_account_id|body|string \| null|false|Plaid's unique identifier for the origination account for this transfer. If you have more than one origination account, this value must be specified.|

## Retrieve Liabilities data

<a id="opIdprocessorLiabilitiesGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/processor/liabilities/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "processor_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /processor/liabilities/get`

The `/processor/liabilities/get` endpoint returns various details about a loan or credit account. Liabilities data is available primarily for US financial institutions, with some limited coverage of Canadian institutions. Currently supported account types are account type `credit` with account subtype `credit card` or `paypal`, and account type `loan` with account subtype `student` or `mortgage`.

The types of information returned by Liabilities can include balances and due dates, loan terms, and account details such as original loan amount and guarantor. Data is refreshed approximately once per day; the latest data can be retrieved by calling `/processor/liabilities/get`.

Note: This request may take some time to complete if `liabilities` was not specified as an initial product when creating the processor token. This is because Plaid must communicate directly with the institution to retrieve the additional data.

<a href="/api/processor-partners/#processorliabilitiesget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "processor_token": "string"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ProcessorLiabilitiesGetRequest](#schemaprocessorliabilitiesgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» processor_token|body|[ProcessorToken](#schemaprocessortoken)|true|The processor token obtained from the Plaid integration partner. Processor tokens are in the format: `processor-<environment>-<identifier>`|

## Retrieve identity match score

<a id="opIdprocessorIdentityMatch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/processor/identity/match \
  -X POST \
```

`POST /processor/identity/match`

The `/processor/identity/match` endpoint generates a match score, which indicates how well the provided identity data matches the identity information on file with the account holder's financial institution.

Fields within the `balances` object will always be null when retrieved by `/processor/identity/match`. Instead, use the `/processor/balance/get` endpoint to retrieve balance data.

## Retrieve Balance data

<a id="opIdprocessorBalanceGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/processor/balance/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

      "min_last_updated_datetime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /processor/balance/get`

The `/processor/balance/get` endpoint returns the real-time balance for the account associated with the processor token. While other endpoints may return a balance object, only `/processor/balance/get` forces the available and current balance fields to be refreshed rather than cached. 

<a href="/api/processor-partners/#processorbalanceget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "processor_token": "string",
  "options": {
    "min_last_updated_datetime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-balance-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ProcessorBalanceGetRequest](#schemaprocessorbalancegetrequest)|true|The `/processor/balance/get` endpoint returns the real-time balance for the account associated with a given `processor_token`.<br><br>The current balance is the total amount of funds in the account. The available balance is the current balance less any outstanding holds or debits that have not yet posted to the account.<br><br>Note that not all institutions calculate the available balance. In the event that available balance is unavailable from the institution, Plaid will return an available balance value of `null`.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» processor_token|body|[ProcessorToken](#schemaprocessortoken)|true|The processor token obtained from the Plaid integration partner. Processor tokens are in the format: `processor-<environment>-<identifier>`|
|» options|body|[ProcessorBalanceGetRequestOptions](#schemaprocessorbalancegetrequestoptions)|false|Optional parameters to `/processor/balance/get`.|

<a id="opIditemAccessTokenInvalidate"></a>

`POST /item/access_token/invalidate`

By default, the `access_token` associated with an Item does not expire and should be stored in a persistent, secure manner.

You can use the `/item/access_token/invalidate` endpoint to rotate the `access_token` associated with an Item. The endpoint returns a new `access_token` and immediately invalidates the previous `access_token`.

## List webhook events

<a id="opIdbetaWebhookEventsList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/beta/webhook_events/list \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "7f57eb3d2a9j6480121fx361",
    "secret": "79g03eoofwl8240v776r2h667442119",
    "count": 100
  }'
```

`POST /beta/webhook_events/list`

`/beta/webhook_events/list` returns the webhooks Plaid sent to your account in the last 7 days, including webhooks that weren't delivered. Use it to recover webhooks your endpoint missed. Events are returned oldest first.

`TRANSACTIONS` webhooks are not included. To recover Transactions updates, use [`/transactions/sync`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#transactionssync).

To page through events, omit `cursor` on your first request, then pass the previous response's `next_cursor` on each later request. Store `next_cursor` even when `has_more` is `false`, so your next poll returns only newer events.

Filters are optional. An event matches a filter if it matches any of the filter's values, and must match every filter you provide.

Events older than 7 days are not retained. If your cursor or `start_time` is older than that, the request fails with `WEBHOOK_EVENTS_CURSOR_EXPIRED` or `WEBHOOK_EVENTS_START_TIME_OUT_OF_RANGE`.

This endpoint is in beta and may change in backwards-incompatible ways. Send feedback to building@plaid.com.

<a href="/api/webhooks/webhook-events/#betawebhook_eventslist">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "7f57eb3d2a9j6480121fx361",
  "secret": "79g03eoofwl8240v776r2h667442119",
  "count": 100
}
```

<h3 id="list-webhook-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BetaWebhookEventsListRequest](#schemabetawebhookeventslistrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» cursor|body|string|false|The `next_cursor` from a previous `/beta/webhook_events/list` response. Omit on your first request. If provided, `start_time` is ignored.|
|» start_time|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return events sent at or after this time, in ISO 8601 format. Must be within the last 7 days. Ignored if `cursor` is provided. If you omit both `cursor` and `start_time`, results start with the oldest retained event.|
|» count|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of webhook events to return. Fewer events may be returned even when more are available; use `has_more` to determine whether to request another page.|
|» webhook_types|body|[string]|false|Return only events with these webhook types, for example `ITEM`. Case-sensitive.|
|» webhook_codes|body|[string]|false|Return only events with these webhook codes, for example `ERROR`. Case-sensitive.|
|» item_ids|body|[string]|false|Return only events for these Items.|
|» delivery_statuses|body|[[WebhookEventDeliveryStatus](#schemawebhookeventdeliverystatus)]|false|Return only events with these delivery statuses.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» delivery_statuses|PENDING|
|» delivery_statuses|DELIVERED|
|» delivery_statuses|FAILED|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "webhook_events": [
    {
      "webhook_message_id": "whmsg_4tQ9pNzL2vBxYK",
      "webhook_type": "ITEM",
      "webhook_code": "PENDING_EXPIRATION",
      "item_id": "abc123",
      "sent_time": "2026-07-21T14:32:00Z",
      "payload": {
        "webhook_type": "ITEM",
        "webhook_code": "PENDING_EXPIRATION"
      },
      "destination_url": "https://client.example.com/webhook",
      "delivery_status": "DELIVERED",
      "last_http_status_code": 200,
      "attempt_count": 1,
      "last_attempt_time": "2026-07-21T14:32:01Z"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "eyJzZW50X3RpbWUiOiIyMDI2LTA3LTIxVDE0OjMyOjAwWiIsIndlYmhvb2tfbWVzc2FnZV9pZCI6IndobXNnXzR0UTlwTnpMMnZCeFlLIn0",
  "request_id": "4zlKapIkTm8p5KM"
}
```

> default Response

```json

  "error_type": "INVALID_INPUT",
  "error_code": "WEBHOOK_EVENTS_CURSOR_EXPIRED",
```

<a id="opIdwebhookVerificationKeyGet"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.com/webhook_verification_key/get \
```

`POST /webhook_verification_key/get`

Plaid signs all outgoing webhooks and provides JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) so that you can verify the authenticity of any incoming webhooks to your application. A message signature is included in the `Plaid-Verification` header.

The `/webhook_verification_key/get` endpoint provides a JSON Web Key (JWK) that can be used to verify a JWT.

<a href="/api/webhooks/webhook-verification/#get-webhook-verification-key">External documentation</a>

## Retrieve Liabilities data

<a id="opIdliabilitiesGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/liabilities/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "access_token": "string",
    "options": {
      "account_ids": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /liabilities/get`

The `/liabilities/get` endpoint returns various details about an Item with loan or credit accounts. Liabilities data is available primarily for US financial institutions, with some limited coverage of Canadian institutions. Supported account types are account type `credit` with account subtype `credit card` or `paypal`; and account type `loan` with account subtype `auto`, `commercial`, `commercial line of credit`, `consumer`, `home equity`, `home equity loan`, `line of credit`, `loan`, `mortgage`, or `student`. To limit accounts listed in Link to types and subtypes supported by Liabilities, you can use the `account_filters` parameter when [creating a Link token](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/#linktokencreate).

To receive the expanded loan subtype values, use plaid-go 10.1.0 or later, plaid-java 44.0.0 or later, plaid-python 8.3.0 or later, or plaid-ruby 14.4.0 or later. Earlier client library versions may receive `loan` instead of `home equity loan` and `line of credit` instead of `commercial line of credit`.

The types of information returned by Liabilities can include balances and due dates, loan terms, and account details such as original loan amount and guarantor. Data is refreshed approximately once per day; the latest data can be retrieved by calling `/liabilities/get`.

<a href="/api/products/liabilities/#liabilitiesget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "access_token": "string",
  "options": {
    "account_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-liabilities-data-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[LiabilitiesGetRequest](#schemaliabilitiesgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|
|» options|body|[LiabilitiesGetRequestOptions](#schemaliabilitiesgetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object to filter `/liabilities/get` results. If provided, `options` cannot be null.|

## Create payment recipient

<a id="opIdpaymentInitiationRecipientCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/payment_initiation/recipient/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "iban": "stringstringstr",
    "bacs": {
      "account": "string",
      "sort_code": "string"
    },
    "address": {
      "street": [
        "string"
      ],
      "city": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "country": "st"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /payment_initiation/recipient/create`

Create a payment recipient for payment initiation.  The recipient must be in Europe, within a country that is a member of the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) or a non-Eurozone country [supported](https://support.plaid.com/hc/en-us/articles/27895826947735-What-Plaid-products-are-supported-in-each-country-and-region) by Plaid. For a standing order (recurring) payment, the recipient must be in the UK.

It is recommended to use `bacs` in the UK and `iban` in EU.

The endpoint is idempotent: if a developer has already made a request with the same payment details, Plaid will return the same `recipient_id`.


<a href="/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiationrecipientcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "iban": "stringstringstr",
  "bacs": {
    "account": "string",
    "sort_code": "string"
  },
  "address": {
    "street": [
      "string"
    ],
    "city": "string",
    "postal_code": "string",
    "country": "st"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-payment-recipient-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PaymentInitiationRecipientCreateRequest](#schemapaymentinitiationrecipientcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the recipient. We recommend using strings of length 18 or less and avoid special characters to ensure compatibility with all institutions.|
|» iban|body|string \| null|false|The International Bank Account Number (IBAN) for the recipient. If Bacs data is not provided, an IBAN is required.|
|» bacs|body|[RecipientBACSNullable](#schemarecipientbacsnullable)|false|An object containing a Bacs account number and sort code. If an IBAN is not provided or if this recipient needs to accept domestic GBP-denominated payments, Bacs data is required.|
|» address|body|[PaymentInitiationAddress](#schemapaymentinitiationaddress)|false|The optional address of the payment recipient's bank account. Required by most institutions outside of the UK.|

## Reverse an existing payment

<a id="opIdpaymentInitiationPaymentReverse"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/payment_initiation/payment/reverse \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "payment_id": "string",
    "idempotency_key": "string",
    "reference": "string",
    "amount": {
      "currency": "GBP",
      "value": 0.01
    },
    "counterparty_date_of_birth": "1970-01-01",
    "counterparty_address": {
      "street": [
        "string"
      ],
      "city": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "country": "st"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /payment_initiation/payment/reverse`

Reverse a settled payment from a Plaid virtual account.

The original payment must be in a settled state to be refunded.
To refund partially, specify the amount as part of the request.
If the amount is not specified, the refund amount will be equal to all
of the remaining payment amount that has not been refunded yet.

The refund will go back to the source account that initiated the payment.
The original payment must have been initiated to a Plaid virtual account
so that this account can be used to initiate the refund.

Providing counterparty information such as date of birth and address increases
the likelihood of refund being successful without human intervention.


<a href="/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiationpaymentreverse">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "payment_id": "string",
  "idempotency_key": "string",
  "reference": "string",
  "amount": {
    "currency": "GBP",
    "value": 0.01
  },
  "counterparty_date_of_birth": "1970-01-01",
  "counterparty_address": {
    "street": [
      "string"
    ],
    "city": "string",
    "postal_code": "string",
    "country": "st"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="reverse-an-existing-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PaymentInitiationPaymentReverseRequest](#schemapaymentinitiationpaymentreverserequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» payment_id|body|string|true|The ID of the payment to reverse|
|» idempotency_key|body|[WalletTransactionIdempotencyKey](#schemawallettransactionidempotencykey)|true|A random key provided by the client, per unique wallet transaction. Maximum of 128 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. If a request to execute a wallet transaction fails due to a network connection error, then after a minimum delay of one minute, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single wallet transaction is created. If the request was successfully processed, it will prevent any transaction that uses the same idempotency key, and was received within 48 hours of the first request, from being processed.|
|» reference|body|string|true|A reference for the refund. This must be a string of 6 to 18 characters containing only letters, numbers, and spaces.|
|» amount|body|[PaymentAmountToRefund](#schemapaymentamounttorefund)|false|The amount and currency of a payment|
|» counterparty_date_of_birth|body|string(date) \| null|false|The counterparty's birthdate, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) (YYYY-MM-DD) format.|
|» counterparty_address|body|[PaymentInitiationAddress](#schemapaymentinitiationaddress)|false|The optional address of the payment recipient's bank account. Required by most institutions outside of the UK.|

## Create a payment

<a id="opIdpaymentInitiationPaymentCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/payment_initiation/payment/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "recipient_id": "string",
    "user_id": "string",
    "reference": "string",
    "amount": {
      "currency": "GBP",
      "value": 0
    },
    "schedule": {
      "interval": "WEEKLY",
      "interval_execution_day": 0,
      "start_date": "1970-01-01",
      "end_date": "1970-01-01",
      "adjusted_start_date": "1970-01-01"
    },
    "options": {
      "request_refund_details": true,
      "iban": "stringstringstr",
      "bacs": {
        "account": "string",
        "sort_code": "string"
      },
      "scheme": null
    }
  }'
```

`POST /payment_initiation/payment/create`

After creating a payment recipient, you can use the `/payment_initiation/payment/create` endpoint to create a payment to that recipient.  Payments can be one-time or standing order (recurring) and can be denominated in EUR, GBP, or another chosen [currency](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiation-payment-create-request-amount-currency).  If making domestic GBP-denominated payments, your recipient must have been created with Bacs numbers. In general, EUR-denominated payments will be sent via SEPA Credit Transfer, GBP-denominated payments will be sent via the Faster Payments network and for non-Eurozone markets typically via the local payment scheme, but the payment network used will be determined by the institution. Payments sent via Faster Payments will typically arrive immediately, while payments sent via SEPA Credit Transfer or other local payment schemes will typically arrive in one business day.

Standing orders (recurring payments) must be denominated in GBP and can only be sent to recipients in the UK. Once created, standing order payments cannot be modified or canceled via the API. An end user can cancel or modify a standing order directly on their banking application or website, or by contacting the bank. Standing orders will follow the payment rules of the underlying rails (Faster Payments in UK). Payments can be sent Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. If the pre-arranged date falls on a weekend or bank holiday, the payment is made on the next working day. It is not possible to guarantee the exact time the payment will reach the recipient's account, although at least 90% of standing order payments are sent by 6am.

<a href="/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiationpaymentcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "recipient_id": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "reference": "string",
  "amount": {
    "currency": "GBP",
    "value": 0
  },
  "schedule": {
    "interval": "WEEKLY",
    "interval_execution_day": 0,
    "start_date": "1970-01-01",
    "end_date": "1970-01-01",
    "adjusted_start_date": "1970-01-01"
  },
  "options": {
    "request_refund_details": true,
    "iban": "stringstringstr",
    "bacs": {
      "account": "string",
      "sort_code": "string"
    },
    "scheme": null
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PaymentInitiationPaymentCreateRequest](#schemapaymentinitiationpaymentcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» recipient_id|body|string|true|The ID of the recipient the payment is for.|
|» user_id|body|string|false|The `user_id` of the end user the payment is initiated for, as returned by [`/user/create`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/#usercreate). The user must have a `name` and either an email address or a phone number. Required for new integrations.|
|» reference|body|string|true|A reference for the payment. This must be a string of at most 18 characters containing only letters, numbers, and spaces (since not all institutions support them).<br>In order to track settlement via Payment Confirmation, each payment must have a unique reference. If the reference provided through the API is not unique, Plaid will adjust it.<br>Some institutions may limit the reference to less than 18 characters. If necessary, Plaid will adjust the reference by truncating it to fit the institution's requirements.<br>Both the originally provided and automatically adjusted references (if any) can be found in the `reference` and `adjusted_reference` fields, respectively.|
|» amount|body|[PaymentAmount](#schemapaymentamount)|true|The amount and currency of a payment|
|» schedule|body|[ExternalPaymentScheduleRequest](#schemaexternalpaymentschedulerequest)|false|The schedule that the payment will be executed on. If a schedule is provided, the payment is automatically set up as a standing order. If no schedule is specified, the payment will be executed only once.|
|» options|body|[ExternalPaymentOptions](#schemaexternalpaymentoptions)|false|Additional payment options|

```json
  "payment_id": "payment-id-sandbox-feca8a7a-5591-4aef-9297-f3062bb735d3",
  "status": "PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED",
  "request_id": "4ciYVmesrySiUAB"
}
```

## Create payment token

<a id="opIdcreatePaymentToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/payment_initiation/payment/token/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  }'
```

`POST /payment_initiation/payment/token/create`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

The `/payment_initiation/payment/token/create` endpoint has been deprecated. New Plaid customers will be unable to use this endpoint, and existing customers are encouraged to migrate to the newer, `link_token`-based flow. The recommended flow is to provide the `payment_id` to `/link/token/create`, which returns a `link_token` used to initialize Link.

The `/payment_initiation/payment/token/create` endpoint is used to create a `payment_token`, which can then be used in Link initialization to enter a payment initiation flow. You can only use a `payment_token` once. If this attempt fails, the end user aborts the flow, or the token expires, you will need to create a new payment token. Creating a new payment token does not require end user input.

<a href="/link/maintain-legacy-integration/#creating-a-payment-token">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "payment_id": "string"
}
```

`POST /payment_initiation/consent/create`

The `/payment_initiation/consent/create` endpoint is used to create a payment consent, which can be used to initiate payments on behalf of the user. Payment consents are created with `UNAUTHORISED` status by default and must be authorised by the user before payments can be initiated.

Consents can be limited in time and scope, and have constraints that describe limitations for payments.

<a href="/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiationconsentcreate">External documentation</a>

```json
      }
    ]
  },
  "options": {
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|body|body|[PaymentInitiationConsentCreateRequest](#schemapaymentinitiationconsentcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|

<a id="opIdpaymentInitiationConsentPaymentExecute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/payment_initiation/consent/payment/execute \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "consent_id": "string",
    "amount": {
      "currency": "GBP",
      "value": 0
    },
    "idempotency_key": "string",
    "reference": "string",
    "scope": {},
    "processing_mode": "ASYNC"
  }'
```

`POST /payment_initiation/consent/payment/execute`

The `/payment_initiation/consent/payment/execute` endpoint can be used to execute payments using payment consent.

<a href="/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiationconsentpaymentexecute">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "consent_id": "string",
  "amount": {
    "currency": "GBP",
    "value": 0
  },
  "idempotency_key": "string",
  "reference": "string",
  "scope": {},
  "processing_mode": "ASYNC"
}
```

<h3 id="execute-a-single-payment-using-consent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PaymentInitiationConsentPaymentExecuteRequest](#schemapaymentinitiationconsentpaymentexecuterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» consent_id|body|string|true|The consent ID.|
|» amount|body|[PaymentAmount](#schemapaymentamount)|true|The amount and currency of a payment|
|» idempotency_key|body|[ConsentPaymentIdempotencyKey](#schemaconsentpaymentidempotencykey)|true|A random key provided by the client, per unique consent payment. Maximum of 128 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. If a request to execute a consent payment fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single payment is created. If the request was successfully processed, it will prevent any payment that uses the same idempotency key, and was received within 48 hours of the first request, from being processed.|
|» reference|body|string \| null|false|A reference for the payment. This must be a string of at most 18 characters containing only letters, numbers, and spaces (since not all institutions support them).<br>If not provided, Plaid will automatically fall back to the reference from consent. In order to track settlement via Payment Confirmation, each payment must have a unique reference. If the reference provided through the API is not unique, Plaid will adjust it.<br>Some institutions may limit the reference to less than 18 characters. If necessary, Plaid will adjust the reference by truncating it to fit the institution's requirements.<br>Both the originally provided and automatically adjusted references (if any) can be found in the `reference` and `adjusted_reference` fields, respectively.|
|» scope|body|object|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» processing_mode|body|[PaymentInitiationConsentProcessingMode](#schemapaymentinitiationconsentprocessingmode)|false|Decides the mode under which the payment processing should be performed, using `IMMEDIATE` as default.<br><br>`IMMEDIATE`: Will immediately execute the payment, waiting for a response from the ASPSP before returning the result of the payment initiation. This is ideal for user-present flows.<br><br> `ASYNC`: Will accept a payment execution request and schedule it for processing, immediately returning the new `payment_id`. Listen for webhooks to obtain real-time updates on the payment status. This is ideal for non user-present flows.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» processing_mode|ASYNC|
|» processing_mode|IMMEDIATE|

```json
  "payment_id": "payment-id-sandbox-feca8a7a-5591-4aef-9297-f3062bb735d3",
  "request_id": "4ciYccesdqSiUAB",
  "status": "PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED"
}
```

## Force a Sandbox Item into an error state

<a id="opIdsandboxItemResetLogin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sandbox/item/reset_login \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "access_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sandbox/item/reset_login`

`/sandbox/item/reset_login` forces an Item into an `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` state in order to simulate an Item whose login is no longer valid. This makes it easy to test Link's [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode) flow in the Sandbox environment.  After calling `/sandbox/item/reset_login`, you can then use Plaid Link update mode to restore the Item to a good state. An `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` webhook will also be fired after a call to this endpoint, if one is associated with the Item.
In the Sandbox, Items will transition to an `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` error state automatically after 30 days, even if this endpoint is not called.

<a href="/api/sandbox/#sandboxitemreset_login">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "access_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="force-a-sandbox-item-into-an-error-state-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SandboxItemResetLoginRequest](#schemasandboxitemresetloginrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|

`POST /sandbox/item/application/seed`

The `access_token` must belong to a Permissions Manager Item created via `/item/import` in Sandbox. The `application_id` identifies the application to seed as a connected app. To disconnect a seeded application, use `/item/application/unlink`.

## Seed an FDX consent grant for a sandbox data partner

<a id="opIdsandboxFdxConsentSeed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sandbox/fdx/consent/seed \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "customer_id": "string",
    "application_id": "string",
    "consent_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sandbox/fdx/consent/seed`

`/sandbox/fdx/consent/seed` creates a test FDX consent grant (and a backing Item) for a data provider's customer in Sandbox, so the FDX Consent API endpoints can be exercised end-to-end without a live data provider connection.

`customer_id` is the data provider's identifier for the end user and `application_id` identifies the data recipient application the consent is granted to; both are required. Optionally provide `consent_id` (a UUIDv4) to control the seeded grant's identifier; one is generated when omitted. The seeded grant is returned by `/fdx/consents` and `/fdx/consents/{consentId}`, and can be revoked via `/fdx/consents/{consentId}/revocation`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "customer_id": "string",
  "application_id": "string",
  "consent_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="seed-an-fdx-consent-grant-for-a-sandbox-data-partner-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SandboxFdxConsentSeedRequest](#schemasandboxfdxconsentseedrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» customer_id|body|string|true|The data provider's identifier for the end user to associate the seeded consent grant with.|
|» application_id|body|[ApplicationID](#schemaapplicationid)|true|This field will map to the application ID that is returned from `/item/application/list`, or provided to the institution in an oauth redirect.|
|» consent_id|body|string|false|Optional UUIDv4 identifier for the seeded consent grant. If omitted, one is generated. Seeding fails if a grant with this identifier already exists.|

## Force item(s) for a Sandbox User into an error state

<a id="opIdsandboxUserResetLogin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sandbox/user/reset_login \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_token": "string",
    "item_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "user_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sandbox/user/reset_login`

`/sandbox/user/reset_login` functions the same as `/sandbox/item/reset_login`, but will modify Items related to a User. This endpoint forces each Item into an `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` state in order to simulate an Item whose login is no longer valid. This makes it easy to test Link's [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode) flow in the Sandbox environment.  After calling `/sandbox/user/reset_login`, you can then use Plaid Link update mode to restore Items associated with the User to a good state. An `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` webhook will also be fired after a call to this endpoint, if one is associated with the Item.
In the Sandbox, Items will transition to an `ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` error state automatically after 30 days, even if this endpoint is not called.

<a href="/api/sandbox/#sandboxuserreset_login">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_token": "string",
  "item_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "user_id": "string"
}
```

## Exchange public token for an access token

<a id="opIditemPublicTokenExchange"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/item/public_token/exchange \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "public_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /item/public_token/exchange`

Exchange a Link `public_token` for an API `access_token`. Link hands off the `public_token` client-side via the `onSuccess` callback once a user has successfully created an Item. The `public_token` is ephemeral and expires after 30 minutes. An `access_token` does not expire, but can be revoked by calling `/item/remove`.

The response also includes an `item_id` that should be stored with the `access_token`. The `item_id` is used to identify an Item in a webhook. The `item_id` can also be retrieved by making an `/item/get` request.

<a href="/api/items/#itempublic_tokenexchange">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "public_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="exchange-public-token-for-an-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ItemPublicTokenExchangeRequest](#schemaitempublictokenexchangerequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» public_token|body|string|true|Your `public_token`, obtained from the Link `onSuccess` callback or `/sandbox/public_token/create`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "access-sandbox-de3ce8ef-33f8-452c-a685-8671031fc0f6",
  "item_id": "M5eVJqLnv3tbzdngLDp9FL5OlDNxlNhlE55op",
  "request_id": "Aim3b"
}
```

<a id="opIditemCreatePublicToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/item/public_token/create \
```

`POST /item/public_token/create`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Note: As of July 2020, the `/item/public_token/create` endpoint is deprecated. Instead, use `/link/token/create` with an `access_token` to create a Link token for use with [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode).

If you need your user to take action to restore or resolve an error associated with an Item, generate a public token with the `/item/public_token/create` endpoint and then initialize Link with that `public_token`.

A `public_token` is one-time use and expires after 30 minutes. You use a `public_token` to initialize Link in [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode) for a particular Item. You can generate a `public_token` for an Item even if you did not use Link to create the Item originally.

The `/item/public_token/create` endpoint is **not** used to create your initial `public_token`. If you have not already received an `access_token` for a specific Item, use Link to obtain your `public_token` instead. See the [Quickstart](https://plaid.com/docs/quickstart) for more information.

<a href="/api/link/#itempublic_tokencreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
```

## Create user

<a id="opIduserCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/create \
  -X POST \

  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "client_user_id": "string",
    "identity": {
      "name": {
        "given_name": "string",
        "family_name": "string"
      },
      "date_of_birth": "1970-01-01",
      "emails": [
        {
          "data": "string",
          "primary": true
        }
      ],
      "phone_numbers": [
        {
          "data": "string",
          "primary": true
        }
      ],
      "addresses": [
        {
          "street_1": "string",
          "street_2": "string",
          "city": "string",
          "region": "string",
          "country": "string",
          "postal_code": "string",
          "primary": true
        }
      ],
      "id_numbers": [
        {
          "value": "123456789",
          "type": "us_ssn"
        }
      ]
    },
    "end_customer": "string",
    "consumer_report_user_identity": {
      "first_name": "string",
      "last_name": "string",
      "phone_numbers": [
        "string"
      ],
      "emails": [
        "string"
      ],
      "ssn_full": "string",
      "ssn_last_4": "stri",
      "date_of_birth": "1970-01-01",
      "primary_address": {
        "city": "string",
        "region": "string",
        "street": "string",
        "postal_code": "string",
        "country": "string"
      }
    },
    "with_upgraded_user": true
  }'
```

`POST /user/create`

For Plaid products and flows that use the user object, `/user/create` provides you a single token to access all data associated with the user. You must call this endpoint before calling `/link/token/create` if you are using any of the following: Plaid Check, Income Verification, Multi-Item Link, or Plaid Protect (Identity). If you are using Plaid Protect Link session scoring, you do not need to call `/user/create` first; Plaid will resolve or create the user when `user.client_user_id` is provided in `/link/token/create`.
For customers who began using this endpoint on or after December 10, 2025, this endpoint takes a `client_user_id` and an `identity` object and will return a `user_id`. For customers who began using it before that date, the endpoint takes a `client_user_id` and a `consumer_report_user_identity` object and will return a `user_token` and `user_id`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).
In order to create a Plaid Check Consumer Report for a user, or to use Payment Initiation, Variable Recurring Payments, or Virtual Accounts, the `identity` (new) or `consumer_report_user_identity` (legacy) object must be present. If it is not provided during the `/user/create` call, it can be added later by calling `/user/update`.


When using Payment Initiation, Variable Recurring Payments, or Virtual Accounts, the `identity` object must contain a `name` and either an email address or a phone number.


In order to generate a Plaid Check Consumer Report, the following `identity` fields, at minimum, are required and must be non-empty: `name`, `date_of_birth`, `emails`, `phone_numbers`, and `addresses` (with at least one email, phone number, and address designated as `primary`). Plaid Check Consumer Reports can only be created for US-based users; the user's address country must be `US`. If creating a report for sharing with a GSE such as Fannie or Freddie, the user's full SSN must be provided via the `id_numbers` field. Providing at least a partial SSN is also strongly recommended for all use cases, since it improves the accuracy of matching user records during compliance processes such as file disclosure, dispute, or security freeze requests.


When using Plaid Protect, it is highly recommended that you provide an `identity` object to better identify and block fraud across your Link sessions.


Plaid will normalize identity fields before storing them and utilize the same identity across different user-based products.

<a href="/api/users/#usercreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "client_user_id": "string",
  "identity": {
    "name": {
      "given_name": "string",
      "family_name": "string"
    },
    "date_of_birth": "1970-01-01",
    "emails": [
      {
        "data": "string",
        "primary": true
      }
    ],
    "phone_numbers": [
      {
        "data": "string",
        "primary": true
      }
    ],
    "addresses": [
      {
        "street_1": "string",
        "street_2": "string",
        "city": "string",
        "region": "string",
        "country": "string",
        "postal_code": "string",
        "primary": true
      }
    ],
    "id_numbers": [
      {
        "value": "123456789",
        "type": "us_ssn"
      }
    ]
  },
  "end_customer": "string",
  "consumer_report_user_identity": {
    "first_name": "string",
    "last_name": "string",
    "phone_numbers": [
      "string"
    ],
    "emails": [
      "string"
    ],
    "ssn_full": "string",
    "ssn_last_4": "stri",
    "date_of_birth": "1970-01-01",
    "primary_address": {
      "city": "string",
      "region": "string",
      "street": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "country": "string"
    }
  },
  "with_upgraded_user": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Plaid-New-User-API-Enabled|header|boolean|false|The HTTP header used in API requests to determine which set of User APIs to invoke: the legacy CRA version or the new User API version.|
|body|body|[UserCreateRequest](#schemausercreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» client_user_id|body|string|true|A unique ID representing the end user. Maximum of 128 characters. Typically this will be a user ID number from your application. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|» identity|body|[ClientUserIdentity](#schemaclientuseridentity)|false|The identity fields associated with a user. For a user to be eligible for a Plaid Check Consumer Report, all fields are required except `id_numbers`. Providing a partial SSN is strongly recommended, and improves the accuracy of matching user records during compliance processes such as file disclosure, dispute, or security freeze requests. If creating a report that will be shared with GSEs such as Fannie or Freddie, a full Social Security Number must be provided via the `id_numbers` field.|
|» end_customer|body|string|false|A unique ID representing a CRA reseller's end customer. Maximum of 128 characters.|
|» consumer_report_user_identity|body|[ConsumerReportUserIdentity](#schemaconsumerreportuseridentity)|false|This field is only used by integrations created before December 10, 2025. All other integrations must use the `identity` object instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).<br>To create a Plaid Check Consumer Report for a user when using a `user_token`, this field must be present. If this field is not provided during user token creation, you can add it to the user later by calling `/user/update`. Once the field has been added to the user, you will be able to call `/link/token/create` with a non-empty `consumer_report_permissible_purpose` (which will automatically create a Plaid Check Consumer Report), or call `/cra/check_report/create` for that user.|
|» with_upgraded_user|body|boolean|false|If your integration with the User API predates December 10, 2025, set this field to `true` to opt into the [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis/). When enabled, you can use the `identity` field instead of `consumer_report_user_identity`.|

```json
  "request_id": "Aim3b"
}
```

<a id="opIduserIdentityRemove"></a>

`POST /user/identity/remove`

This endpoint allows customers to explicitly purge identity/PII data provided to Plaid for a given user. This is not exposed to customers by default, as it is meant for special scenarios or requests, but Plaid is obligated to enable customers to delete PII provided to us.

<a href="/api/users/#useridentityremove">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_id": "string"
}
```

`POST /user/update`

This endpoint updates user information for an existing `user_id` or `user_token`. If an existing `user_id` or `user_token` is missing fields required for a given use case (e.g. creating a Consumer Report) use `/user/update` to add values for those fields.

Identity updates use merge semantics: provided fields overwrite existing ones; omitted fields remain unchanged.

<a href="/api/users/#userupdate">External documentation</a>

Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|

For a user to be eligible for a Plaid Check Consumer Report, all fields are required except `id_numbers`. Providing a partial SSN is strongly recommended, and improves the accuracy of matching user records during compliance processes such as file disclosure, dispute, or security freeze requests. If creating a report that will be shared with GSEs such as Fannie or Freddie, a full Social Security Number must be provided via the `id_numbers` field.|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|false|The user token associated with the user for which data is being requested. This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» consumer_report_user_identity|body|[ConsumerReportUserIdentity](#schemaconsumerreportuseridentity)|false|This field is only used by integrations created before December 10, 2025. All other integrations must use the `identity` object instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).<br>To create a Plaid Check Consumer Report for a user when using a `user_token`, this field must be present. If this field is not provided during user token creation, you can add it to the user later by calling `/user/update`. Once the field has been added to the user, you will be able to call `/link/token/create` with a non-empty `consumer_report_permissible_purpose` (which will automatically create a Plaid Check Consumer Report), or call `/cra/check_report/create` for that user.|

## Terminate products for a user

<a id="opIduserProductsTerminate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/products/terminate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "usr_8c3ZbDBYjaqUXZ",
    "reason_code": "CONSUMER_ACCOUNT_CLOSED",
    "reason_note": "User closed account with client."
  }'
```

`POST /user/products/terminate`

Terminates Financial Management, Plaid Protect, and Servicing products associated with a `user_id`. Use this endpoint when offboarding a user or ending their subscriptions. Item access tokens are not required.

For Financial Management products, including Transactions, Liabilities, and Investments, this endpoint removes each associated Item that contains one of these products. Removal makes the Item inaccessible, initiates deletion of its product data, and terminates its per-Item subscription billing. The entire Item is removed, including access to any other products on that Item. To connect the accounts again, the user must complete Link to create a new Item.

If the user has at least one associated Item and every associated Item contains a Financial Management product, this endpoint also removes the associated Plaid user. The removed `user_id` can no longer be used to access the user.

For Plaid Protect, this endpoint terminates Protect products. For Servicing, it cancels the subscription and preserves CRA Items and historical data for future report requests.

<a href="/api/users/#userproductsterminate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_id": "usr_8c3ZbDBYjaqUXZ",
  "reason_code": "CONSUMER_ACCOUNT_CLOSED",
  "reason_note": "User closed account with client."
}
```

<h3 id="terminate-products-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[UserProductsTerminateRequest](#schemauserproductsterminaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|true|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» reason_code|body|[ProductsTerminateReasonCode](#schemaproductsterminatereasoncode)|true|The reason for terminating products.<br><br>`FRAUD_FIRST_PARTY`: The end user who owns the connected bank account committed fraud using their real identity<br><br>`FRAUD_FALSE_IDENTITY`: The connection was created using a false or stolen identity<br><br>`FRAUD_ABUSE`: The end user is abusing the client's service or platform (for example, automation or excessive retries) through their connected account<br><br>`FRAUD_OTHER`: Fraud-related, but not covered by the specific fraud categories above; `reason_note` should clarify<br><br>`FRAUD_TRANSACTION`: Fraud occurred at the transaction level, such as an unauthorized transaction, card testing, chargeback, ACH return, or dispute<br><br>`CONSUMER_LOAN_PAID_OFF`: The end user paid off their loan and no longer needs the product<br><br>`CONSUMER_ACCOUNT_CLOSED`: The end user closed their account with the client and no longer needs the product<br><br>`CONSUMER_CHARGE_OFF`: The end user's account has been charged off<br><br>`CONSUMER_PAYMENT_METHOD_SWITCHED`: The end user switched to a different payment method and no longer needs the product<br><br>`USER_OFFBOARDING`: The user is offboarding from the client's service or platform<br><br>`DUPLICATE_ITEM`: This Item is a duplicate of another active Item for the same user<br><br>`BILLING_TERMINATION`: The client's billing or subscription relationship with the end user has ended<br><br>`OTHER`: None of the above; `reason_note` should clarify<br>|
|» reason_note|body|string \| null|false|Additional context or details about the reason for terminating user-based products. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be included in the `reason_note`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» reason_code|FRAUD_FIRST_PARTY|
|» reason_code|FRAUD_FALSE_IDENTITY|
|» reason_code|FRAUD_ABUSE|
|» reason_code|FRAUD_OTHER|
|» reason_code|FRAUD_TRANSACTION|
|» reason_code|CONSUMER_LOAN_PAID_OFF|
|» reason_code|CONSUMER_ACCOUNT_CLOSED|
|» reason_code|CONSUMER_CHARGE_OFF|
|» reason_code|CONSUMER_PAYMENT_METHOD_SWITCHED|
|» reason_code|USER_OFFBOARDING|
|» reason_code|DUPLICATE_ITEM|
|» reason_code|BILLING_TERMINATION|
|» reason_code|OTHER|

```json
  "request_id": "TxlxEcCmP9HTTT"
}
```

## Remove Items from a User

<a id="opIduserItemsRemove"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/items/remove \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_token": "string",
    "user_id": "string",
    "item_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /user/items/remove`

Removes specific Items associated with a user. It is equivalent to calling `/item/remove` on each Item individually, but supports use cases (such as Plaid Check) where access tokens are not available. All specified Items must belong to the user or the entire operation fails. Similar to `/item/remove`, this deletes Item product data and terminates billing on the Item's products. Once removed, Items cannot be reconnected without going through Link again.
This endpoint is not intended to remove all data for a user, as it will only remove Items and no other data for the user. If the user has any user-based recurring subscription products (Financial Management, Plaid Protect, or CRA Servicing) and is deleting their account with your product, also call `/user/products/terminate` to end those subscriptions; per-Item billing is already terminated by this endpoint. For a user initiated data deletion request, see the [Consumer Service Center](https://plaid.com/check/consumer-service-center/) to revoke access to data.

<a href="/api/users/#useritemsremove">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_token": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "item_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="remove-items-from-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[UserItemsRemoveRequest](#schemauseritemsremoverequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|false|The user token associated with the user for which data is being requested. This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» item_ids|body|[[ItemId](#schemaitemid)]|true|An array of `item_id`s to be deleted. All Items for removal must be currently associated with the provided `user_id` or `user_token`. Otherwise, the entire operation will error and no Items will be deleted.|

## Create a third-party user token

<a id="opIduserThirdPartyTokenCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/third_party_token/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \

  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{

    "secret": "string",
    "user_token": "string",
    "third_party_client_id": "string",
    "expiration_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "user_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /user/third_party_token/create`

This endpoint is used to create a third-party user token. This token can be shared with and used by a specified third-party client to access data associated with the user through supported endpoints.

Ensure you store the `third_party_user_token` along with the `user_token` and `third_party_client_id`, as it is not possible to retrieve a previously created `third_party_user_token`.

<a href="/api/users/#userthirdpartytokencreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_token": "string",
  "third_party_client_id": "string",
  "expiration_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "user_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-third-party-user-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[UserThirdPartyTokenCreateRequest](#schemauserthirdpartytokencreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|false|The user token associated with the user for which data is being requested. This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» third_party_client_id|body|string|true|The Plaid API `client_id` of the third-party client the token will be shared with. The token will only be valid for the specified client.|
|» expiration_time|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The expiration date and time for the third-party user token in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`). The expiration is restricted to a maximum of 24 hours from the token's creation time. If not provided, the token will automatically expire after 24 hours.|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|

## Get payment details

<a id="opIdpaymentInitiationPaymentGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/payment_initiation/payment/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "payment_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /payment_initiation/payment/get`

The `/payment_initiation/payment/get` endpoint can be used to check the status of a payment, as well as to receive basic information such as recipient and payment amount. In the case of standing orders, the `/payment_initiation/payment/get` endpoint will provide information about the status of the overall standing order itself; the API cannot be used to retrieve payment status for individual payments within a standing order.

Polling for status updates in Production is highly discouraged. Repeatedly calling `/payment_initiation/payment/get` to check a payment's status is unreliable and may trigger API rate limits. Only the `PAYMENT_STATUS_UPDATE` webhook should be used to receive real-time status updates in Production.

<a href="/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiationpaymentget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "payment_id": "string"
}
```

|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» payment_id|body|string|true|The `payment_id` returned from `/payment_initiation/payment/create`.|
