Authorization was obtained in writing either in person or via an electronic document signing, e.g. Docusign, by the consumer. Can be used for credits or debits.<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry. The transfer debits a consumer's bank account. Authorization from the consumer is obtained over the Internet (e.g. a web or mobile application). Can be used for single debits or recurring debits.<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry. The transfer debits a consumer. Debit authorization has been received orally over the telephone via a recorded call.|
|» amount|body|[TransferAmount](#schematransferamount)|true|The amount of the transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00"). When calling `/transfer/authorization/create`, specify the maximum amount to authorize. When calling `/transfer/create`, specify the exact amount of the transfer, up to a maximum of the amount authorized. If this field is left blank when calling `/transfer/create`, the maximum amount authorized in the `authorization_id` will be sent. If the authorization's `guarantee_details.outcome` is `PARTIAL_INSTANT_ONLY`, this field is required when calling `/transfer/create`.|
|» user_present|body|boolean \| null|false|If the end user is initiating the specific transfer themselves via an interactive UI, this should be `true`; for automatic recurring payments where the end user is not actually initiating each individual transfer, it should be `false`.|
|» iso_currency_code|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** The currency of the transfer amount. The default value is "USD".|
|» description|body|string|true|The description of the recurring transfer.|
|» test_clock_id|body|string \| null|false|Plaid's unique identifier for a test clock. This field may only be used when using the `sandbox` environment. If provided, the created `recurring_transfer` is associated with the `test_clock`. New originations are automatically generated when the associated `test_clock` advances. For more details, see [Simulating recurring transfers](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/sandbox/#simulating-recurring-transfers).|
|» schedule|body|[TransferRecurringSchedule](#schematransferrecurringschedule)|true|The schedule that the recurring transfer will be executed on.|
|» user|body|[TransferUserInRequest](#schematransferuserinrequest)|true|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|
|» device|body|[TransferDevice](#schematransferdevice)|false|Information about the device being used to initiate the authorization.|

## Cancel a transfer

<a id="opIdtransferCancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transfer/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "transfer_id": "string",
    "originator_client_id": "string",
    "reason_code": "AC03"
  }'
```

`POST /transfer/cancel`

Use the `/transfer/cancel` endpoint to cancel a transfer.  A transfer is eligible for cancellation if the `cancellable` property returned by `/transfer/get` is `true`.

<a href="/api/products/transfer/initiating-transfers/#transfercancel">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "transfer_id": "string",
  "originator_client_id": "string",
  "reason_code": "AC03"
}
```

<h3 id="cancel-a-transfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferCancelRequest](#schematransfercancelrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» transfer_id|body|[TransferID](#schematransferid)|true|Plaid's unique identifier for a transfer.|
|» originator_client_id|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** The Plaid client ID of the transfer originator. Should only be present if `client_id` is a third-party sender (TPS).|
|» reason_code|body|[ReasonCode](#schemareasoncode)|false|Specifies the reason for cancelling transfer. This is required for RfP transfers, and will be ignored for other networks.<br><br>`"AC03"` - Invalid Creditor Account Number<br><br>`"AM09"` - Incorrect Amount<br><br>`"CUST"` - Requested By Customer - Cancellation requested<br><br>`"DUPL"` - Duplicate Payment<br><br>`"FRAD"` - Fraudulent Payment - Unauthorized or fraudulently induced<br><br>`"TECH"` - Technical Problem - Cancellation due to system issues<br><br>`"UPAY"` - Undue Payment - Payment was made through another channel<br><br>`"AC14"` - Invalid or Missing Creditor Account Type<br><br>`"AM06"` - Amount Too Low<br><br>`"BE05"` - Unrecognized Initiating Party<br><br>`"FOCR"` - Following Refund Request<br><br>`"MS02"` - No Specified Reason - Customer<br><br>`"MS03"` - No Specified Reason - Agent<br><br>`"RR04"` - Regulatory Reason<br><br>`"RUTA"` - Return Upon Unable To Apply|

#### Enumerated Values

|» reason_code|AM09|
|» reason_code|CUST|
|» reason_code|DUPL|
|» reason_code|FRAD|

|» reason_code|AC14|
|» reason_code|AM06|
|» reason_code|BE05|
|» reason_code|FOCR|
|» reason_code|MS02|
|» reason_code|MS03|
|» reason_code|RR04|

|» offset|body|integer \| null|false|The offset into the list of transfer events. When `count`=25 and `offset`=0, the first 25 events will be returned. When `count`=25 and `offset`=25, the next 25 events will be returned.|

`POST /transfer/event/sync`

`/transfer/event/sync` allows you to request up to the next 500 transfer events that happened after a specific `event_id`. Use the `/transfer/event/sync` endpoint to guarantee you have seen all transfer events.

|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Sync bank transfer events

<a id="opIdbankTransferEventSync"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/bank_transfer/event/sync \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "after_id": 0,
    "count": 25
  }'
```

`POST /bank_transfer/event/sync`

`/bank_transfer/event/sync` allows you to request up to the next 25 Plaid-initiated bank transfer events that happened after a specific `event_id`. When using Auth with micro-deposit verification enabled, this endpoint can be used to fetch status updates on ACH micro-deposits. For more details, see [micro-deposit events](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/microdeposit-events/).

<a href="/api/products/auth/#bank_transfereventsync">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "after_id": 0,
  "count": 25
}
```

<h3 id="sync-bank-transfer-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BankTransferEventSyncRequest](#schemabanktransfereventsyncrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» after_id|body|integer|true|The latest (largest) `event_id` fetched via the sync endpoint, or 0 initially.|
|» count|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of bank transfer events to return.|

## List sweeps

<a id="opIdtransferSweepList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transfer/sweep/list \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "start_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "end_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "count": 25,
    "offset": 0,
    "amount": "string",
    "status": "pending",
    "originator_client_id": "string",
    "funding_account_id": "string",
    "transfer_id": "string",
    "trigger": "manual"
  }'
```

`POST /transfer/sweep/list`

The `/transfer/sweep/list` endpoint fetches sweeps matching the given filters.

<a href="/api/products/transfer/reading-transfers/#transfersweeplist">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "start_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "end_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "count": 25,
  "offset": 0,
  "amount": "string",
  "status": "pending",
  "originator_client_id": "string",
  "funding_account_id": "string",
  "transfer_id": "string",
  "trigger": "manual"
}
```

<h3 id="list-sweeps-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferSweepListRequest](#schematransfersweeplistrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» start_date|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The start `created` datetime of sweeps to return (RFC 3339 format).|
|» end_date|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The end `created` datetime of sweeps to return (RFC 3339 format).|
|» count|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of sweeps to return.|
|» offset|body|integer|false|The number of sweeps to skip before returning results.|
|» amount|body|string \| null|false|Filter sweeps to only those with the specified amount.|
|» status|body|[SweepStatus](#schemasweepstatus)|false|The status of a sweep transfer<br><br>`"pending"` - The sweep is currently pending<br><br>`"posted"` - The sweep has been posted<br><br>`"settled"` - The sweep has settled. This is the terminal state of a successful credit sweep.<br><br>`"returned"` - The sweep has been returned. This is the terminal state of a returned sweep. Returns of a sweep are extremely rare, since sweeps are money movement between your own bank account and your own Ledger.<br><br>`"funds_available"` - Funds from the sweep have been released from hold and applied to the ledger's available balance. (Only applicable to deposits.) This is the terminal state of a successful deposit sweep.<br><br>`"failed"` - The sweep has failed. This is the terminal state of a failed sweep.|
|» originator_client_id|body|string \| null|false|Filter sweeps to only those with the specified originator client.|
|» funding_account_id|body|string \| null|false|Filter sweeps to only those with the specified `funding_account_id`.|
|» transfer_id|body|string \| null|false|Filter sweeps to only those with the included `transfer_id`.|
|» trigger|body|[SweepTrigger](#schemasweeptrigger)|false|The trigger of the sweep<br><br>`"manual"` - The sweep is created manually by the customer<br><br>`"incoming"` - The sweep is created by incoming funds flow (e.g. Incoming Wire)<br><br>`"balance_threshold"` - The sweep is created by balance threshold setting<br><br>`"automatic_aggregate"` - The sweep is created by the Plaid automatic aggregation process. These funds did not pass through the Plaid Ledger balance.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|pending|
|» status|posted|
|» status|settled|
|» status|funds_available|
|» status|returned|
|» status|failed|
|» status|null|
|» trigger|manual|
|» trigger|incoming|
|» trigger|balance_threshold|
|» trigger|automatic_aggregate|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "sweeps": [
    {
      "id": "d5394a4d-0b04-4a02-9f4a-7ca5c0f52f9d",
```

`POST /bank_transfer/balance/get`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Use the `/bank_transfer/balance/get` endpoint to see the available balance in your bank transfer account. Debit transfers increase this balance once their status is posted. Credit transfers decrease this balance when they are created.

The transactable balance shows the amount in your account that you are able to use for transfers, and is essentially your available balance minus your minimum balance.

Note that this endpoint can only be used with FBO accounts, when using Bank Transfers in the Full Service configuration. It cannot be used on your own account when using Bank Transfers in the BTS Platform configuration.

<a href="/bank-transfers/reference#bank_transferbalanceget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "origination_account_id": "string"
}
```

`POST /bank_transfer/migrate_account`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

As an alternative to adding Items via Link, you can also use the `/bank_transfer/migrate_account` endpoint to migrate known account and routing numbers to Plaid Items.  Note that Items created in this way are not compatible with endpoints for other products, such as `/accounts/balance/get`, and can only be used with Bank Transfer endpoints.  If you require access to other endpoints, create the Item through Link instead.  Access to `/bank_transfer/migrate_account` is not enabled by default; to obtain access, contact your Plaid account manager.

`POST /transfer/migrate_account`

As an alternative to adding Items via Link, you can also use the `/transfer/migrate_account` endpoint to migrate previously-verified account and routing numbers to Plaid Items. This endpoint is also required when adding an Item for use with wire transfers; if you intend to create wire transfers on this account, you must provide `wire_routing_number`. Note that Items created in this way are not compatible with endpoints for other products, such as `/accounts/balance/get`, and can only be used with Transfer endpoints.  If you require access to other endpoints, create the Item through Link instead.  Access to `/transfer/migrate_account` is not enabled by default; to obtain access, contact your Plaid account manager or [support](https://dashboard.plaid.com/support).

<a href="/api/products/transfer/account-linking/#transfermigrate_account">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "account_number": "string",
  "routing_number": "string",
  "wire_routing_number": "string",
  "account_type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="migrate-account-into-transfers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferMigrateAccountRequest](#schematransfermigrateaccountrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» account_number|body|string|true|The user's account number.|
|» routing_number|body|string|true|The user's routing number.|
|» wire_routing_number|body|string|false|The user's wire transfer routing number. This is the ABA number; for some institutions, this may differ from the ACH number used in `routing_number`. This field must be set for the created item to be eligible for wire transfers.|
|» account_type|body|string|true|The type of the bank account (`checking` or `savings`).|

## Create a transfer intent object to invoke the Transfer UI

<a id="opIdtransferIntentCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transfer/intent/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "account_id": "string",
    "funding_account_id": "string",
    "mode": "PAYMENT",
    "network": "same-day-ach",
    "amount": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "ach_class": "ccd",
    "origination_account_id": "string",
    "user": {
      "legal_name": "string",
      "phone_number": "string",
      "email_address": "string",
      "address": {
        "street": "string",
        "city": "string",
        "region": "string",
        "postal_code": "string",
        "country": "string"
      }
    },
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "iso_currency_code": "string",
    "require_guarantee": false
  }'
```

`POST /transfer/intent/create`

Use the `/transfer/intent/create` endpoint to generate a transfer intent object and invoke the Transfer UI.

<a href="/api/products/transfer/account-linking/#transferintentcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "account_id": "string",
  "funding_account_id": "string",
  "mode": "PAYMENT",
  "network": "same-day-ach",
  "amount": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "ach_class": "ccd",
  "origination_account_id": "string",
  "user": {
    "legal_name": "string",
    "phone_number": "string",
    "email_address": "string",
    "address": {
      "street": "string",
      "city": "string",
      "region": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "country": "string"
    }
  },
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "iso_currency_code": "string",
  "require_guarantee": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-transfer-intent-object-to-invoke-the-transfer-ui-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferIntentCreateRequest](#schematransferintentcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» account_id|body|string \| null|false|The Plaid `account_id` corresponding to the end-user account that will be debited or credited.|
|» funding_account_id|body|[TransferMigratedFundingAccountIDRequest](#schematransfermigratedfundingaccountidrequest)|false|Specify the account used to fund the transfer. Should be specified if using legacy funding methods only. If using Plaid Ledger, leave this field blank. Customers can find a list of `funding_account_id`s in the Accounts page of your Plaid Dashboard, under the "Account ID" column. If this field is left blank and you are using legacy funding methods, this will default to the default `funding_account_id` specified during onboarding. Otherwise, Plaid Ledger will be used.|
|» mode|body|[TransferIntentCreateMode](#schematransferintentcreatemode)|true|The direction of the flow of transfer funds.<br><br>`PAYMENT`: Transfers funds from an end user's account to your business account.<br><br>`DISBURSEMENT`: Transfers funds from your business account to an end user's account.|
|» network|body|[TransferIntentCreateNetwork](#schematransferintentcreatenetwork)|false|The network or rails used for the transfer. Defaults to `same-day-ach`.<br><br>For transfers submitted using `ach`, the Standard ACH cutoff is 8:30 PM Eastern Time.<br><br>For transfers submitted using `same-day-ach`, the Same Day ACH cutoff is 3:00 PM Eastern Time. It is recommended to send the request 15 minutes prior to the cutoff to ensure that it will be processed in time for submission before the cutoff. If the transfer is processed after this cutoff but before the Standard ACH cutoff, it will be sent over Standard ACH rails and will not incur same-day charges.<br><br>For transfers submitted using `rtp`, in the case that the account being credited does not support RTP, the transfer will be sent over ACH as long as an `ach_class` is provided in the request. If RTP isn't supported by the account and no `ach_class` is provided, the transfer will fail to be submitted.|
|» amount|body|[TransferAmount](#schematransferamount)|true|The amount of the transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00"). When calling `/transfer/authorization/create`, specify the maximum amount to authorize. When calling `/transfer/create`, specify the exact amount of the transfer, up to a maximum of the amount authorized. If this field is left blank when calling `/transfer/create`, the maximum amount authorized in the `authorization_id` will be sent. If the authorization's `guarantee_details.outcome` is `PARTIAL_INSTANT_ONLY`, this field is required when calling `/transfer/create`.|
|» description|body|string|true|A description for the underlying transfer. Maximum of 15 characters.|
|» ach_class|body|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|false|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network. For more details, see [ACH SEC codes](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/creating-transfers/#ach-sec-codes).<br><br>Codes supported for credits: `ccd`, `ppd`<br>Codes supported for debits: `ccd`, `ppd`, `tel`, `web`<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - The transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer. Authorization was obtained in writing either in person or via an electronic document signing, e.g. Docusign, by the consumer. Can be used for credits or debits.<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry. The transfer debits a consumer's bank account. Authorization from the consumer is obtained over the Internet (e.g. a web or mobile application). Can be used for single debits or recurring debits.<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry. The transfer debits a consumer. Debit authorization has been received orally over the telephone via a recorded call.|
|» origination_account_id|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Plaid's unique identifier for the origination account for the intent. If not provided, the default account will be used.|
|» user|body|[TransferUserInRequest](#schematransferuserinrequest)|true|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|
|» metadata|body|[TransferMetadata](#schematransfermetadata)|false|The Metadata object is a mapping of client-provided string fields to any string value. The following limitations apply:<br>The JSON values must be Strings (no nested JSON objects allowed)<br>Only ASCII characters may be used<br>Maximum of 50 key/value pairs<br>Maximum key length of 40 characters<br>Maximum value length of 500 characters<br>|
|» iso_currency_code|body|string|false|The currency of the transfer amount, e.g. "USD"|
|» require_guarantee|body|boolean \| null|false|When `true`, the transfer requires a `GUARANTEED` decision by Plaid to proceed (Guarantee customers only).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» mode|PAYMENT|
|» mode|DISBURSEMENT|
|» network|ach|
|» network|same-day-ach|
|» network|rtp|
|» ach_class|ccd|
|» ach_class|ppd|
|» ach_class|tel|
|» ach_class|web|

> Example responses

`POST /transfer/repayment/list`

The `/transfer/repayment/list` endpoint fetches repayments matching the given filters. Repayments are returned in reverse-chronological order (most recent first) starting at the given `start_date`.

<a href="/api/products/transfer/#transferrepaymentlist">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "start_date": "2022-01-10T12:34:56Z",
  "count": 1
}
```

|» end_date|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The end `created` datetime of repayments to return (RFC 3339 format).|

```bash
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "count": 1,
    "repayment_id": "d4bfce70-2470-4298-ae87-5e9b3e18bfaf"
  }'
```

`POST /transfer/repayment/return/list`

The `/transfer/repayment/return/list` endpoint retrieves the set of returns that were batched together into the specified repayment. The sum of amounts of returns retrieved by this request equals the amount of the repayment.

<a href="/api/products/transfer/#transferrepaymentreturnlist">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "count": 1,
  "repayment_id": "d4bfce70-2470-4298-ae87-5e9b3e18bfaf"
}
```

<h3 id="list-the-returns-included-in-a-repayment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferRepaymentReturnListRequest](#schematransferrepaymentreturnlistrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» repayment_id|body|string|true|Identifier of the repayment to query.|
|» count|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of repayments to return.|
|» offset|body|integer|false|The number of repayments to skip before returning results.|

`POST /transfer/diligence/document/upload`

Third-party sender customers can use the `/transfer/diligence/document/upload` endpoint to upload a document on behalf of their end customer (i.e. originator) to Plaid. You'll need to send a request of type `multipart/form-data`.
You must provide the `client_id` in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header and `secret` in the `PLAID-SECRET` header.

<a href="/api/products/transfer/platform-payments/#transferdiligencedocumentupload">External documentation</a>

```json
  "originator_client_id": "string",

  "purpose": "DUE_DILIGENCE"
```

|» file|body|string(binary)|true|A file to upload. The file size must be less than 20MB. Supported file extensions: .pdf.|
|» purpose|body|[TransferDocumentPurpose](#schematransferdocumentpurpose)|true|Specifies the purpose of the uploaded file.<br><br>`"DUE_DILIGENCE"` - The transfer due diligence document of the originator.|

## Create a refund

<a id="opIdtransferRefundCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transfer/refund/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "transfer_id": "string",
    "amount": "string",
    "idempotency_key": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /transfer/refund/create`

Use the `/transfer/refund/create` endpoint to create a refund for a transfer. A transfer can be refunded if the transfer was initiated in the past 180 days.

Refunds come out of the available balance of the ledger used for the original debit transfer. If there are not enough funds in the available balance to cover the refund amount, the refund will be rejected. Plaid does not impose a hold time before a refund can be created; you do not need to wait for the original transfer to settle.

A refund can still be issued even if the Item's `access_token` is no longer valid (e.g. if the user revoked OAuth consent or the Item was deleted via `/item/remove`), as long as the account and routing number pair used to make the original transaction is still valid. A refund cannot be issued if the Item has an [invalidated TAN](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/#tokenized-account-numbers), which can occur at Chase or PNC.

<a href="/api/products/transfer/refunds/#transferrefundcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "transfer_id": "string",
  "amount": "string",
  "idempotency_key": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-refund-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferRefundCreateRequest](#schematransferrefundcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» transfer_id|body|[TransferIDForRefund](#schematransferidforrefund)|true|The ID of the transfer to refund.|
|» amount|body|[TransferRefundAmount](#schematransferrefundamount)|true|The amount of the refund (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|» idempotency_key|body|[TransferRefundIdempotencyKey](#schematransferrefundidempotencykey)|true|A random key provided by the client, per unique refund. Maximum of 50 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create a refund fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single refund is created.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "refund": {
    "id": "667af684-9ee1-4f5f-862a-633ec4c545cc",
    "transfer_id": "460cbe92-2dcc-8eae-5ad6-b37d0ec90fd9",

    "status": "pending",
    "created": "2020-08-06T17:27:15Z",

    "network_trace_id": null
  },
  "request_id": "saKrIBuEB9qJZno"
}
```

## Report a return recovery

<a id="opIdtransferReturnRecover"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transfer/return/recover \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "transfer_id": "string",
    "amount": "string",
    "idempotency_key": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /transfer/return/recover`

Use the `/transfer/return/recover` endpoint to notify Plaid that you have recovered some or all of the loss on a returned guaranteed transfer.

Recovery can be reported in full or in parts; the sum of recovered amounts across calls cannot exceed the guaranteed amount of the original transfer.

<a href="none">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "transfer_id": "string",
  "amount": "string",
  "idempotency_key": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="report-a-return-recovery-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransferReturnRecoverRequest](#schematransferreturnrecoverrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» transfer_id|body|[TransferReturnRecoverTransferID](#schematransferreturnrecovertransferid)|true|The ID of the returned transfer that was recovered.|
|» amount|body|[TransferReturnRecoverAmount](#schematransferreturnrecoveramount)|true|The amount being recovered (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00"). The sum of recovered amounts across calls cannot exceed the guaranteed amount of the original transfer.|
|» idempotency_key|body|[TransferReturnRecoverIdempotencyKey](#schematransferreturnrecoveridempotencykey)|true|A random key provided by the client, per unique recovery. Maximum of 50 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. ## Simulate creating a sweep

<a id="opIdsandboxTransferSweepSimulate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sandbox/transfer/sweep/simulate \
  -X POST \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "test_clock_id": "string",
    "webhook": "http://example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /sandbox/transfer/sweep/simulate`

Use the `/sandbox/transfer/sweep/simulate` endpoint to create a sweep and associated events in the Sandbox environment. Upon calling this endpoint, all transfers with a sweep status of `swept` will become `swept_settled`, all `posted` or `pending` transfers with a sweep status of `unswept` will become `swept`, and all `returned` transfers with a sweep status of `swept` will become `return_swept`.

<a href="/api/sandbox/#sandboxtransfersweepsimulate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "test_clock_id": "string",
  "webhook": "http://example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="simulate-creating-a-sweep-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SandboxTransferSweepSimulateRequest](#schemasandboxtransfersweepsimulaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» test_clock_id|body|string \| null|false|Plaid's unique identifier for a test clock. If provided, the sweep to be simulated is created on the day of the `virtual_time` on the `test_clock`. If the date of `virtual_time` is on weekend or a federal holiday, the next available banking day is used.|
|» webhook|body|string(url)|false|The webhook URL to which a `TRANSFER_EVENTS_UPDATE` webhook should be sent.|

<h3 id="simulate-a-refund-event-in-sandbox-parameters">Parameters</h3>

`POST /sandbox/transfer/test_clock/create`

Use the `/sandbox/transfer/test_clock/create` endpoint to create a `test_clock` in the Sandbox environment.

A test clock object represents an independent timeline and has a `virtual_time` field indicating the current timestamp of the timeline. Test clocks are used for testing recurring transfers in Sandbox.

A test clock can be associated with up to 5 recurring transfers.

|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Advance a test clock

<a id="opIdsandboxTransferTestClockAdvance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sandbox/transfer/test_clock/advance \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "test_clock_id": "string",
    "new_virtual_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /sandbox/transfer/test_clock/advance`

Use the `/sandbox/transfer/test_clock/advance` endpoint to advance a `test_clock` in the Sandbox environment.

A test clock object represents an independent timeline and has a `virtual_time` field indicating the current timestamp of the timeline. A test clock can be advanced by incrementing `virtual_time`, but may never go back to a lower `virtual_time`.

If a test clock is advanced, we will simulate the changes that ought to occur during the time that elapsed.

For example, a client creates a weekly recurring transfer with a test clock set at t. When the client advances the test clock by setting `virtual_time` = t + 15 days, 2 new originations should be created, along with the webhook events.

The advancement of the test clock from its current `virtual_time` should be limited such that there are no more than 20 originations resulting from the advance operation on each `recurring_transfer` associated with the `test_clock`.

For example, if the recurring transfer associated with this test clock originates once every 4 weeks, you can advance the `virtual_time` up to 80 weeks on each API call.

<a href="/api/sandbox/#sandboxtransfertest_clockadvance">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "test_clock_id": "string",
  "new_virtual_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="advance-a-test-clock-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SandboxTransferTestClockAdvanceRequest](#schemasandboxtransfertestclockadvancerequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» test_clock_id|body|[TransferTestClockID](#schematransfertestclockid)|true|Plaid's unique identifier for a test clock. For more details, see [Simulating recurring transfers](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/sandbox/#simulating-recurring-transfers).|
|» new_virtual_time|body|[VirtualTime](#schemavirtualtime)|true|The virtual timestamp on the test clock. This will be of the form `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "request_id": "mdqfuVxeoza6mhu"
}
```

<a id="opIdsandboxPaymentProfileResetLogin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sandbox/payment_profile/reset_login \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
```

`POST /sandbox/payment_profile/reset_login`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

`/sandbox/payment_profile/reset_login` forces a Payment Profile into a state where the login is no longer valid. This makes it easy to test update mode for Payment Profile in the Sandbox environment.

 After calling `/sandbox/payment_profile/reset_login`, calls to the `/transfer/authorization/create` with the Payment Profile will result in a `decision_rationale` `PAYMENT_PROFILE_LOGIN_REQUIRED`. You can then use update mode for Payment Profile to restore it into a good state.

 In order to invoke this endpoint, you must first [create a Payment Profile](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/add-to-app/#create-a-payment-profile-optional) and [go through the Link flow](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/add-to-app/#create-a-link-token).

<a href="/api/sandbox/#sandboxpayment_profilereset_login">External documentation</a>

`POST /employers/search`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

`/employers/search` allows you the ability to search Plaid's database of known employers, for use with Deposit Switch. You can use this endpoint to look up a user's employer in order to confirm that they are supported. Users with non-supported employers can then be routed out of the Deposit Switch flow.

The data in the employer database is currently limited. As the Deposit Switch and Income products progress through their respective beta periods, more employers are being regularly added. Because the employer database is frequently updated, we recommend that you do not cache or store data from this endpoint for more than a day.

<a href="/api/employers/#employerssearch">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "query": "string",
  "products": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="deprecated-search-employer-database-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[EmployersSearchRequest](#schemaemployerssearchrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» query|body|string|true|The employer name to be searched for.|
|» products|body|[string]|true|The Plaid products the returned employers should support. Currently, this field must be set to `"deposit_switch"`.|

`POST /income/verification/create`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

`/income/verification/create` begins the income verification process by returning an `income_verification_id`. You can then provide the `income_verification_id` to `/link/token/create` under the `income_verification` parameter in order to create a Link instance that will prompt the user to go through the income verification flow. Plaid will fire an `INCOME` webhook once the user completes the Payroll Income flow, or when the uploaded documents in the Document Income flow have finished processing. 

<a href="/api/products/income/#incomeverificationcreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "webhook": "string",
  "precheck_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "access_tokens": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

|» webhook|body|string|true|The URL endpoint to which Plaid should send webhooks related to the progress of the income verification process.|

`POST /income/verification/paystubs/get`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated

`/income/verification/paystubs/get` returns the information collected from the paystubs that were used to verify an end user's income. It can be called once the status of the verification has been set to `VERIFICATION_STATUS_PROCESSING_COMPLETE`, as reported by the `INCOME: verification_status` webhook. This endpoint has been deprecated; new integrations should use `/credit/payroll_income/get` instead.

## (Deprecated) Download the original documents used for income verification

<a id="opIdincomeVerificationDocumentsDownload"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.com/income/verification/documents/download \
  -X POST \

```

`POST /income/verification/documents/download`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

`/income/verification/documents/download` provides the ability to download the source documents associated with the verification.

If Document Income was used, the documents will be those the user provided in Link. For Payroll Income, the most recent files available for download from the payroll provider will be available from this endpoint.

The response to `/income/verification/documents/download` is a ZIP file in binary data. If a `document_id` is passed, a single document will be contained in this file.
If not, the response will contain all documents associated with the verification.

The `request_id` is returned in the `Plaid-Request-ID` header.

<a href="/api/products/income/#incomeverificationdocumentsdownload">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "income_verification_id": "string",
  "access_token": "string",
  "document_id": "string"
}
```

`POST /income/verification/precheck`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

`/income/verification/precheck` is an optional endpoint that can be called before initializing a Link session for income verification. It evaluates whether a given user is supportable by digital income verification and returns a `precheck_id` that can be provided to `/link/token/create`. If the user is eligible for digital verification, providing the `precheck_id` in this way will generate a Link UI optimized for the end user and their specific employer. If the user cannot be confirmed as eligible, the `precheck_id` can still be provided to `/link/token/create` and the user can still use the income verification flow, but they may be required to manually upload a paystub to verify their income.

While all request fields are optional, providing either `employer` or `transactions_access_tokens` data will increase the chance of receiving a useful result.

This endpoint has been deprecated; new integrations should use `/credit/payroll_income/precheck` instead.

<a href="/api/products/income/#incomeverificationprecheck">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
    "email_address": "string",

      "city": "string",
      "region": "string",

      "postal_code": "string",
      "country": "string"
    }
  },
  "employer": {
    "name": "string",
    "address": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "region": "string",
      "street": "string"
    },
    "tax_id": "string",
    "url": "http://example.com"
  },

    "name": "string"
  },

  "transactions_access_tokens": [
    "string"
  ],
  "us_military_info": {
    "is_active_duty": true,
    "branch": "string"
  }
}
```

## Create Asset or Income Report Audit Copy Token

<a id="opIdcreditAuditCopyTokenCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/audit_copy_token/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "report_tokens": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /credit/audit_copy_token/create`

Plaid can create an Audit Copy token of an Asset Report and/or Income Report to share with a participating Government-Sponsored Enterprise (GSE) if you participate in Fannie Mae's Day 1 Certainty™ program or utilize Freddie Mac's Loan Product Advisor® (LPA®) Asset and Income Modeler (AIM). An Audit Copy token contains the same underlying data as the Asset Report and/or Income Report (result of `/credit/payroll_income/get`).

Use the `/credit/audit_copy_token/create` endpoint to create an `audit_copy_token` and then pass that token to the GSE who needs access.

<a href="/api/products/income/#creditaudit_copy_tokencreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "report_tokens": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-asset-or-income-report-audit-copy-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditAuditCopyTokenCreateRequest](#schemacreditauditcopytokencreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» report_tokens|body|[string]|true|List of report tokens; can include at most one VOA/standard Asset Report tokens and one VOE Asset Report Token.|

## Remove an Audit Copy token

<a id="opIdcreditReportAuditCopyRemove"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/audit_copy_token/remove \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "audit_copy_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/audit_copy_token/remove`

The `/credit/audit_copy_token/remove` endpoint allows you to remove an Audit Copy. Removing an Audit Copy invalidates the `audit_copy_token` associated with it, meaning both you and any third parties holding the token will no longer be able to use it to access Report data. Items associated with the Report data and other Audit Copies of it are not affected and will remain accessible after removing the given Audit Copy.

<a href="/api/products/income/#creditaudit_copy_tokenremove">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "audit_copy_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="remove-an-audit-copy-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditAuditCopyTokenRemoveRequest](#schemacreditauditcopytokenremoverequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» audit_copy_token|body|string|true|The `audit_copy_token` granting access to the Audit Copy you would like to revoke.|

## Retrieve an Asset Report with Freddie Mac format (aka VOA - Verification Of Assets), and a Verification Of Employment (VOE) report if this one is available. Only Freddie Mac can use this endpoint.

<a id="opIdcreditFreddieMacReportsGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/freddie_mac/reports/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "audit_copy_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/freddie_mac/reports/get`

The `/credit/freddie_mac/reports/get` endpoint retrieves the Verification of Assets and Verification of Employment reports.

<a href="/none/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "audit_copy_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditFreddieMacReportsGetRequest](#schemacreditfreddiemacreportsgetrequest)|true|none|
|» audit_copy_token|body|string|true|A token that can be shared with a third party auditor to allow them to obtain access to the Asset Report. This token should be stored securely.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|

## Retrieve information from the bank accounts used for employment verification

<a id="opIdcreditBankEmploymentGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/beta/credit/v1/bank_employment/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /beta/credit/v1/bank_employment/get`

`/beta/credit/v1/bank_employment/get` returns the employment report(s) derived from bank transaction data for a specified user.

<a href="/api/products/income/#creditbank_employmentget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-information-from-the-bank-accounts-used-for-employment-verification-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditBankEmploymentGetRequest](#schemacreditbankemploymentgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|true|The user token associated with the user for which data is being requested. This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. ## Retrieve information from the bank accounts used for income verification

<a id="opIdcreditBankIncomeGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/bank_income/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_token": "string",
    "user_id": "string",
    "options": {
      "count": 1
    }
  }'
```

`POST /credit/bank_income/get`

`/credit/bank_income/get` returns the bank income report(s) for a specified user. A single report corresponds to all institutions linked in a single Link session. To include multiple institutions in a single report, use [Multi-Item Link](https://plaid.com/docs/link/multi-item-link). To return older reports, use the `options.count` field.

<a href="/api/products/income/#creditbank_incomeget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_token": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "count": 1
  }
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-information-from-the-bank-accounts-used-for-income-verification-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditBankIncomeGetRequest](#schemacreditbankincomegetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|false|The user token associated with the user for which data is being requested. This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» options|body|[CreditBankIncomeGetRequestOptions](#schemacreditbankincomegetrequestoptions)|false|An optional object for `/credit/bank_income/get` request options.|

## Retrieve information from the bank accounts used for income verification in PDF format

<a id="opIdcreditBankIncomePdfGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/bank_income/pdf/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_token": "string",
    "user_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/bank_income/pdf/get`

`/credit/bank_income/pdf/get` returns the most recent bank income report for a specified user in PDF format.  A single report corresponds to all institutions linked in a single Link session. To include multiple institutions in a single report, use [Multi-Item Link](https://plaid.com/docs/link/multi-item-link).

<a href="/api/products/income/#creditbank_incomepdfget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_token": "string",
  "user_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-information-from-the-bank-accounts-used-for-income-verification-in-pdf-format-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditBankIncomePDFGetRequest](#schemacreditbankincomepdfgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|false|The user token associated with the user for which data is being requested. This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|

## Refresh a user's bank income information

<a id="opIdcreditBankIncomeRefresh"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/bank_income/refresh \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_token": "string",
    "user_id": {},
    "options": {
      "days_requested": 0
    }
  }'
```

`POST /credit/bank_income/refresh`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

`/credit/bank_income/refresh` is deprecated. The backend implementation was removed (returns an `Unimplemented` error at runtime), and the endpoint is no longer part of the documented API surface. To refresh Bank Income data for an existing user, send the user through Link's update mode so they can confirm their income sources. For a fully backend refresh, migrate to CRA Income Insights and call `/cra/check_report/create`.

<a href="/api/products/income/#creditbank_incomerefresh">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_token": "string",
  "user_id": {},
  "options": {
    "days_requested": 0
  }
}
```

## Retrieve fraud insights for a user's manually uploaded document(s).

<a id="opIdcreditPayrollIncomeRiskSignalsGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/payroll_income/risk_signals/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_token": "string",
    "user_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/payroll_income/risk_signals/get`

`/credit/payroll_income/risk_signals/get` can be used as part of the Document Income flow to assess a user-uploaded document for signs of potential fraud or tampering. It returns a risk score for each uploaded document that indicates the likelihood of the document being fraudulent, in addition to details on the individual risk signals contributing to the score.

To trigger risk signal generation for an Item, call `/link/token/create` with `parsing_config` set to include `risk_signals`, or call `/credit/payroll_income/parsing_config/update`. Once risk signal generation has been triggered, `/credit/payroll_income/risk_signals/get` can be called at any time after the `INCOME_VERIFICATION_RISK_SIGNALS` webhook has been fired.

`/credit/payroll_income/risk_signals/get` is offered as an add-on to Document Income and is billed separately. To request access to this endpoint, submit a product access request or contact your Plaid account manager.

<a href="/api/products/income/#creditpayroll_incomerisk_signalsget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_token": "string",
  "user_id": "string"
}
```

This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» user_id|body|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. ## Check income verification eligibility and optimize conversion

<a id="opIdcreditPayrollIncomePrecheck"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/payroll_income/precheck \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "user_token": "string",
    "user_id": {},
    "access_tokens": [
      "string"
    ],
    "employer": {
      "name": "string",
      "address": {
        "city": "string",
        "country": "string",
        "postal_code": "string",
        "region": "string",
        "street": "string"
      },
      "tax_id": "string",
      "url": "http://example.com"
    },
    "us_military_info": {
      "is_active_duty": true,
      "branch": "string"
    },
    "payroll_institution": {
      "name": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /credit/payroll_income/precheck`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

`/credit/payroll_income/precheck` is an optional endpoint that can be called before initializing a Link session for income verification. It evaluates whether a given user is supportable by digital income verification. If the user is eligible for digital verification, that information will be associated with the user token, and in this way will generate a Link UI optimized for the end user and their specific employer. If the user cannot be confirmed as eligible, the user can still use the income verification flow, but they may be required to manually upload a paystub to verify their income.

While all request fields are optional, providing `employer` data will increase the chance of receiving a useful result.

When testing in Sandbox, you can control the results by providing special test values in the `access_tokens` field. `access_good` and `access_bad` will result in `HIGH` and `LOW` confidence values, respectively. Any other valid Sandbox access token will result in `UNKNOWN` confidence; other strings return an `INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN` error.

<a href="/api/products/income/#creditpayroll_incomeprecheck">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user_token": "string",
  "user_id": {},
  "access_tokens": [
    "string"
  ],
  "employer": {
    "name": "string",
    "address": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "region": "string",
      "street": "string"
    },
    "tax_id": "string",
    "url": "http://example.com"
  },
  "us_military_info": {
    "is_active_duty": true,
    "branch": "string"
  },
  "payroll_institution": {
    "name": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="check-income-verification-eligibility-and-optimize-conversion-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditPayrollIncomePrecheckRequest](#schemacreditpayrollincomeprecheckrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» user_token|body|[UserToken](#schemausertoken)|false|The user token associated with the user for which data is being requested. This field is used only by customers with pre-existing integrations that already use the `user_token` field. All other customers should use the `user_id` instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|» user_id|body|object|false|none|
|» access_tokens|body|[[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)]|false|An array of access tokens corresponding to Items belonging to the user whose eligibility is being checked. Note that if the Items specified here are not already initialized with `transactions`, providing them in this field will cause these Items to be initialized with (and billed for) the Transactions product.|
|» employer|body|[IncomeVerificationPrecheckEmployer](#schemaincomeverificationprecheckemployer)|false|Information about the end user's employer|
|» us_military_info|body|[IncomeVerificationPrecheckMilitaryInfo](#schemaincomeverificationprecheckmilitaryinfo)|false|Data about military info in the income verification precheck.|
|» payroll_institution|body|[IncomeVerificationPrecheckPayrollInstitution](#schemaincomeverificationprecheckpayrollinstitution)|false|Information about the end user's payroll institution|

```json
}
```

## Create a relay token to share an Asset Report with a partner client

<a id="opIdcreditRelayCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/relay/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "report_tokens": [
      "string"
    ],
    "secondary_client_id": "string",
    "webhook": "http://example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/relay/create`

Plaid can share an Asset Report directly with a participating third party on your behalf. The shared Asset Report is the exact same Asset Report originally created in `/asset_report/create`.

To grant a third party access to an Asset Report, use the `/credit/relay/create` endpoint to create a `relay_token` and then pass that token to your third party. Each third party has its own `secondary_client_id`; for example, `ce5bd328dcd34123456`. You'll need to create a separate `relay_token` for each third party that needs access to the report on your behalf.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#creditrelaycreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "report_tokens": [
    "string"
  ],
  "secondary_client_id": "string",
  "webhook": "http://example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-relay-token-to-share-an-asset-report-with-a-partner-client-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditRelayCreateRequest](#schemacreditrelaycreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» report_tokens|body|[string]|true|List of report token strings, with at most one token of each report type. Currently only Asset Report token is supported.|
|» secondary_client_id|body|string|true|The `secondary_client_id` is the client id of the third party with whom you would like to share the relay token.|
|» webhook|body|string(url) \| null|false|URL to which Plaid will send webhooks when the Secondary Client successfully retrieves an Asset Report by calling `/credit/relay/get`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "relay_token": "credit-relay-production-8218d5f8-6d6d-403d-92f5-13a9afaa4398",
  "request_id": "Iam3b"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
  "error_code": "string",
  "error_code_reason": "string",
  "error_message": "string",
  "display_message": "string",
  "request_id": "string",
  "causes": [
    null
  ],
  "status": 0,
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "suggested_action": "string",
  "required_account_subtypes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "provided_account_subtypes": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

## Retrieve the reports associated with a relay token that was shared with you

<a id="opIdcreditRelayGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/relay/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "relay_token": "string",
    "report_type": "asset",
    "include_insights": false
  }'
```

`POST /credit/relay/get`

`/credit/relay/get` allows third parties to receive a report that was shared with them, using a `relay_token` that was created by the report owner.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#creditrelayget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "relay_token": "string",
  "report_type": "asset",
  "include_insights": false
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-the-reports-associated-with-a-relay-token-that-was-shared-with-you-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditRelayGetRequest](#schemacreditrelaygetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» relay_token|body|string|true|The `relay_token` granting access to the report you would like to get.|
|» report_type|body|[ReportType](#schemareporttype)|true|The report type. It can be `asset`. Income report types are not yet supported.|
|» include_insights|body|boolean|false|`true` if you would like to retrieve the Asset Report with Insights, `false` otherwise. This field defaults to `false` if omitted.|

|---|---|

## Retrieve the PDF reports associated with a relay token that was shared with you (beta)

<a id="opIdcreditRelayPdfGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/relay/pdf/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "relay_token": "string",
    "report_type": "asset"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/relay/pdf/get`

`/credit/relay/pdf/get` allows third parties to receive a PDF report that was shared with them, using a `relay_token` that was created by the report owner.

The `/credit/relay/pdf/get` endpoint retrieves the Asset Report in PDF format. Before calling `/credit/relay/pdf/get`, you must first create the Asset Report using `/credit/relay/create` and then wait for the [`PRODUCT_READY`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/assets/#product_ready) webhook to fire, indicating that the Report is ready to be retrieved.

The response to `/credit/relay/pdf/get` is the PDF binary data. The `request_id` is returned in the `Plaid-Request-ID` header.

[View a sample PDF Asset Report](https://plaid.com/documents/sample-asset-report.pdf).

<a href="/api/products/assets/#creditrelaypdfget">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "relay_token": "string",
  "report_type": "asset"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-the-pdf-reports-associated-with-a-relay-token-that-was-shared-with-you-beta-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditRelayPDFGetRequest](#schemacreditrelaypdfgetrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» relay_token|body|string|true|The `relay_token` granting access to the report you would like to get.|
|» report_type|body|[ReportType](#schemareporttype)|true|The report type. It can be `asset`. Income report types are not yet supported.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» report_type|asset|

## Refresh a report of a relay token

<a id="opIdcreditRelayRefresh"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/relay/refresh \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "relay_token": "string",
    "report_type": "asset",
    "webhook": "http://example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/relay/refresh`

The `/credit/relay/refresh` endpoint allows third parties to refresh a report that was relayed to them, using a `relay_token` that was created by the report owner. A new report will be created with the original report parameters, but with the most recent data available based on the `days_requested` value of the original report.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#creditrelayrefresh">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "relay_token": "string",
  "report_type": "asset",
  "webhook": "http://example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="refresh-a-report-of-a-relay-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditRelayRefreshRequest](#schemacreditrelayrefreshrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» relay_token|body|string|true|The `relay_token` granting access to the report you would like to refresh.|
|» report_type|body|[ReportType](#schemareporttype)|true|The report type. It can be `asset`. Income report types are not yet supported.|
|» webhook|body|string(url) \| null|false|The URL registered to receive webhooks when the report of a relay token has been refreshed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» report_type|asset|

## Remove relay token

<a id="opIdcreditRelayRemove"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/credit/relay/remove \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "relay_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /credit/relay/remove`

The `/credit/relay/remove` endpoint allows you to invalidate a `relay_token`. The third party holding the token will no longer be able to access or refresh the reports which the `relay_token` gives access to. The original report, associated Items, and other relay tokens that provide access to the same report are not affected and will remain accessible after removing the given `relay_token`.

<a href="/api/products/assets/#creditrelayremove">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "relay_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="remove-relay-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreditRelayRemoveRequest](#schemacreditrelayremoverequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» relay_token|body|string|true|The `relay_token` you would like to revoke.|

> Example responses

<a id="opIdsandboxIncomeFireWebhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sandbox/income/fire_webhook \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```
