```bash
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "item_id": "string",
    "user_id": "string",
    "webhook": "http://example.com",
    "verification_status": "VERIFICATION_STATUS_PROCESSING_COMPLETE",
    "webhook_code": "INCOME_VERIFICATION"
  }'
```

`POST /sandbox/income/fire_webhook`

Use the `/sandbox/income/fire_webhook` endpoint to manually trigger a Payroll or Document Income webhook in the Sandbox environment.

<a href="/api/sandbox/#sandboxincomefire_webhook">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "item_id": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "webhook": "http://example.com",
  "verification_status": "VERIFICATION_STATUS_PROCESSING_COMPLETE",
  "webhook_code": "INCOME_VERIFICATION"
}
```

<h3 id="manually-fire-an-income-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SandboxIncomeFireWebhookRequest](#schemasandboxincomefirewebhookrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» item_id|body|string|true|The Item ID associated with the verification.|
|» user_id|body|string|false|The user identifier to include in the test webhook. For `USER_INCOME_VERIFICATION` and `USER_INCOME_VERIFICATION_RISK_SIGNALS`, use the `user_id` returned by `/user/create`, which begins with `usr_`. For `INCOME_VERIFICATION` and `INCOME_VERIFICATION_RISK_SIGNALS`, use the legacy webhook `user_id` associated with the user token.|
|» webhook|body|string(url)|true|The URL to which the webhook should be sent.|
|» verification_status|body|string|false|Required when `webhook_code` is `INCOME_VERIFICATION` or `USER_INCOME_VERIFICATION`.<br><br>`VERIFICATION_STATUS_PROCESSING_COMPLETE`: The income verification status processing has completed. If the user uploaded multiple documents, this webhook will fire when all documents have finished processing. Call the `/income/verification/paystubs/get` endpoint and check the document metadata to see which documents were successfully parsed.<br><br>`VERIFICATION_STATUS_PROCESSING_FAILED`: A failure occurred when attempting to process the verification documentation.<br><br>`VERIFICATION_STATUS_DOCUMENT_REJECTED`: The documentation was rejected.|
|» webhook_code|body|[SandboxIncomeWebhookFireRequestWebhookCode](#schemasandboxincomewebhookfirerequestwebhookcode)|true|The webhook codes that can be fired by this test endpoint.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

|» verification_status|VERIFICATION_STATUS_PROCESSING_COMPLETE|
|» verification_status|VERIFICATION_STATUS_PROCESSING_FAILED|
|» verification_status|VERIFICATION_STATUS_DOCUMENT_REJECTED|
|» webhook_code|INCOME_VERIFICATION|
|» webhook_code|USER_INCOME_VERIFICATION|
|» webhook_code|INCOME_VERIFICATION_RISK_SIGNALS|
|» webhook_code|USER_INCOME_VERIFICATION_RISK_SIGNALS|

`POST /sandbox/cra/servicing/simulate`

Use the `/sandbox/cra/servicing/simulate` endpoint to synchronously seed a CRA Servicing report in the Sandbox environment and return a `report_id` that can be fetched via `/cra/check_report/base_report/get` or `/cra/check_report/income_insights/get`. This endpoint also fires a `CRA_REPORT_UPDATED` webhook, mirroring the notification a live subscription would emit.

<a href="/api/sandbox/#sandboxcraservicingsimulate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "subscription_id": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "options": {
    "transactions_end_date": "1970-01-01",
    "error_webhook_code": "USER_NOT_FOUND"
  }
}
```

|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» subscription_id|body|string|true|The Servicing subscription to simulate an update for. Upon calling this endpoint, Plaid will simulate a report creation for all products referenced by this subscription ID.|

```bash
    "ruleset_key": "string"

```

`POST /signal/evaluate`

Use `/signal/evaluate` to evaluate a planned ACH transaction to get a return risk assessment and additional risk signals.

Before using `/signal/evaluate`, you must first [create a ruleset](https://plaid.com/docs/signal/signal-rules/) in the Dashboard under [**Signal->Rules**](https://dashboard.plaid.com/signal/risk-profiles).

`/signal/evaluate` can be used with either Signal Transaction Scores or the Balance product. Which product is used will be determined by the `ruleset_key` that you provide. For more details, see [Signal Rules](https://plaid.com/docs/signal/signal-rules/).

Note: This request may have higher latency when using a Balance-only ruleset. This is because Plaid must communicate directly with the institution to request data. Balance-only rulesets may have latency of up to 30 seconds or more; if you encounter errors, you may find it necessary to adjust your timeout period when making requests.

<a href="/api/products/signal#signalevaluate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "access_token": "string",
  "account_id": "string",
  "client_transaction_id": "string",
  "amount": 0,
  "user_present": true,
  "client_user_id": "string",
  "is_recurring": true,
  "default_payment_method": "string",
  "user": {
    "name": {
      "prefix": "string",
      "given_name": "string",
      "middle_name": "string",
      "family_name": "string",
      "suffix": "string"
    },
    "phone_number": "string",
    "email_address": "string",
    "address": {
      "city": "string",
      "region": "string",
      "street": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "country": "string"
    }
  },
  "device": {
    "ip_address": "string",
    "user_agent": "string"
  },
  "risk_profile_key": "string",
  "ruleset_key": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="evaluate-a-planned-ach-transaction-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SignalEvaluateRequest](#schemasignalevaluaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|
|» account_id|body|string|true|The Plaid `account_id` of the account that is the funding source for the proposed transaction. The `account_id` is returned in the `/accounts/get` endpoint as well as the [`onSuccess`](https://plaid.com/docs/link/ios/#link-ios-onsuccess-linkSuccess-metadata-accounts-id) callback metadata.<br><br>This will return an [`INVALID_ACCOUNT_ID`](https://plaid.com/docs/errors/invalid-input/#invalid_account_id) error if the account has been removed at the bank or if the `account_id` is no longer valid.|
|» client_transaction_id|body|string|true|The unique ID that you would like to use to refer to this evaluation attempt - for example, a payment attempt ID. You will use this later to debug this evaluation, and/or report an ACH return, etc. The max length for this field is 36 characters. The `client_transaction_id` also functions as an idempotency key; calling `/signal/evaluate` with a previously used `client_transaction_id` will return the results of the previous evaluation rather than triggering a fresh evaluation.|
|» amount|body|number(double)|true|The transaction amount, in USD (e.g. `102.05`)|
|» user_present|body|boolean \| null|false|**Deprecated.** `true` if the end user is present while initiating the ACH transfer and the endpoint is being called; `false` otherwise (for example, when the ACH transfer is scheduled and the end user is not present, or you call this endpoint after the ACH transfer but before submitting the Nacha file for ACH processing). When using a Balance-only ruleset, this field is ignored. This field is not currently used as part of Signal Transaction Score evaluations, but may be used in the future.|
|» client_user_id|body|string|false|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. This ID is used to correlate requests by a user with multiple Items. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|» is_recurring|body|boolean \| null|false|Use `true` if the ACH transaction is a part of recurring schedule (for example, a monthly repayment); `false` otherwise. When using a Balance-only ruleset, this field is ignored.|
|» default_payment_method|body|string \| null|false|The default ACH payment method to complete the transaction. When using a Balance-only ruleset, this field is ignored.<br><br>`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH by Nacha. The debit transaction is processed and settled on the same day.<br><br>`STANDARD_ACH`: Standard ACH by Nacha.<br><br>`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: If there is no default debit rail or there are multiple payment methods.<br><br>Possible values:  `SAME_DAY_ACH`, `STANDARD_ACH`, `MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`|
|» user|body|[SignalUser](#schemasignaluser)|false|Details about the end user initiating the transaction (i.e., the account holder). These fields are optional, but strongly recommended to increase the accuracy of results when using Signal Transaction Scores. When using a Balance-only ruleset, if the Signal Addendum has been signed, these fields are ignored; if the Addendum has not been signed, using these fields will result in an error.|
|» device|body|[SignalDevice](#schemasignaldevice)|false|Details about the end user's device. These fields are optional, but strongly recommended to increase the accuracy of results when using Signal Transaction Scores. When using a Balance-only Ruleset, these fields are ignored if the Signal Addendum has been signed; if it has not been signed, using these fields will result in an error.|
|» risk_profile_key|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Specifying `risk_profile_key` is deprecated. Please provide `ruleset` instead.|
|» ruleset_key|body|string \| null|false|The key of the ruleset to use for evaluating this transaction. You can create a ruleset using the Plaid Dashboard, under [Signal->Rules](https://dashboard.plaid.com/signal/risk-profiles). If not provided, for all new customers as of October 15, 2025, the `default` ruleset will be used. For existing Signal Transaction Scores customers as of October 15, 2025, by default, no ruleset will be used if the `ruleset_key` is not provided. For more information, or to opt out of using rulesets, see [Signal Rules](https://plaid.com/docs/signal/signal-rules/).|

<h3 id="schedule-a-planned-ach-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SignalScheduleRequest](#schemasignalschedulerequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|
|» account_id|body|string|true|The Plaid `account_id` of the account that is the funding source for the proposed transaction. The `account_id` is returned in the `/accounts/get` endpoint as well as the [`onSuccess`](https://plaid.com/docs/link/ios/#link-ios-onsuccess-linkSuccess-metadata-accounts-id) callback metadata.<br><br>This will return an [`INVALID_ACCOUNT_ID`](https://plaid.com/docs/errors/invalid-input/#invalid_account_id) error if the account has been removed at the bank or if the `account_id` is no longer valid.|

|» amount|body|number(double)|true|The transaction amount, in USD (e.g. `102.05`)|
|» default_payment_method|body|[SignalScheduleDefaultPaymentMethod](#schemasignalscheduledefaultpaymentmethod)|false|The payment method specified in the `default_payment_method` field directly impacts the timing recommendations provided by the API for submitting the debit entry to your processor or ODFI. If unspecified, defaults to `STANDARD_ACH`.<br><br>`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH (as defined by Nacha). The API assumes the settlement will occur on the same business day as submission. Note: The actual cutoff time can vary depending on your payment processor or ODFI. Nacha has established three processing windows for Same Day ACH (Eastern Time): 10:30 AM, 2:45 PM, and 4:45 PM.<br><br>`STANDARD_ACH`: Standard ACH (as defined by Nacha), typically settled one to three business days after submission.<br><br>`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: Indicates that there is no default debit rail or multiple payment methods are available, and the transaction could use any of them based on customer policy or availability.|

## Report whether you initiated an ACH transaction

<a id="opIdsignalDecisionReport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/signal/decision/report \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "client_transaction_id": "string",
    "initiated": true,
    "days_funds_on_hold": 0,
    "decision_outcome": "APPROVE",
    "payment_method": "SAME_DAY_ACH",
    "amount_instantly_available": 0,
    "submitted_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /signal/decision/report`

After you call `/signal/evaluate`, Plaid will normally infer the outcome from your Signal Rules. However, if you are not using Signal Rules, if the Signal Rules outcome was `REVIEW`, or if you take a different action than the one determined by the Signal Rules, you will need to call `/signal/decision/report`. This helps improve Signal Transaction Score accuracy for your account and is necessary for proper functioning of the rule performance and rule tuning capabilities in the Dashboard. If your effective decision changes after calling `/signal/decision/report` (for example, you indicated that you accepted a transaction, but later on, your payment processor rejected it, so it was never initiated), call `/signal/decision/report` again for the transaction to correct Plaid's records.

If you are using Plaid Transfer as your payment processor, you also do not need to call `/signal/decision/report`, as Plaid can infer outcomes from your Transfer activity.

If using a Balance-only ruleset, this endpoint will not impact scores (Balance does not use scores), but is necessary to view accurate transaction outcomes and tune rule logic in the Dashboard.

<a href="/api/products/signal#signaldecisionreport">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "client_transaction_id": "string",
  "initiated": true,
  "days_funds_on_hold": 0,
  "decision_outcome": "APPROVE",
  "payment_method": "SAME_DAY_ACH",
  "amount_instantly_available": 0,
  "submitted_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="report-whether-you-initiated-an-ach-transaction-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SignalDecisionReportRequest](#schemasignaldecisionreportrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» client_transaction_id|body|string|true|Must be the same as the `client_transaction_id` supplied when calling `/signal/evaluate`|
|» initiated|body|boolean|true|`true` if the ACH transaction was initiated, `false` otherwise.<br><br>This field must be returned as a boolean. If formatted incorrectly, this will result in an [`INVALID_FIELD`](https://plaid.com/docs/errors/invalid-request/#invalid_field) error.|
|» days_funds_on_hold|body|integer \| null|false|The actual number of days (hold time) since the ACH debit transaction that you wait before making funds available to your customers. The holding time could affect the ACH return rate.<br><br>For example, use 0 if you make funds available to your customers instantly or the same day following the debit transaction, or 1 if you make funds available the next day following the debit initialization.|
|» decision_outcome|body|[SignalDecisionOutcome](#schemasignaldecisionoutcome)|false|The payment decision from the risk assessment.<br><br>`APPROVE`: approve the transaction without requiring further actions from your customers. For example, use this field if you are placing a standard hold for all the approved transactions before making funds available to your customers. You should also use this field if you decide to accelerate the fund availability for your customers.<br><br>`REVIEW`: the transaction requires manual review<br><br>`REJECT`: reject the transaction<br><br>`TAKE_OTHER_RISK_MEASURES`: for example, placing a longer hold on funds than those approved transactions or introducing customer frictions such as step-up verification/authentication<br><br>`NOT_EVALUATED`: if only logging the results without using them<br>|
|» payment_method|body|[SignalPaymentMethod](#schemasignalpaymentmethod)|false|The payment method to complete the transaction after the risk assessment. It may be different from the default payment method.<br><br>`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH by Nacha. The debit transaction is processed and settled on the same day.<br><br>`STANDARD_ACH`: Standard ACH by Nacha.<br><br>`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: if there is no default debit rail or there are multiple payment methods.<br>|
|» amount_instantly_available|body|number(double) \| null|false|The amount (in USD) made available to your customers instantly following the debit transaction. It could be a partial amount of the requested transaction (example: 102.05).|
|» submitted_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The date the ACH debit was submitted to the bank for processing (in ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`). This field should correspond to the attempt initiated after the `/signal/schedule` call.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» decision_outcome|APPROVE|
|» decision_outcome|REVIEW|
|» decision_outcome|REJECT|
|» decision_outcome|TAKE_OTHER_RISK_MEASURES|
|» decision_outcome|NOT_EVALUATED|
|» payment_method|SAME_DAY_ACH|
|» payment_method|NEXT_DAY_ACH|
|» payment_method|STANDARD_ACH|
|» payment_method|MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS|
|» payment_method|null|

```json
}
```

## Opt-in an Item to Signal Transaction Scores

<a id="opIdsignalPrepare"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/signal/prepare \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "access_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /signal/prepare`

When an Item is not initialized with `signal`, call `/signal/prepare` to opt-in that Item to the data collection process used to develop a Signal Transaction Score. This should be done on Items where `signal` was added in the `additional_consented_products` array but not in the `products`, `optional_products`, or `required_if_supported_products` array. If `/signal/prepare` is skipped on an Item that is not initialized with `signal`, the initial call to `/signal/evaluate` on that Item will be less accurate, because Plaid will have access to less data for computing the Signal Transaction Score.

If your integration is purely Balance-only, this endpoint will have no effect, as Balance-only rulesets do not calculate a Signal Transaction Score.

If run on an Item that is already initialized with `signal`, this endpoint will return a 200 response and will not modify the Item.

<a href="/api/products/signal#signalprepare">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "access_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="opt-in-an-item-to-signal-transaction-scores-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SignalPrepareRequest](#schemasignalpreparerequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|

`POST /wallet/transaction/execute`

Execute a transaction using the specified e-wallet.
Specify the e-wallet to debit from, the counterparty to credit to, the idempotency key to prevent duplicate transactions, the amount and reference for the transaction.
Transactions will settle in seconds to several days, depending on the underlying payment rail.

<a href="/api/products/virtual-accounts/#wallettransactionexecute">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "idempotency_key": "string",
  "wallet_id": "string",
  "counterparty": {
    "name": "string",
    "numbers": {
      "bacs": {
        "account": "string",
        "sort_code": "string"
      },
      "international": {
        "iban": "stringstringstr"
      }
    },
    "address": {
      "street": [
        "string"
      ],
      "city": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "country": "st"
    },
    "date_of_birth": "1970-01-01",
    "holder_category": {},
    "is_verified": true
  },
  "amount": {
    "iso_currency_code": "GBP",
    "value": 0.01
  },
  "user_id": "string",
  "reference": "string",
  "originating_fund_source": {
    "full_name": "string",
    "address": {
      "street": [
        "string"
      ],
      "city": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "country": "st"
    },
    "account_number": "string",
    "bic": "stringst"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="execute-a-transaction-using-an-e-wallet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[WalletTransactionExecuteRequest](#schemawallettransactionexecuterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» idempotency_key|body|[WalletTransactionIdempotencyKey](#schemawallettransactionidempotencykey)|true|A random key provided by the client, per unique wallet transaction. Maximum of 128 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. If a request to execute a wallet transaction fails due to a network connection error, then after a minimum delay of one minute, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single wallet transaction is created. If the request was successfully processed, it will prevent any transaction that uses the same idempotency key, and was received within 48 hours of the first request, from being processed.|
|» wallet_id|body|string|true|The ID of the e-wallet to debit from|
|» counterparty|body|[WalletTransactionCounterparty](#schemawallettransactioncounterparty)|true|An object representing the e-wallet transaction's counterparty|
|» amount|body|[WalletTransactionAmount](#schemawallettransactionamount)|true|The amount and currency of a transaction|
|» user_id|body|string|false|The `user_id` of the end user the transaction is for, as returned by [`/user/create`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/#usercreate). The user must have a `name` and either an email address or a phone number. Required for new integrations.|
|» reference|body|string|true|A reference for the transaction. This must be a string of 6 to 18 characters containing only letters, numbers, and spaces.<br>Ensure that the `reference` field is unique for each transaction.|
|» originating_fund_source|body|[OriginatingFundSource](#schemaoriginatingfundsource)|false|The original source of the funds. This field is required by local regulation for certain businesses (e.g. money remittance) to send payouts to recipients in the EU and UK.|

```json
  "transaction_id": "wallet-transaction-id-production-53e58b32-fc1c-46fe-bbd6-e584b27a88",

}
```

`POST /wallet/transaction/list`

This endpoint lists the latest transactions of the specified e-wallet. Transactions are returned in descending order by the `created_at` time.

<a href="/api/products/virtual-accounts/#wallettransactionlist">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "wallet_id": "string",
  "cursor": "string",
  "count": 10,
  "options": {
    "start_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "end_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="list-e-wallet-transactions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[WalletTransactionListRequest](#schemawallettransactionlistrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» wallet_id|body|string|true|The ID of the e-wallet to fetch transactions from|
|» cursor|body|string|false|A value representing the latest transaction to be included in the response. Set this from `next_cursor` received in the previous `/wallet/transaction/list` request. If provided, the response will only contain that transaction and transactions created before it. If omitted, the response will contain transactions starting from the most recent, and in descending order by the `created_at` time.|
|» count|body|integer|false|The number of transactions to fetch|
|» options|body|[WalletTransactionListRequestOptions](#schemawallettransactionlistrequestoptions)|false|Additional wallet transaction options|

`POST /beta/transactions/rules/v1/create`

The `/beta/transactions/rules/v1/create` endpoint creates transaction categorization rules.

Rules will be applied on the Item's transactions returned in `/transactions/get` response.

The product is currently in beta. To request access, contact transactions-feedback@plaid.com.

## Get EWA Score Report

<a id="opIdbetaEwaReportV1Get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/beta/ewa_report/v1/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "access-sandbox-71e02f71-0960-4a27-abd2-5631e04f2175"
  }'
```

`POST /beta/ewa_report/v1/get`

The `/beta/ewa_report/v1/get` endpoint provides an Earned Wage Access (EWA) score that quantifies the delinquency risk associated with a given item. The score is derived from a combination of cashflow patterns and network-based behavioral features.

The response returns a list of EWA scores, where each score corresponds to a potential advance amount range. These scores estimate the likelihood of repayment for advances within that range.

Score range: 1-99

Interpretation: Higher scores indicate a greater likelihood of repayment.

This endpoint enables clients to assess repayment risk and make data-driven decisions when determining eligibility or limits for earned wage advances.

<a href="/api/products/beta/#betaewareportv1get">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "access-sandbox-71e02f71-0960-4a27-abd2-5631e04f2175"
}
```

<h3 id="get-ewa-score-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BetaEwaReportV1GetRequest](#schemabetaewareportv1getrequest)|true|none|
|» access_token|body|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

## Get Cash Advance income insights

<a id="opIdbetaCashAdvanceIncomeInsightsV1Get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/beta/cash_advance/income_insights/v1/get \
  -X POST \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \

    "client_id": "${PLAID_CLIENT_ID}",
    "secret": "${PLAID_SECRET}",
    "user_id": "usr_9nSp2KuZ2x4JDw"
  }'
```

`POST /beta/cash_advance/income_insights/v1/get`

The `/beta/cash_advance/income_insights/v1/get` endpoint returns a user's top income streams across all of the user's active Items, ranked by historical net monthly income and capped at three, along with the next payment date and amount of the highest-ranked stream.

Only USD income streams are returned. If some, but not all, of the user's Items could not be evaluated, the response is based on the remaining Items.

<a href="/api/products/beta/#betacashadvanceincomeinsightsv1get">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "${PLAID_CLIENT_ID}",
  "secret": "${PLAID_SECRET}",
  "user_id": "usr_9nSp2KuZ2x4JDw"
}
```

`POST /beta/issues/v1/subscribe`

Subscribe a webhook URL to resolution notifications for an institution issue. A client has a single subscription per issue, so subscribing again for the same issue overwrites the previously registered webhook URL.

```json

  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "issue_id": "string",
```

|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» issue_id|body|string|true|The KI- or INC-prefixed identifier of the issue to subscribe to.|

<a id="opIdissuesSearch"></a>

`POST /issues/search`

Search for an issue associated with one of the following identifiers:  `item_id`, `link_session_id` or Link session `request_id`. This endpoint returns a list containing at most one issue. If no issues are associated with the provided identifier, `issues` is omitted. At least one of the identifiers must be provided to perform the search.

<a href="/none/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "item_id": "string",
  "link_session_id": "string",
  "link_session_request_id": "string"
}
```

|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» item_id|body|string|false|A unique identifier for the Plaid Item.|
|» link_session_id|body|string|false|A unique identifier for the Link session.|

`POST /partner/customer/create`

The `/partner/customer/create` endpoint is used by reseller partners to create end customers. To create end customers, it should be called in the Production environment only, even when creating Sandbox API keys. If called in the Sandbox environment, it will return a sample response, but no customer will be created and the API keys will not be valid.

<a href="/api/partner/#partnercustomercreate">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

<h3 id="creates-a-new-end-customer-for-a-plaid-reseller-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PartnerCustomerCreateRequest](#schemapartnercustomercreaterequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» company_name|body|string|true|The company name of the end customer being created. This will be used to display the end customer in the Plaid Dashboard. It will not be shown to end users.|
|» is_diligence_attested|body|boolean|true|Denotes whether or not the partner has completed attestation of diligence for the end customer to be created.|
|» products|body|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|The products to be enabled for the end customer. If empty or `null`, this field will default to the products enabled for the reseller at the time this endpoint is called.|
|» create_link_customization|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the end customer's default Link customization will be set to match the partner's. You can always change the end customer's Link customization in the Plaid Dashboard. See the [Link Customization docs](https://plaid.com/docs/link/customization/) for more information. If you require the ability to programmatically create end customers using multiple different Link customization profiles, contact your Plaid account manager for assistance.<br><br>Important: Data Transparency Messaging (DTM) use cases will not be copied to the end customer's Link customization unless the **Publish changes** button is clicked after the use cases are applied. Link will not work in Production unless the end customer's DTM use cases are configured. For more details, see [Data Transparency Messaging](https://plaid.com/docs/link/data-transparency-messaging-migration-guide/).|
|» logo|body|string|false|Base64-encoded representation of the end customer's logo. Must be a PNG of size 1024x1024 under 4MB. The logo will be shared with financial institutions and shown to the end user during Link flows. A logo is required if `create_link_customization` is `true`. If `create_link_customization` is `false` and the logo is omitted, the partner's logo will be used if one exists, otherwise a stock logo will be used.|
|» legal_entity_name|body|string|true|The end customer's legal name. This will be shared with financial institutions as part of the OAuth registration process. It will not be shown to end users.|
|» website|body|string|true|The end customer's website.|
|» application_name|body|string|true|The name of the end customer's application. This will be shown to end users when they go through the Plaid Link flow. The application name must be unique and cannot match the name of another application already registered with Plaid.|
|» technical_contact|body|[PartnerEndCustomerTechnicalContact](#schemapartnerendcustomertechnicalcontact)|false|The technical contact for the end customer. Defaults to partner's technical contact if omitted.|
|» billing_contact|body|[PartnerEndCustomerBillingContact](#schemapartnerendcustomerbillingcontact)|false|The billing contact for the end customer. Defaults to partner's billing contact if omitted.|
|» customer_support_info|body|[PartnerEndCustomerCustomerSupportInfo](#schemapartnerendcustomercustomersupportinfo)|false|This information is public. Users of your app will see this information when managing connections between your app and their bank accounts in Plaid Portal. Defaults to partner's customer support info if omitted. This field is mandatory for partners whose Plaid accounts were created after November 26, 2024 and will be mandatory for all partners by the 1033 compliance deadline.|
|» address|body|[PartnerEndCustomerAddress](#schemapartnerendcustomeraddress)|true|The end customer's address.|
|» is_bank_addendum_completed|body|boolean|true|Denotes whether the partner has forwarded the Plaid bank addendum to the end customer.|
|» assets_under_management|body|[PartnerEndCustomerAssetsUnderManagement](#schemapartnerendcustomerassetsundermanagement)|false|Assets under management for the given end customer. Required for end customers with monthly service commitments.|
|» redirect_uris|body|[string]|false|A list of URIs indicating the destination(s) where a user can be forwarded after completing the Link flow; used to support OAuth authentication flows when launching Link in the browser or another app. URIs should not contain any query parameters. When used in Production, URIs must use https. To modify redirect URIs for an end customer after creating them, go to the end customer's [API page](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api) in the Dashboard.|
|» registration_number|body|string|false|The unique identifier assigned to a financial institution by regulatory authorities, if applicable. For banks, this is the FDIC Certificate Number. For credit unions, this is the Credit Union Charter Number.|

<h3 id="creates-a-new-end-customer-for-a-plaid-reseller-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BetaPartnerCustomerV1CreateRequest](#schemabetapartnercustomerv1createrequest)|true|none|
|» client_id|body|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|» secret|body|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|» company_name|body|string|true|The company name of the end customer being created. This will be used to display the end customer in the Plaid Dashboard. It will not be shown to end users.|
|» is_diligence_attested|body|boolean|false|Denotes whether or not the partner has completed attestation of diligence for the end customer to be created.|
|» products|body|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|The products to be enabled for the end customer. If empty or `null`, this field will default to the products enabled for the reseller at the time this endpoint is called.|
|» create_link_customization|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the end customer's default Link customization will be set to match the partner's. You can always change the end customer's Link customization in the Plaid Dashboard. See the [Link Customization docs](https://plaid.com/docs/link/customization/) for more information. If you require the ability to programmatically create end customers using multiple different Link customization profiles, contact your Plaid account manager for assistance.<br><br>Important: Data Transparency Messaging (DTM) use cases will not be copied to the end customer's Link customization unless the **Publish changes** button is clicked after the use cases are applied. Link will not work in Production unless the end customer's DTM use cases are configured. For more details, see [Data Transparency Messaging](https://plaid.com/docs/link/data-transparency-messaging-migration-guide/).|
|» logo|body|string|false|Base64-encoded representation of the end customer's logo. Must be a PNG of size 1024x1024 under 4MB. The logo will be shared with financial institutions and shown to the end user during Link flows. A logo is required if `create_link_customization` is `true`. If `create_link_customization` is `false` and the logo is omitted, the partner's logo will be used if one exists, otherwise a stock logo will be used.|
|» legal_entity_name|body|string|false|The end customer's legal name. This will be shared with financial institutions as part of the OAuth registration process. It will not be shown to end users.|
|» website|body|string|true|The end customer's website.|
|» application_name|body|string|true|The name of the end customer's application. This will be shown to end users when they go through the Plaid Link flow. The application name must be unique and cannot match the name of another application already registered with Plaid.|
|» technical_contact|body|[PartnerEndCustomerTechnicalContact](#schemapartnerendcustomertechnicalcontact)|false|The technical contact for the end customer. Defaults to partner's technical contact if omitted.|
|» billing_contact|body|[PartnerEndCustomerBillingContact](#schemapartnerendcustomerbillingcontact)|false|The billing contact for the end customer. Defaults to partner's billing contact if omitted.|
|» customer_support_info|body|[PartnerEndCustomerCustomerSupportInfo](#schemapartnerendcustomercustomersupportinfo)|true|This information is public. Users of your app will see this information when managing connections between your app and their bank accounts in Plaid Portal. Defaults to partner's customer support info if omitted. This field is mandatory for partners whose Plaid accounts were created after November 26, 2024 and will be mandatory for all partners by the 1033 compliance deadline.|
|» address|body|[PartnerEndCustomerAddress](#schemapartnerendcustomeraddress)|true|The end customer's address.|
|» redirect_uris|body|[string]|false|A list of URIs indicating the destination(s) where a user can be forwarded after completing the Link flow; used to support OAuth authentication flows when launching Link in the browser or another app. URIs should not contain any query parameters. When used in Production, URIs must use https. To modify redirect URIs for an end customer after creating them, go to the end customer's [API page](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api) in the Dashboard.|
|» bank_addendum_acceptance|body|[PartnerEndCustomerBankAddendumAcceptance](#schemapartnerendcustomerbankaddendumacceptance)|false|The bank addendum acceptance for the end customer.|
|» questionnaires|body|[PartnerEndCustomerQuestionnaires](#schemapartnerendcustomerquestionnaires)|false|The questionnaires for the end customer.|

|» category|body|[FDXNotificationCategory](#schemafdxnotificationcategory)|true|Category of Notification|
|» severity|body|[FDXNotificationSeverity](#schemafdxnotificationseverity)|false|Severity level of notification|
|» priority|body|[FDXNotificationPriority](#schemafdxnotificationpriority)|false|Priority of notification|
|» publisher|body|[FDXParty](#schemafdxparty)|false|FDX Participant - an entity or person that is a part of a FDX API transaction|
|» subscriber|body|[FDXParty](#schemafdxparty)|false|FDX Participant - an entity or person that is a part of a FDX API transaction|

## Revoke FDX consent grant

<a id="opIdfdxConsentsRevoke"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/fdx/consents/string/revocation \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "PLAID-CLIENT-ID: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "PLAID-SECRET: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Plaid-Version: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "initiator": "DATA_ACCESS_PLATFORM",
    "reason": "BUSINESS_RULE",
    "otherReason": "string",
    "updatedTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`PUT /fdx/consents/{consentId}/revocation`

Revokes a consent grant, ending the data recipient's ongoing access to the customer's data.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "initiator": "DATA_ACCESS_PLATFORM",
  "reason": "BUSINESS_RULE",
  "otherReason": "string",
  "updatedTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="revoke-fdx-consent-grant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|consentId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the consent grant.|
|body|body|[FDXConsentRevocation](#schemafdxconsentrevocation)|true|none|
|» initiator|body|[FDXPartyType](#schemafdxpartytype)|true|Identifies the type of a party|
|» reason|body|[FDXUpdateReason](#schemafdxupdatereason)|true|Reason for lifecycle event status change|
|» otherReason|body|string|false|Additional information or description of an `OTHER` reason|
|» updatedTime|body|string(date-time)|false|When the revocation was effected on the initiator's side|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» initiator|DATA_ACCESS_PLATFORM|
|» initiator|DATA_PROVIDER|
|» initiator|DATA_RECIPIENT|
|» initiator|INDIVIDUAL|
|» initiator|MERCHANT|
|» initiator|VENDOR|
|» reason|BUSINESS_RULE|
|» reason|SECURITY_EVENT|
|» reason|USER_ACTION|
|» reason|OTHER|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
{
  "error_type": "string",
  "error_code": "string",
  "error_message": "string"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|204|No Content|No Content|None|
|default|Default|Error response|[FDXError](#schemafdxerror)|

Returns metadata for a single recipient (application), identified by `recipientId`.

<h3 id="get-recipient-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|recipientId|path|string|true|The recipient's (application's) identifier (a UUID), as returned by `/fdx/recipients`.|
|OAUTH-STATE-ID|header|string|false|Optional. If this lookup happens during an active OAuth flow, pass the value of the OAuth `state` parameter to help Plaid correlate this request in logs.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "recipient_id": "7bf0b839-861e-444e-b103-9007610ffbaf",
  "client_name": "My Example Client",
  "logo_uri": "https://client-logos.plaid.com/logo.png",
  "third_party_legal_name": "My Example Client LLC"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
  "error_code": "string",
  "error_code_reason": "string",
  "error_message": "string",
  "display_message": "string",
  "request_id": "string",
  "causes": [
    null
  ],
  "status": 0,
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "suggested_action": "string",
  "required_account_subtypes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "provided_account_subtypes": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-recipient-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[GetRecipientResponse](#schemagetrecipientresponse)|
|default|Default|Error response|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
clientId & secret & plaidVersion
</aside>

An object containing identifying numbers used for making electronic transfers to and from the `accounts`. The identifying number type (ACH, EFT, IBAN, or Bacs) used will depend on the country of the account. An account may have more than one number type. If a particular identifying number type is not used by any `accounts` for which data has been requested, the array for that type will be empty.

AuthVerifyResponse defines the response schema for `/auth/verify`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|
|item_id|string \| null|false|none|The `item_id` value of the Item created for verification. If numbers data provided is invalid, an Item may not be created.|
|verification_status|string|true|none|Indicates the Item's database verification status. Possible values are:<br><br>`database_insights_fail`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources and have signal for being invalid and/or have no signal for being valid. Typically this indicates that the routing number is invalid, the account number does not match the account number format associated with the routing number, or the account has been reported as closed or frozen. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_insights_pass`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources: the routing and account number match a routing and account number of an account recognized on the Plaid network, and the account is not known by Plaid to be frozen or closed. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_insights_pass_with_caution`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources and have some signal for being valid: the routing and account number were not recognized on the Plaid network, but the routing number is valid and the account number is a potential valid account number for that routing number. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br>|
|verification_insights|[AccountVerificationInsights](#schemaaccountverificationinsights)|true|none|Insights from performing database verification for the account. Only returned for Auth Items using Database Auth.|

### Properties

<h2 id="tocS_PersonalFinanceCategoryVersion">PersonalFinanceCategoryVersion</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapersonalfinancecategoryversion"></a>
<a id="schema_PersonalFinanceCategoryVersion"></a>
<a id="tocSpersonalfinancecategoryversion"></a>
<a id="tocspersonalfinancecategoryversion"></a>

```json
"v1"
```

Indicates which version of the personal finance category taxonomy is being used. [View PFCv2 and PFCv1 taxonomies](https://plaid.com/documents/pfc-taxonomy-all.csv).

If you enabled Transactions or Enrich before December 3, 2025 you will receive the `v1` taxonomy by default and may request `v2` by explicitly setting this field to `v2` in the request.

If you enabled Transactions or Enrich on or after December 3, 2025, you may only receive the `v2` taxonomy.

<h2 id="tocS_TransactionsGetRequestOptions">TransactionsGetRequestOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransactionsgetrequestoptions"></a>
<a id="schema_TransactionsGetRequestOptions"></a>
<a id="tocStransactionsgetrequestoptions"></a>
<a id="tocstransactionsgetrequestoptions"></a>

```json
{
  "account_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "count": 100,
  "offset": 0,
  "include_original_description": false,
  "include_personal_finance_category_beta": false,
  "include_personal_finance_category": false,
  "include_logo_and_counterparty_beta": false,
  "personal_finance_category_version": "v1",
  "days_requested": 90
}
```

An optional object to be used with the request. If specified, `options` must not be `null`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_ids|[string]|false|none|A list of `account_ids` to retrieve for the Item<br><br>Note: An error will be returned if a provided `account_id` is not associated with the Item.|
|count|integer|false|none|The number of transactions to fetch.|
|offset|integer|false|none|The number of transactions to skip. The default value is 0.|
|include_original_description|boolean \| null|false|none|Include the raw unparsed transaction description from the financial institution.|
|include_personal_finance_category_beta|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Personal finance categories are now returned by default.|
|include_personal_finance_category|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Personal finance categories are now returned by default.|
|include_logo_and_counterparty_beta|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Counterparties and extra merchant fields are now returned by default.|
|personal_finance_category_version|[PersonalFinanceCategoryVersion](#schemapersonalfinancecategoryversion)|false|none|Indicates which version of the personal finance category taxonomy is being used. [View PFCv2 and PFCv1 taxonomies](https://plaid.com/documents/pfc-taxonomy-all.csv).<br><br>If you enabled Transactions or Enrich before December 3, 2025 you will receive the `v1` taxonomy by default and may request `v2` by explicitly setting this field to `v2` in the request.<br><br>If you enabled Transactions or Enrich on or after December 3, 2025, you may only receive the `v2` taxonomy.<br>|
|days_requested|integer|false|none|This field only applies to calls for Items where the Transactions product has not already been initialized (i.e. by specifying `transactions` in the `products`, `optional_products`, or `required_if_supported_products` array when calling `/link/token/create` or by making a previous call to `/transactions/sync` or `/transactions/get`). In those cases, the field controls the maximum number of days of transaction history that Plaid will request from the financial institution. The more transaction history is requested, the longer the historical update poll will take. If no value is specified, 90 days of history will be requested by default. In Production, if a value under 30 is provided, a minimum of 30 days of history will be requested.<br><br>If you are initializing your Items with transactions during the `/link/token/create` call (e.g. by including `transactions` in the `/link/token/create` `products` array), you must use the [`transactions.days_requested`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/#link-token-create-request-transactions-days-requested) field in the `/link/token/create` request instead of in the `/transactions/get` request.<br><br>If the Item has already been initialized with the Transactions product, this field will have no effect. The maximum amount of transaction history to request on an Item cannot be updated if Transactions has already been added to the Item. To request older transaction history on an Item where Transactions has already been added, you must delete the Item via `/item/remove` and send the user through Link to create a new Item.<br><br>Customers using [Recurring Transactions](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#transactionsrecurringget) should request at least 180 days of history for optimal results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|personal_finance_category_version|v1|
|personal_finance_category_version|v2|

Transactions are returned in reverse chronological order, with the most recent at the beginning of the array. The maximum number of transactions returned is determined by the `count` parameter.|
|total_transactions|integer|true|none|The total number of transactions available within the date range specified. If `total_transactions` is larger than the size of the `transactions` array, more transactions are available and can be fetched via manipulating the `offset` parameter.|
|item|[Item](#schemaitem)|true|none|Metadata about the Item.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

CashflowReportGetResponse defines the response schema for `/cashflow_report/get`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accounts|[[BusinessAccount](#schemabusinessaccount)]|true|none|An array containing the `accounts` associated with the Item for which transactions are being returned. Each transaction can be mapped to its corresponding account via the `account_id` field.|
|transactions|[[CashflowReportTransaction](#schemacashflowreporttransaction)]|true|none|An array containing transactions from the account. Transactions are returned in reverse chronological order, with the most recent at the beginning of the array. The maximum number of transactions returned is determined by the `count` parameter.|
|total_transactions|integer|true|none|The total number of transactions available within the date range specified. If `total_transactions` is larger than the size of the `transactions` array, more transactions are available and can be fetched using the `cursor` parameter.|
|item|[Item](#schemaitem)|true|none|Metadata about the Item.|
|next_cursor|string|true|none|Cursor used for fetching any future updates after the latest update provided in this response.|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|Represents if more than requested count of transactions exists to be fetched|
|last_successful_update_time|string(date-time)|true|none|The last successful update time in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format ( `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ` )|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

Monthly summary statistics derived from transaction-level data.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_date|string(date)|true|none|The start date of the period covered in this monthly summary.<br><br>This date will be the first day of the month, unless the month being covered is a partial month because it is the first month included in the summary and the date range being requested does not begin with the first day of the month.<br><br>The date will be returned in an ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|end_date|string(date)|true|none|The end date of the period included in this monthly summary.<br><br>This date will be the last day of the month, unless the month being covered is a partial month because it is the last month included in the summary and the date range being requested does not end with the last day of the month.<br><br>The date will be returned in an ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|starting_balance|[CashflowReportMonthlySummaryStartingBalance](#schemacashflowreportmonthlysummarystartingbalance)|true|none|The starting balance of the month. This will be the same as the ending balance of the previous month. This field will not be available for the first monthly summary.|
|ending_balance|[CashflowReportMonthlySummaryEndingBalance](#schemacashflowreportmonthlysummaryendingbalance)|true|none|The ending balance of the month. This will be the same as the starting balance of the next month. This field will not be available for the last monthly summary.|
|average_daily_ending_balance|[CashflowReportMonthlySummaryAverageDailyEndingBalance](#schemacashflowreportmonthlysummaryaveragedailyendingbalance)|true|none|Calendar-day average of the ending balance.|
|average_daily_inflow_amount|[CashflowReportMonthlySummaryAverageDailyInflowAmount](#schemacashflowreportmonthlysummaryaveragedailyinflowamount)|true|none|The average daily sum of inflow transactions, calculated over the month. Always represented as a positive monetary amount.|
|average_daily_outflow_amount|[CashflowReportMonthlySummaryAverageDailyOutflowAmount](#schemacashflowreportmonthlysummaryaveragedailyoutflowamount)|true|none|The average daily sum of outflow transactions, calculated over the month. Always represented as a positive monetary amount.|
|average_daily_net_cashflow_amount|[CashflowReportMonthlySummaryAverageDailyNetCashflowAmount](#schemacashflowreportmonthlysummaryaveragedailynetcashflowamount)|true|none|The average daily net cash flow amount, calculated as total daily inflows less total daily outflows.|
|average_daily_inflow_transaction_count|number|true|none|The average count of the number of daily inflow transactions. Rounded to 2 decimal places.|
|average_daily_outflow_transaction_count|number|true|none|The average count of the number of daily outflow transactions. Rounded to 2 decimal places.|
|total_revenue|[CashflowReportMonthlySummaryTotalRevenue](#schemacashflowreportmonthlysummarytotalrevenue)|true|none|The total amount of all revenue transactions during this month.|
|total_loan_payment|[CashflowReportMonthlySummaryTotalLoanPayment](#schemacashflowreportmonthlysummarytotalloanpayment)|true|none|The total amount of all loan payment transactions during this month.|
|total_variable_expense|[CashflowReportMonthlySummaryTotalVariableExpense](#schemacashflowreportmonthlysummarytotalvariableexpense)|true|none|The total amount of all variable expense transactions during this month.|
|total_payroll|[CashflowReportMonthlySummaryTotalPayroll](#schemacashflowreportmonthlysummarytotalpayroll)|true|none|The total amount of all payroll transactions during this month.|
|nsf_transaction_count|integer|true|none|The total number of all NSF transactions during this month.|
|overdraft_transaction_count|integer|true|none|The total number of all overdraft transactions during this month.|
|negative_ending_balance_day_count|integer|true|none|The number of days with a negative daily average ending balance. The daily average is calculated across all valid accounts. Values will be in the range [0, 31].|

Business identity information about an account

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|Plaid's unique identifier for the account. This value will not change unless Plaid can't reconcile the account with the data returned by the financial institution. This may occur, for example, when the name of the account changes. If this happens a new `account_id` will be assigned to the account.<br><br>The `account_id` can also change if the `access_token` is deleted and the same credentials that were used to generate that `access_token` are used to generate a new `access_token` on a later date. In that case, the new `account_id` will be different from the old `account_id`.<br><br>If an account with a specific `account_id` disappears instead of changing, the account is likely closed. Closed accounts are not returned by the Plaid API.<br><br>When using a CRA endpoint (an endpoint associated with Plaid Check Consumer Report, i.e. any endpoint beginning with `/cra/`), the `account_id` returned will not match the `account_id` returned by a non-CRA endpoint.<br><br>Like all Plaid identifiers, the `account_id` is case sensitive.|
|balances|[AccountBalance](#schemaaccountbalance)|true|none|A set of fields describing the balance for an account. For real-time values, use `/accounts/balance/get` or `/signal/evaluate` (with a Balance-only ruleset), which are fetched live from the institution at request time. Values returned by other endpoints may be cached, or adjusted by Plaid to reflect transaction activity received since the last refresh.|
|mask|string \| null|true|none|The last 2-4 alphanumeric characters of either the account's displayed mask or the account's official account number. Note that the mask may be non-unique between an Item's accounts.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the account, either assigned by the user or by the financial institution itself|
|official_name|string \| null|true|none|The official name of the account as given by the financial institution|
|type|[AccountType](#schemaaccounttype)|true|none|`investment:` Investment account. In API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier, this type is called `brokerage` instead.<br><br>`credit:` Credit card<br><br>`depository:` Depository account<br><br>`loan:` Loan account<br><br>`other:` Non-specified account type<br><br>See the [Account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema) for a full listing of account types and corresponding subtypes.|
|subtype|[AccountSubtype](#schemaaccountsubtype)|true|none|See the [Account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#account-type-schema) for a full listing of account types and corresponding subtypes.|
|verification_status|string|false|none|Indicates an Item's micro-deposit-based verification or database verification status. This field is only populated when using Auth and falling back to micro-deposit or database verification. Possible values are:<br><br>`pending_automatic_verification`: The Item is pending automatic verification.<br><br>`pending_manual_verification`: The Item is pending manual micro-deposit verification. Items remain in this state until the user successfully verifies the code.<br><br>`automatically_verified`: The Item has successfully been automatically verified.<br><br>`manually_verified`: The Item has successfully been manually verified.<br><br>`verification_expired`: Plaid was unable to automatically verify the deposit within 7 calendar days and will no longer attempt to validate the Item. Users may retry by submitting their information again through Link.<br><br>`verification_failed`: The Item failed manual micro-deposit verification because the user exhausted all 3 verification attempts. Users may retry by submitting their information again through Link.<br><br>`unsent`: The Item is pending micro-deposit verification, but Plaid has not yet sent the micro-deposit.<br><br>`database_insights_fail`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources and have signal for being invalid and/or have no signal for being valid. Typically this indicates that the routing number is invalid, the account number does not match the account number format associated with the routing number, or the account has been reported as closed or frozen. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_insights_pass`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources: the routing and account number match a routing and account number of an account recognized on the Plaid network, and the account is not known by Plaid to be frozen or closed. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_insights_pass_with_caution`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources and have some signal for being valid: the routing and account number were not recognized on the Plaid network, but the routing number is valid and the account number is a potential valid account number for that routing number. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_matched`: (deprecated) The Item has successfully been verified using Plaid's data sources. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Match.<br><br>Omitted or empty string: Neither micro-deposit-based verification nor database verification are being used for the Item.|
|verification_name|string|false|none|The account holder name that was used for micro-deposit and/or database verification. Only returned for Auth Items created via micro-deposit or database verification. This name was manually-entered by the user during Link, unless it was otherwise provided via the `user.legal_name` request field in `/link/token/create` for the Link session that created the Item.|
|verification_insights|[AccountVerificationInsights](#schemaaccountverificationinsights)|false|none|Insights from performing database verification for the account. Only returned for Auth Items using Database Auth.|
|persistent_account_id|string|false|none|A unique and persistent identifier for accounts that can be used to trace multiple instances of the same account across different Items for depository accounts. This field is currently supported only for Items at institutions that use Tokenized Account Numbers (i.e., Chase, PNC, and US Bank). Because these accounts have a different account number each time they are linked, this field may be used instead of the account number to uniquely identify an account across multiple Items for payments use cases, helping to reduce duplicate Items or attempted fraud. In Sandbox, this field is populated for TAN-based institutions (`ins_56`, `ins_13`, `ins_127990`) as well as the OAuth Sandbox institution (`ins_127287`); in Production, it will only be populated for accounts at applicable institutions.|
|apy|number(double) \| null|false|none|The annual percentage yield (APY) on an interest-bearing deposit account, expressed as a percentage (e.g. `4.25` means 4.25%). In the event that the APY is not provided by the financial institution, Plaid will return a value of `null`.|
|holder_category|[AccountHolderCategory](#schemaaccountholdercategory)|false|none|Indicates the account's categorization as either a personal or a business account. This field is currently in beta; to request access, contact your account manager. Coverage varies by institution, with approximately 70% of accounts populated overall.|
|paired_account_id|string \| null|false|none|The `account_id` of the account on the paired Item (see `paired_item_id`) that represents the same bank account as this one. For an account on a Plaid Inc Item, this is the matching account on its paired Plaid Check Item, and the reverse for an account on a Plaid Check Item. Only returned for accounts on an Item that has a paired Item. `null` means the Item has a paired Item but Plaid could not confidently match this account to an account on it. Like `account_id`, this value can change if Plaid re-creates the paired account.|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|official_name|string \| null|true|none|none|
|mask|string \| null|true|none|none|
|verification_name|string|false|none|none|
|owners|[[Owner](#schemaowner)]|false|none|Data returned by the financial institution about the account owner or owners. For business accounts, the name reported may be either the name of the individual or the name of the business, depending on the institution. Multiple owners on a single account will be represented in the same owner object, not in multiple owner objects within the array.|

TransactionsSyncRequest defines the request schema for `/transactions/sync`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|access_token|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|none|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|cursor|string|false|none|The cursor value represents the last update requested. Providing it will cause the response to only return changes after this update.<br>If omitted, the entire history of updates will be returned, starting with the first-added transactions on the Item. The cursor also accepts the special value of `"now"`, which can be used to fast-forward the cursor as part of migrating an existing Item from `/transactions/get` to `/transactions/sync`. For more information, see the [Transactions sync migration guide](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/sync-migration/). Note that using the `"now"` value is not supported for any use case other than migrating existing Items from `/transactions/get`.<br><br>The upper-bound length of this cursor is 256 characters of base64.|
|count|integer|false|none|The number of transaction updates to fetch.|
|options|[TransactionsSyncRequestOptions](#schematransactionssyncrequestoptions)|false|none|An optional object to be used with the request. If specified, `options` must not be `null`.|

<h2 id="tocS_TransactionsSyncRequestOptions">TransactionsSyncRequestOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransactionssyncrequestoptions"></a>
<a id="schema_TransactionsSyncRequestOptions"></a>
<a id="tocStransactionssyncrequestoptions"></a>
<a id="tocstransactionssyncrequestoptions"></a>

```json
{
  "include_original_description": false,
  "include_personal_finance_category": false,
  "include_logo_and_counterparty_beta": false,
  "personal_finance_category_version": "v1",
  "days_requested": 90,
  "account_id": "string"
}
```

An optional object to be used with the request. If specified, `options` must not be `null`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include_original_description|boolean \| null|false|none|Include the raw unparsed transaction description from the financial institution.|
|include_personal_finance_category|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Personal finance categories are now returned by default.|
|include_logo_and_counterparty_beta|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Counterparties and extra merchant fields are now returned by default.|
|personal_finance_category_version|[PersonalFinanceCategoryVersion](#schemapersonalfinancecategoryversion)|false|none|Indicates which version of the personal finance category taxonomy is being used. [View PFCv2 and PFCv1 taxonomies](https://plaid.com/documents/pfc-taxonomy-all.csv).<br><br>If you enabled Transactions or Enrich before December 3, 2025 you will receive the `v1` taxonomy by default and may request `v2` by explicitly setting this field to `v2` in the request.<br><br>If you enabled Transactions or Enrich on or after December 3, 2025, you may only receive the `v2` taxonomy.<br>|
|days_requested|integer|false|none|This field only applies to calls for Items where the Transactions product has not already been initialized (i.e., by specifying `transactions` in the `products`, `required_if_supported_products`, or `optional_products` array when calling `/link/token/create` or by making a previous call to `/transactions/sync` or `/transactions/get`). In those cases, the field controls the maximum number of days of transaction history that Plaid will request from the financial institution. The more transaction history is requested, the longer the historical update poll will take. If no value is specified, 90 days of history will be requested by default. In Production, if a value less than 30 is provided, a minimum of 30 days of transaction history will be requested.<br><br>If you are initializing your Items with transactions during the `/link/token/create` call (e.g. by including `transactions` in the `/link/token/create` `products` array), you must use the [`transactions.days_requested`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/#link-token-create-request-transactions-days-requested) field in the `/link/token/create` request instead of in the `/transactions/sync` request.<br><br>If the Item has already been initialized with the Transactions product, this field will have no effect. The maximum amount of transaction history to request on an Item cannot be updated if Transactions has already been added to the Item. To request older transaction history on an Item where Transactions has already been added, you must delete the Item via `/item/remove` and send the user through Link to create a new Item.<br><br>Customers using [Recurring Transactions](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#transactionsrecurringget) should request at least 180 days of history for optimal results.|
|account_id|string|false|none|If provided, the returned updates and cursor will only reflect the specified account's transactions. Omitting `account_id` returns updates for all accounts under the Item. Note that specifying an `account_id` effectively creates a separate incremental update stream -- and therefore a separate cursor -- for that account. If multiple accounts are queried this way, you will maintain multiple cursors, one per `account_id`.<br><br>If you decide to begin filtering by `account_id` after using no `account_id`, start fresh with a null cursor and maintain separate `(account_id, cursor)` pairs going forward. Do not reuse any previously saved cursors, as this can cause pagination errors or incomplete data.<br><br>Note: An error will be returned if a provided `account_id` is not associated with the Item.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|personal_finance_category_version|v1|
|personal_finance_category_version|v2|

TransactionsSyncResponse defines the response schema for `/transactions/sync`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transactions_update_status|[TransactionsUpdateStatus](#schematransactionsupdatestatus)|true|none|A description of the update status for transaction pulls of an Item. This field contains the same information provided by transactions webhooks, and may be helpful for webhook troubleshooting or when recovering from missed webhooks.<br><br>`TRANSACTIONS_UPDATE_STATUS_UNKNOWN`: Unable to fetch transactions update status for Item.<br><br>`NOT_READY`: The Item is pending transaction pull.<br><br>`INITIAL_UPDATE_COMPLETE`: Initial pull for the Item is complete, historical pull is pending.<br><br>`HISTORICAL_UPDATE_COMPLETE`: Both initial and historical pull for Item are complete.|
|accounts|[[AccountBase](#schemaaccountbase)]|true|none|An array of accounts at a financial institution associated with the transactions in this response. Only accounts that have associated transactions will be shown. For example, `investment`-type accounts will be omitted.|
|added|[[Transaction](#schematransaction)]|true|none|Transactions that have been added to the Item since `cursor` ordered by ascending last modified time.|
|modified|[[Transaction](#schematransaction)]|true|none|Transactions that have been modified on the Item since `cursor` ordered by ascending last modified time.|
|removed|[[RemovedTransaction](#schemaremovedtransaction)]|true|none|Transactions that have been removed from the Item since `cursor` ordered by ascending last modified time.|
|next_cursor|string|true|none|Cursor used for fetching any future updates after the latest update provided in this response. The cursor obtained after all pages have been pulled (indicated by `has_more` being `false`) will be valid for at least 1 year. This cursor should be persisted for later calls. If transactions are not yet available, this will be an empty string.<br><br>If `account_id` is included in the request, the returned cursor will reflect updates for that specific account.|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|Represents if more than requested count of transaction updates exist. If true, the additional updates can be fetched by making an additional request with `cursor` set to `next_cursor`.
