An optional object to filter `/institutions/get` results.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|none|Filter the Institutions based on which products they support. Will only return institutions that support all listed products. When filtering based on `auth`, an institution must support Instant Auth to match the criterion. To filter for Signal Transaction Scores support, use `balance`. To filter for Transfer support, use `auth`.|
|routing_numbers|[string]|false|none|Specify an array of routing numbers to filter institutions. The response will only return institutions that match all of the routing numbers in the array. Routing number records used for this matching are generally comprehensive; however, failure to match a given routing number to an institution does not necessarily mean that the institution is unsupported by Plaid. Invalid routing numbers (numbers that are not 9 digits in length or do not have a valid checksum) will be filtered from the array before the response is processed. If all provided routing numbers are invalid, an `INVALID_REQUEST` error with the code of `INVALID_FIELD` will be returned.|
|oauth|boolean \| null|false|none|Limit results to institutions with or without OAuth login flows. Note that institutions will have `oauth` set to `true` if some Items associated with that institution are required to use OAuth flows; institutions in a state of migration to OAuth will have the `oauth` attribute set to `true`.|
|include_optional_metadata|boolean|false|none|When `true`, return the institution's homepage URL, logo and primary brand color. Not all institutions' logos are available.<br><br>Note that Plaid does not own any of the logos shared by the API, and that by accessing or using these logos, you agree that you are doing so at your own risk and will, if necessary, obtain all required permissions from the appropriate rights holders and adhere to any applicable usage guidelines. Plaid disclaims all express or implied warranties with respect to the logos.|
|include_auth_metadata|boolean|false|none|When `true`, returns metadata related to the Auth product indicating which auth methods are supported.|
|include_payment_initiation_metadata|boolean|false|none|When `true`, returns metadata related to the Payment Initiation product indicating which payment configurations are supported.|


Optional parameters to `/accounts/balance/get`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_ids|[string]|false|none|A list of `account_ids` to retrieve for the Item. The default value is `null`.<br><br>Note: An error will be returned if a provided `account_id` is not associated with the Item.|
|min_last_updated_datetime|[MinLastUpdatedDatetime](#schemaminlastupdateddatetime)|false|none|Timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`) indicating the oldest acceptable balance when making a request to `/accounts/balance/get`.<br><br>This field is only necessary when the institution is `ins_128026` (Capital One), *and* the Item has one or more non-depository accounts (such as a credit card), even if `account_ids` requests only depository accounts, as Capital One does not provide real-time balance for non-depository accounts. It is also necessary for all accounts when the institution is `ins_136439` (Apple Card), which provides only cached balances. In these cases, a value must be provided or an `INVALID_REQUEST` error with the code of `INVALID_FIELD` will be returned. For all other institutions, as well as for depository accounts at Capital One (including all checking and savings accounts) this field is ignored and real-time balance information will be fetched.<br><br>If this field is not ignored, and no acceptable balance is available, an `INVALID_RESULT` error with the code `LAST_UPDATED_DATETIME_OUT_OF_RANGE` will be returned.|

<h2 id="tocS_MinLastUpdatedDatetime">MinLastUpdatedDatetime</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaminlastupdateddatetime"></a>
<a id="schema_MinLastUpdatedDatetime"></a>
<a id="tocSminlastupdateddatetime"></a>
<a id="tocsminlastupdateddatetime"></a>

```json
"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
```

Timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`) indicating the oldest acceptable balance when making a request to `/accounts/balance/get`.

This field is only necessary when the institution is `ins_128026` (Capital One), *and* the Item has one or more non-depository accounts (such as a credit card), even if `account_ids` requests only depository accounts, as Capital One does not provide real-time balance for non-depository accounts. It is also necessary for all accounts when the institution is `ins_136439` (Apple Card), which provides only cached balances. In these cases, a value must be provided or an `INVALID_REQUEST` error with the code of `INVALID_FIELD` will be returned. For all other institutions, as well as for depository accounts at Capital One (including all checking and savings accounts) this field is ignored and real-time balance information will be fetched.

If this field is not ignored, and no acceptable balance is available, an `INVALID_RESULT` error with the code `LAST_UPDATED_DATETIME_OUT_OF_RANGE` will be returned.

<h2 id="tocS_IdentityMatchUser">IdentityMatchUser</h2>

```json
{
  "legal_name": "string",
  "phone_number": "string",
  "email_address": "string",
  "address": {
    "city": "string",
    "region": "string",
    "street": "string",
    "postal_code": "string",
    "country": "string"
  }
}
```

The user's legal name, phone number, email address and address used to perform fuzzy match. If Financial Account Matching is enabled in the Identity Verification product, leave this field empty to automatically match against PII collected from the Identity Verification checks.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|legal_name|string \| null|false|none|The user's full legal name.|
|phone_number|string \| null|false|none|The user's phone number, in E.164 format: +{countrycode}{number}. For example: "+14157452130". Phone numbers provided in other formats will be parsed on a best-effort basis. Phone number input is validated against valid number ranges; number strings that do not match a real-world phone numbering scheme may cause the request to fail, even in the Sandbox test environment.|
|email_address|string \| null|false|none|The user's email address.|
|address|[AddressDataNullableNoRequiredFields](#schemaaddressdatanullablenorequiredfields)|false|none|Data about the components comprising an address.|

IdentityMatchListRequest defines the request schema for `/identity/match/list`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|start_time|string(date-time)|true|none|Inclusive start of the query window in RFC 3339 format. On the first request, this cannot be earlier than one calendar year before the current time.|
|end_time|string(date-time)|true|none|Inclusive end of the query window in RFC 3339 format. Must be on or after `start_time`.|
|count|integer|false|none|Maximum number of attempts to return in one page.|
|cursor|string|false|none|Opaque pagination cursor. Omit on the first request. For subsequent requests, set this field to the `next_cursor` from the previous response and use the same `start_time` and `end_time`. You may change `count` between pages.|

A Link-originated Identity Match attempt.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|attempt_id|string|true|none|Identifier for the Identity Match attempt.|
|item_id|string \| null|true|none|Item ID associated with the attempt. Null if the ID is unavailable.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Time at which the attempt was created.|
|link_session_id|string|true|none|Link session that produced the attempt.|
|link_customization_name|string|true|none|Link customization that supplied the ruleset.|
|ruleset_revision|integer|true|none|Revision of the Identity Match ruleset that was applied.|
|outcome|[IdentityMatchListOutcome](#schemaidentitymatchlistoutcome)|true|none|The Identity Match decision for the attempt.<br><br>`PASS`: The decision was to allow the user to continue.<br>`FAIL`: The decision was to block the user.<br>`UNKNOWN`: The attempt's decision is unavailable or unrecognized.|
|outcome_account_id|string \| null|true|none|Account ID associated with a `PASS` outcome. Null for `FAIL` or `UNKNOWN` outcomes, or if the ID is unavailable.|
|scores|[[IdentityMatchListAttemptScore](#schemaidentitymatchlistattemptscore)]|true|none|Per-account match scores. Empty if the attempt data is unavailable.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|outcome|PASS|
|outcome|FAIL|
|outcome|UNKNOWN|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
{
  "account_id": "string",
  "legal_name": {
    "score": 0,
    "is_first_name_or_last_name_match": true,
    "is_nickname_match": true,
    "is_business_name_detected": true
  },
  "phone_number": {
    "score": 0
  },
  "email_address": {
    "score": 0
  },
  "address": {
    "score": 0,
    "is_postal_code_match": true
  }
}
```

Identity Match scores for one account. Scores compare the user identity data supplied for the Link session through `/link/token/create` with the account owner information from the financial institution.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string \| null|true|none|Account ID for the account that was scored. Null if the ID is unavailable.|
|legal_name|[NameMatchScore](#schemanamematchscore)|true|none|Score found by matching name provided by the API with the name on the account at the financial institution. If the account contains multiple owners, the maximum match score is filled.|
|phone_number|[PhoneNumberMatchScore](#schemaphonenumbermatchscore)|true|none|Score found by matching phone number provided by the API with the phone number on the account at the financial institution. 100 is a perfect match and 0 is a no match. If the account contains multiple owners, the maximum match score is filled.|
|email_address|[EmailAddressMatchScore](#schemaemailaddressmatchscore)|true|none|Score found by matching email provided by the API with the email on the account at the financial institution. 100 is a perfect match and 0 is a no match. If the account contains multiple owners, the maximum match score is filled.|
|address|[AddressMatchScore](#schemaaddressmatchscore)|true|none|Score found by matching address provided by the API with the address on the account at the financial institution. The score can range from 0 to 100 where 100 is a perfect match and 0 is a no match. If the account contains multiple owners, the maximum match score is filled.|

`PASS`: The decision was to allow the user to continue.
`FAIL`: The decision was to block the user.
`UNKNOWN`: The attempt's decision is unavailable or unrecognized.

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|account|[AccountBase](#schemaaccountbase)|true|none|A single account at a financial institution.|

|is_investments_fallback_item|boolean|false|none|When true, this field indicates that the Item's portfolio was manually created with the Investments Fallback flow.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

An optional object to be used with the request. If specified, `options` must not be `null`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|integer|false|none|The number of transactions to fetch.|
|offset|integer|false|none|The number of transactions to skip. The default value is 0.|
|include_original_description|boolean \| null|false|none|Include the raw unparsed transaction description from the financial institution.|
|include_personal_finance_category_beta|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Personal finance categories are now returned by default.|
|include_personal_finance_category|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Personal finance categories are now returned by default.|
|include_logo_and_counterparty_beta|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Counterparties and extra merchant fields are now returned by default.|

ProcessorTransactionsGetResponse defines the response schema for `/processor/transactions/get`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|[AccountBase](#schemaaccountbase)|true|none|A single account at a financial institution.|
|transactions|[[Transaction](#schematransaction)]|true|none|An array containing transactions from the account. Transactions are returned in reverse chronological order, with the most recent at the beginning of the array. The maximum number of transactions returned is determined by the `count` parameter.|
|total_transactions|integer|true|none|The total number of transactions available within the date range specified. If `total_transactions` is larger than the size of the `transactions` array, more transactions are available and can be fetched via manipulating the `offset` parameter.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

ProcessorTransactionsSyncResponse defines the response schema for `/processor/transactions/sync`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transactions_update_status|[TransactionsUpdateStatus](#schematransactionsupdatestatus)|true|none|A description of the update status for transaction pulls of an Item. This field contains the same information provided by transactions webhooks, and may be helpful for webhook troubleshooting or when recovering from missed webhooks.<br><br>`TRANSACTIONS_UPDATE_STATUS_UNKNOWN`: Unable to fetch transactions update status for Item.<br><br>`NOT_READY`: The Item is pending transaction pull.<br><br>`INITIAL_UPDATE_COMPLETE`: Initial pull for the Item is complete, historical pull is pending.<br><br>`HISTORICAL_UPDATE_COMPLETE`: Both initial and historical pull for Item are complete.|
|account|[AccountBaseNullable](#schemaaccountbasenullable)|true|none|A single account at a financial institution.|
|added|[[Transaction](#schematransaction)]|true|none|Transactions that have been added to the Item since `cursor` ordered by ascending last modified time.|
|modified|[[Transaction](#schematransaction)]|true|none|Transactions that have been modified on the Item since `cursor` ordered by ascending last modified time.|
|removed|[[RemovedTransaction](#schemaremovedtransaction)]|true|none|Transactions that have been removed from the Item since `cursor` ordered by ascending last modified time.|
|next_cursor|string|true|none|Cursor used for fetching any future updates after the latest update provided in this response. The cursor obtained after all pages have been pulled (indicated by `has_more` being `false`) will be valid for at least 1 year. This cursor should be persisted for later calls. If transactions are not yet available, this will be an empty string.|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|Represents if more than requested count of transaction updates exist. If true, the additional updates can be fetched by making an additional request with `cursor` set to `next_cursor`. If `has_more` is true, it's important to pull all available pages, to make it less likely for underlying data changes to conflict with pagination.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|transactions_update_status|TRANSACTIONS_UPDATE_STATUS_UNKNOWN|
|transactions_update_status|NOT_READY|
|transactions_update_status|INITIAL_UPDATE_COMPLETE|
|transactions_update_status|HISTORICAL_UPDATE_COMPLETE|

Defines the request schema for `/processor/bank_transfer/create`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|idempotency_key|[BankTransferIdempotencyKey](#schemabanktransferidempotencykey)|true|none|A random key provided by the client, per unique bank transfer. Maximum of 50 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create a bank transfer fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single bank transfer is created.|
|processor_token|[ProcessorToken](#schemaprocessortoken)|true|none|The processor token obtained from the Plaid integration partner. Processor tokens are in the format: `processor-<environment>-<identifier>`|
|type|[BankTransferType](#schemabanktransfertype)|true|none|The type of bank transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into the origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of the origination account.|
|network|[BankTransferNetwork](#schemabanktransfernetwork)|true|none|The network or rails used for the transfer. Valid options are `ach`, `same-day-ach`, or `wire`.|
|amount|[BankTransferAmount](#schemabanktransferamount)|true|none|The amount of the bank transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|iso_currency_code|string|true|none|The currency of the transfer amount - should be set to "USD".|
|description|string|true|none|The transfer description. Maximum of 10 characters.|
|ach_class|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|false|none|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network. For more details, see [ACH SEC codes](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/creating-transfers/#ach-sec-codes).<br><br>Codes supported for credits: `ccd`, `ppd`<br>Codes supported for debits: `ccd`, `ppd`, `tel`, `web`<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - The transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer. Authorization was obtained in writing either in person or via an electronic document signing, e.g. Docusign, by the consumer. Can be used for credits or debits.<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry. The transfer debits a consumer's bank account. Authorization from the consumer is obtained over the Internet (e.g. a web or mobile application). Can be used for single debits or recurring debits.<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry. The transfer debits a consumer. Debit authorization has been received orally over the telephone via a recorded call.|
|user|[BankTransferUser](#schemabanktransferuser)|true|none|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|
|custom_tag|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string provided by the client for storage with the bank transfer. May be up to 100 characters.|
|metadata|[BankTransferMetadata](#schemabanktransfermetadata)|false|none|The Metadata object is a mapping of client-provided string fields to any string value. The following limitations apply:<br>The JSON values must be Strings (no nested JSON objects allowed)<br>Only ASCII characters may be used<br>Maximum of 50 key/value pairs<br>Maximum key length of 40 characters<br>Maximum value length of 500 characters<br>|
|origination_account_id|string \| null|false|none|Plaid's unique identifier for the origination account for this transfer. If you have more than one origination account, this value must be specified.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|debit|
|type|credit|
|network|ach|
|network|same-day-ach|
|network|wire|
|ach_class|ccd|
|ach_class|ppd|
|ach_class|tel|
|ach_class|web|

An object containing identifying numbers used for making electronic transfers to and from the `account`. The identifying number type (ACH, EFT, IBAN, or Bacs) used will depend on the country of the account. An account may have more than one number type. If a particular identifying number type is not used by the `account` for which auth data has been requested, a null value will be returned.

|---|---|---|---|---|

|eft|[NumbersEFTNullable](#schemanumberseftnullable)|false|none|Identifying information for transferring money to or from a Canadian bank account via EFT.|
|international|[NumbersInternationalNullable](#schemanumbersinternationalnullable)|false|none|Identifying information for transferring money to or from an international bank account via wire transfer.|
|bacs|[NumbersBACSNullable](#schemanumbersbacsnullable)|false|none|Identifying information for transferring money to or from a UK bank account via Bacs.|

```json
}
```

Optional parameters to `/processor/balance/get`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|min_last_updated_datetime|[MinLastUpdatedDatetime](#schemaminlastupdateddatetime)|false|none|Timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`) indicating the oldest acceptable balance when making a request to `/accounts/balance/get`.<br><br>This field is only necessary when the institution is `ins_128026` (Capital One), *and* the Item has one or more non-depository accounts (such as a credit card), even if `account_ids` requests only depository accounts, as Capital One does not provide real-time balance for non-depository accounts. It is also necessary for all accounts when the institution is `ins_136439` (Apple Card), which provides only cached balances. In these cases, a value must be provided or an `INVALID_REQUEST` error with the code of `INVALID_FIELD` will be returned. For all other institutions, as well as for depository accounts at Capital One (including all checking and savings accounts) this field is ignored and real-time balance information will be fetched.<br><br>If this field is not ignored, and no acceptable balance is available, an `INVALID_RESULT` error with the code `LAST_UPDATED_DATETIME_OUT_OF_RANGE` will be returned.|

|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|

|start_time|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Return events sent at or after this time, in ISO 8601 format. Must be within the last 7 days. Ignored if `cursor` is provided. If you omit both `cursor` and `start_time`, results start with the oldest retained event.|
|count|integer \| null|false|none|The maximum number of webhook events to return. Fewer events may be returned even when more are available; use `has_more` to determine whether to request another page.|
|webhook_types|[string]|false|none|Return only events with these webhook types, for example `ITEM`. Case-sensitive.|
|webhook_codes|[string]|false|none|Return only events with these webhook codes, for example `ERROR`. Case-sensitive.|
|item_ids|[string]|false|none|Return only events for these Items.|
|delivery_statuses|[[WebhookEventDeliveryStatus](#schemawebhookeventdeliverystatus)]|false|none|Return only events with these delivery statuses.|

<h2 id="tocS_JWKPublicKey">JWKPublicKey</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajwkpublickey"></a>
<a id="schema_JWKPublicKey"></a>
<a id="tocSjwkpublickey"></a>
<a id="tocsjwkpublickey"></a>

```json
{
  "alg": "string",
  "crv": "string",
  "kid": "string",
  "kty": "string",
  "use": "string",
  "x": "string",
  "y": "string",
  "created_at": 0,
  "expired_at": 0
}
```

A JSON Web Key (JWK) that can be used in conjunction with [JWT libraries](https://jwt.io/#libraries-io) to verify Plaid webhooks

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alg|string|true|none|The alg member identifies the cryptographic algorithm family used with the key.|
|crv|string|true|none|The crv member identifies the cryptographic curve used with the key.|
|kid|string|true|none|The kid (Key ID) member can be used to match a specific key. This can be used, for instance, to choose among a set of keys within the JWK during key rollover.|
|kty|string|true|none|The kty (key type) parameter identifies the cryptographic algorithm family used with the key, such as RSA or EC.|
|use|string|true|none|The use (public key use) parameter identifies the intended use of the public key.|
|x|string|true|none|The x member contains the x coordinate for the elliptic curve point, provided as a base64url-encoded string of the coordinate's big endian representation.|
|y|string|true|none|The y member contains the y coordinate for the elliptic curve point, provided as a base64url-encoded string of the coordinate's big endian representation.|
|created_at|integer|true|none|The timestamp when the key was created, in Unix time.|
|expired_at|integer \| null|true|none|The timestamp when the key expired, in Unix time.|

PaymentInitiationPaymentReverseResponse defines the response schema for `/payment_initiation/payment/reverse`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|refund_id|string|true|none|A unique ID identifying the refund|
|status|[WalletTransactionStatus](#schemawallettransactionstatus)|true|none|The status of the transaction.<br><br>`AUTHORISING`: The transaction is being processed for validation and compliance.<br><br>`INITIATED`: The transaction has been initiated and is currently being processed.<br><br>`EXECUTED`: The transaction has been successfully executed and is considered complete. This is only applicable for debit transactions.<br><br>`SETTLED`: The transaction has settled and funds are available for use. This is only applicable for credit transactions. A transaction will typically settle within seconds to several days, depending on which payment rail is used.<br><br>`FAILED`: The transaction failed to process successfully. This is a terminal status.<br><br>`BLOCKED`: The transaction has been blocked for violating compliance rules. This is a terminal status.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|AUTHORISING|
|status|INITIATED|
|status|EXECUTED|
|status|SETTLED|
|status|BLOCKED|
|status|FAILED|

|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|recipient_id|string|true|none|The ID of the recipient the payment is for.|
|user_id|string|false|none|The `user_id` of the end user the payment is initiated for, as returned by [`/user/create`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/#usercreate). The user must have a `name` and either an email address or a phone number. Required for new integrations.|
|reference|string|true|none|A reference for the payment. This must be a string of at most 18 characters containing only letters, numbers, and spaces (since not all institutions support them).<br>In order to track settlement via Payment Confirmation, each payment must have a unique reference. If the reference provided through the API is not unique, Plaid will adjust it.<br>Some institutions may limit the reference to less than 18 characters. If necessary, Plaid will adjust the reference by truncating it to fit the institution's requirements.<br>Both the originally provided and automatically adjusted references (if any) can be found in the `reference` and `adjusted_reference` fields, respectively.|
|amount|[PaymentAmount](#schemapaymentamount)|true|none|The amount and currency of a payment|
|schedule|[ExternalPaymentScheduleRequest](#schemaexternalpaymentschedulerequest)|false|none|The schedule that the payment will be executed on. If a schedule is provided, the payment is automatically set up as a standing order. If no schedule is specified, the payment will be executed only once.|
|options|[ExternalPaymentOptions](#schemaexternalpaymentoptions)|false|none|Additional payment options|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

Maximum of 128 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. If a request to execute a wallet transaction fails due to a network connection error, then after a minimum delay of one minute, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single wallet transaction is created. If the request was successfully processed, it will prevent any transaction that uses the same idempotency key, and was received within 48 hours of the first request, from being processed.|

UserCreateRequest defines the request schema for `/user/create`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|client_user_id|string|true|none|A unique ID representing the end user. Maximum of 128 characters. Typically this will be a user ID number from your application. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|identity|[ClientUserIdentity](#schemaclientuseridentity)|false|none|The identity fields associated with a user. For a user to be eligible for a Plaid Check Consumer Report, all fields are required except `id_numbers`. Providing a partial SSN is strongly recommended, and improves the accuracy of matching user records during compliance processes such as file disclosure, dispute, or security freeze requests. If creating a report that will be shared with GSEs such as Fannie or Freddie, a full Social Security Number must be provided via the `id_numbers` field.|
|end_customer|string|false|none|A unique ID representing a CRA reseller's end customer. Maximum of 128 characters.|
|consumer_report_user_identity|[ConsumerReportUserIdentity](#schemaconsumerreportuseridentity)|false|none|This field is only used by integrations created before December 10, 2025. All other integrations must use the `identity` object instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).<br>To create a Plaid Check Consumer Report for a user when using a `user_token`, this field must be present. If this field is not provided during user token creation, you can add it to the user later by calling `/user/update`. Once the field has been added to the user, you will be able to call `/link/token/create` with a non-empty `consumer_report_permissible_purpose` (which will automatically create a Plaid Check Consumer Report), or call `/cra/check_report/create` for that user.|
|with_upgraded_user|boolean|false|none|If your integration with the User API predates December 10, 2025, set this field to `true` to opt into the [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis/). When enabled, you can use the `identity` field instead of `consumer_report_user_identity`.|

UserProductsTerminateRequest defines the request schema for `/user/products/terminate`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|

Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|reason_code|[ProductsTerminateReasonCode](#schemaproductsterminatereasoncode)|true|none|The reason for terminating products.<br><br>`FRAUD_FIRST_PARTY`: The end user who owns the connected bank account committed fraud using their real identity<br><br>`FRAUD_FALSE_IDENTITY`: The connection was created using a false or stolen identity<br><br>`FRAUD_ABUSE`: The end user is abusing the client's service or platform (for example, automation or excessive retries) through their connected account<br><br>`FRAUD_OTHER`: Fraud-related, but not covered by the specific fraud categories above; `reason_note` should clarify<br><br>`FRAUD_TRANSACTION`: Fraud occurred at the transaction level, such as an unauthorized transaction, card testing, chargeback, ACH return, or dispute<br><br>`CONSUMER_LOAN_PAID_OFF`: The end user paid off their loan and no longer needs the product<br><br>`CONSUMER_ACCOUNT_CLOSED`: The end user closed their account with the client and no longer needs the product<br><br>`CONSUMER_CHARGE_OFF`: The end user's account has been charged off<br><br>`CONSUMER_PAYMENT_METHOD_SWITCHED`: The end user switched to a different payment method and no longer needs the product<br><br>`USER_OFFBOARDING`: The user is offboarding from the client's service or platform<br><br>`DUPLICATE_ITEM`: This Item is a duplicate of another active Item for the same user<br><br>`BILLING_TERMINATION`: The client's billing or subscription relationship with the end user has ended<br><br>`OTHER`: None of the above; `reason_note` should clarify<br>|
|reason_note|string \| null|false|none|Additional context or details about the reason for terminating user-based products. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be included in the `reason_note`.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|reason_code|FRAUD_FIRST_PARTY|
|reason_code|FRAUD_FALSE_IDENTITY|
|reason_code|FRAUD_ABUSE|
|reason_code|FRAUD_OTHER|
|reason_code|FRAUD_TRANSACTION|
|reason_code|CONSUMER_LOAN_PAID_OFF|
|reason_code|CONSUMER_ACCOUNT_CLOSED|
|reason_code|CONSUMER_CHARGE_OFF|
|reason_code|CONSUMER_PAYMENT_METHOD_SWITCHED|
|reason_code|USER_OFFBOARDING|
|reason_code|DUPLICATE_ITEM|
|reason_code|BILLING_TERMINATION|
|reason_code|OTHER|

<h2 id="tocS_ConsumerReportUserIdentity">ConsumerReportUserIdentity</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaconsumerreportuseridentity"></a>
<a id="schema_ConsumerReportUserIdentity"></a>
<a id="tocSconsumerreportuseridentity"></a>
<a id="tocsconsumerreportuseridentity"></a>

```json
{
  "first_name": "string",
  "last_name": "string",
  "phone_numbers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "emails": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ssn_full": "string",
  "ssn_last_4": "stri",
  "date_of_birth": "1970-01-01",
  "primary_address": {
    "city": "string",
    "region": "string",
    "street": "string",
    "postal_code": "string",
    "country": "string"
  }
}
```

This field is only used by integrations created before December 10, 2025. All other integrations must use the `identity` object instead. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).
To create a Plaid Check Consumer Report for a user when using a `user_token`, this field must be present. If this field is not provided during user token creation, you can add it to the user later by calling `/user/update`. Once the field has been added to the user, you will be able to call `/link/token/create` with a non-empty `consumer_report_permissible_purpose` (which will automatically create a Plaid Check Consumer Report), or call `/cra/check_report/create` for that user.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|first_name|string|true|none|The user's first name|
|last_name|string|true|none|The user's last name|
|phone_numbers|[string]|true|none|The user's phone number, in E.164 format: +{countrycode}{number}. For example: "+14157452130". Phone numbers provided in other formats will be parsed on a best-effort basis. Phone number input is validated against valid number ranges; number strings that do not match a real-world phone numbering scheme may cause the request to fail, even in the Sandbox test environment.|
|emails|[string]|true|none|The user's emails|
|ssn_full|string \| null|false|none|The user's full Social Security number. This field should only be provided by lenders intending to share the resulting consumer report with a Government-Sponsored Enterprise (GSE), such as Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac.<br><br>Format: "ddd-dd-dddd"|
|ssn_last_4|string \| null|false|none|The last 4 digits of the user's Social Security number.|
|date_of_birth|string(date) \| null|true|none|To be provided in the format "yyyy-mm-dd".<br>This field is required for all Plaid Check customers.|
|primary_address|[AddressData](#schemaaddressdata)|true|none|Data about the components comprising an address.|

```json
{
  "name": {
    "given_name": "string",
    "family_name": "string"
  },
  "date_of_birth": "1970-01-01",
  "emails": [
    {
      "data": "string",
      "primary": true
    }
  ],

      "primary": true
    }
  ],
  "addresses": [
    {
      "street_1": "string",
      "street_2": "string",
      "city": "string",
      "region": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "primary": true
    }
  ],
  "id_numbers": [
    {
      "value": "123456789",
      "type": "us_ssn"
    }
  ]
}
```

The identity fields associated with a user. For a user to be eligible for a Plaid Check Consumer Report, all fields are required except `id_numbers`. Providing a partial SSN is strongly recommended, and improves the accuracy of matching user records during compliance processes such as file disclosure, dispute, or security freeze requests. If creating a report that will be shared with GSEs such as Fannie or Freddie, a full Social Security Number must be provided via the `id_numbers` field.

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|

|emails|[[ClientUserIdentityEmail](#schemaclientuseridentityemail)]|false|none|The user's emails.|
|phone_numbers|[[ClientUserIdentityPhoneNumber](#schemaclientuseridentityphonenumber)]|false|none|The user's phone numbers, in E.164 format: +{countrycode}{number}. For example: "+14157452130". Phone numbers provided in other formats will be parsed on a best-effort basis. Phone number input is validated against valid number ranges; number strings that do not match a real-world phone numbering scheme may cause the request to fail, even in the Sandbox test environment.|
|addresses|[[ClientUserIdentityAddress](#schemaclientuseridentityaddress)]|false|none|The user's addresses.|
|id_numbers|[[UserIDNumber](#schemauseridnumber)]|false|none|The user's ID numbers.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|payment_id|string|true|none|The ID of the payment. Like all Plaid identifiers, the `payment_id` is case sensitive.|
|amount|[PaymentAmount](#schemapaymentamount)|true|none|The amount and currency of a payment|
|status|[PaymentInitiationPaymentStatus](#schemapaymentinitiationpaymentstatus)|true|none|The status of the payment.<br><br>Core lifecycle statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED`**: Transitional. The payment is awaiting user input to continue processing. It may re-enter this state if additional input is required.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_AUTHORISING`:** Transitional. The payment is being authorised by the financial institution. It will automatically move on once authorisation completes.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED`:** The payment has been authorised and accepted by the financial institution. In many EU markets, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not supported, and a payment will remain in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` until the funds settle, making this a terminal success state in those cases. A payment in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` should be treated as a successfully submitted payment; do not gate downstream processing on reaching `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`. For a full explanation of payment statuses and how to handle each, see the [Payment Status guide](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/payment-status/).<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`: Terminal.** The funds have left the payer's account and the payment is en route to settlement. Note that this status does not confirm that funds have arrived in the recipient's account; do not use it as proof of fund receipt. Support is more common in the UK than in the EU; where unsupported, a successful payment remains in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` before settling. When using Plaid Virtual Accounts, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not terminal -- the payment will continue to `PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED` once funds are available.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED`: Terminal.** The funds are available in the recipient's account. Only available to customers using [Plaid Virtual Accounts](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/virtual-accounts/).<br><br>Failure statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: Terminal.** The payment failed due to insufficient funds. No further retries will succeed until the payer's balance is replenished.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_FAILED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment could not be initiated due to a system error or outage. Retry once the root cause is resolved.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_BLOCKED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment was blocked by Plaid (e.g., flagged as risky). Resolve any compliance or risk issues and retry.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_REJECTED`: Terminal.** The payment was rejected by the financial institution. No automatic retry is possible.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_CANCELLED`: Terminal.** The end user cancelled the payment during authorisation.<br><br>Standing-order statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_ESTABLISHED`: Terminal.** A recurring/standing order has been successfully created.<br><br>Deprecated (to be removed in a future release):<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_UNKNOWN`: The payment status is unknown.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_PROCESSING`: The payment is currently being processed.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_COMPLETED`: Indicates that the standing order has been successfully established.|
|recipient_id|string|true|none|The ID of the recipient|
|reference|string|true|none|A reference for the payment.|
|adjusted_reference|string \| null|false|none|The value of the reference sent to the bank after adjustment to pass bank validation rules.|
|last_status_update|string(date-time)|true|none|The date and time of the last time the `status` was updated, in ISO 8601 format|
|schedule|[ExternalPaymentScheduleGet](#schemaexternalpaymentscheduleget)|false|none|The schedule that the payment will be executed on. If a schedule is provided, the payment is automatically set up as a standing order. If no schedule is specified, the payment will be executed only once.|

|refund_ids|[string]|false|none|Refund IDs associated with the payment.|
|amount_refunded|[PaymentAmountRefunded](#schemapaymentamountrefunded)|false|none|The amount and currency of a payment|

In responses, if the scheme is not explicitly specified in the request, this field is omitted. Using unsupported values will result in a failed payment.<br><br>`LOCAL_DEFAULT`: The default payment scheme for the selected market and currency will be used.<br><br>`LOCAL_INSTANT`: The instant payment scheme for the selected market and currency will be used (if applicable). Fees may be applied by the institution.<br><br>`SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER`: The standard payment to a beneficiary within the SEPA area.<br><br>`SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER_INSTANT`: Instant payment within the SEPA area. May involve additional fees and may not be available at some banks.|
|adjusted_scheme|[PaymentScheme](#schemapaymentscheme)|false|none|Payment scheme. If not specified - the default in the region will be used (e.g. `SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER` for EU). In responses, if the scheme is not explicitly specified in the request, this field is omitted. Using unsupported values will result in a failed payment.<br><br>`LOCAL_DEFAULT`: The default payment scheme for the selected market and currency will be used.<br><br>`LOCAL_INSTANT`: The instant payment scheme for the selected market and currency will be used (if applicable). Fees may be applied by the institution.<br><br>`SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER`: The standard payment to a beneficiary within the SEPA area.<br><br>`SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER_INSTANT`: Instant payment within the SEPA area. May involve additional fees and may not be available at some banks.|
|consent_id|string \| null|false|none|The payment consent ID that this payment was initiated with. Is present only when payment was initiated using the payment consent.|

<h2 id="tocS_PaymentInitiationPaymentStatus">PaymentInitiationPaymentStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapaymentinitiationpaymentstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_PaymentInitiationPaymentStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSpaymentinitiationpaymentstatus"></a>
<a id="tocspaymentinitiationpaymentstatus"></a>

```json
"PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED"
```

The status of the payment.

Core lifecycle statuses:

**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED`**: Transitional. The payment is awaiting user input to continue processing. It may re-enter this state if additional input is required.

**`PAYMENT_STATUS_AUTHORISING`:** Transitional. The payment is being authorised by the financial institution. It will automatically move on once authorisation completes.

**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED`:** The payment has been authorised and accepted by the financial institution. In many EU markets, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not supported, and a payment will remain in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` until the funds settle, making this a terminal success state in those cases. A payment in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` should be treated as a successfully submitted payment; do not gate downstream processing on reaching `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`. For a full explanation of payment statuses and how to handle each, see the [Payment Status guide](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/payment-status/).

**`PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`: Terminal.** The funds have left the payer's account and the payment is en route to settlement. Note that this status does not confirm that funds have arrived in the recipient's account; do not use it as proof of fund receipt. Support is more common in the UK than in the EU; where unsupported, a successful payment remains in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` before settling. When using Plaid Virtual Accounts, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not terminal -- the payment will continue to `PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED` once funds are available.

**`PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED`: Terminal.** The funds are available in the recipient's account. Only available to customers using [Plaid Virtual Accounts](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/virtual-accounts/).

Failure statuses:

**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: Terminal.** The payment failed due to insufficient funds. No further retries will succeed until the payer's balance is replenished.

**`PAYMENT_STATUS_FAILED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment could not be initiated due to a system error or outage. Retry once the root cause is resolved.

**`PAYMENT_STATUS_BLOCKED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment was blocked by Plaid (e.g., flagged as risky). Resolve any compliance or risk issues and retry.

**`PAYMENT_STATUS_REJECTED`: Terminal.** The payment was rejected by the financial institution. No automatic retry is possible.

**`PAYMENT_STATUS_CANCELLED`: Terminal.** The end user cancelled the payment during authorisation.

Standing-order statuses:

**`PAYMENT_STATUS_ESTABLISHED`: Terminal.** A recurring/standing order has been successfully created.

Deprecated (to be removed in a future release):

`PAYMENT_STATUS_UNKNOWN`: The payment status is unknown.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_PROCESSING`: The payment is currently being processed.

`PAYMENT_STATUS_COMPLETED`: Indicates that the standing order has been successfully established.

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payment_id|string|true|none|The ID of the payment. Like all Plaid identifiers, the `payment_id` is case sensitive.|

|status|[PaymentInitiationPaymentStatus](#schemapaymentinitiationpaymentstatus)|true|none|The status of the payment.<br><br>Core lifecycle statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED`**: Transitional. The payment is awaiting user input to continue processing. It may re-enter this state if additional input is required.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_AUTHORISING`:** Transitional. The payment is being authorised by the financial institution. It will automatically move on once authorisation completes.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED`:** The payment has been authorised and accepted by the financial institution. In many EU markets, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not supported, and a payment will remain in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` until the funds settle, making this a terminal success state in those cases. A payment in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` should be treated as a successfully submitted payment; do not gate downstream processing on reaching `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`. For a full explanation of payment statuses and how to handle each, see the [Payment Status guide](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/payment-status/).<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`: Terminal.** The funds have left the payer's account and the payment is en route to settlement. Note that this status does not confirm that funds have arrived in the recipient's account; do not use it as proof of fund receipt. Support is more common in the UK than in the EU; where unsupported, a successful payment remains in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` before settling. When using Plaid Virtual Accounts, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not terminal -- the payment will continue to `PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED` once funds are available.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED`: Terminal.** The funds are available in the recipient's account. Only available to customers using [Plaid Virtual Accounts](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/virtual-accounts/).<br><br>Failure statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: Terminal.** The payment failed due to insufficient funds. No further retries will succeed until the payer's balance is replenished.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_FAILED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment could not be initiated due to a system error or outage. Retry once the root cause is resolved.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_BLOCKED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment was blocked by Plaid (e.g., flagged as risky). Resolve any compliance or risk issues and retry.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_REJECTED`: Terminal.** The payment was rejected by the financial institution. No automatic retry is possible.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_CANCELLED`: Terminal.** The end user cancelled the payment during authorisation.<br><br>Standing-order statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_ESTABLISHED`: Terminal.** A recurring/standing order has been successfully created.<br><br>Deprecated (to be removed in a future release):<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_UNKNOWN`: The payment status is unknown.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_PROCESSING`: The payment is currently being processed.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_COMPLETED`: Indicates that the standing order has been successfully established.|
|recipient_id|string|true|none|The ID of the recipient|
|reference|string|true|none|A reference for the payment.|
|adjusted_reference|string \| null|false|none|The value of the reference sent to the bank after adjustment to pass bank validation rules.|
|last_status_update|string(date-time)|true|none|The date and time of the last time the `status` was updated, in ISO 8601 format|
|schedule|[ExternalPaymentScheduleGet](#schemaexternalpaymentscheduleget)|false|none|The schedule that the payment will be executed on. If a schedule is provided, the payment is automatically set up as a standing order. If no schedule is specified, the payment will be executed only once.|
|refund_details|[ExternalPaymentRefundDetails](#schemaexternalpaymentrefunddetails)|false|none|Details about external payment refund|
|bacs|[SenderBACSNullable](#schemasenderbacsnullable)|true|none|An object containing a Bacs account number and sort code. If an IBAN is not provided or if this recipient needs to accept domestic GBP-denominated payments, Bacs data is required.|
|iban|string \| null|true|none|The International Bank Account Number (IBAN) for the sender, if specified in the `/payment_initiation/payment/create` call.|
|refund_ids|[string]|false|none|Refund IDs associated with the payment.|
|amount_refunded|[PaymentAmountRefunded](#schemapaymentamountrefunded)|false|none|The amount and currency of a payment|
|wallet_id|string \| null|false|none|The EMI (E-Money Institution) wallet that this payment is associated with, if any. This wallet is used as an intermediary account to enable Plaid to reconcile the settlement of funds for Payment Initiation requests.|
|scheme|[PaymentScheme](#schemapaymentscheme)|false|none|Payment scheme. If not specified - the default in the region will be used (e.g. `SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER` for EU). In responses, if the scheme is not explicitly specified in the request, this field is omitted. Using unsupported values will result in a failed payment.<br><br>`LOCAL_DEFAULT`: The default payment scheme for the selected market and currency will be used.<br><br>`LOCAL_INSTANT`: The instant payment scheme for the selected market and currency will be used (if applicable). Fees may be applied by the institution.<br><br>`SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER`: The standard payment to a beneficiary within the SEPA area.<br><br>`SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER_INSTANT`: Instant payment within the SEPA area. May involve additional fees and may not be available at some banks.|
|adjusted_scheme|[PaymentScheme](#schemapaymentscheme)|false|none|Payment scheme. If not specified - the default in the region will be used (e.g. `SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER` for EU). In responses, if the scheme is not explicitly specified in the request, this field is omitted. Using unsupported values will result in a failed payment.<br><br>`LOCAL_DEFAULT`: The default payment scheme for the selected market and currency will be used.<br><br>`LOCAL_INSTANT`: The instant payment scheme for the selected market and currency will be used (if applicable). Fees may be applied by the institution.<br><br>`SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER`: The standard payment to a beneficiary within the SEPA area.<br><br>`SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER_INSTANT`: Instant payment within the SEPA area. May involve additional fees and may not be available at some banks.|
|consent_id|string \| null|false|none|The payment consent ID that this payment was initiated with. Is present only when payment was initiated using the payment consent.|
|transaction_id|string \| null|false|none|The transaction ID that this payment is associated with, if any. This is present only when a payment was initiated using virtual accounts.|
|end_to_end_id|string \| null|false|none|A unique identifier assigned by Plaid to each payment for tracking and reconciliation purposes.<br><br>Note: Not all banks handle `end_to_end_id` consistently. To ensure accurate matching, clients should convert both the incoming `end_to_end_id` and the one provided by Plaid to the same case (either lower or upper) before comparison. For virtual account payments, Plaid manages this field automatically.|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|false|none|Errors are identified by `error_code` and categorized by `error_type`. Use these in preference to HTTP status codes to identify and handle specific errors. HTTP status codes are set and provide the broadest categorization of errors: 4xx codes are for developer- or user-related errors, and 5xx codes are for Plaid-related errors, and the status will be 2xx in non-error cases. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|consent_id|string|true|none|The consent ID.|
|status|[PaymentInitiationConsentStatus](#schemapaymentinitiationconsentstatus)|true|none|The status of the payment consent.<br><br>`UNAUTHORISED`: Consent created, but requires user authorisation.<br><br>`REJECTED`: Consent authorisation was rejected by the bank.<br><br>`AUTHORISED`: Consent is active and ready to be used.<br><br>`REVOKED`: Consent has been revoked and can no longer be used.<br><br>`EXPIRED`: Consent is no longer valid.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Consent creation timestamp, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|recipient_id|string|true|none|The ID of the recipient the payment consent is for.|
|reference|string|true|none|A reference for the payment consent.|
|constraints|[PaymentInitiationConsentConstraints](#schemapaymentinitiationconsentconstraints)|true|none|Limitations that will be applied to payments initiated using the payment consent.|
|scopes|[[PaymentInitiationConsentScope](#schemapaymentinitiationconsentscope)]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use the 'type' field instead.|
|type|[PaymentInitiationConsentType](#schemapaymentinitiationconsenttype)|false|none|Payment consent type. Defines possible use case for payments made with the given consent.<br><br>`SWEEPING`: Allows moving money between accounts owned by the same user.<br><br>`COMMERCIAL`: Allows initiating payments from the user's account to third parties.|
|payer_details|[ExternalPaymentRefundDetails](#schemaexternalpaymentrefunddetails)|false|none|Details about external payment refund|

|status|AUTHORISED|
|status|REVOKED|
|status|REJECTED|
|status|EXPIRED|
|scopes|ME_TO_ME|
|scopes|EXTERNAL|
|type|SWEEPING|
|type|COMMERCIAL|

```json
"UNAUTHORISED"
```

The status of the payment consent.

`UNAUTHORISED`: Consent created, but requires user authorisation.

`REJECTED`: Consent authorisation was rejected by the bank.

`AUTHORISED`: Consent is active and ready to be used.

`REVOKED`: Consent has been revoked and can no longer be used.

`EXPIRED`: Consent is no longer valid.

PaymentInitiationConsentPaymentExecuteRequest defines the request schema for `/payment_initiation/consent/payment/execute`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|consent_id|string|true|none|The consent ID.|
|amount|[PaymentAmount](#schemapaymentamount)|true|none|The amount and currency of a payment|
|idempotency_key|[ConsentPaymentIdempotencyKey](#schemaconsentpaymentidempotencykey)|true|none|A random key provided by the client, per unique consent payment. Maximum of 128 characters.<br><br>The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. If a request to execute a consent payment fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single payment is created. If the request was successfully processed, it will prevent any payment that uses the same idempotency key, and was received within 48 hours of the first request, from being processed.|
|reference|string \| null|false|none|A reference for the payment. This must be a string of at most 18 characters containing only letters, numbers, and spaces (since not all institutions support them).<br>If not provided, Plaid will automatically fall back to the reference from consent. In order to track settlement via Payment Confirmation, each payment must have a unique reference. If the reference provided through the API is not unique, Plaid will adjust it.<br>Some institutions may limit the reference to less than 18 characters. If necessary, Plaid will adjust the reference by truncating it to fit the institution's requirements.<br>Both the originally provided and automatically adjusted references (if any) can be found in the `reference` and `adjusted_reference` fields, respectively.|
|scope|object|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|processing_mode|[PaymentInitiationConsentProcessingMode](#schemapaymentinitiationconsentprocessingmode)|false|none|Decides the mode under which the payment processing should be performed, using `IMMEDIATE` as default.<br><br>`IMMEDIATE`: Will immediately execute the payment, waiting for a response from the ASPSP before returning the result of the payment initiation. This is ideal for user-present flows.<br><br> `ASYNC`: Will accept a payment execution request and schedule it for processing, immediately returning the new `payment_id`. Listen for webhooks to obtain real-time updates on the payment status. This is ideal for non user-present flows.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|processing_mode|ASYNC|
|processing_mode|IMMEDIATE|

PaymentInitiationConsentPaymentExecuteResponse defines the response schema for `/payment_initiation/consent/payment/execute`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payment_id|string|true|none|A unique ID identifying the payment|
|status|[PaymentInitiationPaymentStatus](#schemapaymentinitiationpaymentstatus)|true|none|The status of the payment.<br><br>Core lifecycle statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED`**: Transitional. The payment is awaiting user input to continue processing. It may re-enter this state if additional input is required.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_AUTHORISING`:** Transitional. The payment is being authorised by the financial institution. It will automatically move on once authorisation completes.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED`:** The payment has been authorised and accepted by the financial institution. In many EU markets, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not supported, and a payment will remain in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` until the funds settle, making this a terminal success state in those cases. A payment in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` should be treated as a successfully submitted payment; do not gate downstream processing on reaching `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`. For a full explanation of payment statuses and how to handle each, see the [Payment Status guide](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/payment-status/).<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`: Terminal.** The funds have left the payer's account and the payment is en route to settlement. Note that this status does not confirm that funds have arrived in the recipient's account; do not use it as proof of fund receipt. Support is more common in the UK than in the EU; where unsupported, a successful payment remains in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` before settling. When using Plaid Virtual Accounts, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not terminal -- the payment will continue to `PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED` once funds are available.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED`: Terminal.** The funds are available in the recipient's account. Only available to customers using [Plaid Virtual Accounts](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/virtual-accounts/).<br><br>Failure statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: Terminal.** The payment failed due to insufficient funds. No further retries will succeed until the payer's balance is replenished.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_FAILED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment could not be initiated due to a system error or outage. Retry once the root cause is resolved.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_BLOCKED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment was blocked by Plaid (e.g., flagged as risky). Resolve any compliance or risk issues and retry.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_REJECTED`: Terminal.** The payment was rejected by the financial institution. No automatic retry is possible.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_CANCELLED`: Terminal.** The end user cancelled the payment during authorisation.<br><br>Standing-order statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_ESTABLISHED`: Terminal.** A recurring/standing order has been successfully created.<br><br>Deprecated (to be removed in a future release):<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_UNKNOWN`: The payment status is unknown.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_PROCESSING`: The payment is currently being processed.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_COMPLETED`: Indicates that the standing order has been successfully established.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|false|none|Errors are identified by `error_code` and categorized by `error_type`. Use these in preference to HTTP status codes to identify and handle specific errors. HTTP status codes are set and provide the broadest categorization of errors: 4xx codes are for developer- or user-related errors, and 5xx codes are for Plaid-related errors, and the status will be 2xx in non-error cases. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_PROCESSING|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_COMPLETED|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_FAILED|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_BLOCKED|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_UNKNOWN|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_AUTHORISING|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_CANCELLED|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_ESTABLISHED|
|status|PAYMENT_STATUS_REJECTED|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|

|access_token|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|none|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|
|options|[InvestmentsAuthGetRequestOptions](#schemainvestmentsauthgetrequestoptions)|false|none|An optional object to filter `/investments/auth/get` results.|

InvestmentsAuthGetResponse defines the response schema for `/investments/auth/get`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accounts|[[InvestmentAccount](#schemainvestmentaccount)]|true|none|The accounts for which data is being retrieved|
|holdings|[[Holding](#schemaholding)]|true|none|The holdings belonging to investment accounts associated with the Item. Details of the securities in the holdings are provided in the `securities` field. |
|securities|[[Security](#schemasecurity)]|true|none|Objects describing the securities held in the accounts associated with the Item. |
|owners|[[InvestmentsAuthOwner](#schemainvestmentsauthowner)]|true|none|Information about the account owners for the accounts associated with the Item. |
|numbers|[InvestmentsAuthGetNumbers](#schemainvestmentsauthgetnumbers)|true|none|Identifying information for transferring holdings to an investment account.|
|data_sources|[InvestmentsAuthDataSources](#schemainvestmentsauthdatasources)|true|none|Object with metadata pertaining to the source of data for the account numbers, owners, and holdings that are returned.|
|account_details_401k|[[InvestmentsAuthAccountDetails401k](#schemainvestmentsauthaccountdetails401k)]|false|none|Additional information for accounts of 401k subtype.|
|item|[Item](#schemaitem)|true|none|Metadata about the Item.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

ProcessorInvestmentsTransactionsGetRequest defines the request schema for `/processor/investments/transactions/get`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|options|[InvestmentsTransactionsGetRequestOptions](#schemainvestmentstransactionsgetrequestoptions)|false|none|An optional object to filter `/investments/transactions/get` results. If provided, must be non-`null`.|
|processor_token|[ProcessorToken](#schemaprocessortoken)|true|none|The processor token obtained from the Plaid integration partner. Processor tokens are in the format: `processor-<environment>-<identifier>`|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|start_date|string(date)|true|none|The earliest date for which data should be returned. Dates should be formatted as YYYY-MM-DD. Plaid returns all investment transaction history stored for the Item (up to 2 years prior to the initial linking of the Item).|
|end_date|string(date)|true|none|The latest date for which data should be returned. Dates should be formatted as YYYY-MM-DD.|

ProcessorInvestmentsTransactionsGetResponse defines the response schema for `/processor/investments/transactions/get`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|[InvestmentAccount](#schemainvestmentaccount)|true|none|A single account at a financial institution, with additional investment-specific balance information.|
|investment_transactions|[[InvestmentTransaction](#schemainvestmenttransaction)]|true|none|An array containing investment transactions from the account. Investments transactions are returned in reverse chronological order, with the most recent at the beginning of the array. The maximum number of transactions returned is determined by the `count` parameter.|
|securities|[[Security](#schemasecurity)]|true|none|All securities for which there is a corresponding transaction being fetched.|
|total_investment_transactions|integer|true|none|The total number of transactions available within the date range specified. If `total_investment_transactions` is larger than the size of the `transactions` array, more transactions are available and can be fetched via manipulating the `offset` parameter.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|
|is_investments_fallback_item|boolean|false|none|When true, this field indicates that the Item's portfolio was manually created with the Investments Fallback flow.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|access_token|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|none|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|
|start_date|string(date)|true|none|The earliest date for which to fetch transaction history. Dates should be formatted as YYYY-MM-DD. Plaid returns all investment transaction history stored for the Item (up to 2 years prior to the initial linking of the Item).|

<h2 id="tocS_InvestmentsTransactionsGetRequestOptions">InvestmentsTransactionsGetRequestOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainvestmentstransactionsgetrequestoptions"></a>
<a id="schema_InvestmentsTransactionsGetRequestOptions"></a>
<a id="tocSinvestmentstransactionsgetrequestoptions"></a>
<a id="tocsinvestmentstransactionsgetrequestoptions"></a>

```json
{
  "account_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "count": 100,
  "offset": 0,
  "async_update": false
}
```

An optional object to filter `/investments/transactions/get` results. If provided, must be non-`null`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_ids|[string]|false|none|An array of `account_ids` to retrieve for the Item.|
|count|integer|false|none|The number of transactions to fetch.<br>|
|offset|integer|false|none|The number of transactions to skip when fetching transaction history|
|async_update|boolean|false|none|If the Item was not initialized with the investments product via the `products`, `required_if_supported_products`, or `optional_products` array when calling `/link/token/create`, and `async_update` is set to true, the initial Investments extraction will happen asynchronously. Plaid will subsequently fire a `HISTORICAL_UPDATE` webhook when the extraction completes. When `false`, Plaid will wait to return a response until extraction completion and no `HISTORICAL_UPDATE` webhook will fire. Note that while the extraction is happening asynchronously, calls to `/investments/transactions/get` and `/investments/refresh` will return `PRODUCT_NOT_READY` errors until the extraction completes.|

|is_investments_fallback_item|boolean|false|none|When true, this field indicates that the Item's portfolio was manually created with the Investments Fallback flow.|
