LinkTokenCreateRequest defines the request schema for `/link/token/create`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|client_name|string|true|none|The name of your application, as it should be displayed in Link. Maximum length of 30 characters. If a value longer than 30 characters is provided, Link will display "This Application" instead.|
|language|string|true|none|The language that Link should be displayed in. When initializing with Identity Verification, this field is not used; for more details, see [Identity Verification supported languages](https://plaid.com/docs/identity-verification/#supported-languages).<br><br>Supported languages are:<br>- Danish (`'da'`)<br>- Dutch (`'nl'`)<br>- English (`'en'`)<br>- Estonian (`'et'`)<br>- French (`'fr'`)<br>- German (`'de'`)<br>- Haitian Creole (`'ht'`)<br>- Hindi (`'hi'`)<br>- Italian (`'it'`)<br>- Latvian (`'lv'`)<br>- Lithuanian (`'lt'`)<br>- Norwegian Bokmål (`'nb'`)<br>- Polish (`'pl'`)<br>- Portuguese (`'pt'`)<br>- Romanian (`'ro'`)<br>- Spanish (`'es'`)<br>- Swedish (`'sv'`)<br>- Vietnamese (`'vi'`)<br><br>When using a Link customization, the language configured here must match the setting in the customization, or the customization will not be applied.|
|country_codes|[[CountryCode](#schemacountrycode)]|true|none|Specify an array of Plaid-supported country codes using the ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 country code standard. Institutions from all listed countries will be shown. For a complete mapping of supported products by country, see [What Plaid products are supported in each country and region?](https://support.plaid.com/hc/en-us/articles/27895826947735-What-Plaid-products-are-supported-in-each-country-and-region). For access to additional countries beyond what you have been approved for, [contact sales](https://plaid.com/contact/), your account manager, or support.<br><br>If using Identity Verification, `country_codes` should be set to the country where your company is based, not the country where your user is located. For all other products, `country_codes` represents the location of your user's financial institution.<br><br>If Link is launched with multiple country codes, only products that you are enabled for in all countries will be used by Link. While all countries are enabled by default in Sandbox, in Production only the countries you have requested access for are shown. To request access to additional countries, [file a product access Support ticket](https://dashboard.plaid.com/support/new/product-and-development/product-troubleshooting/request-product-access) via the Plaid dashboard.<br><br>If using a Link customization, make sure the country codes in the customization match those specified in `country_codes`, or the customization may not be applied.<br><br>If using the Auth features Instant Match, Instant Micro-deposits, Same-Day Micro-deposits, or Automated Micro-deposits, `country_codes` must be set to `['US']`. If using Database Auth, `country_codes` must be set to `['US']` or `['CA']`.|
|user|[LinkTokenCreateRequestUser](#schemalinktokencreaterequestuser)|false|none|An object specifying information about the end user who will be linking their account. **Required** if `user_id` isn't included.|
|user_id|string|false|none|A `user_id` generated using `/user/create`. Required for integrations that began using Plaid Protect, Multi-Item Link, or Plaid Check Consumer Report after December 10, 2025. Required for new integrations that use Payment Initiation, Variable Recurring Payments, or Virtual Accounts. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis). One of either the `user_id` or the `user` field is required.|
|products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|none|List of Plaid product(s) that the linked Item must support. If launching Link in update mode, should be omitted (unless you are using update mode to add a credit product, such as Assets, Statements, Income, or Plaid Check Consumer Report, to an existing Item); at least one `product` is required otherwise.<br><br>To maximize the number of institutions and accounts available, initialize Link with the minimal product set required for your use case, as the products specified will limit which institutions and account types will be available to your users in Link. Only institutions that support *all* requested products can be selected; if a user attempts to select an institution that does not support a listed product, a "Connectivity not supported" error message will appear in Link. For each specified product, the Item connected by the user must contain at least one compatible account. For details on compatible product / account type combinations, see [the account type/product support matrix](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#account-type--product-support-matrix).<br><br>To add products without limiting the institution list or account types, use the [`optional_products`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/#link-token-create-request-optional-products) or  [`required_if_supported_products`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/#link-token-create-request-required-if-supported-products) fields. Products can also be added to an Item by calling the product endpoint after obtaining an access token; this may require the product to be listed in the [`additional_consented_products`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/#link-token-create-request-additional-consented-products) array. For details, see [Choosing when to initialize products](https://plaid.com/docs/link/initializing-products/).<br><br>`balance` is *not* a valid value, the Balance product does not require explicit initialization and will automatically be initialized when any other product is initialized.<br><br>If launching Link with CRA products, `cra_base_report` is required and must be included in the `products` array.<br><br>Note that, unless you have opted to disable Instant Match support, institutions that support Instant Match will also be shown in Link if `auth` is specified as a product, even though these institutions do not contain `auth` in their product array.<br><br>In Production, you will be billed for each product that you specify when initializing Link. Note that a product cannot be removed from an Item once the Item has been initialized with that product. To stop billing on an Item for subscription-based products, such as Liabilities, Investments, and Transactions, remove the Item via `/item/remove`.|
|required_if_supported_products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|none|List of Plaid product(s) you wish to use only if the institution and account(s) selected by the user support the product. Institutions that do not support these products will still be shown in Link. The products will only be extracted and billed if the user selects an institution and account type that supports them.<br><br>There should be no overlap between this array and the `products`, `optional_products`, or `additional_consented_products` arrays. The `products` array must have at least one product.<br><br>For more details on using this feature, see [Required if Supported Products](https://plaid.com/docs/link/initializing-products/#required-if-supported-products).|
|optional_products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|none|List of Plaid product(s) that will enhance the consumer's use case, but that your app can function without. Plaid will attempt to fetch data for these products on a best-effort basis, and failure to support these products will not affect Item creation.<br><br>There should be no overlap between this array and the `products`, `required_if_supported_products`, or `additional_consented_products` arrays. The `products` array must have at least one product.<br><br>For more details on using this feature, see [Optional Products](https://plaid.com/docs/link/initializing-products/#optional-products).|
|additional_consented_products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|none|List of additional Plaid product(s) you wish to collect consent for to support your use case. These products will not be billed until you start using them by calling the relevant endpoints.<br><br>`balance` is *not* a valid value, the Balance product does not require explicit initialization and will automatically have consent collected.<br><br>Institutions that do not support these products will still be shown in Link.<br><br>There should be no overlap between this array and the `products`, `required_if_supported_products`, or `optional_products` arrays.<br><br>If you include `signal` in `additional_consented_products`, you will need to call [`/signal/prepare`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/signal/#signalprepare) before calling `/signal/evaluate` for the first time on an Item in order to get the most accurate results. For more details, see [`/signal/prepare`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/signal/#signalprepare).|
|webhook|string(url)|false|none|The destination URL to which any webhooks should be sent. Note that webhooks for Payment Initiation (e-wallet transactions only), Transfer, Bank Transfer (including Auth micro-deposit notification webhooks), Monitor, and Identity Verification are configured via the Dashboard instead. In update mode, this field will not have an effect; to update the webhook receiver endpoint for an existing Item, use `/item/webhook/update` instead.|
|access_token|string \| null|false|none|The `access_token` associated with the Item to update or reference, used when updating, modifying, or accessing an existing `access_token`. Used when launching Link in update mode, when completing the Same-Day Micro-deposit (manual) flow, or (optionally) when initializing Link for a returning user as part of the Transfer UI flow.|
|access_tokens|[string]|false|none|A list of access tokens associated with the items to update in Link update mode for the Assets product. Using this instead of the `access_token` field allows the updating of multiple items at once. This feature is in closed beta, please contact your account manager for more info.|
|link_customization_name|string|false|none|The name of the Link customization from the Plaid Dashboard to be applied to Link. If not specified, the `default` customization will be used. When using a Link customization, the language in the customization must match the language selected via the `language` parameter, and the countries in the customization should match the country codes selected via `country_codes`.|
|appearance_mode|[LinkTokenCreateRequestAppearanceMode](#schemalinktokencreaterequestappearancemode)|false|none|Enum representing the desired appearance mode for Link, used to force light or dark modes or set Link to change depending on user system settings. Currently in closed beta.|
|redirect_uri|[LinkTokenCreateRequestRedirectUri](#schemalinktokencreaterequestredirecturi)|false|none|A URI indicating the destination where a user should be forwarded after completing the Link flow; used to support OAuth authentication flows when launching Link in the browser or another app. The `redirect_uri` should not contain any query parameters. When used in Production, must be an https URI. Note that any redirect URI must also be added to the Allowed redirect URIs list in the [developer dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api). If initializing on Android, `android_package_name` must be specified instead and `redirect_uri` should be left blank.|
|android_package_name|string|false|none|The name of your app's Android package. Required if using the `link_token` to initialize Link on Android. Any package name specified here must also be added to the Allowed Android package names setting on the [developer dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api). When creating a `link_token` for initializing Link on other platforms, `android_package_name` must be left blank and `redirect_uri` should be used instead.|
|institution_data|[LinkTokenCreateInstitutionData](#schemalinktokencreateinstitutiondata)|false|none|A map containing data used to highlight institutions in Link.|
|card_switch|[LinkTokenCreateCardSwitch](#schemalinktokencreatecardswitch)|false|none|A map containing data to pass in for the Card Switch flow.|
|account_filters|[LinkTokenAccountFilters](#schemalinktokenaccountfilters)|false|none|By default, Link will provide limited account filtering: it will only display Institutions that are compatible with all products supplied in the `products` parameter of `/link/token/create`, and, if `auth` is specified in the `products` array, will also filter out accounts other than `checking`, `savings`, and `cash management` accounts on the Account Select pane. You can further limit the accounts shown in Link by using `account_filters` to specify the account subtypes to be shown in Link. Only the specified subtypes will be shown. This filtering applies to both the Account Select view (if enabled) and the Institution Select view. Institutions that do not support the selected subtypes will be omitted from Link. To indicate that all subtypes should be shown, use the value `"all"`. If the `account_filters` filter is used, any account type for which a filter is not specified will be entirely omitted from Link. For a full list of valid types and subtypes, see the [Account schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema).<br><br>The filter may or may not impact the list of accounts shown by the institution in the OAuth account selection flow, depending on the specific institution. If the user selects excluded account subtypes in the OAuth flow, these accounts will not be added to the Item. If the user selects only excluded account subtypes, the link attempt will fail and the user will be prompted to try again.<br>|
|eu_config|[LinkTokenEUConfig](#schemalinktokeneuconfig)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Configuration parameters for EU flows|
|institution_id|string|false|none|Used for certain legacy use cases|
|payment_configuration|[LinkTokenCreateRequestPaymentConfiguration](#schemalinktokencreaterequestpaymentconfiguration)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Pay By Bank flow. This is an optional field to configure the user experience, and currently requires the amount field to be set.|
|payment_initiation|[LinkTokenCreateRequestPaymentInitiation](#schemalinktokencreaterequestpaymentinitiation)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Payment Initiation (Europe) product. This field is required if `payment_initiation` is included in the `products` array. Either `payment_id` or `consent_id` must be provided.|
|employment|[LinkTokenCreateRequestEmployment](#schemalinktokencreaterequestemployment)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Employment product. This field is required if `employment` is included in the `products` array.|
|income_verification|[LinkTokenCreateRequestIncomeVerification](#schemalinktokencreaterequestincomeverification)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Income product. This field is required if `income_verification` is included in the `products` array.|
|base_report|[LinkTokenCreateRequestBaseReport](#schemalinktokencreaterequestbasereport)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Base Report product. This field is required if `assets` is included in the `products` array and the client is CRA-enabled.|
|credit_partner_insights|[LinkTokenCreateRequestCreditPartnerInsights](#schemalinktokencreaterequestcreditpartnerinsights)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Credit Partner Insights product.|
|cra_options|[LinkTokenCreateRequestCraOptions](#schemalinktokencreaterequestcraoptions)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with Plaid Check products|
|cra_report_parameter|[LinkTokenCreateRequestCraReportParameter](#schemalinktokencreaterequestcrareportparameter)|false|none|Specifies the report parameters for Plaid Check products, mirroring the parameters accepted on `/cra/report/create`.|
|consumer_report_permissible_purpose|[ConsumerReportPermissiblePurpose](#schemaconsumerreportpermissiblepurpose)|false|none|Describes the reason you are generating a Consumer Report for this user. When calling `/link/token/create`, this field is required when using Plaid Check (CRA) products; invalid if not using Plaid Check (CRA) products.<br><br>`ACCOUNT_REVIEW_CREDIT`: In connection with a consumer credit transaction for the review or collection of an account pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(A).<br><br>`ACCOUNT_REVIEW_NON_CREDIT`: For a legitimate business need of the information to review a non-credit account provided primarily for personal, family, or household purposes to determine whether the consumer continues to meet the terms of the account pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(F)(2).<br><br>`EXTENSION_OF_CREDIT`: In connection with a credit transaction initiated by and involving the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(A).<br><br>`LEGITIMATE_BUSINESS_NEED_TENANT_SCREENING`: For a legitimate business need in connection with a business transaction initiated by the consumer primarily for personal, family, or household purposes in connection with a property rental assessment pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(F)(i).<br><br>`LEGITIMATE_BUSINESS_NEED_OTHER`: For a legitimate business need in connection with a business transaction made primarily for personal, family, or household initiated by the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(F)(i).<br><br>`WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION_PREQUALIFICATION`: In accordance with the written instructions of the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(2), to evaluate an application's profile to make an offer to the consumer.<br><br>`WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION_OTHER`: In accordance with the written instructions of the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(2), such as when an individual agrees to act as a guarantor or assumes personal liability for a consumer, business, or commercial loan.<br><br>`ELIGIBILITY_FOR_GOVT_BENEFITS`:  In connection with an eligibility determination for a government benefit where the entity is required to consider an applicant's financial status pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(D).|
|auth|[LinkTokenCreateRequestAuth](#schemalinktokencreaterequestauth)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Auth product. This field can be used to enable or disable extended Auth flows for the resulting Link session. Omitting any field will result in a default that can be configured by your account manager. The default behavior described in the documentation is the default behavior that will apply if you have not requested your account manager to apply a different default. If you have enabled the [Dashboard Account Verification pane](https://dashboard.plaid.com/account-verification), the settings enabled there will override any settings in this object.|
|transfer|[LinkTokenCreateRequestTransfer](#schemalinktokencreaterequesttransfer)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Transfer product.|
|update|[LinkTokenCreateRequestUpdate](#schemalinktokencreaterequestupdate)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode).|
|identity_verification|[LinkTokenCreateRequestIdentityVerification](#schemalinktokencreaterequestidentityverification)|false|none|Specifies option for initializing Link for use with the Identity Verification product.|
|statements|[LinkTokenCreateRequestStatements](#schemalinktokencreaterequeststatements)|false|none|Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Statements product. This field is required for the statements product.|
|third_party_user_token|string|false|none|A third party user token associated with the current user.|
|investments|[LinkTokenInvestments](#schemalinktokeninvestments)|false|none|Configuration parameters for the Investments product|
|investments_auth|[LinkTokenInvestmentsAuth](#schemalinktokeninvestmentsauth)|false|none|Configuration parameters for the Investments Move product|
|hosted_link|[LinkTokenCreateHostedLink](#schemalinktokencreatehostedlink)|false|none|Configuration parameters for Hosted Link. To enable the session for Hosted Link, send this object in the request. It can be empty.|
|transactions|[LinkTokenTransactions](#schemalinktokentransactions)|false|none|Configuration parameters for the Transactions product|
|cashflow_report|[LinkTokenCashflowReport](#schemalinktokencashflowreport)|false|none|Configuration parameters for the Cashflow Report product. Currently in closed beta.|
|cra_enabled|boolean|false|none|If `true`, request a CRA connection. Defaults to `false`.|
|identity|[LinkTokenCreateIdentity](#schemalinktokencreateidentity)|false|none|Identity object used to specify document upload|
|financekit_supported|boolean|false|none|If `true`, indicates that client supports linking FinanceKit / AppleCard items. Defaults to `false`.|
|enable_multi_item_link|boolean|false|none|If `true`, enable linking multiple items in the same Link session. Defaults to `false`.|
|user_token|string|false|none|A user token generated using `/user/create`. Any Item created during the Link session will be associated with the user. Integrations that began using Plaid Protect, Multi-Item Link, or Plaid Check Consumer Report before December 10, 2025 use this field instead of the `user_id`.|

<h2 id="tocS_LinkTokenAccountFilters">LinkTokenAccountFilters</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalinktokenaccountfilters"></a>
<a id="schema_LinkTokenAccountFilters"></a>
<a id="tocSlinktokenaccountfilters"></a>
<a id="tocslinktokenaccountfilters"></a>

```json
{
  "depository": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "checking"
    ],
    "limited_purpose_types": [
      "RENT_MORTGAGE"
    ]
  },
  "credit": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "credit card"
    ]
  },
  "loan": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "auto"
    ]
  },
  "investment": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "529"
    ]
  },
  "other": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "other"
    ]
  }
}
```

By default, Link will provide limited account filtering: it will only display Institutions that are compatible with all products supplied in the `products` parameter of `/link/token/create`, and, if `auth` is specified in the `products` array, will also filter out accounts other than `checking`, `savings`, and `cash management` accounts on the Account Select pane. You can further limit the accounts shown in Link by using `account_filters` to specify the account subtypes to be shown in Link. Only the specified subtypes will be shown. This filtering applies to both the Account Select view (if enabled) and the Institution Select view. Institutions that do not support the selected subtypes will be omitted from Link. To indicate that all subtypes should be shown, use the value `"all"`. If the `account_filters` filter is used, any account type for which a filter is not specified will be entirely omitted from Link. For a full list of valid types and subtypes, see the [Account schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema).

The filter may or may not impact the list of accounts shown by the institution in the OAuth account selection flow, depending on the specific institution. If the user selects excluded account subtypes in the OAuth flow, these accounts will not be added to the Item. If the user selects only excluded account subtypes, the link attempt will fail and the user will be prompted to try again.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|depository|[DepositoryFilter](#schemadepositoryfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `depository`-type accounts|
|credit|[CreditFilter](#schemacreditfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `credit`-type accounts|
|loan|[LoanFilter](#schemaloanfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `loan`-type accounts|
|investment|[InvestmentFilter](#schemainvestmentfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `investment`-type accounts (or `brokerage`-type accounts for API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier).|
|other|[OtherFilter](#schemaotherfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `other`-type accounts|

<h2 id="tocS_LinkTokenCreateHostedLink">LinkTokenCreateHostedLink</h2>

<a id="tocslinktokencreatehostedlink"></a>

```json
{
  "delivery_method": "sms",
  "completion_redirect_uri": "string",
  "url_lifetime_seconds": 0,
  "is_mobile_app": false
}
```

Configuration parameters for Hosted Link. To enable the session for Hosted Link, send this object in the request. It can be empty.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delivery_method|[HostedLinkDeliveryMethod](#schemahostedlinkdeliverymethod)|false|none|How Plaid should deliver the Plaid Link session to the customer. Only available to customers enabled for Link Delivery (beta). To request Link Delivery access, contact your account manager.<br><br>`sms` will deliver via SMS. Must pass `user.phone_number`.<br><br>`email` will deliver via email. Must pass `user.email_address`.<br><br>Link Delivery is only available in Production.<br>|
|completion_redirect_uri|[HostedLinkCompletionRedirectURI](#schemahostedlinkcompletionredirecturi)|false|none|URI that Hosted Link will redirect to upon completion of the Link flow. This will only occur in Hosted Link sessions, not in other implementation methods.<br>|
|url_lifetime_seconds|[HostedLinkURLLifetimeSeconds](#schemahostedlinkurllifetimeseconds)|false|none|How many seconds the link will be valid for. Must be positive. Cannot be longer than 21 days. The default lifetime is 7 days for links delivered by email, 1 day for links delivered via SMS, and 30 minutes for links not sent via Plaid Link delivery. This parameter will override the value of all three link types.<br>|
|is_mobile_app|[HostedLinkIsMobileApp](#schemahostedlinkismobileapp)|false|none|This indicates whether the client is opening Hosted Link in a mobile app in an `AsWebAuthenticationSession` or Chrome custom tab.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|delivery_method|sms|
|delivery_method|email|

<h2 id="tocS_SessionTokenCreateRequest">SessionTokenCreateRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasessiontokencreaterequest"></a>
<a id="schema_SessionTokenCreateRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSsessiontokencreaterequest"></a>
<a id="tocssessiontokencreaterequest"></a>

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "template_id": "string",
  "user": {
    "client_user_id": "string",
    "user_id": {}
  },
  "redirect_uri": "string",
  "android_package_name": "string",
  "webhook": "http://example.com",
  "user_id": "string"
}
```

SessionTokenCreateRequest defines the request schema for `/session/token/create`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|template_id|string|true|none|The id of a template defined in Plaid Dashboard|
|user|[SessionTokenCreateRequestUser](#schemasessiontokencreaterequestuser)|false|none|Details about the end user. Required if a root-level `user_id` is not provided.|
|redirect_uri|[LinkTokenCreateRequestRedirectUri](#schemalinktokencreaterequestredirecturi)|false|none|A URI indicating the destination where a user should be forwarded after completing the Link flow; used to support OAuth authentication flows when launching Link in the browser or another app. The `redirect_uri` should not contain any query parameters. When used in Production, must be an https URI. Note that any redirect URI must also be added to the Allowed redirect URIs list in the [developer dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api). If initializing on Android, `android_package_name` must be specified instead and `redirect_uri` should be left blank.|
|android_package_name|string|false|none|The name of your app's Android package. Required if using the session token to initialize Layer on Android. Any package name specified here must also be added to the Allowed Android package names setting on the [developer dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api). When creating a session token for initializing Layer on other platforms, `android_package_name` must be left blank and `redirect_uri` should be used instead.|
|webhook|string(url)|false|none|The destination URL to which any webhooks should be sent. If you use the same webhook listener for all Sandbox or all Production activity, set this value in the Layer template editor in the Dashboard instead. Only provide a value in this field if you need to use multiple webhook URLs per environment (an uncommon use case). If provided, a value in this field will take priority over webhook values set in the Layer template editor.|
|user_id|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|none|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|

<h2 id="tocS_LinkTokenCreateRequestAuth">LinkTokenCreateRequestAuth</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalinktokencreaterequestauth"></a>
<a id="schema_LinkTokenCreateRequestAuth"></a>
<a id="tocSlinktokencreaterequestauth"></a>
<a id="tocslinktokencreaterequestauth"></a>

```json
{
  "auth_type_select_enabled": true,
  "automated_microdeposits_enabled": true,
  "instant_match_enabled": true,
  "same_day_microdeposits_enabled": true,
  "instant_microdeposits_enabled": true,
  "reroute_to_credentials": "OFF",
  "database_match_enabled": true,
  "database_insights_enabled": true,
  "flow_type": "FLEXIBLE_AUTH",
  "sms_microdeposits_verification_enabled": true
}
```

Specifies options for initializing Link for use with the Auth product. This field can be used to enable or disable extended Auth flows for the resulting Link session. Omitting any field will result in a default that can be configured by your account manager. The default behavior described in the documentation is the default behavior that will apply if you have not requested your account manager to apply a different default. If you have enabled the [Dashboard Account Verification pane](https://dashboard.plaid.com/account-verification), the settings enabled there will override any settings in this object.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auth_type_select_enabled|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether Auth Type Select is enabled for the Link session, allowing the end user to choose between linking via a credentials-based flow (i.e. Instant Auth, Instant Match, Automated Micro-deposits) or a manual flow that does not require login (all other Auth flows) prior to selecting their financial institution. Default behavior is `false`.|
|automated_microdeposits_enabled|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the Link session is enabled for the Automated Micro-deposits flow. Default behavior is `false`.|
|instant_match_enabled|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the Link session is enabled for the Instant Match flow. Instant Match is enabled by default. Instant Match can be disabled by setting this field to `false`.|
|same_day_microdeposits_enabled|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the Link session is enabled for the Same-Day Micro-deposits flow.  Default behavior is `false`.|
|instant_microdeposits_enabled|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the Link session is enabled for the Instant Micro-deposits flow.  Default behavior for Plaid teams created after November 2023 is `false`; default behavior for Plaid teams created before that date is `true`.|
|reroute_to_credentials|string|false|none|Specifies what type of [Reroute to Credentials](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/flow-options/#removing-manual-verification-entry-points-with-reroute-to-credentials) pane should be used in the Link session for the Same-Day Micro-deposits flow. Default behavior is `OPTIONAL`.|
|database_match_enabled|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Database Match has been deprecated and replaced with Database Auth. Use the [Account Verification Dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/account-verification) to enable Database Auth.|
|database_insights_enabled|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Database Insights has been deprecated and replaced with Database Auth. Use the [Account Verification Dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/account-verification) to enable Database Auth.|
|flow_type|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** This field has been deprecated in favor of `auth_type_select_enabled`.|
|sms_microdeposits_verification_enabled|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the Link session is enabled for SMS micro-deposits verification. Default behavior is `true`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|reroute_to_credentials|OFF|
|reroute_to_credentials|OPTIONAL|
|reroute_to_credentials|FORCED|
|flow_type|FLEXIBLE_AUTH|

<h2 id="tocS_LinkTokenCreateRequestUser">LinkTokenCreateRequestUser</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalinktokencreaterequestuser"></a>
<a id="schema_LinkTokenCreateRequestUser"></a>
<a id="tocSlinktokencreaterequestuser"></a>
<a id="tocslinktokencreaterequestuser"></a>

```json
{
  "client_user_id": "string",
  "legal_name": "string",
  "name": {
    "given_name": "Leslie",
    "family_name": "Knope"
  },
  "phone_number": "string",
  "phone_number_verified_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "email_address": "string",
  "email_address_verified_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "ssn": "string",
  "date_of_birth": "1970-01-01",
  "address": {
    "street": "123 Main St.",
    "street2": "Unit 42",
    "city": "Pawnee",
    "region": "IN",
    "postal_code": "46001",
    "country": "US"
  },
  "id_number": {
    "value": "123456789",
    "type": "us_ssn"
  }
}
```

An object specifying information about the end user who will be linking their account. **Required** if `user_id` isn't included.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_user_id|string|true|none|A unique ID representing the end user. Typically this will be a user ID number from your application. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`. It is currently used as a means of searching logs for the given user in the Plaid Dashboard.|
|legal_name|string|false|none|The user's full legal name, used for [micro-deposit based verification flows](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/). For a small number of customers on legacy flows, providing this field is required to enable micro-deposit-based flows. For all other customers, this field is optional. Providing the user's name in this field when using micro-deposit-based verification will streamline the end user experience, as the user will not be prompted to enter their name during the Link flow; Plaid will use the provided legal name instead.|
|name|object|false|none|none|
|phone_number|string|false|none|The user's phone number in [E.164](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) format. If supplied, will be used when applicable to prefill phone number fields in Link for the [returning user flow](https://plaid.com/docs/link/returning-user) and the [Identity Verification flow](https://plaid.com/docs/identity-verification). Phone number input is validated against valid number ranges; number strings that do not match a real-world phone numbering scheme may cause the request to fail, even in the Sandbox test environment.|
|phone_number_verified_time|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The date and time the phone number was verified in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`). This was previously an optional field used in the [returning user experience](https://plaid.com/docs/link/returning-user). This field is no longer required to enable the returning user experience.<br><br> Only pass a verification time for a phone number that you have verified. If you have performed verification but don't have the time, you may supply a signal value of the start of the UNIX epoch.<br><br> Example: `2020-01-01T00:00:00Z`<br>|
|email_address|string|false|none|The user's email address. Can be used to prefill Link fields when used with [Identity Verification](https://plaid.com/docs/identity-verification).|
|email_address_verified_time|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The date and time the email address was verified in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`). This was previously an optional field used in the [returning user experience](https://plaid.com/docs/link/returning-user). This field is no longer required to enable the returning user experience.<br><br> Only pass a verification time for an email address that you have verified. If you have performed verification but don't have the time, you may supply a signal value of the start of the UNIX epoch.<br><br> Example: `2020-01-01T00:00:00Z`|
|ssn|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated and not currently used, use the `id_number` field instead.|
|date_of_birth|string(date) \| null|false|none|To be provided in the format "yyyy-mm-dd". Can be used to prefill Link fields when used with Identity Verification.|
|address|object|false|none|none|
|id_number|object|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_LinkTokenCreateRequestUpdate">LinkTokenCreateRequestUpdate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalinktokencreaterequestupdate"></a>
<a id="schema_LinkTokenCreateRequestUpdate"></a>
<a id="tocSlinktokencreaterequestupdate"></a>
<a id="tocslinktokencreaterequestupdate"></a>

```json
{
  "account_selection_enabled": false,
  "reauthorization_enabled": true,
  "user": false,
  "item_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

Specifies options for initializing Link for [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_selection_enabled|boolean|false|none|If `true`, enables [update mode with Account Select](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode/#using-update-mode-to-request-new-accounts) for institutions in the US and Canada that do not use OAuth, or that use OAuth but do not have their own account selection flow. For institutions in the US that have an OAuth account selection flow (i.e. most OAuth-enabled institutions), update mode with Account Select will always be enabled, regardless of the value of this field.|
|reauthorization_enabled|boolean|false|none|Note: this field is not currently used. Plaid may enable this field in the future if 1033-related expiration begins to be enforced.<br><br>By default, Plaid will enable the reauthorization flow during update mode for an Item enabled for [Data Transparency Messaging](https://plaid.com/docs/link/data-transparency-messaging-migration-guide/) if the Item expires within six months. During a reauthorization flow, an end user will review Plaid's end user privacy policy, use case and data scope consents, and account access consents; they may also be required to log in to their financial institution's OAuth flow. After the end user successfully completes the reauthorization flow, the Item's expiration date will be extended to 12 months from the time that the reauthorization took place. This field allows you to optionally override the default reauthorization scheduling logic to either forcibly enable or disable the reauthorization flow for a given update mode session. This field does not impact the flow for Items at institutions in the EU or UK.<br>|
|user|boolean|false|none|If `true`, a `user_token` or `user_id` must also be provided, and Link will open in update mode for the given user.|
|item_ids|[[ItemId](#schemaitemid)]|false|none|An array of `item_id`s associated with the user to be updated in update mode. If empty or `null`, this field will default to initializing update mode for the most recent unhealthy Item associated with the user. A `user_token` or `user_id` must also be provided, and `update.user` must be `true`. Only one `item_id` may currently be specified.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_LinkTokenCreateRequestAccountSubtypes">LinkTokenCreateRequestAccountSubtypes</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalinktokencreaterequestaccountsubtypes"></a>
<a id="schema_LinkTokenCreateRequestAccountSubtypes"></a>
<a id="tocSlinktokencreaterequestaccountsubtypes"></a>
<a id="tocslinktokencreaterequestaccountsubtypes"></a>

```json
{
  "depository": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "checking"
    ],
    "limited_purpose_types": [
      "RENT_MORTGAGE"
    ]
  },
  "credit": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "credit card"
    ]
  },
  "loan": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "auto"
    ]
  },
  "investment": {
    "account_subtypes": [
      "529"
    ]
  }
}
```

By default, Link will only display account types that are compatible with all products supplied in the `products` parameter of `/link/token/create`. You can further limit the accounts shown in Link by using `account_filters` to specify the account subtypes to be shown in Link. Only the specified subtypes will be shown. This filtering applies to both the Account Select view (if enabled) and the Institution Select view. Institutions that do not support the selected subtypes will be omitted from Link. To indicate that all subtypes should be shown, use the value `"all"`. If the `account_filters` filter is used, any account type for which a filter is not specified will be entirely omitted from Link.

For a full list of valid types and subtypes, see the [Account schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema).

For institutions using OAuth, the filter will not affect the list of institutions or accounts shown by the bank in the OAuth window.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|depository|[LinkTokenCreateDepositoryFilter](#schemalinktokencreatedepositoryfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `depository`-type accounts|
|credit|[LinkTokenCreateCreditFilter](#schemalinktokencreatecreditfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `credit`-type accounts|
|loan|[LinkTokenCreateLoanFilter](#schemalinktokencreateloanfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `loan`-type accounts|
|investment|[LinkTokenCreateInvestmentFilter](#schemalinktokencreateinvestmentfilter)|false|none|A filter to apply to `investment`-type accounts (or `brokerage`-type accounts for API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier).|

<h2 id="tocS_LinkTokenCreateRequestRedirectUri">LinkTokenCreateRequestRedirectUri</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalinktokencreaterequestredirecturi"></a>
<a id="schema_LinkTokenCreateRequestRedirectUri"></a>
<a id="tocSlinktokencreaterequestredirecturi"></a>
<a id="tocslinktokencreaterequestredirecturi"></a>

```json
"string"
```

A URI indicating the destination where a user should be forwarded after completing the Link flow; used to support OAuth authentication flows when launching Link in the browser or another app. The `redirect_uri` should not contain any query parameters. When used in Production, must be an https URI. Note that any redirect URI must also be added to the Allowed redirect URIs list in the [developer dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api). If initializing on Android, `android_package_name` must be specified instead and `redirect_uri` should be left blank.

<a id="schemalinkoauthcorrelationidexchangerequest"></a>
<a id="schema_LinkOAuthCorrelationIdExchangeRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSlinkoauthcorrelationidexchangerequest"></a>
<a id="tocslinkoauthcorrelationidexchangerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "link_correlation_id": "string"
}
```

LinkOAuthCorrelationIdExchangeRequest defines the request schema for `/link/oauth/correlation_id/exchange`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|link_correlation_id|string|true|none|A `link_correlation_id` from a received OAuth redirect URI callback|

<h2 id="tocS_LinkOAuthCorrelationIdExchangeResponse">LinkOAuthCorrelationIdExchangeResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalinkoauthcorrelationidexchangeresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_LinkOAuthCorrelationIdExchangeResponse"></a>
<a id="tocSlinkoauthcorrelationidexchangeresponse"></a>
<a id="tocslinkoauthcorrelationidexchangeresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "link_token": "string",
  "request_id": "string"
}
```

LinkOAuthCorrelationIdExchangeResponse defines the response schema for `/link/oauth/correlation_id/exchange`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|link_token|string|true|none|The `link_token` associated to the given `link_correlation_id`, which can be used to re-initialize Link.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

LinkTokenGetResponse defines the response schema for `/link/token/get`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|link_token|string|true|none|A `link_token`, which can be supplied to Link in order to initialize it and receive a `public_token`, which can be exchanged for an `access_token`.|
|created_at|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|The creation timestamp for the `link_token`, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|expiration|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|The expiration timestamp for the `link_token`, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|link_sessions|[[LinkTokenGetSessionsResponse](#schemalinktokengetsessionsresponse)]|false|none|Information about Link sessions created using this `link_token`. Session data will be provided for up to six hours after the session has ended.|
|metadata|[LinkTokenGetMetadataResponse](#schemalinktokengetmetadataresponse)|true|none|An object specifying the arguments originally provided to the `/link/token/create` call.|
|user_id|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|none|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

An object containing information about a link session. Session data will be provided for up to six hours after the session has ended.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|link_session_id|string|true|none|The unique ID for the link session.|
|started_at|string(date-time)|false|none|The timestamp at which the link session was first started, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|finished_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The timestamp at which the link session was finished, if available, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|on_success|[LinkSessionSuccess](#schemalinksessionsuccess)|false|none|**Deprecated.** An object representing an [onSuccess](https://plaid.com/docs/link/web/#onsuccess) callback from Link. This field is returned only for legacy integrations and is deprecated in favor of [`results.item_add_results`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/#link-token-get-response-link-sessions-results-item-add-results) which can support multiple public tokens in a single Link session, for flows such as multi-Item Link. If you are receiving `on_success`, contact your account manager to migrate to `results.item_add_results` instead.|
|on_exit|[LinkSessionExitDeprecated](#schemalinksessionexitdeprecated)|false|none|**Deprecated.** An object representing an [onExit](https://plaid.com/docs/link/web/#onexit) callback from Link. This field is returned only for legacy implementations and has been deprecated in favor of [`exit`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/#link-token-get-response-link-sessions-exit), for improved naming consistency. If you are receiving this field, contact your account manager to migrate to the newer `exit` field.|
|exit|[LinkSessionExit](#schemalinksessionexit)|false|none|An object representing an [onExit](https://plaid.com/docs/link/web/#onexit) callback from Link. If you are not receiving this field and are instead receiving the deprecated `on_exit` field, contact your account manager to update your integration.|
|events|[[LinkEvent](#schemalinkevent)]|false|none|List of customer-related Link events|
|results|[LinkSessionResults](#schemalinksessionresults)|false|none|The set of results for a Link session.|

The set of results for a Link session.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|item_add_results|[[LinkSessionItemAddResult](#schemalinksessionitemaddresult)]|true|none|The set of Item adds for the Link session. If you are not receiving this field and are instead receiving the deprecated `on_success` field, contact your account manager to update your integration.|
|cra_item_add_results|[[LinkSessionCraItemAddResult](#schemalinksessioncraitemaddresult)]|true|none|The set of Plaid Check Item adds for the Link session.|
|cra_update_results|[[LinkSessionCraUpdateResult](#schemalinksessioncraupdateresult)]|true|none|The set of Plaid Check Item updates for the Link session.|
|bank_income_results|[[LinkSessionBankIncomeResult](#schemalinksessionbankincomeresult)]|true|none|The set of bank income verifications for the Link session.|
|payroll_income_results|[[LinkSessionPayrollIncomeResult](#schemalinksessionpayrollincomeresult)]|true|none|The set of payroll income verifications for the Link session.|
|document_income_results|[CreditSessionDocumentIncomeResult](#schemacreditsessiondocumentincomeresult)|true|none|The details of a document income verification in Link|
|cra_document_upload_results|[LinkSessionCraDocumentUploadResult](#schemalinksessioncradocumentuploadresult)|false|none|The details of a document upload CRA session in Link|

The details of an Item add in Link.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|public_token|string|true|none|Returned once a user has successfully linked their Item.|
|accounts|[[LinkSessionSuccessMetadataAccount](#schemalinksessionsuccessmetadataaccount)]|true|none|A list of accounts attached to the connected Item. If Account Select is enabled via the developer dashboard, `accounts` will only include selected accounts.|
|institution|[LinkSessionSuccessMetadataInstitution](#schemalinksessionsuccessmetadatainstitution)|true|none|An institution object. If the Item was created via Same-Day or Instant micro-deposit verification, `name` and `institution_id` will be omitted.|

The details of a Plaid Check Item add in Link.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|item_id|string|true|none|The Plaid Check Item ID. The `item_id` is always unique; linking the same account at the same institution twice will result in two Items with different `item_id` values. The `item_id` is case-sensitive.|
|accounts|[[LinkSessionSuccessMetadataAccount](#schemalinksessionsuccessmetadataaccount)]|true|none|A list of accounts attached to the connected Item. If Account Select is enabled via the developer dashboard, `accounts` will only include selected accounts.|
|institution|[LinkSessionSuccessMetadataInstitution](#schemalinksessionsuccessmetadatainstitution)|true|none|An institution object. If the Item was created via Same-Day or Instant micro-deposit verification, `name` and `institution_id` will be omitted.|

<h2 id="tocS_LinkSessionSuccessMetadataAccount">LinkSessionSuccessMetadataAccount</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",

  "type": "string",
  "subtype": "string",
  "verification_status": "string",
  "class_type": "string"
}
```

An account attached to the connected Item.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The Plaid `account_id`<br>|
|name|string|false|none|The official account name|
|mask|string \| null|false|none|The last 2-4 alphanumeric characters of an account's official account number. Note that the mask may be non-unique between an Item's accounts. It may also not match the mask that the bank displays to the user.|
|type|string|false|none|The account type. See the [Account schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema) for a full list of possible values|
|subtype|string|false|none|The account subtype. See the [Account schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema) for a full list of possible values|
|verification_status|string \| null|false|none|Indicates an Item's micro-deposit-based verification or database verification status. This field is only populated when using Auth and falling back to micro-deposit or database verification. Possible values are:<br><br>`pending_automatic_verification`: The Item is pending automatic verification.<br><br>`pending_manual_verification`: The Item is pending manual micro-deposit verification. Items remain in this state until the user successfully verifies the code.<br><br>`automatically_verified`: The Item has successfully been automatically verified.<br><br>`manually_verified`: The Item has successfully been manually verified.<br><br>`verification_expired`: Plaid was unable to automatically verify the deposit within 7 calendar days and will no longer attempt to validate the Item. Users may retry by submitting their information again through Link.<br><br>`verification_failed`: The Item failed manual micro-deposit verification because the user exhausted all 3 verification attempts. Users may retry by submitting their information again through Link.<br><br>`unsent`: The Item is pending micro-deposit verification, but Plaid has not yet sent the micro-deposit.<br><br>`database_insights_pending`: The Database Auth result is pending and will be available upon Auth request.<br><br>`database_insights_fail`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources and have signal for being invalid and/or have no signal for being valid. Typically this indicates that the routing number is invalid, the account number does not match the account number format associated with the routing number, or the account has been reported as closed or frozen. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_insights_pass`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources: the routing and account number match a routing and account number of an account recognized on the Plaid network, and the account is not known by Plaid to be frozen or closed. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_insights_pass_with_caution`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources and have some signal for being valid: the routing and account number were not recognized on the Plaid network, but the routing number is valid and the account number is a potential valid account number for that routing number. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_matched`: (deprecated) The Item has successfully been verified using Plaid's data sources. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Match.<br><br>`null` or empty string: Neither micro-deposit-based verification nor database verification are being used for the Item.<br>|
|class_type|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** If micro-deposit verification was being used, indicates the user's selection when asked if the account being verified is a `business` or `personal` account. This field is deprecated as Plaid no longer collects this information during the micro-deposit flow. To see whether an account is business or personal, use the `holder_category` field instead.|

|link_token|string|true|none|A `link_token`, which can be supplied to Link in order to initialize it and receive a `public_token`, which can be exchanged for an `access_token`.|
|expiration|string(date-time)|true|none|The expiration date and time for the `link_token`, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format. By default, a `link_token` created to generate a `public_token` that will be exchanged for a new `access_token` expires after 4 hours, and a `link_token` created for an existing Item (such as when updating an existing `access_token` by launching Link in update mode) expires after 30 minutes. If using [Hosted Link](https://plaid.com/docs/link/hosted-link/), the `link_token` will expire at the same time as the Hosted Link URL, and you can customize the duration using the `hosted_link.url_lifetime_seconds` option in the request. If using Link Delivery (beta), the `link_token` will expire by default after 24 hours if sent via SMS and after 7 days if sent via email. If using Identity Verification, Link token expiration will not be enforced; an Identity Verification Link session can be created with an expired Link token.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|
|hosted_link_url|string|false|none|A URL of a Plaid-hosted Link flow that will use the Link token returned by this request. Only present if the session is enabled for Hosted Link. To enable the session for Hosted Link, send a `hosted_link` object in the request.|
|user_id|[NewUserID](#schemanewuserid)|false|none|A unique user identifier, created by `/user/create`. Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|

<h2 id="tocS_PlaidError">PlaidError</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaplaiderror"></a>
<a id="schema_PlaidError"></a>
<a id="tocSplaiderror"></a>
<a id="tocsplaiderror"></a>

```json
{
  "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
  "error_code": "string",
  "error_code_reason": "string",
  "error_message": "string",
  "display_message": "string",
  "request_id": "string",
  "causes": [
    null
  ],
  "status": 0,
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "suggested_action": "string",
  "required_account_subtypes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "provided_account_subtypes": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

Errors are identified by `error_code` and categorized by `error_type`. Use these in preference to HTTP status codes to identify and handle specific errors. HTTP status codes are set and provide the broadest categorization of errors: 4xx codes are for developer- or user-related errors, and 5xx codes are for Plaid-related errors, and the status will be 2xx in non-error cases. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error_type|[PlaidErrorType](#schemaplaiderrortype)|true|none|A broad categorization of the error. Safe for programmatic use.|
|error_code|string|true|none|The particular error code. Safe for programmatic use.|
|error_code_reason|string \| null|false|none|The specific reason for the error code. Currently, reasons are only supported for OAuth-based item errors; the field is omitted otherwise. Safe for programmatic use.<br><br>Possible values:<br><br>`OAUTH_INVALID_TOKEN`: The user's OAuth connection to this institution has been invalidated.<br><br>`OAUTH_CONSENT_EXPIRED`: The user's access consent for this OAuth connection to this institution has expired.<br><br>`OAUTH_USER_REVOKED`: The user's OAuth connection to this institution is invalid because the user revoked their connection.|
|error_message|string|true|none|A developer-friendly representation of the error code. This may change over time and is not safe for programmatic use.|
|display_message|string \| null|true|none|A user-friendly representation of the error code. `null` if the error is not related to user action.<br><br>This may change over time and is not safe for programmatic use.|
|request_id|string|false|none|A unique ID identifying the request, to be used for troubleshooting purposes. This field will be omitted in errors provided by webhooks.|
|causes|[object]|false|none|In this product, a request can pertain to more than one Item. If an error is returned for such a request, `causes` will return an array of errors containing a breakdown of these errors on the individual Item level, if any can be identified.<br><br>`causes` will be provided for the `error_type` `ASSET_REPORT_ERROR` or `CHECK_REPORT_ERROR`, and for the `USER_ERROR` codes `USER_ITEM_ASSOCIATION_FAILED` and `USER_ITEM_REMOVAL_FAILED`. `causes` will also not be populated inside an error nested within a `warning` object.|
|status|integer \| null|false|none|The HTTP status code associated with the error. This will only be returned in the response body when the error information is provided via a webhook.|
|documentation_url|string|false|none|The URL of a Plaid documentation page with more information about the error|
|suggested_action|string \| null|false|none|Suggested steps for resolving the error|
|required_account_subtypes|[string]|false|none|A list of the account subtypes that were requested via the `account_filters` parameter in `/link/token/create`. Currently only populated for `NO_ACCOUNTS` errors from Items with `investments_auth` as an enabled product.<br>|
|provided_account_subtypes|[string]|false|none|A list of the account subtypes that were extracted but did not match the requested subtypes via the `account_filters` parameter in `/link/token/create`. Currently only populated for `NO_ACCOUNTS` errors from Items with `investments_auth` as an enabled product.<br>|

A single account at a financial institution.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|Plaid's unique identifier for the account. This value will not change unless Plaid can't reconcile the account with the data returned by the financial institution. This may occur, for example, when the name of the account changes. If this happens a new `account_id` will be assigned to the account.<br><br>The `account_id` can also change if the `access_token` is deleted and the same credentials that were used to generate that `access_token` are used to generate a new `access_token` on a later date. In that case, the new `account_id` will be different from the old `account_id`.<br><br>If an account with a specific `account_id` disappears instead of changing, the account is likely closed. Closed accounts are not returned by the Plaid API.<br><br>When using a CRA endpoint (an endpoint associated with Plaid Check Consumer Report, i.e. any endpoint beginning with `/cra/`), the `account_id` returned will not match the `account_id` returned by a non-CRA endpoint.<br><br>Like all Plaid identifiers, the `account_id` is case sensitive.|
|balances|[AccountBalance](#schemaaccountbalance)|true|none|A set of fields describing the balance for an account. For real-time values, use `/accounts/balance/get` or `/signal/evaluate` (with a Balance-only ruleset), which are fetched live from the institution at request time. Values returned by other endpoints may be cached, or adjusted by Plaid to reflect transaction activity received since the last refresh.|
|mask|string \| null|true|none|The last 2-4 alphanumeric characters of either the account's displayed mask or the account's official account number. Note that the mask may be non-unique between an Item's accounts.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the account, either assigned by the user or by the financial institution itself|
|official_name|string \| null|true|none|The official name of the account as given by the financial institution|
|type|[AccountType](#schemaaccounttype)|true|none|`investment:` Investment account. In API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier, this type is called `brokerage` instead.<br><br>`credit:` Credit card<br><br>`depository:` Depository account<br><br>`loan:` Loan account<br><br>`other:` Non-specified account type<br><br>See the [Account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema) for a full listing of account types and corresponding subtypes.|
|subtype|[AccountSubtype](#schemaaccountsubtype)|true|none|See the [Account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#account-type-schema) for a full listing of account types and corresponding subtypes.|
|verification_status|string|false|none|Indicates an Item's micro-deposit-based verification or database verification status. This field is only populated when using Auth and falling back to micro-deposit or database verification. Possible values are:<br><br>`pending_automatic_verification`: The Item is pending automatic verification.<br><br>`pending_manual_verification`: The Item is pending manual micro-deposit verification. Items remain in this state until the user successfully verifies the code.<br><br>`automatically_verified`: The Item has successfully been automatically verified.<br><br>`manually_verified`: The Item has successfully been manually verified.<br><br>`verification_expired`: Plaid was unable to automatically verify the deposit within 7 calendar days and will no longer attempt to validate the Item. Users may retry by submitting their information again through Link.<br><br>`verification_failed`: The Item failed manual micro-deposit verification because the user exhausted all 3 verification attempts. Users may retry by submitting their information again through Link.<br><br>`unsent`: The Item is pending micro-deposit verification, but Plaid has not yet sent the micro-deposit.<br><br>`database_insights_fail`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources and have signal for being invalid and/or have no signal for being valid. Typically this indicates that the routing number is invalid, the account number does not match the account number format associated with the routing number, or the account has been reported as closed or frozen. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_insights_pass`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources: the routing and account number match a routing and account number of an account recognized on the Plaid network, and the account is not known by Plaid to be frozen or closed. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_insights_pass_with_caution`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources and have some signal for being valid: the routing and account number were not recognized on the Plaid network, but the routing number is valid and the account number is a potential valid account number for that routing number. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_matched`: (deprecated) The Item has successfully been verified using Plaid's data sources. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Match.<br><br>Omitted or empty string: Neither micro-deposit-based verification nor database verification are being used for the Item.|
|verification_name|string|false|none|The account holder name that was used for micro-deposit and/or database verification. Only returned for Auth Items created via micro-deposit or database verification. This name was manually-entered by the user during Link, unless it was otherwise provided via the `user.legal_name` request field in `/link/token/create` for the Link session that created the Item.|
|verification_insights|[AccountVerificationInsights](#schemaaccountverificationinsights)|false|none|Insights from performing database verification for the account. Only returned for Auth Items using Database Auth.|
|persistent_account_id|string|false|none|A unique and persistent identifier for accounts that can be used to trace multiple instances of the same account across different Items for depository accounts. This field is currently supported only for Items at institutions that use Tokenized Account Numbers (i.e., Chase, PNC, and US Bank). Because these accounts have a different account number each time they are linked, this field may be used instead of the account number to uniquely identify an account across multiple Items for payments use cases, helping to reduce duplicate Items or attempted fraud. In Sandbox, this field is populated for TAN-based institutions (`ins_56`, `ins_13`, `ins_127990`) as well as the OAuth Sandbox institution (`ins_127287`); in Production, it will only be populated for accounts at applicable institutions.|
|apy|number(double) \| null|false|none|The annual percentage yield (APY) on an interest-bearing deposit account, expressed as a percentage (e.g. `4.25` means 4.25%). In the event that the APY is not provided by the financial institution, Plaid will return a value of `null`.|
|holder_category|[AccountHolderCategory](#schemaaccountholdercategory)|false|none|Indicates the account's categorization as either a personal or a business account. This field is currently in beta; to request access, contact your account manager. Coverage varies by institution, with approximately 70% of accounts populated overall.|
|paired_account_id|string \| null|false|none|The `account_id` of the account on the paired Item (see `paired_item_id`) that represents the same bank account as this one. For an account on a Plaid Inc Item, this is the matching account on its paired Plaid Check Item, and the reverse for an account on a Plaid Check Item. Only returned for accounts on an Item that has a paired Item. `null` means the Item has a paired Item but Plaid could not confidently match this account to an account on it. Like `account_id`, this value can change if Plaid re-creates the paired account.|

Items remain in this state until the user successfully verifies the code.<br><br>`automatically_verified`: The Item has successfully been automatically verified.<br><br>`manually_verified`: The Item has successfully been manually verified.<br><br>`verification_expired`: Plaid was unable to automatically verify the deposit within 7 calendar days and will no longer attempt to validate the Item. Users may retry by submitting their information again through Link.<br><br>`verification_failed`: The Item failed manual micro-deposit verification because the user exhausted all 3 verification attempts. Users may retry by submitting their information again through Link.<br><br>`unsent`: The Item is pending micro-deposit verification, but Plaid has not yet sent the micro-deposit.<br><br>`database_insights_fail`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources and have signal for being invalid and/or have no signal for being valid. Typically this indicates that the routing number is invalid, the account number does not match the account number format associated with the routing number, or the account has been reported as closed or frozen. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_insights_pass`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources: the routing and account number match a routing and account number of an account recognized on the Plaid network, and the account is not known by Plaid to be frozen or closed. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_insights_pass_with_caution`: The Item's numbers have been verified using Plaid's data sources and have some signal for being valid: the routing and account number were not recognized on the Plaid network, but the routing number is valid and the account number is a potential valid account number for that routing number. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Auth.<br><br>`database_matched`: (deprecated) The Item has successfully been verified using Plaid's data sources. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Match.<br><br>Omitted or empty string: Neither micro-deposit-based verification nor database verification are being used for the Item.|
|verification_name|string|false|none|The account holder name that was used for micro-deposit and/or database verification. Only returned for Auth Items created via micro-deposit or database verification. This name was manually-entered by the user during Link, unless it was otherwise provided via the `user.legal_name` request field in `/link/token/create` for the Link session that created the Item.|
|verification_insights|[AccountVerificationInsights](#schemaaccountverificationinsights)|false|none|Insights from performing database verification for the account. Only returned for Auth Items using Database Auth.|
|persistent_account_id|string|false|none|A unique and persistent identifier for accounts that can be used to trace multiple instances of the same account across different Items for depository accounts. This field is currently supported only for Items at institutions that use Tokenized Account Numbers (i.e., Chase, PNC, and US Bank). Because these accounts have a different account number each time they are linked, this field may be used instead of the account number to uniquely identify an account across multiple Items for payments use cases, helping to reduce duplicate Items or attempted fraud. In Sandbox, this field is populated for TAN-based institutions (`ins_56`, `ins_13`, `ins_127990`) as well as the OAuth Sandbox institution (`ins_127287`); in Production, it will only be populated for accounts at applicable institutions.|
|apy|number(double) \| null|false|none|The annual percentage yield (APY) on an interest-bearing deposit account, expressed as a percentage (e.g. `4.25` means 4.25%). In the event that the APY is not provided by the financial institution, Plaid will return a value of `null`.|
|holder_category|[AccountHolderCategory](#schemaaccountholdercategory)|false|none|Indicates the account's categorization as either a personal or a business account. This field is currently in beta; to request access, contact your account manager. Coverage varies by institution, with approximately 70% of accounts populated overall.|
|paired_account_id|string \| null|false|none|The `account_id` of the account on the paired Item (see `paired_item_id`) that represents the same bank account as this one. For an account on a Plaid Inc Item, this is the matching account on its paired Plaid Check Item, and the reverse for an account on a Plaid Check Item. Only returned for accounts on an Item that has a paired Item. `null` means the Item has a paired Item but Plaid could not confidently match this account to an account on it. Like `account_id`, this value can change if Plaid re-creates the paired account.|
