|fees|number(double)|false|none|The combined value of all fees applied to this transaction.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the investment transaction. Possible values are:<br><br>`buy`: Buying an investment<br><br>`sell`: Selling an investment<br><br>`cash`: Activity that modifies a cash position<br><br>`fee`: A fee on the account<br><br>`transfer`: Activity that modifies a position, but not through buy/sell activity e.g. options exercise, portfolio transfer|
|currency|string|true|none|Either a valid `iso_currency_code` or `unofficial_currency_code`|
|security|[SecurityOverride](#schemasecurityoverride)|false|none|Specify the security associated with the holding or investment transaction. When inputting custom security data to the Sandbox, Plaid will perform post-data-retrieval normalization and enrichment. These processes may cause the data returned by the Sandbox to be slightly different from the data you input. An ISO-4217 currency code and a security identifier (`ticker_symbol`, `cusip`, or `isin`) are required.|

Used to configure Sandbox test data for the Liabilities product

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the liability object: `credit` for a credit card, `student` for a student loan, `loan` for a closed-end loan, or `line_of_credit` for a line of credit. Mortgages are not currently supported in the custom Sandbox.|
|purchase_apr|number(double)|false|none|The purchase APR percentage value, between 0 and 100. For simplicity, this is the only interest rate used to calculate interest charges. Can only be set if `type` is `credit`.|
|cash_apr|number(double)|false|none|The cash APR percentage value, between 0 and 100. Can only be set if `type` is `credit`.|
|balance_transfer_apr|number(double)|false|none|The balance transfer APR percentage value, between 0 and 100. Can only be set if `type` is `credit`.|
|special_apr|number(double)|false|none|The special APR percentage value, between 0 and 100. Can only be set if `type` is `credit`.|
|last_payment_amount|number(double)|false|none|Override the `last_payment_amount` field. Can only be set if `type` is `credit`, `loan`, or `line_of_credit`.|
|last_statement_balance|number(double)|false|none|Override the `last_statement_balance` field. Can only be set if `type` is `credit` or `line_of_credit`.|
|minimum_payment_amount|number(double)|false|none|Override the `minimum_payment_amount` field. Can only be set if `type` is `credit`, `student`, or `line_of_credit`.|
|is_overdue|boolean|false|none|Override the `is_overdue` field. Can only be set if `type` is `credit` or `student`.|
|origination_date|string(date)|false|none|The date on which the loan was initially lent, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) (YYYY-MM-DD) format. Can only be set if `type` is `student` or `loan`.|
|principal|number(double)|false|none|The original loan principal. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|nominal_apr|number(double)|false|none|The interest rate on the loan as a percentage, between 0 and 100. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|interest_capitalization_grace_period_months|integer|false|none|If set, interest capitalization begins at the given number of months after loan origination. By default interest is never capitalized. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|repayment_model|[StudentLoanRepaymentModel](#schemastudentloanrepaymentmodel)|false|none|Student loan repayment information used to configure Sandbox test data for the Liabilities product|
|expected_payoff_date|string(date)|false|none|Override the `expected_payoff_date` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|guarantor|string|false|none|Override the `guarantor` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|is_federal|boolean|false|none|Override the `is_federal` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|loan_name|string|false|none|Override the `loan_name` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|loan_status|[StudentLoanStatus](#schemastudentloanstatus)|false|none|An object representing the status of the student loan|
|payment_reference_number|string|false|none|Override the `payment_reference_number` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|pslf_status|[PSLFStatus](#schemapslfstatus)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Information about the student's eligibility in the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program. This is only returned if the institution is FedLoan (`ins_116527`). Since FedLoan no longer services student loans, this field is no longer returned. |
|repayment_plan_description|string|false|none|Override the `repayment_plan.description` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|repayment_plan_type|string|false|none|Override the `repayment_plan.type` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`. Possible values are: `"extended graduated"`, `"extended standard"`, `"graduated"`, `"income-contingent repayment"`, `"income-based repayment"`, `"income-sensitive repayment"`, `"interest only"`, `"other"`, `"pay as you earn"`, `"revised pay as you earn"`, `"standard"`, or `"saving on a valuable education"`.|
|sequence_number|number|false|none|Override the `sequence_number` field. Can only be set if `type` is `student`.|
|servicer_address|[AddressDataOverride](#schemaaddressdataoverride)|false|none|Data about the components comprising an address.|
|account_number|string|false|none|Override the `account_number` field. Can only be set if `type` is `loan`.|
|interest_rate|[LiabilityOverrideInterestRate](#schemaliabilityoverrideinterestrate)|false|none|Override the `interest_rate` field. Can only be set if `type` is `loan` or `line_of_credit`.|
|principal_balance|number(double)|false|none|Override the `principal_balance` field. Can only be set if `type` is `loan` or `line_of_credit`.|
|origination_principal_amount|number(double)|false|none|Override the `origination_principal_amount` field. Can only be set if `type` is `loan`.|
|loan_term_months|integer|false|none|Override the `loan_term_months` field with a non-negative whole number. Can only be set if `type` is `loan`.|
|maturity_date|string(date)|false|none|Override the `maturity_date` field, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) (YYYY-MM-DD) format. Can only be set if `type` is `loan`.|
|payment_count|integer|false|none|Override the `payment_count` field with a non-negative whole number. Can only be set if `type` is `loan`.|
|payment_frequency|string|false|none|Override the `payment_frequency` field. Can only be set if `type` is `loan`.|
|next_payment_amount|number(double)|false|none|Override the `next_payment_amount` field. Can only be set if `type` is `loan` or `line_of_credit`.|

|payoff_amount|number(double)|false|none|Override the `payoff_amount` field. Can only be set if `type` is `loan`.|
|ytd_interest_paid|number(double)|false|none|Override the `ytd_interest_paid` field. Can only be set if `type` is `loan`.|
|compounding_period|string|false|none|Override the `compounding_period` field. Can only be set if `type` is `loan`.|
|credit_limit|number(double)|false|none|Override the `credit_limit` field. Can only be set if `type` is `line_of_credit`.|
|available_credit|number(double)|false|none|Override the `available_credit` field. Can only be set if `type` is `line_of_credit`.|
|last_statement_issue_date|string(date)|false|none|Override the `last_statement_issue_date` field, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) (YYYY-MM-DD) format. Can only be set if `type` is `line_of_credit`.|
|past_due_amount|number(double)|false|none|Override the `past_due_amount` field. Can only be set if `type` is `line_of_credit`.|
|finance_charges|number(double)|false|none|Override the `finance_charges` field. Can only be set if `type` is `line_of_credit`.|

<h2 id="tocS_InflowModel">InflowModel</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainflowmodel"></a>
<a id="schema_InflowModel"></a>
<a id="tocSinflowmodel"></a>
<a id="tocsinflowmodel"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "income_amount": 0,
  "payment_day_of_month": null,
  "transaction_name": "string",
  "statement_day_of_month": null
}
```

The `inflow_model` allows you to model a test account that receives regular income or makes regular payments on a loan. Any transactions generated by the `inflow_model` will appear in addition to randomly generated test data or transactions specified by `override_accounts`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|Inflow model. One of the following:<br><br>`none`: No income<br><br>`monthly-income`: Income occurs once per month<br><br>`monthly-balance-payment`: Pays off the balance on a liability account at the given statement day of month.<br><br>`monthly-interest-only-payment`: Makes an interest-only payment on a liability account at the given statement day of month.<br><br>Note that account types supported by Liabilities will accrue interest in the Sandbox. The types impacted are account type `credit` with subtype `credit` or `paypal`, and account type `loan` with subtype `student` or `mortgage`.|
|income_amount|number(double)|false|none|Amount of income per month. This value is required if `type` is `monthly-income`.|
|payment_day_of_month|object|false|none|Either a whole number between 1 and 28 or the string `last`, meaning the last day of the month. The day of the month on which the income transaction will appear. This field is required if `type` is `monthly-income`, `monthly-balance-payment` or `monthly-interest-only-payment`.|
|transaction_name|string|false|none|The name of the income transaction. This field is required if `type` is `monthly-income`, `monthly-balance-payment` or `monthly-interest-only-payment`.|
|statement_day_of_month|object|false|none|Either a whole number between 1 and 28 or the string `last`, meaning the last day of the month. The day of the month on which the balance is calculated for the next payment. This field is required if `type` is `monthly-balance-payment` or `monthly-interest-only-payment`.|

<h2 id="tocS_AuthDefaultUpdateWebhook">AuthDefaultUpdateWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaauthdefaultupdatewebhook"></a>
<a id="schema_AuthDefaultUpdateWebhook"></a>
<a id="tocSauthdefaultupdatewebhook"></a>
<a id="tocsauthdefaultupdatewebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "webhook_type": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "item_id": "string",
  "account_ids_with_new_auth": [
    "string"
  ],
  "account_ids_with_updated_auth": {
    "property1": [
      "account_number"
    ],
    "property2": [
      "account_number"
    ]
  },
  "error": {
    "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "error_code": "string",
    "error_code_reason": "string",
    "error_message": "string",
    "display_message": "string",
    "request_id": "string",
    "causes": [
      null
    ],
    "status": 0,
    "documentation_url": "string",
    "suggested_action": "string",
    "required_account_subtypes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "provided_account_subtypes": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

Plaid will trigger a `DEFAULT_UPDATE` webhook for Items that undergo a change in Auth data. This is generally caused by data partners notifying Plaid of a change in their account numbering system or to their routing numbers. To avoid returned transactions, customers that receive a `DEFAULT_UPDATE` webhook with the `account_ids_with_updated_auth` object populated should immediately discontinue all usages of existing Auth data for those accounts and call `/auth/get` or `/processor/auth/get` to obtain updated account and routing numbers.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`AUTH`|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`DEFAULT_UPDATE`|
|item_id|[ItemId](#schemaitemid)|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this webhook, warning, or error|
|account_ids_with_new_auth|[string]|true|none|An array of `account_id`'s for accounts that contain new auth.|
|account_ids_with_updated_auth|[AccountIdsWithUpdatedAuth](#schemaaccountidswithupdatedauth)|true|none|An object with keys of `account_id`'s that are mapped to their respective auth attributes that changed. Possible values are `account_number`, `routing_number`, and `account_number_mask`.<br><br>Example: `{ "XMBvvyMGQ1UoLbKByoMqH3nXMj84ALSdE5B58": ["account_number"] }`<br>|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|true|none|Errors are identified by `error_code` and categorized by `error_type`. Use these in preference to HTTP status codes to identify and handle specific errors. HTTP status codes are set and provide the broadest categorization of errors: 4xx codes are for developer- or user-related errors, and 5xx codes are for Plaid-related errors, and the status will be 2xx in non-error cases. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

Fired when an Item is verified via automated micro-deposits. We recommend communicating to your users when this event is received to notify them that their account is verified and ready for use.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`AUTH`|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`AUTOMATICALLY_VERIFIED`|
|account_id|string|true|none|The `account_id` of the account associated with the webhook|
|item_id|[ItemId](#schemaitemid)|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this webhook, warning, or error|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|false|none|Errors are identified by `error_code` and categorized by `error_type`. Use these in preference to HTTP status codes to identify and handle specific errors. HTTP status codes are set and provide the broadest categorization of errors: 4xx codes are for developer- or user-related errors, and 5xx codes are for Plaid-related errors, and the status will be 2xx in non-error cases. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

Fired when an Item's access consent is expiring in 7 days. This can be resolved by having the user go through Link's update mode. This webhook is fired only for Items associated with institutions in Europe (including the UK); for Items associated with institutions in the US or Canada, see [`PENDING_DISCONNECT`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/items/#pending_disconnect) instead.

  "webhook_type": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",

}
```

Fired when new ACH events are available. To begin receiving this webhook, you must first register your webhook listener endpoint via the [webhooks page in the Dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/webhooks). The `BANK_TRANSFERS_EVENTS_UPDATE` webhook can be used to track the progress of ACH transfers used in [micro-deposit verification](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/microdeposit-events/). Receiving this webhook indicates you should fetch the new events from `/bank_transfer/event/sync`. Note that [Transfer](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer) customers should use Transfer webhooks instead of using `BANK_TRANSFERS_EVENTS_UPDATE`; see [micro-deposit events documentation](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/microdeposit-events/) for more details.

<h2 id="tocS_LayerAuthenticationPassedWebhook">LayerAuthenticationPassedWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalayerauthenticationpassedwebhook"></a>

```json

  "webhook_type": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "environment": "sandbox",
  "link_session_id": "string",
  "link_token": "string"
}
```

Indicates that Plaid's authentication process has completed for a user and that Plaid has verified that the user owns their phone number. If you receive this webhook, you should skip your own OTP phone number verification flow for the user, even if the user does not complete the entire Link flow. If the user doesn't complete the full Link flow (as verified by your being able to successfully call `/user_account/session/get` using the `public_token` from the `onSuccess` callback) it is recommended that you implement [webhook verification](https://plaid.com/docs/api/webhooks/webhook-verification/) or another technique to avoid webhook spoofing attacks.

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`LAYER`|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`LAYER_AUTHENTICATION_PASSED`|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|
|link_session_id|string|true|none|An identifier for the Link session these events occurred in|
|link_token|string|true|none|The Link token used to create the Link session these events are from|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

<h2 id="tocS_RecurringTransferSkippedWebhook">RecurringTransferSkippedWebhook</h2>

```json
{
  "webhook_type": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "recurring_transfer_id": "string",
  "authorization_decision": "approved",
  "authorization_decision_rationale_code": "NSF",
  "skipped_origination_date": "1970-01-01",
  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

Fired when Plaid is unable to originate a new ACH transaction of the recurring transfer on the planned date.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`TRANSFER`|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`RECURRING_TRANSFER_SKIPPED`|
|recurring_transfer_id|[RecurringTransferID](#schemarecurringtransferid)|true|none|Plaid's unique identifier for a recurring transfer.|
|authorization_decision|[TransferAuthorizationDecision](#schematransferauthorizationdecision)|true|none|<br>A decision regarding the proposed transfer.<br><br>`approved` - The proposed transfer has received the end user's consent and has been approved for processing by Plaid. The `decision_rationale` field is set if Plaid was unable to fetch the account information. You may proceed with the transfer, but further review is recommended. Refer to the `code` field in the `decision_rationale` object for details.<br><br>`declined` - Plaid reviewed the proposed transfer and declined processing. Refer to the `code` field in the `decision_rationale` object for details.<br><br>`user_action_required` - An action is required before Plaid can assess the transfer risk and make a decision. The most common scenario is to update authentication for an Item. To complete the required action, initialize Link by setting `transfer.authorization_id` in the request of `/link/token/create`. After Link flow is completed, you may re-attempt the authorization request.<br><br>For `guarantee` requests, `approved` indicates the transfer is eligible for Plaid's guarantee, and `declined` indicates Plaid will not provide guarantee coverage for the transfer. `user_action_required` indicates you should follow the above guidance before re-attempting.|
|authorization_decision_rationale_code|[TransferAuthorizationDecisionRationaleCode](#schematransferauthorizationdecisionrationalecode)|false|none|A code representing the rationale for approving or declining the proposed transfer.<br><br>If the `rationale_code` is `null`, the transfer passed the authorization check.<br><br>Any non-`null` value for an `approved` transfer indicates that the authorization check could not be run and that you should perform your own risk assessment on the transfer. The code will indicate why the check could not be run. Possible values for an `approved` transfer are:<br><br>`MANUALLY_VERIFIED_ITEM` - Item created via a manual entry flow (i.e. Same-Day Micro-deposit, Instant Micro-deposit, or database-based verification), limited information available.<br><br>`ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` - Unable to collect the account information due to Item staleness. Can be resolved by using Link and setting [`transfer.authorization_id`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/#link-token-create-request-transfer-authorization-id) in the request to `/link/token/create`.<br><br>`PAYMENT_PROFILE_LOGIN_REQUIRED` - The Payment Profile associated with the call to `/transfer/authorization/create` is in a state that requires the end user to re-authenticate. Can be resolved by using Link to refresh the Payment Profile.<br><br>`MIGRATED_ACCOUNT_ITEM` - Item created via `/transfer/migrate_account` endpoint, limited information available.<br><br>`ERROR` - Unable to collect the account information due to an unspecified error.<br><br>These codes can also accompany a `declined` decision, for example when your Signal Rules decline the transfer.<br><br>The following codes indicate that the authorization decision was `declined`:<br><br>`NSF` - Transaction has an elevated risk of resulting in a return due to insufficient funds.<br><br>`RISK` - Transaction is high-risk.<br><br>`TRANSFER_LIMIT_REACHED` - One or several transfer limits are reached, e.g. monthly transfer limit. Check the accompanying `description` field to understand which limit has been reached.<br><br>`ADMIN` - Transaction has an elevated risk of resulting in an administrative return (for example a closed, invalid, or unauthorized account).<br><br>`FRAUD` - Transaction has an elevated risk of being fraudulent.|
|skipped_origination_date|string(date)|true|none|The planned date on which Plaid is unable to originate a new ACH transaction of the recurring transfer. This will be of the form YYYY-MM-DD.|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|

#### Enumerated Values

|authorization_decision_rationale_code|TRANSFER_LIMIT_REACHED|
|authorization_decision_rationale_code|MANUALLY_VERIFIED_ITEM|

|authorization_decision_rationale_code|ADMIN|
|authorization_decision_rationale_code|FRAUD|
|authorization_decision_rationale_code|null|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

<h2 id="tocS_PendingDisconnectWebhookReason">PendingDisconnectWebhookReason</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapendingdisconnectwebhookreason"></a>
<a id="schema_PendingDisconnectWebhookReason"></a>
<a id="tocSpendingdisconnectwebhookreason"></a>
<a id="tocspendingdisconnectwebhookreason"></a>

```json
"INSTITUTION_MIGRATION"
```

Reason why the Item is about to be disconnected.

`INSTITUTION_MIGRATION`: The institution is moving to API or to a different integration. For example, this can occur when an institution moves from a non-OAuth integration to an OAuth integration.

`INSTITUTION_TOKEN_EXPIRATION`: The consent on an Item associated with a US or CA institution is about to expire.

<h2 id="tocS_PendingDisconnectWebhook">PendingDisconnectWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapendingdisconnectwebhook"></a>

  "webhook_code": "string",

  "user_id": "string",
  "reason": "INSTITUTION_MIGRATION",
  "disconnect_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

Fired when an Item is expected to be disconnected. The webhook will currently be fired 7 days before the existing Item is scheduled for disconnection. This can be resolved by having the user go through Link's [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode). Currently, this webhook is fired only for US or Canadian institutions; in the UK or EU, you should continue to listen for the [`PENDING_EXPIRATION`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/items/#pending_expiration) webhook instead.

For example, this can occur when an institution moves from a non-OAuth integration to an OAuth integration.<br><br>`INSTITUTION_TOKEN_EXPIRATION`: The consent on an Item associated with a US or CA institution is about to expire.|

An error object and associated `item_id` used to identify a specific Item and error when a batch operation operating on multiple Items has encountered an error in one of the Items.

### Properties

|error_code_reason|string \| null|false|none|The specific reason for the error code. Currently, reasons are only supported for OAuth-based item errors; the field is omitted otherwise. Safe for programmatic use.<br><br>Possible values:<br><br>`OAUTH_INVALID_TOKEN`: The user's OAuth connection to this institution has been invalidated.<br><br>`OAUTH_CONSENT_EXPIRED`: The user's access consent for this OAuth connection to this institution has expired.<br><br>`OAUTH_USER_REVOKED`: The user's OAuth connection to this institution is invalid because the user revoked their connection.|
|error_message|string|true|none|A developer-friendly representation of the error code. This may change over time and is not safe for programmatic use.|
|display_message|string \| null|true|none|A user-friendly representation of the error code. `null` if the error is not related to user action.<br><br>This may change over time and is not safe for programmatic use.|
|request_id|string|false|none|A unique ID identifying the request, to be used for troubleshooting purposes. This field will be omitted in errors provided by webhooks.|
|causes|[object]|false|none|In this product, a request can pertain to more than one Item. If an error is returned for such a request, `causes` will return an array of errors containing a breakdown of these errors on the individual Item level, if any can be identified.<br><br>`causes` will be provided for the `error_type` `ASSET_REPORT_ERROR` or `CHECK_REPORT_ERROR`, and for the `USER_ERROR` codes `USER_ITEM_ASSOCIATION_FAILED` and `USER_ITEM_REMOVAL_FAILED`. `causes` will also not be populated inside an error nested within a `warning` object.|
|status|integer \| null|false|none|The HTTP status code associated with the error. This will only be returned in the response body when the error information is provided via a webhook.|
|documentation_url|string|false|none|The URL of a Plaid documentation page with more information about the error|
|suggested_action|string \| null|false|none|Suggested steps for resolving the error|
|required_account_subtypes|[string]|false|none|A list of the account subtypes that were requested via the `account_filters` parameter in `/link/token/create`. Currently only populated for `NO_ACCOUNTS` errors from Items with `investments_auth` as an enabled product.<br>|

Currently only populated for `NO_ACCOUNTS` errors from Items with `investments_auth` as an enabled product.<br>|

Fired when the status of a payment has changed. Not fired when the new status is `PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED`, `PAYMENT_STATUS_AUTHORISING`, or `PAYMENT_STATUS_PROCESSING`. For a full explanation of payment statuses and how to handle each, see the [Payment Status guide](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/payment-status/).

Note: For standard Payment Initiation, Plaid payment statuses do not constitute proof that funds have arrived in the recipient's account, and you should not use `new_payment_status` to confirm fund settlement. For options that provide confirmation of fund receipt, see [Virtual Accounts](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/virtual-accounts/payment-confirmation/).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`PAYMENT_INITIATION`|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`PAYMENT_STATUS_UPDATE`|
|payment_id|string|true|none|The `payment_id` for the payment being updated|
|transaction_id|string \| null|false|none|The transaction ID that this payment is associated with, if any. This is present only when a payment was initiated using virtual accounts.|
|new_payment_status|[PaymentInitiationPaymentStatus](#schemapaymentinitiationpaymentstatus)|true|none|The status of the payment.<br><br>Core lifecycle statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED`**: Transitional. The payment is awaiting user input to continue processing. It may re-enter this state if additional input is required.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_AUTHORISING`:** Transitional. The payment is being authorised by the financial institution. It will automatically move on once authorisation completes.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED`:** The payment has been authorised and accepted by the financial institution. In many EU markets, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not supported, and a payment will remain in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` until the funds settle, making this a terminal success state in those cases. A payment in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` should be treated as a successfully submitted payment; do not gate downstream processing on reaching `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`. For a full explanation of payment statuses and how to handle each, see the [Payment Status guide](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/payment-status/).<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`: Terminal.** The funds have left the payer's account and the payment is en route to settlement. Note that this status does not confirm that funds have arrived in the recipient's account; do not use it as proof of fund receipt. Support is more common in the UK than in the EU; where unsupported, a successful payment remains in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` before settling. When using Plaid Virtual Accounts, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not terminal -- the payment will continue to `PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED` once funds are available.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED`: Terminal.** The funds are available in the recipient's account. Only available to customers using [Plaid Virtual Accounts](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/virtual-accounts/).<br><br>Failure statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: Terminal.** The payment failed due to insufficient funds. No further retries will succeed until the payer's balance is replenished.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_FAILED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment could not be initiated due to a system error or outage. Retry once the root cause is resolved.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_BLOCKED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment was blocked by Plaid (e.g., flagged as risky). Resolve any compliance or risk issues and retry.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_REJECTED`: Terminal.** The payment was rejected by the financial institution. No automatic retry is possible.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_CANCELLED`: Terminal.** The end user cancelled the payment during authorisation.<br><br>Standing-order statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_ESTABLISHED`: Terminal.** A recurring/standing order has been successfully created.<br><br>Deprecated (to be removed in a future release):<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_UNKNOWN`: The payment status is unknown.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_PROCESSING`: The payment is currently being processed.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_COMPLETED`: Indicates that the standing order has been successfully established.|
|old_payment_status|[PaymentInitiationPaymentStatus](#schemapaymentinitiationpaymentstatus)|true|none|The status of the payment.<br><br>Core lifecycle statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INPUT_NEEDED`**: Transitional. The payment is awaiting user input to continue processing. It may re-enter this state if additional input is required.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_AUTHORISING`:** Transitional. The payment is being authorised by the financial institution. It will automatically move on once authorisation completes.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED`:** The payment has been authorised and accepted by the financial institution. In many EU markets, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not supported, and a payment will remain in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` until the funds settle, making this a terminal success state in those cases. A payment in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` should be treated as a successfully submitted payment; do not gate downstream processing on reaching `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`. For a full explanation of payment statuses and how to handle each, see the [Payment Status guide](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/payment-status/).<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`: Terminal.** The funds have left the payer's account and the payment is en route to settlement. Note that this status does not confirm that funds have arrived in the recipient's account; do not use it as proof of fund receipt. Support is more common in the UK than in the EU; where unsupported, a successful payment remains in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` before settling. When using Plaid Virtual Accounts, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not terminal -- the payment will continue to `PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED` once funds are available.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED`: Terminal.** The funds are available in the recipient's account. Only available to customers using [Plaid Virtual Accounts](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/virtual-accounts/).<br><br>Failure statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: Terminal.** The payment failed due to insufficient funds. No further retries will succeed until the payer's balance is replenished.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_FAILED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment could not be initiated due to a system error or outage. Retry once the root cause is resolved.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_BLOCKED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment was blocked by Plaid (e.g., flagged as risky). Resolve any compliance or risk issues and retry.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_REJECTED`: Terminal.** The payment was rejected by the financial institution. No automatic retry is possible.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_CANCELLED`: Terminal.** The end user cancelled the payment during authorisation.<br><br>Standing-order statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_ESTABLISHED`: Terminal.** A recurring/standing order has been successfully created.<br><br>Deprecated (to be removed in a future release):<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_UNKNOWN`: The payment status is unknown.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_PROCESSING`: The payment is currently being processed.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_COMPLETED`: Indicates that the standing order has been successfully established.|
|original_reference|string \| null|true|none|The original value of the reference when creating the payment.|
|adjusted_reference|string \| null|false|none|The value of the reference sent to the bank after adjustment to pass bank validation rules.|
|original_start_date|string(date) \| null|true|none|The original value of the `start_date` provided during the creation of a standing order. If the payment is not a standing order, this field will be `null`.|
|adjusted_start_date|string(date) \| null|true|none|The start date sent to the bank after adjusting for holidays or weekends.  Will be provided in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD). If the start date did not require adjustment, or if the payment is not a standing order, this field will be `null`.|
|timestamp|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp of the update, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format, e.g. `"2017-09-14T14:42:19.350Z"`|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|false|none|Errors are identified by `error_code` and categorized by `error_type`. Use these in preference to HTTP status codes to identify and handle specific errors. HTTP status codes are set and provide the broadest categorization of errors: 4xx codes are for developer- or user-related errors, and 5xx codes are for Plaid-related errors, and the status will be 2xx in non-error cases. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|

The `security_id` does not typically change, but may change if inherent details of the security change due to a corporate action, for example, in the event of a ticker symbol change or CUSIP change.|

Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|
|market_identifier_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-10383 Market Identifier Code of the exchange or market in which the security is being traded.|
|sector|string \| null|true|none|The sector classification of the security, such as Finance, Health Technology, etc.<br><br>For a complete list of possible values, please refer to the ["Sectors and Industries" spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L7aXUdqLhxgM8qe7hK67qqKXiUdQqILpwZ0LpxvCVnc).|
|industry|string \| null|true|none|The industry classification of the security, such as Biotechnology, Airlines, etc.<br><br>For a complete list of possible values, please refer to the ["Sectors and Industries" spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L7aXUdqLhxgM8qe7hK67qqKXiUdQqILpwZ0LpxvCVnc).|
|cfi_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-10962 Classification of Financial Instruments Code used to classify the security based on its structure and function.|
|figi|string \| null|true|none|12-character FIGI, a unique Financial Instrument Global Identifier assigned to securities that is immutable and stays consistent across most corporate actions. This is an open data standard issued by the Object Management Group and administered by Bloomberg L.P.|

<h2 id="tocS_YieldRate">YieldRate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

}
```

Details about a fixed income security's expected rate of return.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|percentage|number(double)|true|none|The fixed income security's expected rate of return.|
|type|[YieldRateType](#schemayieldratetype)|true|none|The type of rate which indicates how the predicted yield was calculated. It is one of:<br><br>`coupon`: the annualized interest rate for securities with a one-year term or longer, such as treasury notes and bonds.<br><br>`coupon_equivalent`: the calculated equivalent for the annualized interest rate factoring in the discount rate and time to maturity, for shorter term, non-interest-bearing securities such as treasury bills.<br><br>`discount`: the rate at which the present value or cost is discounted from the future value upon maturity, also known as the face value.<br><br>`yield`: the total predicted rate of return factoring in both the discount rate and the coupon rate, applicable to securities such as exchange-traded bonds which can both be interest-bearing as well as sold at a discount off their face value.|

#### Enumerated Values

<h2 id="tocS_YieldRateType">YieldRateType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemayieldratetype"></a>
<a id="schema_YieldRateType"></a>
<a id="tocSyieldratetype"></a>
<a id="tocsyieldratetype"></a>

```json
"coupon"
```

The type of rate which indicates how the predicted yield was calculated. It is one of:

`coupon`: the annualized interest rate for securities with a one-year term or longer, such as treasury notes and bonds.

`coupon_equivalent`: the calculated equivalent for the annualized interest rate factoring in the discount rate and time to maturity, for shorter term, non-interest-bearing securities such as treasury bills.

`discount`: the rate at which the present value or cost is discounted from the future value upon maturity, also known as the face value.

`yield`: the total predicted rate of return factoring in both the discount rate and the coupon rate, applicable to securities such as exchange-traded bonds which can both be interest-bearing as well as sold at a discount off their face value.

A transaction within an investment account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|investment_transaction_id|string|true|none|The ID of the Investment transaction, unique across all Plaid transactions. Like all Plaid identifiers, the `investment_transaction_id` is case sensitive.|
|cancel_transaction_id|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** A legacy field formerly used internally by Plaid to identify certain canceled transactions.|
|account_id|string|true|none|The `account_id` of the account against which this transaction posted.|
|security_id|string \| null|true|none|The `security_id` to which this transaction is related.|
|date|string(date)|true|none|The [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) posting date for the transaction. This is typically the settlement date.|
|transaction_datetime|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`) representing when the order was initiated. This field is returned for select financial institutions and reflects the value provided by the institution. When the institution only provides a date without time-of-day information, this field will reflect the date that the order was initiated with a time component that defaults to `T00:00:00Z`. This does not indicate that the order was initiated at midnight UTC.|
|name|string|true|none|The institution's description of the transaction.|
|quantity|number(double)|true|none|The number of units of the security involved in this transaction. Positive for buy transactions; negative for sell transactions.|
|amount|number(double)|true|none|The complete value of the transaction. Positive values when cash is debited, e.g. purchases of stock; negative values when cash is credited, e.g. sales of stock. Treatment remains the same for cash-only movements unassociated with securities. For transactions representing a simultaneous cash contribution and purchase of a security, the portion of the transaction representing the purchase takes precedence, and the `amount` is represented as positive.|
|price|number(double)|true|none|The price of the security at which this transaction occurred.|
|fees|number(double) \| null|true|none|The combined value of all fees applied to this transaction|
|type|[InvestmentTransactionType](#schemainvestmenttransactiontype)|true|none|Value is one of the following:<br><br>`buy`: Buying an investment<br><br>`sell`: Selling an investment<br><br>`cancel`: A cancellation of a pending transaction<br><br>`cash`: Activity that modifies a cash position<br><br>`fee`: A fee on the account<br><br>`transfer`: Activity which modifies a position, but not through buy/sell activity e.g. options exercise, portfolio transfer<br><br>For descriptions of possible transaction types and subtypes, see the [Investment transaction types schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#investment-transaction-types-schema).|
|subtype|[InvestmentTransactionSubtype](#schemainvestmenttransactionsubtype)|true|none|For descriptions of possible transaction types and subtypes, see the [Investment transaction types schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#investment-transaction-types-schema).|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the transaction. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the transaction. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`. Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|

<h2 id="tocS_UserPermissionRevokedWebhook">UserPermissionRevokedWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemauserpermissionrevokedwebhook"></a>
<a id="schema_UserPermissionRevokedWebhook"></a>
<a id="tocSuserpermissionrevokedwebhook"></a>
<a id="tocsuserpermissionrevokedwebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "webhook_type": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "item_id": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "error": {
    "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "error_code": "string",
    "error_code_reason": "string",
    "error_message": "string",
    "display_message": "string",
    "request_id": "string",
    "causes": [
      null
    ],
    "status": 0,
    "documentation_url": "string",
    "suggested_action": "string",
    "required_account_subtypes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "provided_account_subtypes": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

The `USER_PERMISSION_REVOKED` webhook may be fired when an end user has revoked the permission that they previously granted to access an Item. If the end user revoked their permissions through Plaid (such as via the Plaid Portal or by contacting Plaid support), the webhook will fire. If the end user revoked their permissions directly through the institution, this webhook may not always fire, since some institutions' consent portals do not trigger this webhook. To attempt to restore the Item, it can be sent through [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode). Depending on the exact process the end user used to revoke permissions, it may not be possible to launch update mode for the Item. If you encounter an error when attempting to create a Link token for update mode on an Item with revoked permissions, create a fresh Link token for the user.

Note that when working with tokenized account numbers with Auth or Transfer, the account number provided by Plaid will no longer work for creating transfers once user permission has been revoked, except for US Bank Items.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`ITEM`|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`USER_PERMISSION_REVOKED`|
|item_id|[ItemId](#schemaitemid)|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this webhook, warning, or error|
|user_id|[UserId](#schemauserid)|false|none|The Plaid `user_id` of the User associated with this webhook, warning, or error.|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|false|none|Errors are identified by `error_code` and categorized by `error_type`. Use these in preference to HTTP status codes to identify and handle specific errors. HTTP status codes are set and provide the broadest categorization of errors: 4xx codes are for developer- or user-related errors, and 5xx codes are for Plaid-related errors, and the status will be 2xx in non-error cases. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

Represents a transfer within the Transfers API.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[TransferID](#schematransferid)|true|none|Plaid's unique identifier for a transfer.|
|authorization_id|[TransferAuthorizationID](#schematransferauthorizationid)|true|none|Plaid's unique identifier for a transfer authorization.|
|ach_class|[ACHClass](#schemaachclass)|false|none|Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network. For more details, see [ACH SEC codes](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/creating-transfers/#ach-sec-codes).<br><br>Codes supported for credits: `ccd`, `ppd`<br>Codes supported for debits: `ccd`, `ppd`, `tel`, `web`<br><br>`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts<br><br>`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - The transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer. Authorization was obtained in writing either in person or via an electronic document signing, e.g. Docusign, by the consumer. Can be used for credits or debits.<br><br>`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry. The transfer debits a consumer's bank account. Authorization from the consumer is obtained over the Internet (e.g. a web or mobile application). Can be used for single debits or recurring debits.<br><br>`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry. The transfer debits a consumer. Debit authorization has been received orally over the telephone via a recorded call.|
|account_id|string|false|none|The Plaid `account_id` corresponding to the end-user account that will be debited or credited.|
|funding_account_id|[TransferFundingAccountIDResponseNullable](#schematransferfundingaccountidresponsenullable)|true|none|The id of the associated funding account, available in the Plaid Dashboard. If present, this indicates which of your business checking accounts will be credited or debited.|
|ledger_id|[TransferLedgerID](#schematransferledgerid)|false|none|Plaid's unique identifier for a Plaid Ledger Balance.|
|type|[TransferType](#schematransfertype)|true|none|The type of transfer. This will be either `debit` or `credit`.  A `debit` indicates a transfer of money into the origination account; a `credit` indicates a transfer of money out of the origination account.|
|user|[TransferUserInResponse](#schematransferuserinresponse)|true|none|The legal name and other information for the account holder.|
|amount|[TransferAmount](#schematransferamount)|true|none|The amount of the transfer (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00"). When calling `/transfer/authorization/create`, specify the maximum amount to authorize. When calling `/transfer/create`, specify the exact amount of the transfer, up to a maximum of the amount authorized. If this field is left blank when calling `/transfer/create`, the maximum amount authorized in the `authorization_id` will be sent. If the authorization's `guarantee_details.outcome` is `PARTIAL_INSTANT_ONLY`, this field is required when calling `/transfer/create`.|
|description|string|true|none|The description of the transfer.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|none|The datetime when this transfer was created. This will be of the form `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`|
|status|[TransferStatus](#schematransferstatus)|true|none|The status of the transfer.<br><br>`pending`: A new transfer was created; it is in the pending state.<br><br>`posted`: The transfer has been successfully submitted to the payment network.<br><br>`settled`: The transfer was successfully completed by the payment network. Note that funds from received debits are not available to be moved out of the Ledger until the transfer reaches `funds_available` status. For credit transactions, `settled` means the funds have been delivered to the receiving bank account. This is the terminal state of a successful credit transfer.<br><br>`funds_available`: Funds from the transfer have been released from hold and applied to the ledger's available balance. (Only applicable to ACH debits.) This is the terminal state of a successful debit transfer.<br><br>`cancelled`: The transfer was cancelled by the client. This is the terminal state of a cancelled transfer.<br><br>`failed`: The transfer failed, no funds were moved. This is the terminal state of a failed transfer.<br><br>`returned`: A posted transfer was returned. This is the terminal state of a returned transfer.|
|sweep_status|[TransferSweepStatus](#schematransfersweepstatus)|false|none|The status of the sweep for the transfer.<br><br>`unswept`: The transfer hasn't been swept yet.<br><br>`swept`: The transfer was swept to the sweep account.<br><br>`swept_settled`: Credits are available to be withdrawn or debits have been deducted from the customer's business checking account.<br><br>`return_swept`: The transfer was returned, funds were pulled back or pushed back to the sweep account.<br><br>`null`: The transfer will never be swept (e.g. if the transfer is cancelled or returned before being swept)|
|network|[TransferNetwork](#schematransfernetwork)|true|none|The network or rails used for the transfer.<br><br>For transfers submitted as `ach` or `same-day-ach`, the Standard ACH cutoff is 8:30 PM Eastern Time.<br><br>For transfers submitted as `same-day-ach`, the Same Day ACH cutoff is 3:00 PM Eastern Time.  It is recommended to send the request 15 minutes prior to the cutoff to ensure that it will be processed in time for submission before the cutoff. If the transfer is processed after this cutoff but before the Standard ACH cutoff, it will be sent over Standard ACH rails and will not incur same-day charges; this will apply to both legs of the transfer if applicable. The transaction limit for a Same Day ACH transfer is $1,000,000. Authorization requests sent with an amount greater than $1,000,000 will fail.<br><br>For transfers submitted as `rtp`, Plaid will automatically route between the Real-Time Payments (RTP) rail by TCH or FedNow rails as necessary. If a transfer is submitted as `rtp` and the counterparty account is not eligible for RTP, the `/transfer/authorization/create` request will fail with an `INVALID_FIELD` error code. To pre-check to determine whether a counterparty account can support RTP, call `/transfer/capabilities/get` before calling `/transfer/authorization/create`.<br><br>Wire transfers are currently in early availability. To request access to `wire` as a payment network, contact your account manager. For transfers submitted as `wire`, the `type` must be `credit`; wire debits are not supported. The cutoff to submit a wire payment is 6:30 PM Eastern Time on a business day; wires submitted after that time will be processed on the next business day. The transaction limit for a wire is $999,999.99. Authorization requests sent with an amount greater than $999,999.99 will fail.<br><br>Support for `rfp` (request for payment) is currently in closed beta. To learn more, contact your Plaid account manager. For transfers submitted as `rfp`, the `type` must be `debit`.|
|wire_details|[TransferWireDetails](#schematransferwiredetails)|false|none|Information specific to wire transfers.|
|cancellable|boolean|true|none|When `true`, you can still cancel this transfer.|
|failure_reason|[TransferFailure](#schematransferfailure)|true|none|The failure reason if the event type for a transfer is `"failed"` or `"returned"`, or the adjustment reason if the event type is `"adjustment"`. Null value otherwise.|
|metadata|[TransferMetadata](#schematransfermetadata)|true|none|The Metadata object is a mapping of client-provided string fields to any string value. The following limitations apply:<br>The JSON values must be Strings (no nested JSON objects allowed)<br>Only ASCII characters may be used<br>Maximum of 50 key/value pairs<br>Maximum key length of 40 characters<br>Maximum value length of 500 characters<br>|
|origination_account_id|string|true|none|**Deprecated.** Plaid's unique identifier for the origination account that was used for this transfer.|
|guarantee_decision|object|true|none|**Deprecated.**|
|guarantee_decision_rationale|[TransferAuthorizationGuaranteeDecisionRationale](#schematransferauthorizationguaranteedecisionrationale)|true|none|**Deprecated.** The rationale for Plaid's decision to not guarantee a transfer. Will be `null` unless `guarantee_decision` is `NOT_GUARANTEED`.|
|guarantee_details|[TransferGuaranteeDetails](#schematransferguaranteedetails)|false|none|Adaptive guarantee details for a transfer, including the guaranteed amount and settlement schedule. Omitted when no guarantee was attempted.|
|iso_currency_code|string|true|none|The currency of the transfer amount, e.g. "USD"|
|standard_return_window|string(date) \| null|true|none|The date 3 business days from settlement date indicating the following ACH returns can no longer happen: R01, R02, R03, R29. This will be of the form YYYY-MM-DD.|
|unauthorized_return_window|string(date) \| null|true|none|The date 61 business days from settlement date indicating the following ACH returns can no longer happen: R05, R07, R10, R11, R51, R33, R37, R38, R52, R53. This will be of the form YYYY-MM-DD.|
|expected_settlement_date|string(date) \| null|true|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated for Plaid Ledger clients, use `expected_funds_available_date` instead.|
|expected_funds_available_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The expected date when funds from a transfer will be made available and can be withdrawn from the associated ledger balance, assuming the debit does not return before this date. If the transfer does return before this date, this field will be null. Only applies to debit transfers. This will be of the form YYYY-MM-DD.|
|originator_client_id|string \| null|true|none|The Plaid client ID that is the originator of this transfer. Only present if created on behalf of another client as a [Platform customer](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/application/#originators-vs-platforms).|
|refunds|[[TransferRefund](#schematransferrefund)]|true|none|A list of refunds associated with this transfer.|
|recurring_transfer_id|string \| null|true|none|The id of the recurring transfer if this transfer belongs to a recurring transfer.|
|expected_sweep_settlement_schedule|[[TransferExpectedSweepSettlementScheduleItem](#schematransferexpectedsweepsettlementscheduleitem)]|false|none|The expected sweep settlement schedule of this transfer, assuming this transfer is not `returned`. Only applies to ACH debit transfers.|

<h2 id="tocS_ACHClass">ACHClass</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaachclass"></a>
<a id="schema_ACHClass"></a>
<a id="tocSachclass"></a>
<a id="tocsachclass"></a>

```json
"ccd"
```

Specifies the use case of the transfer. Required for transfers on an ACH network. For more details, see [ACH SEC codes](https://plaid.com/docs/transfer/creating-transfers/#ach-sec-codes).

Codes supported for credits: `ccd`, `ppd`
Codes supported for debits: `ccd`, `ppd`, `tel`, `web`

`"ccd"` - Corporate Credit or Debit - fund transfer between two corporate bank accounts

`"ppd"` - Prearranged Payment or Deposit - The transfer is part of a pre-existing relationship with a consumer. Authorization was obtained in writing either in person or via an electronic document signing, e.g. Docusign, by the consumer. Can be used for credits or debits.

`"web"` - Internet-Initiated Entry. The transfer debits a consumer's bank account. Authorization from the consumer is obtained over the Internet (e.g. a web or mobile application). Can be used for single debits or recurring debits.

`"tel"` - Telephone-Initiated Entry. The transfer debits a consumer. Debit authorization has been received orally over the telephone via a recorded call.

```

This field is now deprecated. You may ignore it for transfers created on and after 12/01/2023.

Specifies the source of funds for the transfer. Only valid for `credit` transfers, and defaults to `sweep` if not specified. This field is not specified for `debit` transfers.

`sweep` - Sweep funds from your funding account
`prefunded_rtp_credits` - Use your prefunded RTP credit balance with Plaid
`prefunded_ach_credits` - Use your prefunded ACH credit balance with Plaid

<h2 id="tocS_TransferCreateIdempotencyKey">TransferCreateIdempotencyKey</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransfercreateidempotencykey"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferCreateIdempotencyKey"></a>
<a id="tocStransfercreateidempotencykey"></a>
<a id="tocstransfercreateidempotencykey"></a>

```json
"string"
```

Deprecated. `authorization_id` is now used as idempotency instead.

A random key provided by the client, per unique transfer. Maximum of 50 characters.

The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create a transfer fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single transfer is created.

<h2 id="tocS_TransferAuthorizationIdempotencyKey">TransferAuthorizationIdempotencyKey</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferauthorizationidempotencykey"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferAuthorizationIdempotencyKey"></a>
<a id="tocStransferauthorizationidempotencykey"></a>
<a id="tocstransferauthorizationidempotencykey"></a>

```json
"string"
```

A random key provided by the client, per unique authorization, which expires after 48 hours. Maximum of 50 characters.

The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create an authorization fails due to a network connection error, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single authorization is created.

Idempotency does not apply to authorizations whose decisions are `user_action_required`. Therefore you may re-attempt the authorization after completing the required user action without changing `idempotency_key`.

This idempotency key expires after 48 hours, after which the same key can be reused. Failure to provide this key may result in duplicate charges.

<h2 id="tocS_TransferAuthorizationDecisionRationaleCode">TransferAuthorizationDecisionRationaleCode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferauthorizationdecisionrationalecode"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferAuthorizationDecisionRationaleCode"></a>
<a id="tocStransferauthorizationdecisionrationalecode"></a>
<a id="tocstransferauthorizationdecisionrationalecode"></a>

```json
"NSF"
```

A code representing the rationale for approving or declining the proposed transfer.

If the `rationale_code` is `null`, the transfer passed the authorization check.

Any non-`null` value for an `approved` transfer indicates that the authorization check could not be run and that you should perform your own risk assessment on the transfer. The code will indicate why the check could not be run. Possible values for an `approved` transfer are:

`MANUALLY_VERIFIED_ITEM` - Item created via a manual entry flow (i.e. Same-Day Micro-deposit, Instant Micro-deposit, or database-based verification), limited information available.

`ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` - Unable to collect the account information due to Item staleness. Can be resolved by using Link and setting [`transfer.authorization_id`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/#link-token-create-request-transfer-authorization-id) in the request to `/link/token/create`.

`PAYMENT_PROFILE_LOGIN_REQUIRED` - The Payment Profile associated with the call to `/transfer/authorization/create` is in a state that requires the end user to re-authenticate. Can be resolved by using Link to refresh the Payment Profile.

`MIGRATED_ACCOUNT_ITEM` - Item created via `/transfer/migrate_account` endpoint, limited information available.

`ERROR` - Unable to collect the account information due to an unspecified error.

These codes can also accompany a `declined` decision, for example when your Signal Rules decline the transfer.

The following codes indicate that the authorization decision was `declined`:

`NSF` - Transaction has an elevated risk of resulting in a return due to insufficient funds.

`RISK` - Transaction is high-risk.

`TRANSFER_LIMIT_REACHED` - One or several transfer limits are reached, e.g. monthly transfer limit. Check the accompanying `description` field to understand which limit has been reached.

`ADMIN` - Transaction has an elevated risk of resulting in an administrative return (for example a closed, invalid, or unauthorized account).

`FRAUD` - Transaction has an elevated risk of being fraudulent.

```json

  "code": "NSF",
  "description": "string"
}
```

The rationale for Plaid's decision regarding a proposed transfer. It is always set for `declined` decisions, and may or may not be null for `approved` decisions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|[TransferAuthorizationDecisionRationaleCode](#schematransferauthorizationdecisionrationalecode)|true|none|A code representing the rationale for approving or declining the proposed transfer.<br><br>If the `rationale_code` is `null`, the transfer passed the authorization check.<br><br>Any non-`null` value for an `approved` transfer indicates that the authorization check could not be run and that you should perform your own risk assessment on the transfer. The code will indicate why the check could not be run. Possible values for an `approved` transfer are:<br><br>`MANUALLY_VERIFIED_ITEM` - Item created via a manual entry flow (i.e. Same-Day Micro-deposit, Instant Micro-deposit, or database-based verification), limited information available.<br><br>`ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED` - Unable to collect the account information due to Item staleness. Can be resolved by using Link and setting [`transfer.authorization_id`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/#link-token-create-request-transfer-authorization-id) in the request to `/link/token/create`.<br><br>`PAYMENT_PROFILE_LOGIN_REQUIRED` - The Payment Profile associated with the call to `/transfer/authorization/create` is in a state that requires the end user to re-authenticate. Can be resolved by using Link to refresh the Payment Profile.<br><br>`MIGRATED_ACCOUNT_ITEM` - Item created via `/transfer/migrate_account` endpoint, limited information available.<br><br>`ERROR` - Unable to collect the account information due to an unspecified error.<br><br>These codes can also accompany a `declined` decision, for example when your Signal Rules decline the transfer.<br><br>The following codes indicate that the authorization decision was `declined`:<br><br>`NSF` - Transaction has an elevated risk of resulting in a return due to insufficient funds.<br><br>`RISK` - Transaction is high-risk.<br><br>`TRANSFER_LIMIT_REACHED` - One or several transfer limits are reached, e.g. monthly transfer limit. Check the accompanying `description` field to understand which limit has been reached.<br><br>`ADMIN` - Transaction has an elevated risk of resulting in an administrative return (for example a closed, invalid, or unauthorized account).<br><br>`FRAUD` - Transaction has an elevated risk of being fraudulent.|
|description|string|true|none|A human-readable description of the code associated with a transfer approval or transfer decline.|

#### Enumerated Values

|code|RISK|

|code|PAYMENT_PROFILE_LOGIN_REQUIRED|
|code|ERROR|
|code|MIGRATED_ACCOUNT_ITEM|
|code|ADMIN|
|code|FRAUD|
|code|null|

<h2 id="tocS_TransferGuaranteeOutcome">TransferGuaranteeOutcome</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="tocStransferguaranteeoutcome"></a>
<a id="tocstransferguaranteeoutcome"></a>

```json
"FULL_INSTANT"
```

The adaptive guarantee outcome for a transfer.

`FULL_INSTANT`: The full transfer amount is guaranteed and funds are available instantly.

`PARTIAL_INSTANT_ONLY`: A partial amount is guaranteed and available instantly; the remainder is not guaranteed.

`PARTIAL_INSTANT_WITH_OBSERVATION_WINDOW`: A partial amount is guaranteed instantly; an additional amount is conditionally guaranteed subject to an observation window.

`NOT_GUARANTEED`: Plaid did not provide a guarantee for this transfer.

  "observation_window_expiration_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

A single entry in the adaptive guarantee settlement schedule, describing one tranche of guaranteed funds. Adds `observation_window_expiration_time`, which is only known once a transfer is created.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|string|true|none|The guaranteed amount for this schedule entry (decimal string with two digits of precision e.g. "10.00").|
|observation_window_business_days|integer|true|none|The number of business days in the observation window for this tranche. `0` when the tranche is not subject to an observation window.|
|observation_window_expiration_time|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The datetime when the observation window for this tranche expires. Present only when the tranche is subject to an observation window. This will be of the form `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`.|

<h2 id="tocS_TransferAuthorizationGuaranteeDecisionRationaleCode">TransferAuthorizationGuaranteeDecisionRationaleCode</h2>

```json
"RETURN_BANK"
```

A code representing the reason Plaid declined to guarantee this transfer:

`RETURN_BANK`: The risk of a bank-initiated return (for example, an R01/NSF) is too high to guarantee this transfer.

`RETURN_CUSTOMER`: The risk of a customer-initiated return (for example, a R10/Unauthorized) is too high to guarantee this transfer.

`GUARANTEE_LIMIT_REACHED`: This transfer is low-risk, but Guarantee has exhausted an internal limit on the number or rate of guarantees that applies to this transfer.

`RISK_ESTIMATE_UNAVAILABLE`: A risk estimate is unavailable for this Item.

`REQUIRED_PARAM_MISSING`: Required fields are missing.

<h2 id="tocS_TransferRecurringSchedule">TransferRecurringSchedule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferrecurringschedule"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferRecurringSchedule"></a>
<a id="tocStransferrecurringschedule"></a>
<a id="tocstransferrecurringschedule"></a>

```json
{
  "interval_unit": "week",
  "interval_count": 0,
  "interval_execution_day": 0,
  "start_date": "1970-01-01",
  "end_date": "1970-01-01"
}
```

The schedule that the recurring transfer will be executed on.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|interval_unit|[TransferScheduleIntervalUnit](#schematransferscheduleintervalunit)|true|none|The unit of the recurring interval.|
|interval_count|[TransferScheduleIntervalCount](#schematransferscheduleintervalcount)|true|none|The number of recurring `interval_units` between originations. The recurring interval (before holiday adjustment) is calculated by multiplying `interval_unit` and `interval_count`.<br>For example, to schedule a recurring transfer which originates once every two weeks, set `interval_unit` = `week` and `interval_count` = 2.|
|interval_execution_day|integer|true|none|The day of the interval on which to schedule the transfer.<br><br>If the `interval_unit` is `week`, `interval_execution_day` should be an integer from 1 (Monday) to 5 (Friday).<br><br>If the `interval_unit` is `month`, `interval_execution_day` should be an integer indicating which day of the month to make the transfer on. Integers from 1 to 28 can be used to make a transfer on that day of the month. Negative integers from -1 to -5 can be used to make a transfer relative to the end of the month. To make a transfer on the last day of the month, use -1; to make the transfer on the second-to-last day, use -2, and so on.<br><br>The transfer will be originated on the next available banking day if the designated day is a non banking day.|
|start_date|string(date)|true|none|A date in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD). The recurring transfer will begin on the first `interval_execution_day` on or after the `start_date`.<br><br>For `rtp` recurring transfers, `start_date` must be in the future.<br>Otherwise, if the first `interval_execution_day` on or after the start date is also the same day that `/transfer/recurring/create` was called, the bank *may* make the first payment on that day, but it is not guaranteed to do so.|
|end_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|A date in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD). The recurring transfer will end on the last `interval_execution_day` on or before the `end_date`.<br>If the `interval_execution_day` between the start date and the end date (inclusive) is also the same day that `/transfer/recurring/create` was called, the bank *may* make a payment on that day, but it is not guaranteed to do so.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|interval_unit|week|
|interval_unit|month|

<h2 id="tocS_TransferStatus">TransferStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferStatus"></a>
<a id="tocStransferstatus"></a>
<a id="tocstransferstatus"></a>

```json
"pending"
```

The status of the transfer.

`pending`: A new transfer was created; it is in the pending state.

`posted`: The transfer has been successfully submitted to the payment network.

`settled`: The transfer was successfully completed by the payment network. Note that funds from received debits are not available to be moved out of the Ledger until the transfer reaches `funds_available` status. For credit transactions, `settled` means the funds have been delivered to the receiving bank account. This is the terminal state of a successful credit transfer.

`funds_available`: Funds from the transfer have been released from hold and applied to the ledger's available balance. (Only applicable to ACH debits.) This is the terminal state of a successful debit transfer.

`cancelled`: The transfer was cancelled by the client. This is the terminal state of a cancelled transfer.

`failed`: The transfer failed, no funds were moved. This is the terminal state of a failed transfer.

`returned`: A posted transfer was returned. This is the terminal state of a returned transfer.

`swept`: The transfer was swept to the sweep account.

`swept_settled`: Credits are available to be withdrawn or debits have been deducted from the customer's business checking account.

`return_swept`: The transfer was returned, funds were pulled back or pushed back to the sweep account.

`null`: The transfer will never be swept (e.g. if the transfer is cancelled or returned before being swept)

<h2 id="tocS_TransferIntentCreateNetwork">TransferIntentCreateNetwork</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferintentcreatenetwork"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferIntentCreateNetwork"></a>
<a id="tocStransferintentcreatenetwork"></a>
<a id="tocstransferintentcreatenetwork"></a>

```json
"same-day-ach"
```

The network or rails used for the transfer. Defaults to `same-day-ach`.

For transfers submitted using `ach`, the Standard ACH cutoff is 8:30 PM Eastern Time.

For transfers submitted using `same-day-ach`, the Same Day ACH cutoff is 3:00 PM Eastern Time. It is recommended to send the request 15 minutes prior to the cutoff to ensure that it will be processed in time for submission before the cutoff. If the transfer is processed after this cutoff but before the Standard ACH cutoff, it will be sent over Standard ACH rails and will not incur same-day charges.

For transfers submitted using `rtp`, in the case that the account being credited does not support RTP, the transfer will be sent over ACH as long as an `ach_class` is provided in the request. If RTP isn't supported by the account and no `ach_class` is provided, the transfer will fail to be submitted.

<h2 id="tocS_TransferNetwork">TransferNetwork</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransfernetwork"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferNetwork"></a>
<a id="tocStransfernetwork"></a>
<a id="tocstransfernetwork"></a>

```json
"ach"
```

The network or rails used for the transfer.

For transfers submitted as `ach` or `same-day-ach`, the Standard ACH cutoff is 8:30 PM Eastern Time.

For transfers submitted as `same-day-ach`, the Same Day ACH cutoff is 3:00 PM Eastern Time.  It is recommended to send the request 15 minutes prior to the cutoff to ensure that it will be processed in time for submission before the cutoff. If the transfer is processed after this cutoff but before the Standard ACH cutoff, it will be sent over Standard ACH rails and will not incur same-day charges; this will apply to both legs of the transfer if applicable. The transaction limit for a Same Day ACH transfer is $1,000,000. Authorization requests sent with an amount greater than $1,000,000 will fail.

For transfers submitted as `rtp`, Plaid will automatically route between the Real-Time Payments (RTP) rail by TCH or FedNow rails as necessary. If a transfer is submitted as `rtp` and the counterparty account is not eligible for RTP, the `/transfer/authorization/create` request will fail with an `INVALID_FIELD` error code. To pre-check to determine whether a counterparty account can support RTP, call `/transfer/capabilities/get` before calling `/transfer/authorization/create`.

Wire transfers are currently in early availability. To request access to `wire` as a payment network, contact your account manager. For transfers submitted as `wire`, the `type` must be `credit`; wire debits are not supported. The cutoff to submit a wire payment is 6:30 PM Eastern Time on a business day; wires submitted after that time will be processed on the next business day. The transaction limit for a wire is $999,999.99. Authorization requests sent with an amount greater than $999,999.99 will fail.

Support for `rfp` (request for payment) is currently in closed beta. To learn more, contact your Plaid account manager. For transfers submitted as `rfp`, the `type` must be `debit`.

<h2 id="tocS_TransferACHNetwork">TransferACHNetwork</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferachnetwork"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferACHNetwork"></a>
<a id="tocStransferachnetwork"></a>
<a id="tocstransferachnetwork"></a>

```json
"ach"
```

The ACH networks used for the funds flow.

For requests submitted as either `ach` or `same-day-ach` the cutoff for Same Day ACH is 3:00 PM Eastern Time and the cutoff for Standard ACH transfers is 8:30 PM Eastern Time. It is recommended to submit a request at least 15 minutes before the cutoff time in order to ensure that it will be processed before the cutoff. Any request that is indicated as `same-day-ach` and that misses the Same Day ACH cutoff, but is submitted in time for the Standard ACH cutoff, will be sent over Standard ACH rails and will not incur same-day charges.

<h2 id="tocS_TransferAuthorizationDecision">TransferAuthorizationDecision</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferauthorizationdecision"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferAuthorizationDecision"></a>
<a id="tocStransferauthorizationdecision"></a>
<a id="tocstransferauthorizationdecision"></a>

```json
"approved"
```


A decision regarding the proposed transfer.

`approved` - The proposed transfer has received the end user's consent and has been approved for processing by Plaid. The `decision_rationale` field is set if Plaid was unable to fetch the account information. You may proceed with the transfer, but further review is recommended. Refer to the `code` field in the `decision_rationale` object for details.

`declined` - Plaid reviewed the proposed transfer and declined processing. Refer to the `code` field in the `decision_rationale` object for details.

`user_action_required` - An action is required before Plaid can assess the transfer risk and make a decision. The most common scenario is to update authentication for an Item. To complete the required action, initialize Link by setting `transfer.authorization_id` in the request of `/link/token/create`. After Link flow is completed, you may re-attempt the authorization request.

For `guarantee` requests, `approved` indicates the transfer is eligible for Plaid's guarantee, and `declined` indicates Plaid will not provide guarantee coverage for the transfer. `user_action_required` indicates you should follow the above guidance before re-attempting.
