### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|income_source_id|string|false|none|A unique identifier for an income source.|
|income_description|string|false|none|The most common name or original description for the underlying income transactions.|
|income_category|[CreditBankIncomeCategory](#schemacreditbankincomecategory)|false|none|The income category.<br><br>`BANK_INTEREST`: Interest earned from a bank account.<br><br>`BENEFIT_OTHER`: Government benefits other than retirement, unemployment, child support, or disability. Currently used only in the UK, to represent benefits such as Cost of Living Payments.<br><br>`CASH`: Deprecated and used only for existing legacy implementations. Has been replaced by `CASH_DEPOSIT` and `TRANSFER_FROM_APPLICATION`.<br><br>`CASH_DEPOSIT`: A cash or check deposit.<br><br>`CHILD_SUPPORT`: Child support payments received.<br><br>`GIG_ECONOMY`: Income earned as a gig economy worker, e.g. driving for Uber, Lyft, Postmates, DoorDash, etc.<br><br>`LONG_TERM_DISABILITY`: Disability payments, including Social Security disability benefits.<br><br>`OTHER`: Income that could not be categorized as any other income category.<br><br>`MILITARY`: Veterans benefits. Income earned as salary for serving in the military (e.g. through DFAS) will be classified as `SALARY` rather than `MILITARY`.<br><br>`RENTAL`: Income earned from a rental property. Income may be identified as rental when the payment is received through a rental platform, e.g. Airbnb; rent paid directly by the tenant to the property owner (e.g. via cash, check, or ACH) will typically not be classified as rental income.<br><br>`RETIREMENT`: Payments from private retirement systems, pensions, and government retirement programs, including Social Security retirement benefits.<br><br>`SALARY`: Payment from an employer to an earner or other form of permanent employment.<br><br>`TAX_REFUND`: A tax refund.<br><br>`TRANSFER_FROM_APPLICATION`: Deposits from a money transfer app, such as Venmo, Cash App, or Zelle.<br><br>`UNEMPLOYMENT`: Unemployment benefits. In the UK, includes certain low-income benefits such as the Universal Credit.|
|account_id|string|false|none|Plaid's unique identifier for the account.|
|start_date|string(date)|false|none|Minimum of all dates within the specific income sources in the user's bank account for days requested by the client.<br>The date will be returned in an ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|end_date|string(date)|false|none|Maximum of all dates within the specific income sources in the user's bank account for days requested by the client.<br>The date will be returned in an ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|pay_frequency|[CreditBankIncomePayFrequency](#schemacreditbankincomepayfrequency)|false|none|The income pay frequency.|
|total_amount|number|false|none|Total amount of earnings in the user's bank account for the specific income source for days requested by the client.|
|transaction_count|integer|false|none|Number of transactions for the income source within the start and end date.|
|historical_summary|[[CreditBankIncomeHistoricalSummary](#schemacreditbankincomehistoricalsummary)]|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_CreditBankIncomeCategory">CreditBankIncomeCategory</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreditbankincomecategory"></a>
<a id="schema_CreditBankIncomeCategory"></a>
<a id="tocScreditbankincomecategory"></a>
<a id="tocscreditbankincomecategory"></a>

```json
"SALARY"
```

The income category.

`BANK_INTEREST`: Interest earned from a bank account.

`BENEFIT_OTHER`: Government benefits other than retirement, unemployment, child support, or disability. Currently used only in the UK, to represent benefits such as Cost of Living Payments.

`CASH`: Deprecated and used only for existing legacy implementations. Has been replaced by `CASH_DEPOSIT` and `TRANSFER_FROM_APPLICATION`.

`CASH_DEPOSIT`: A cash or check deposit.

`CHILD_SUPPORT`: Child support payments received.

`GIG_ECONOMY`: Income earned as a gig economy worker, e.g. driving for Uber, Lyft, Postmates, DoorDash, etc.

`LONG_TERM_DISABILITY`: Disability payments, including Social Security disability benefits.

`OTHER`: Income that could not be categorized as any other income category.

`MILITARY`: Veterans benefits. Income earned as salary for serving in the military (e.g. through DFAS) will be classified as `SALARY` rather than `MILITARY`.

`RENTAL`: Income earned from a rental property. Income may be identified as rental when the payment is received through a rental platform, e.g. Airbnb; rent paid directly by the tenant to the property owner (e.g. via cash, check, or ACH) will typically not be classified as rental income.

`RETIREMENT`: Payments from private retirement systems, pensions, and government retirement programs, including Social Security retirement benefits.

`SALARY`: Payment from an employer to an earner or other form of permanent employment.

`TAX_REFUND`: A tax refund.

`TRANSFER_FROM_APPLICATION`: Deposits from a money transfer app, such as Venmo, Cash App, or Zelle.

`UNEMPLOYMENT`: Unemployment benefits. In the UK, includes certain low-income benefits such as the Universal Credit.

|iso_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The ISO 4217 currency code of the amount or balance.<br>Please use [`total_amounts`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/income/#credit-bank_income-get-response-bank-income-items-bank-income-sources-historical-summary-total-amounts) instead.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The unofficial currency code associated with the amount or balance. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-null.<br>Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br>Please use [`total_amounts`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/income/#credit-bank_income-get-response-bank-income-items-bank-income-sources-historical-summary-total-amounts) instead.|

|end_date|string(date)|false|none|The end date of the period included in this monthly summary.<br>This date will be the last day of the month, unless the month being covered is a partial month because it is the last month included in the summary and the date range being requested does not end with the last day of the month.<br>The date will be returned in an ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).|

The transactions data for the end user's income source(s).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|number|false|none|The settled value of the transaction, denominated in the transaction's currency as stated in `iso_currency_code` or `unofficial_currency_code`.<br>Positive values when money moves out of the account; negative values when money moves in.<br>For example, credit card purchases are positive; credit card payment, direct deposits, and refunds are negative.|
|date|string(date)|false|none|For pending transactions, the date that the transaction occurred; for posted transactions, the date that the transaction posted.<br>Both dates are returned in an ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|name|string|false|none|The merchant name or transaction description.|
|original_description|string \| null|false|none|The string returned by the financial institution to describe the transaction.|
|pending|boolean|false|none|When true, identifies the transaction as pending or unsettled.<br>Pending transaction details (name, type, amount, category ID) may change before they are settled.|
|transaction_id|string|false|none|The unique ID of the transaction. Like all Plaid identifiers, the `transaction_id` is case sensitive.|
|check_number|string \| null|false|none|The check number of the transaction. This field is only populated for check transactions.|
|iso_currency_code|[CreditIsoCurrencyCode](#schemacreditisocurrencycode)|false|none|The ISO 4217 currency code of the amount or balance.|
|unofficial_currency_code|[CreditUnofficialCurrencyCode](#schemacreditunofficialcurrencycode)|false|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the amount or balance. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-null.<br>Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.|

Object containing fraud risk data for a set of income documents.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string \| null|true|none|ID of the payroll provider account.|
|single_document_risk_signals|[[SingleDocumentRiskSignal](#schemasingledocumentrisksignal)]|true|none|Array of document metadata and associated risk signals per document|
|multi_document_risk_signals|[[MultiDocumentRiskSignal](#schemamultidocumentrisksignal)]|true|none|Array of risk signals computed from a set of uploaded documents and the associated documents' metadata|

<a id="schemadocumentrisksummary"></a>

<a id="tocSdocumentrisksummary"></a>
<a id="tocsdocumentrisksummary"></a>

```json
{
  "risk_score": 0
}
```

A summary across all risk signals associated with a document

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|risk_score|number \| null|true|none|A number between 0 and 100, inclusive, where a score closer to 0 indicates a document is likely to be trustworthy and a score closer to 100 indicates a document is likely to be fraudulent. You can automatically reject documents with a high risk score, automatically accept documents with a low risk score, and manually review documents in between. We suggest starting with a threshold of 80 for auto-rejection and 20 for auto-acceptance. As you gather more data points on typical risk scores for your use case, you can tune these parameters to reduce the number of documents undergoing manual review.|

Use these in preference to HTTP status codes to identify and handle specific errors. HTTP status codes are set and provide the broadest categorization of errors: 4xx codes are for developer- or user-related errors, and 5xx codes are for Plaid-related errors, and the status will be 2xx in non-error cases. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|

<h2 id="tocS_CreditDocumentMetadata">CreditDocumentMetadata</h2>

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "document_type": "string",
  "download_url": "string",
  "status": "string",
  "page_count": 0,
  "error_message": "string"
}
```

Object representing metadata pertaining to the document.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the document.|
|document_type|[CreditDocumentType](#schemacreditdocumenttype)|true|none|The type of document.<br><br>`PAYSTUB`: A paystub.<br><br>`BANK_STATEMENT`: A bank statement.<br><br>`US_TAX_W2`: A W-2 wage and tax statement provided by a US employer reflecting wages earned by the employee.<br><br>`US_TAX_1099_MISC`: A 1099-MISC tax form reporting miscellaneous income.<br><br>`US_TAX_1099_K`: A 1099-K tax form reporting payment card and third-party network transactions.<br><br>`US_STUDENT_I20`: A Certificate of Eligibility for Nonimmigrant Student Status (Form I-20) issued by a US school.<br><br>`US_MILITARY_ERAS`: An electronic Retirement Account Statement (eRAS) issued by the US military.<br><br>`US_MILITARY_LES`: A Leave and Earnings Statement (LES) issued by the US military.<br><br>`US_MILITARY_CLES`: A Civilian Leave and Earnings Statement (CLES) issued by the US military.<br><br>`GIG`: Used to indicate that the income is related to gig work. Does not necessarily correspond to a specific document type.<br><br>`PLAID_GENERATED_PAYSTUB_PDF`: Used to indicate that the PDF for the paystub was generated by Plaid.<br><br>`NONE`: Used to indicate that there is no underlying document for the data.<br><br>`UNKNOWN`: Document type could not be determined.|
|download_url|string \| null|true|none|Signed URL to retrieve the document(s). The payload will be a .zip file containing the document(s).<br><br>For Payroll Income, the file type of the documents will always be PDF, and the documents may not be available, in which case the field will be `null`. If you would like Plaid to generate a PDF if the original is not available, contact your account manager. [Example generated pay stub](https://plaid.com/documents/plaid-generated-mock-paystub.pdf).<br><br>For Document Income, this field will not be `null`, and the file type of the underlying document(s) will be the original file type uploaded by the user. For more details on available file types, see the [Document Income](https://plaid.com/docs/income/document-income) documentation.<br><br>This download URL can only be used once and expires after two minutes. To generate a new download URL, call `/credit/payroll_income/get` again.|
|status|string \| null|true|none|The processing status of the document.<br><br>`PROCESSING_COMPLETE`: The document was successfully processed.<br><br>`DOCUMENT_ERROR`: The document could not be processed. Possible causes include: The document was an unacceptable document type such as an offer letter or bank statement, the document image was cropped or blurry, or the document was corrupted.<br><br>`UNKNOWN` or `null`: An internal error occurred. If this happens repeatedly, contact support or your Plaid account manager.|
|page_count|integer \| null|false|none|The number of pages of the uploaded document (if available).|
|error_message|string \| null|false|none|The reason why a failure occurred during document processing (if available).|

<h2 id="tocS_CreditDocumentType">CreditDocumentType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreditdocumenttype"></a>
<a id="schema_CreditDocumentType"></a>
<a id="tocScreditdocumenttype"></a>
<a id="tocscreditdocumenttype"></a>

```json
"string"
```

The type of document.

`PAYSTUB`: A paystub.

`BANK_STATEMENT`: A bank statement.

`US_TAX_W2`: A W-2 wage and tax statement provided by a US employer reflecting wages earned by the employee.

`US_TAX_1099_MISC`: A 1099-MISC tax form reporting miscellaneous income.

`US_TAX_1099_K`: A 1099-K tax form reporting payment card and third-party network transactions.

`US_STUDENT_I20`: A Certificate of Eligibility for Nonimmigrant Student Status (Form I-20) issued by a US school.

`US_MILITARY_ERAS`: An electronic Retirement Account Statement (eRAS) issued by the US military.

`US_MILITARY_LES`: A Leave and Earnings Statement (LES) issued by the US military.

`US_MILITARY_CLES`: A Civilian Leave and Earnings Statement (CLES) issued by the US military.

`GIG`: Used to indicate that the income is related to gig work. Does not necessarily correspond to a specific document type.

`PLAID_GENERATED_PAYSTUB_PDF`: Used to indicate that the PDF for the paystub was generated by Plaid.

`NONE`: Used to indicate that there is no underlying document for the data.

`UNKNOWN`: Document type could not be determined.

The warning code identifies a specific kind of warning.

`IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE`: Unable to extract identity for the Item

`TRANSACTIONS_UNAVAILABLE`: Unable to extract transactions for the Item

`ITEM_UNAPPROVED`: User exited flow before giving permission to share data for the Item

`REPORT_DELETED`: Report deleted due to customer or consumer request

`DATA_UNAVAILABLE`: No relevant data was found for the Item

An error object and associated `item_id` used to identify a specific Item and error when a batch operation operating on multiple Items has encountered an error in one of the Items.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error_type|[CreditBankIncomeErrorType](#schemacreditbankincomeerrortype)|true|none|A broad categorization of the error. Safe for programmatic use.|
|error_code|string|true|none|We use standard HTTP response codes for success and failure notifications, and our errors are further classified by `error_type`. In general, 200 HTTP codes correspond to success, 40X codes are for developer- or user-related failures, and 50X codes are for Plaid-related issues. Error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred.|
|error_message|string|true|none|A developer-friendly representation of the error code. This may change over time and is not safe for programmatic use.|
|display_message|string|true|none|A user-friendly representation of the error code. null if the error is not related to user action.<br>This may change over time and is not safe for programmatic use.|
|item_id|string|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this warning.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|error_type|COUNTRY_NOT_SUPPORTED|
|error_type|INSTITUTION_DOWN|
|error_type|INSTITUTION_NO_LONGER_SUPPORTED|

|error_type|INVALID_MFA|

The product access being requested. Used to allow or disallow product access across all accounts. If unset, defaults to all products allowed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|statements|boolean \| null|false|none|Allow access to statements. Only used by certain partners. If relevant to the partner and unset, defaults to `true`.|
|identity|boolean \| null|false|none|Allow access to the Identity product (name, email, phone, address). Only used by certain partners. If relevant to the partner and unset, defaults to `true`.|
|auth|boolean \| null|false|none|Allow access to account number details. Only used by certain partners. If relevant to the partner and unset, defaults to `true`.|
|transactions|boolean \| null|false|none|Allow access to transaction details. Only used by certain partners. If relevant to the partner and unset, defaults to `true`.|
|accounts_details_transactions|boolean \| null|false|none|Allow access to `accounts_details_transactions`. Only used by certain partners. If relevant to the partner and unset, defaults to `true`.|
|accounts_routing_number|boolean \| null|false|none|Allow access to `accounts_routing_number`. Only used by certain partners. If relevant to the partner and unset, defaults to `true`.|
|accounts_statements|boolean \| null|false|none|Allow access to `accounts_statements`. Only used by certain partners. If relevant to the partner and unset, defaults to `true`.|
|accounts_tax_statements|boolean \| null|false|none|Allow access to `accounts_tax_statements`. Only used by certain partners. If relevant to the partner and unset, defaults to `true`.|
|customers_profiles|boolean \| null|false|none|Allow access to `customers_profiles`. Only used by certain partners. If relevant to the partner and unset, defaults to `true`.|

<a id="tocsaccountselectioncardinality"></a>

```json
"SINGLE_SELECT"
```

The application requires that accounts be limited to a specific cardinality.

`MULTI_SELECT`: indicates that the user should be allowed to pick multiple accounts.

`SINGLE_SELECT`: indicates that the user should be allowed to pick only a single account.

`ALL`: indicates that the user must share all of their accounts and should not be given the opportunity to de-select

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|item_id|string|false|none|The Plaid Item ID. The `item_id` is always unique; linking the same account at the same institution twice will result in two Items with different `item_id` values. Like all Plaid identifiers, the `item_id` is case-sensitive.|

|initiator|[ConsentEventInitiator](#schemaconsenteventinitiator)|false|none|The entity that initiated collection of consent.|
|consented_use_cases|[string]|false|none|A list of strings containing the full list of use cases the end user has consented to for the Item.<br><br>See the [full list](https://plaid.com/docs/link/data-transparency-messaging-migration-guide/#updating-link-customizations) of use cases.|
|consented_data_scopes|[string]|false|none|A list of strings containing the full list of data scopes the end user has consented to for the Item. Each value is the data scope's display name, as shown to the end user in Link (for example, `account and balance info`, `contact details`, or `transactions`); these differ from the values returned in `consented_data_scopes` by `/item/get`. The scopes correspond to consented products; see the [full mapping](https://plaid.com/docs/link/data-transparency-messaging-migration-guide/#data-scopes-by-product) of data scopes and products.|

SandboxIncomeFireWebhookRequest defines the request schema for `/sandbox/income/fire_webhook`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|

|item_id|string|true|none|The Item ID associated with the verification.|
|user_id|string|false|none|The user identifier to include in the test webhook. For `USER_INCOME_VERIFICATION` and `USER_INCOME_VERIFICATION_RISK_SIGNALS`, use the `user_id` returned by `/user/create`, which begins with `usr_`. For `INCOME_VERIFICATION` and `INCOME_VERIFICATION_RISK_SIGNALS`, use the legacy webhook `user_id` associated with the user token.|
|webhook|string(url)|true|none|The URL to which the webhook should be sent.|
|verification_status|string|false|none|Required when `webhook_code` is `INCOME_VERIFICATION` or `USER_INCOME_VERIFICATION`.<br><br>`VERIFICATION_STATUS_PROCESSING_COMPLETE`: The income verification status processing has completed. If the user uploaded multiple documents, this webhook will fire when all documents have finished processing. Call the `/income/verification/paystubs/get` endpoint and check the document metadata to see which documents were successfully parsed.<br><br>`VERIFICATION_STATUS_PROCESSING_FAILED`: A failure occurred when attempting to process the verification documentation.<br><br>`VERIFICATION_STATUS_DOCUMENT_REJECTED`: The documentation was rejected.|
|webhook_code|[SandboxIncomeWebhookFireRequestWebhookCode](#schemasandboxincomewebhookfirerequestwebhookcode)|true|none|The webhook codes that can be fired by this test endpoint.|

<h2 id="tocS_SandboxCraServicingSimulateRequestOptions">SandboxCraServicingSimulateRequestOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
{
  "transactions_end_date": "1970-01-01",
  "error_webhook_code": "USER_NOT_FOUND"
}
```

Optional parameters controlling the simulated report.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transactions_end_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The end of the synthesized transaction window ("the present"), as a YYYY-MM-DD date. Accepts past or future dates up to 180 days ahead; defaults to today. A later value appends newer transactions without churning earlier ones.|
|error_webhook_code|[SandboxCraServicingSimulateErrorWebhookCode](#schemasandboxcraservicingsimulateerrorwebhookcode)|false|none|If set, skip report generation and instead fire a `CRA_REPORT_UPDATED` error webhook carrying this code. The accepted values depend on the `scope` of the subscription being simulated, since a simulation can only fire a webhook that scope would send in Production. A `CLIENT_USER` subscription accepts `USER_NOT_FOUND` and `PRODUCT_GENERATION_FAILED`; a `PLAID_NETWORK` subscription accepts `UNMATCH`, `DATA_UNAVAILABLE`, `NO_ELIGIBLE_ITEMS_ON_PROFILE`, and `PRODUCT_GENERATION_FAILED`. Supplying a code that does not match the subscription's scope returns an `INVALID_FIELD` error.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|error_webhook_code|USER_NOT_FOUND|
|error_webhook_code|PRODUCT_GENERATION_FAILED|
|error_webhook_code|UNMATCH|
|error_webhook_code|DATA_UNAVAILABLE|
|error_webhook_code|NO_ELIGIBLE_ITEMS_ON_PROFILE|

If set, skip report generation and instead fire a `CRA_REPORT_UPDATED` error webhook carrying this code. The accepted values depend on the `scope` of the subscription being simulated, since a simulation can only fire a webhook that scope would send in Production. A `CLIENT_USER` subscription accepts `USER_NOT_FOUND` and `PRODUCT_GENERATION_FAILED`; a `PLAID_NETWORK` subscription accepts `UNMATCH`, `DATA_UNAVAILABLE`, `NO_ELIGIBLE_ITEMS_ON_PROFILE`, and `PRODUCT_GENERATION_FAILED`. Supplying a code that does not match the subscription's scope returns an `INVALID_FIELD` error.

<h2 id="tocS_TransferAuthorizationPaymentRisk">TransferAuthorizationPaymentRisk</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferauthorizationpaymentrisk"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferAuthorizationPaymentRisk"></a>
<a id="tocStransferauthorizationpaymentrisk"></a>
<a id="tocstransferauthorizationpaymentrisk"></a>

```json
{
  "bank_initiated_return_score": 1,
  "customer_initiated_return_score": 1,
  "risk_level": "HIGH_RISK",
  "warnings": [
    {
      "warning_type": "string",
      "warning_code": "string",
      "warning_message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

This object includes the scores and risk level. This response is offered as an add-on to `/transfer/authorization/create`. To request access to these fields, please contact your Plaid account manager.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bank_initiated_return_score|integer \| null|true|none|A score from 1-99 that indicates the transaction return risk: a higher risk score suggests a higher return likelihood.<br><br>The score evaluates the transaction return risk because an account is overdrawn or because an ineligible account is used and covers return codes: "R01", "R02", "R03", "R04", "R06", "R08",  "R09", "R13",<br>"R16", "R17", "R20", "R23". These returns have a turnaround time of 2 banking days.|
|customer_initiated_return_score|integer \| null|true|none|A score from 1-99 that indicates the transaction return risk: a higher risk score suggests a higher return likelihood.<br><br>The score evaluates the transaction return risk of an unauthorized debit and covers return codes: "R05", "R07", "R10", "R11", "R29".<br>These returns typically have a return time frame of up to 60 calendar days. During this period, customers of financial institutions can dispute a transaction as unauthorized.|
|risk_level|[TransferAuthorizationRiskLevel](#schematransferauthorizationrisklevel)|true|none|Comprises five risk categories (high risk, medium-high risk, medium risk, medium-low risk, low risk) based on the probability of return|
|warnings|[[SignalWarning](#schemasignalwarning)]|true|none|If bank information was not available to be used, this array contains warnings describing why bank data is missing. If you want to receive an API error instead of scores in the case of missing bank data, file a support ticket or contact your Plaid account manager.|

|Property|Value|

|risk_level|MEDIUM_HIGH_RISK|
|risk_level|MEDIUM_RISK|
|risk_level|MEDIUM_LOW_RISK|
|risk_level|LOW_RISK|

<h2 id="tocS_NewAccountsAvailableWebhook">NewAccountsAvailableWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanewaccountsavailablewebhook"></a>
<a id="schema_NewAccountsAvailableWebhook"></a>
<a id="tocSnewaccountsavailablewebhook"></a>
<a id="tocsnewaccountsavailablewebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "webhook_type": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "item_id": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "error": {
    "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "error_code": "string",
    "error_code_reason": "string",
    "error_message": "string",
    "display_message": "string",
    "request_id": "string",
    "causes": [
      null
    ],
    "status": 0,
    "documentation_url": "string",
    "suggested_action": "string",
    "required_account_subtypes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "provided_account_subtypes": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

Fired when Plaid detects a new account. Upon receiving this webhook, you can prompt your users to share new accounts with you through [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode/#using-update-mode-to-request-new-accounts) (US/CA only). If the end user has opted not to share new accounts with Plaid via their institution's OAuth settings, Plaid will not detect new accounts and this webhook will not fire. For end user accounts in the EU and UK, upon receiving this webhook, you can prompt your user to re-link their account and then delete the old Item via `/item/remove`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|false|none|`ITEM`|
|webhook_code|string|false|none|`NEW_ACCOUNTS_AVAILABLE`|
|item_id|[ItemId](#schemaitemid)|false|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this webhook, warning, or error|
|user_id|[UserId](#schemauserid)|false|none|The Plaid `user_id` of the User associated with this webhook, warning, or error.|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|false|none|Errors are identified by `error_code` and categorized by `error_type`. Use these in preference to HTTP status codes to identify and handle specific errors. HTTP status codes are set and provide the broadest categorization of errors: 4xx codes are for developer- or user-related errors, and 5xx codes are for Plaid-related errors, and the status will be 2xx in non-error cases. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|false|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

<h2 id="tocS_WalletTransactionIdempotencyKey">WalletTransactionIdempotencyKey</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawallettransactionidempotencykey"></a>

<a id="tocSwallettransactionidempotencykey"></a>
<a id="tocswallettransactionidempotencykey"></a>

```json
"string"
```

A random key provided by the client, per unique wallet transaction. Maximum of 128 characters.

The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. If a request to execute a wallet transaction fails due to a network connection error, then after a minimum delay of one minute, you can retry the request with the same idempotency key to guarantee that only a single wallet transaction is created. If the request was successfully processed, it will prevent any transaction that uses the same idempotency key, and was received within 48 hours of the first request, from being processed.

<h2 id="tocS_WalletTransactionRelation">WalletTransactionRelation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawallettransactionrelation"></a>
<a id="schema_WalletTransactionRelation"></a>
<a id="tocSwallettransactionrelation"></a>
<a id="tocswallettransactionrelation"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "type": "PAYOUT"
}
```

Transactions are related when they have a logical connection.

For example, a `PAYOUT` transaction can be returned by the sender, creating a `RETURN` transaction. Each `PAYOUT` transaction can have at most one corresponding `RETURN` transaction in case of reversal.

These relationships are bi-directional, meaning that both entities have references to each other. For instance, when a transaction of type RETURN occurs, it is linked to the original transaction being returned. Likewise, the original transaction has a reference back to the RETURN transaction that represents the return.

This field is only populated for transactions of type `RETURN`, `FUNDS_SWEEP`, `REFUND` and `PAYOUT`.

The relationship between a `PIS_PAY_IN` payment and its corresponding `REFUND` transactions is only available through the `refund_ids` property in the payment object. See [`/payment_initiation/payment/get`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/payment-initiation/#payment_initiation-payment-get-response-refund-ids).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The ID of the related transaction.|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the transaction.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|PAYOUT|
|type|RETURN|
|type|REFUND|
|type|FUNDS_SWEEP|

<h2 id="tocS_WalletTransactionStatus">WalletTransactionStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawallettransactionstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_WalletTransactionStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSwallettransactionstatus"></a>
<a id="tocswallettransactionstatus"></a>

```json
"AUTHORISING"
```

The status of the transaction.

`AUTHORISING`: The transaction is being processed for validation and compliance.

`INITIATED`: The transaction has been initiated and is currently being processed.

`EXECUTED`: The transaction has been successfully executed and is considered complete. This is only applicable for debit transactions.

`SETTLED`: The transaction has settled and funds are available for use. This is only applicable for credit transactions. A transaction will typically settle within seconds to several days, depending on which payment rail is used.

`FAILED`: The transaction failed to process successfully. This is a terminal status.

`BLOCKED`: The transaction has been blocked for violating compliance rules. This is a terminal status.

<h2 id="tocS_WalletTransactionFailureReason">WalletTransactionFailureReason</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawallettransactionfailurereason"></a>
<a id="schema_WalletTransactionFailureReason"></a>
<a id="tocSwallettransactionfailurereason"></a>
<a id="tocswallettransactionfailurereason"></a>

```json
"EXTERNAL_SYSTEM"
```

The error code of a failed transaction. Error codes include:

`EXTERNAL_SYSTEM`: The transaction was declined by an external system.

`EXPIRED`: The transaction request has expired.

`CANCELLED`: The transaction request was rescinded.

`INVALID`: The transaction did not meet certain criteria, such as an inactive account or no valid counterparty, etc.

`ACCOUNT_INVALID`: The transaction could not be processed because the wallet account is invalid or inactive.

`AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`: The transaction could not be processed because authentication with the wallet provider failed.

`UNKNOWN`: The transaction was unsuccessful, but the exact cause is unknown.

<h2 id="tocS_WalletTransactionPayeeVerificationStatus">WalletTransactionPayeeVerificationStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawallettransactionpayeeverificationstatus"></a>

<a id="tocSwallettransactionpayeeverificationstatus"></a>

```json
"FULL_MATCH"
```

Result of payee verification check for EUR and GBP payouts. Payee verification checks whether the payee name provided matches the account holder name at the destination institution.

`FULL_MATCH`: The payee name fully matches the account holder.

`PARTIAL_MATCH`: The payee name partially matches the account holder.

`NO_MATCH`: The payee name does not match the account holder.

`ERROR`: An error occurred during payee verification.

`CHECK_NOT_POSSIBLE`: Payee verification could not be performed.

This field is only populated for applicable EUR and GBP payout transactions and will be `null` for other transaction types.

The supported transaction types that are returned are:<br>`BANK_TRANSFER:` a transaction which credits an e-wallet through an external bank transfer.<br><br>`PAYOUT:` a transaction which debits an e-wallet by disbursing funds to a counterparty.<br><br>`PIS_PAY_IN:` a payment which credits an e-wallet through Plaid's Payment Initiation Services (PIS) APIs. For more information see the [Payment Initiation endpoints](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/payment-initiation/).<br><br>`REFUND:` a transaction which debits an e-wallet by refunding a previously initiated payment made through Plaid's [PIS APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/payment-initiation/).<br><br>`FUNDS_SWEEP`: an automated transaction which debits funds from an e-wallet to a designated client-owned account.<br><br>`RETURN`: an automated transaction where a debit transaction was reversed and money moved back to originating account.<br><br>`RECALL`: a transaction where the sending bank has requested the return of funds due to a fraud claim, technical error, or other issue associated with the payment.<br><br>`ACCOUNT_FUNDING`: an incoming transfer from an allowlisted account. Not automatically refunded.<br><br>`AUTO_REFUND`: an outgoing refund automatically initiated by Plaid in response to an unexpected `BANK_TRANSFER`.<br><br>`TRANSFER_OUT`: a transaction that debits an e-wallet and cannot be classified under another category, typically initiated by a non-Plaid flow due to technical errors, FPS timeouts, or other payment-related issues.|

This is present only for transaction types `PAYOUT` and `REFUND`.<br><br>`FASTER_PAYMENTS`: The standard payment scheme within the UK.<br><br>`SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER`: The standard payment to a beneficiary within the SEPA area.<br><br>`SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER_INSTANT`: Instant payment to a beneficiary within the SEPA area.|
|amount|[WalletTransactionAmount](#schemawallettransactionamount)|true|none|The amount and currency of a transaction|

|status|[WalletTransactionStatus](#schemawallettransactionstatus)|true|none|The status of the transaction.<br><br>`AUTHORISING`: The transaction is being processed for validation and compliance.<br><br>`INITIATED`: The transaction has been initiated and is currently being processed.<br><br>`EXECUTED`: The transaction has been successfully executed and is considered complete. This is only applicable for debit transactions.<br><br>`SETTLED`: The transaction has settled and funds are available for use. This is only applicable for credit transactions. A transaction will typically settle within seconds to several days, depending on which payment rail is used.<br><br>`FAILED`: The transaction failed to process successfully. This is a terminal status.<br><br>`BLOCKED`: The transaction has been blocked for violating compliance rules. This is a terminal status.|

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "client_user_id": "string",
  "client_account_id": "string",
  "account_type": "string",
  "account_subtype": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "amount": 0,
  "direction": "INFLOW",
  "iso_currency_code": "string",
  "location": {
    "country": "string",
    "region": "string",
    "city": "string",
    "address": "string",
    "postal_code": "string"
  },
  "mcc": "string",
  "date_posted": "1970-01-01"
}
```

A client-provided transaction for Plaid to enrich.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A unique ID for the transaction used to help you tie data back to your systems.|
|user_id|string|false|none|The Plaid generated ID that identifies the end user for whom you would like to enrich transactions.|
|client_user_id|string|false|none|A unique user id used to group transactions for a given user, as a unique identifier from your application. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|client_account_id|string|false|none|A unique account id used to group transactions for a given account, as a unique identifier from your application. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_account_id`.|
|account_type|string|false|none|The account type associated with the transaction. For a full list of valid types and subtypes, see the [Account schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema).|
|account_subtype|string|false|none|The account subtype associated with the transaction. For a full list of valid types and subtypes, see the [Account schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema).|
|description|string|true|none|The raw description of the transaction. If you have location data in available an unstructured format, it may be appended to the `description` field.|
|amount|number(double)|true|none|The absolute value of the transaction (>= 0). When testing Enrich, note that `amount` data should be realistic. Unrealistic or inaccurate `amount` data may result in reduced quality output.|
|direction|[EnrichTransactionDirection](#schemaenrichtransactiondirection)|true|none|The direction of the transaction from the perspective of the account holder:<br><br>`OUTFLOW` - Includes outgoing transfers, purchases, and fees. (Typically represented as a negative value on checking accounts and debit cards and a positive value on credit cards.)<br><br>`INFLOW` - Includes incoming transfers, refunds, and income. (Typically represented as a positive value on checking accounts and debit cards and a negative value on credit cards.)|
|iso_currency_code|string|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the transaction e.g. USD.|
|location|[ClientProvidedTransactionLocation](#schemaclientprovidedtransactionlocation)|false|none|A representation of where a transaction took place.<br><br>Use this field to pass in structured location information you may have about your transactions. Providing location data is optional but can increase result quality. If you have unstructured location information, it may be appended to the `description` field.|
|mcc|string|false|none|Merchant category codes (MCCs) are four-digit numbers that describe a merchant's primary business activities.|
|date_posted|string(date)|false|none|The date the transaction posted, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) (YYYY-MM-DD) format.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|INFLOW|
|direction|OUTFLOW|


The direction of the transaction from the perspective of the account holder:

`OUTFLOW` - Includes outgoing transfers, purchases, and fees. (Typically represented as a negative value on checking accounts and debit cards and a positive value on credit cards.)

`INFLOW` - Includes incoming transfers, refunds, and income. (Typically represented as a positive value on checking accounts and debit cards and a negative value on credit cards.)

```json
  "region": "string",
  "city": "string",
  "address": "string",
  "postal_code": "string"
```

A representation of where a transaction took place.

Use this field to pass in structured location information you may have about your transactions. Providing location data is optional but can increase result quality. If you have unstructured location information, it may be appended to the `description` field.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|country|string|false|none|The country where the transaction occurred, formatted as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code ("US" or "CA").|
|region|string|false|none|The region or state where the transaction occurred, formatted as the official two-letter US state or Canadian province postal code, e.g. "CT" or "QC".|
|city|string|false|none|The city where the transaction occurred.|
|address|string|false|none|The street address where the transaction occurred.|
|postal_code|string|false|none|The postal code where the transaction occurred.|

For a full list of legacy categories, see [`/categories/get`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#categoriesget).<br><br>We recommend using the `personal_finance_category` for transaction categorization to obtain the best results.|

|phone_number|string \| null|true|none|The phone number associated with the counterparty in E.164 format. If there is a location match (i.e. a street address is returned in the location object), the phone number will be location specific.|

If you are migrating to personal finance categories from the legacy categories, also refer to the [migration guide](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/pfc-migration/).|
|personal_finance_category_icon_url|string|true|none|The URL of an icon associated with the primary personal finance category. The icon will always be a 100×100 pixel PNG file.|
|website|string \| null|true|none|The website associated with this transaction.|

Insights object for recurring transactions streams.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stream_id|string|true|none|A unique id for the stream.|
|description|string|false|none|The client-provided raw description of the most recent transaction in the stream.|
|merchant_name|string|true|none|The merchant or primary counterparty associated with the transaction stream.|
|oldest_transaction_date|string(date)|false|none|The posted date of the earliest transaction in the stream.|
|newest_transaction_date|string(date)|false|none|The posted date of the latest transaction in the stream.|
|average_days_apart|number(double)|true|none|The average number of days between each of the recurring transactions.|
|frequency|[RecurringTransactionFrequency](#schemarecurringtransactionfrequency)|false|none|Describes the frequency of the transaction stream.<br><br>`WEEKLY`: Assigned to a transaction stream that occurs approximately every week.<br><br>`BIWEEKLY`: Assigned to a transaction stream that occurs approximately every 2 weeks.<br><br>`SEMI_MONTHLY`: Assigned to a transaction stream that occurs approximately twice per month. This frequency is typically seen for inflow transaction streams.<br><br>`MONTHLY`: Assigned to a transaction stream that occurs approximately every month.<br><br>`ANNUALLY`: Assigned to a transaction stream that occurs approximately every year.<br><br>`UNKNOWN`: Assigned to a transaction stream that does not fit any of the pre-defined frequencies.|
|transaction_count|integer|false|none|The number of transactions in this stream.|
|transaction_ids|[string]|false|none|An array of Plaid transaction IDs belonging to the stream, sorted by posted date.|
|average_amount|[TransactionStreamAmount](#schematransactionstreamamount)|false|none|Object with data pertaining to an amount on the transaction stream.|
|newest_transaction_amount|[TransactionStreamAmount](#schematransactionstreamamount)|false|none|Object with data pertaining to an amount on the transaction stream.|
|is_active|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the transaction stream is still live.|
|status|[TransactionStreamStatus](#schematransactionstreamstatus)|false|none|The current status of the transaction stream.<br><br>`MATURE`: A `MATURE` recurring stream should have at least 3 transactions and happen on a regular cadence (For Annual recurring stream, we will mark it `MATURE` after 2 instances).<br><br>`EARLY_DETECTION`: When a recurring transaction first appears in the transaction history and before it fulfills the requirement of a mature stream, the status will be `EARLY_DETECTION`.<br><br>`TOMBSTONED`: A stream that was previously in the `EARLY_DETECTION` status will move to the `TOMBSTONED` status when no further transactions were found at the next expected date.<br><br>`UNKNOWN`: A stream is assigned an `UNKNOWN` status when none of the other statuses are applicable.|
|personal_finance_category_primary|string|false|none|The primary category associated with the transaction stream.|
|personal_finance_category_detailed|string|false|none|The detailed category associated with the transaction stream.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|frequency|UNKNOWN|
|frequency|WEEKLY|
|frequency|BIWEEKLY|
|frequency|SEMI_MONTHLY|
|frequency|MONTHLY|
|frequency|ANNUALLY|
|status|UNKNOWN|
|status|MATURE|
|status|EARLY_DETECTION|
|status|TOMBSTONED|

EwaScore represents an earned wage access score for a specific advance amount range.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lowest_amount|number(float)|false|none|Float value representing the lower bound (inclusive) of the advance amount range associated with a specific EWA score.|

|score|integer|false|none|EWA score for the corresponding amount bucket. Scores range from 1-99, where a higher score indicates a higher likelihood of repayment.|

|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|false|none|Errors are identified by `error_code` and categorized by `error_type`. Use these in preference to HTTP status codes to identify and handle specific errors. HTTP status codes are set and provide the broadest categorization of errors: 4xx codes are for developer- or user-related errors, and 5xx codes are for Plaid-related errors, and the status will be 2xx in non-error cases. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|

|deleted_at|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|Timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`) indicating the time the given Payment Profile was deleted at. Always `null` if the Payment Profile has not been deleted|
|status|[PaymentProfileStatus](#schemapaymentprofilestatus)|true|none|The status of the given Payment Profile.<br><br>`READY`: This Payment Profile is ready to be used to create transfers using `/transfer/authorization/create` and `/transfer/create`.<br><br>`PENDING`: This Payment Profile is not ready to be used. You'll need to call `/link/token/create` and provide the `payment_profile_token` in the `transfer.payment_profile_token` field to initiate the account linking experience.<br><br>`REMOVED`: This Payment Profile has been removed.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

```json
"PENDING"
```

The status of the given Payment Profile.

`READY`: This Payment Profile is ready to be used to create transfers using `/transfer/authorization/create` and `/transfer/create`.

`PENDING`: This Payment Profile is not ready to be used. You'll need to call `/link/token/create` and provide the `payment_profile_token` in the `transfer.payment_profile_token` field to initiate the account linking experience.

`REMOVED`: This Payment Profile has been removed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|company_name|string|true|none|The company name of the end customer being created. This will be used to display the end customer in the Plaid Dashboard. It will not be shown to end users.|
|is_diligence_attested|boolean|true|none|Denotes whether or not the partner has completed attestation of diligence for the end customer to be created.|
|products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|none|The products to be enabled for the end customer. If empty or `null`, this field will default to the products enabled for the reseller at the time this endpoint is called.|
|create_link_customization|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the end customer's default Link customization will be set to match the partner's. You can always change the end customer's Link customization in the Plaid Dashboard. See the [Link Customization docs](https://plaid.com/docs/link/customization/) for more information. If you require the ability to programmatically create end customers using multiple different Link customization profiles, contact your Plaid account manager for assistance.<br><br>Important: Data Transparency Messaging (DTM) use cases will not be copied to the end customer's Link customization unless the **Publish changes** button is clicked after the use cases are applied. Link will not work in Production unless the end customer's DTM use cases are configured. For more details, see [Data Transparency Messaging](https://plaid.com/docs/link/data-transparency-messaging-migration-guide/).|
|logo|string|false|none|Base64-encoded representation of the end customer's logo. Must be a PNG of size 1024x1024 under 4MB. The logo will be shared with financial institutions and shown to the end user during Link flows. A logo is required if `create_link_customization` is `true`. If `create_link_customization` is `false` and the logo is omitted, the partner's logo will be used if one exists, otherwise a stock logo will be used.|
|legal_entity_name|string|true|none|The end customer's legal name. This will be shared with financial institutions as part of the OAuth registration process. It will not be shown to end users.|
|website|string|true|none|The end customer's website.|
|application_name|string|true|none|The name of the end customer's application. This will be shown to end users when they go through the Plaid Link flow. The application name must be unique and cannot match the name of another application already registered with Plaid.|
|technical_contact|[PartnerEndCustomerTechnicalContact](#schemapartnerendcustomertechnicalcontact)|false|none|The technical contact for the end customer. Defaults to partner's technical contact if omitted.|
|billing_contact|[PartnerEndCustomerBillingContact](#schemapartnerendcustomerbillingcontact)|false|none|The billing contact for the end customer. Defaults to partner's billing contact if omitted.|
|customer_support_info|[PartnerEndCustomerCustomerSupportInfo](#schemapartnerendcustomercustomersupportinfo)|false|none|This information is public. Users of your app will see this information when managing connections between your app and their bank accounts in Plaid Portal. Defaults to partner's customer support info if omitted. This field is mandatory for partners whose Plaid accounts were created after November 26, 2024 and will be mandatory for all partners by the 1033 compliance deadline.|
|address|[PartnerEndCustomerAddress](#schemapartnerendcustomeraddress)|true|none|The end customer's address.|
|is_bank_addendum_completed|boolean|true|none|Denotes whether the partner has forwarded the Plaid bank addendum to the end customer.|
|assets_under_management|[PartnerEndCustomerAssetsUnderManagement](#schemapartnerendcustomerassetsundermanagement)|false|none|Assets under management for the given end customer. Required for end customers with monthly service commitments.|
|redirect_uris|[string]|false|none|A list of URIs indicating the destination(s) where a user can be forwarded after completing the Link flow; used to support OAuth authentication flows when launching Link in the browser or another app. URIs should not contain any query parameters. When used in Production, URIs must use https. To modify redirect URIs for an end customer after creating them, go to the end customer's [API page](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api) in the Dashboard.|
|registration_number|string|false|none|The unique identifier assigned to a financial institution by regulatory authorities, if applicable. For banks, this is the FDIC Certificate Number. For credit unions, this is the Credit Union Charter Number.|

<a id="schemapartnerendcustomer"></a>
<a id="schema_PartnerEndCustomer"></a>
<a id="tocSpartnerendcustomer"></a>
<a id="tocspartnerendcustomer"></a>

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "company_name": "string",
  "status": "UNDER_REVIEW"
}
```

The details for an end customer.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|string|false|none|The `client_id` of the end customer.|
|company_name|string|false|none|The company name associated with the end customer.|
|status|[PartnerEndCustomerStatus](#schemapartnerendcustomerstatus)|false|none|The status of the given end customer.<br><br>`UNDER_REVIEW`: The end customer has been created and enabled in the Sandbox environment. The end customer must be manually reviewed by the Plaid team before it can be enabled in Production, at which point its status will automatically transition to `PENDING_ENABLEMENT` or `DENIED`.<br><br>`PENDING_ENABLEMENT`: The end customer is ready to be fully enabled in the Production environment. Call the `/partner/customer/enable` endpoint to enable the end customer in full Production.<br><br>`ACTIVE`: The end customer has been fully enabled in all environments.<br><br>`DENIED`: The end customer has been created and enabled in the Sandbox environment, but it did not pass review by the Plaid team and therefore cannot be enabled for Production access. Talk to your account manager for more information.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|UNDER_REVIEW|
|status|PENDING_ENABLEMENT|
|status|ACTIVE|
|status|DENIED|
|status|MORE_INFORMATION_NEEDED|

<h2 id="tocS_PartnerEndCustomerStatus">PartnerEndCustomerStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapartnerendcustomerstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_PartnerEndCustomerStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSpartnerendcustomerstatus"></a>
<a id="tocspartnerendcustomerstatus"></a>

```json
"UNDER_REVIEW"
```

The status of the given end customer.

`UNDER_REVIEW`: The end customer has been created and enabled in the Sandbox environment. The end customer must be manually reviewed by the Plaid team before it can be enabled in Production, at which point its status will automatically transition to `PENDING_ENABLEMENT` or `DENIED`.

`PENDING_ENABLEMENT`: The end customer is ready to be fully enabled in the Production environment. Call the `/partner/customer/enable` endpoint to enable the end customer in full Production.

`ACTIVE`: The end customer has been fully enabled in all environments.

`DENIED`: The end customer has been created and enabled in the Sandbox environment, but it did not pass review by the Plaid team and therefore cannot be enabled for Production access. Talk to your account manager for more information.

```json
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sandbox|string|false|none|The end customer's secret key for the Sandbox environment.|
|development|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** The end customer's secret key for the Development environment. The Development environment has been removed.|
|production|string|false|none|The end customer's secret key for the Production environment. The end customer will be provided with a limited number of credits to test in the Production environment before full enablement.|

```json
{
  "email": "string",
  "phone_number": "string",
  "contact_url": "string",
  "link_update_url": "string"
}
```

This information is public. Users of your app will see this information when managing connections between your app and their bank accounts in Plaid Portal. Defaults to partner's customer support info if omitted. This field is mandatory for partners whose Plaid accounts were created after November 26, 2024 and will be mandatory for all partners by the 1033 compliance deadline.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email|string|false|none|This field is mandatory for partners whose Plaid accounts were created after November 26, 2024 and will be mandatory for all partners by the 1033 compliance deadline.|
|phone_number|string|false|none|none|
|contact_url|string|false|none|none|
|link_update_url|string|false|none|none|

Request schema for `/beta/partner/customer/v1/create`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|company_name|string|true|none|The company name of the end customer being created. This will be used to display the end customer in the Plaid Dashboard. It will not be shown to end users.|
|is_diligence_attested|boolean|false|none|Denotes whether or not the partner has completed attestation of diligence for the end customer to be created.|
|products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|none|The products to be enabled for the end customer. If empty or `null`, this field will default to the products enabled for the reseller at the time this endpoint is called.|
|create_link_customization|boolean|false|none|If `true`, the end customer's default Link customization will be set to match the partner's. You can always change the end customer's Link customization in the Plaid Dashboard. See the [Link Customization docs](https://plaid.com/docs/link/customization/) for more information. If you require the ability to programmatically create end customers using multiple different Link customization profiles, contact your Plaid account manager for assistance.<br><br>Important: Data Transparency Messaging (DTM) use cases will not be copied to the end customer's Link customization unless the **Publish changes** button is clicked after the use cases are applied. Link will not work in Production unless the end customer's DTM use cases are configured. For more details, see [Data Transparency Messaging](https://plaid.com/docs/link/data-transparency-messaging-migration-guide/).|
|logo|string|false|none|Base64-encoded representation of the end customer's logo. Must be a PNG of size 1024x1024 under 4MB. The logo will be shared with financial institutions and shown to the end user during Link flows. A logo is required if `create_link_customization` is `true`. If `create_link_customization` is `false` and the logo is omitted, the partner's logo will be used if one exists, otherwise a stock logo will be used.|
|legal_entity_name|string|false|none|The end customer's legal name. This will be shared with financial institutions as part of the OAuth registration process. It will not be shown to end users.|
|website|string|true|none|The end customer's website.|
|application_name|string|true|none|The name of the end customer's application. This will be shown to end users when they go through the Plaid Link flow. The application name must be unique and cannot match the name of another application already registered with Plaid.|
|technical_contact|[PartnerEndCustomerTechnicalContact](#schemapartnerendcustomertechnicalcontact)|false|none|The technical contact for the end customer. Defaults to partner's technical contact if omitted.|
|billing_contact|[PartnerEndCustomerBillingContact](#schemapartnerendcustomerbillingcontact)|false|none|The billing contact for the end customer. Defaults to partner's billing contact if omitted.|
|customer_support_info|[PartnerEndCustomerCustomerSupportInfo](#schemapartnerendcustomercustomersupportinfo)|true|none|This information is public. Users of your app will see this information when managing connections between your app and their bank accounts in Plaid Portal. Defaults to partner's customer support info if omitted. This field is mandatory for partners whose Plaid accounts were created after November 26, 2024 and will be mandatory for all partners by the 1033 compliance deadline.|
|address|[PartnerEndCustomerAddress](#schemapartnerendcustomeraddress)|true|none|The end customer's address.|
|redirect_uris|[string]|false|none|A list of URIs indicating the destination(s) where a user can be forwarded after completing the Link flow; used to support OAuth authentication flows when launching Link in the browser or another app. URIs should not contain any query parameters. When used in Production, URIs must use https. To modify redirect URIs for an end customer after creating them, go to the end customer's [API page](https://dashboard.plaid.com/team/api) in the Dashboard.|
|bank_addendum_acceptance|[PartnerEndCustomerBankAddendumAcceptance](#schemapartnerendcustomerbankaddendumacceptance)|false|none|The bank addendum acceptance for the end customer.|
|questionnaires|[PartnerEndCustomerQuestionnaires](#schemapartnerendcustomerquestionnaires)|false|none|The questionnaires for the end customer.|

```json
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "item_id": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "account_id": "string",
  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

The `USER_ACCOUNT_REVOKED` webhook is fired when an end user has revoked access to their account on the Data Provider's portal. This webhook is currently sent only for Chase, PNC, and Truist Items, but may be sent in the future for other financial institutions that allow account-level permissions revocation through their portals. Upon receiving this webhook, it is recommended to delete any Plaid-derived data you have stored that is associated with the revoked account.

If you are using Auth and receive this webhook, this webhook indicates that the TAN associated with the revoked account is no longer valid and cannot be used to create new transfers. You should not create new ACH transfers for the account that was revoked until access has been re-granted.

You can request the user to re-grant access to their account by sending them through [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode). Alternatively, they may re-grant access directly through the Data Provider's portal.

After the user has re-granted access, Auth customers should call the auth endpoint again to obtain the new TAN.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`ITEM`|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`USER_ACCOUNT_REVOKED`|
|item_id|[ItemId](#schemaitemid)|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this webhook, warning, or error|
|user_id|[UserId](#schemauserid)|false|none|The Plaid `user_id` of the User associated with this webhook, warning, or error.|
|account_id|string|true|none|The external account ID of the affected account|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

```json
{
  "webhook_type": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "status": "AVAILABLE",
  "user_id": "string",
  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

For each user's Item enabled for Cash Flow Updates, this webhook will fire between one and four times a day with information on the status of the update. This webhook will not fire immediately upon enrollment in Cash Flow Updates. Upon receiving the webhook, call `/cra/monitoring_insights/get` to retrieve the updated insights. At approximately the same time as the `INSIGHTS_UPDATED` webhook, any event-driven `CASH_FLOW_UPDATES` webhooks (e.g. `LOW_BALANCE_DETECTED`, `LARGE_DEPOSIT_DETECTED`) that were triggered by the update will also fire. This webhook has been replaced by the `CASH_FLOW_INSIGHTS_UPDATED` webhook for all customers who began using Plaid Check on or after December 10, 2025.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`CASH_FLOW_UPDATES`|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`INSIGHTS_UPDATED`|
|status|[MonitoringInsightsStatus](#schemamonitoringinsightsstatus)|true|none|Enum for the status of the insights|
|user_id|string|true|none|The `user_id` that the report is associated with|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|AVAILABLE|
|status|FAILED|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

```json
  "insights": [
    "LARGE_DEPOSIT_DETECTED"
  ],
  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

For each item on an enabled user, this webhook will fire up to four times a day with status information. This webhook will not fire immediately upon enrollment in Cash Flow Updates. The payload may contain an `insights` array with insights that have been detected, if any (e.g. `LOW_BALANCE_DETECTED`, `LARGE_DEPOSIT_DETECTED`). Upon receiving the webhook, call `/cra/monitoring_insights/get` to retrieve the updated insights.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|webhook_code|string|true|none|`CASH_FLOW_INSIGHTS_UPDATED`|
|status|[MonitoringInsightsStatus](#schemamonitoringinsightsstatus)|true|none|Enum for the status of the insights|
|user_id|string|true|none|The `user_id` associated with the user whose data is being requested. This is received by calling `/user/create`.|
|insights|[[CashFlowInsight](#schemacashflowinsight)]|true|none|Array containing the insights detected within the generated report, if any. Possible values include:<br><br>  `LARGE_DEPOSIT_DETECTED`: signaling a deposit over $5,000<br><br>  `LOW_BALANCE_DETECTED`: signaling a balance below $100<br><br>  `NEW_LOAN_PAYMENT_DETECTED`: signaling a new loan payment<br><br>  `NSF_OVERDRAFT_DETECTED`: signaling an NSF overdraft|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|

#### Enumerated Values

|insights|NEW_LOAN_PAYMENT_DETECTED|
|insights|NSF_OVERDRAFT_DETECTED|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|true|none|Errors are identified by `error_code` and categorized by `error_type`. Use these in preference to HTTP status codes to identify and handle specific errors. HTTP status codes are set and provide the broadest categorization of errors: 4xx codes are for developer- or user-related errors, and 5xx codes are for Plaid-related errors, and the status will be 2xx in non-error cases. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|

<h2 id="tocS_CraReportUpdatedWebhook">CraReportUpdatedWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacrareportupdatedwebhook"></a>
<a id="schema_CraReportUpdatedWebhook"></a>
<a id="tocScrareportupdatedwebhook"></a>
<a id="tocscrareportupdatedwebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "webhook_type": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "client_user_id": "string",
  "report_id": "string",
  "scope": "PLAID_NETWORK",
  "successful_products": [
    {
      "product": {},
      "version": "string"
    }
  ],
  "failed_products": [
    {
      "product": {},
      "version": "string"
    }
  ],
  "generated_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "error_code": "string",
  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

Fired when a subscribed Consumer Report has been updated. Retrieve the updated products by calling the relevant product `/get` endpoint. A single webhook covers all Consumer Report update subscriptions; the `successful_products`/`failed_products` fields indicate which products were updated, and the `scope` field indicates the data the report was computed over.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`CRA_REPORT`|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`CRA_REPORT_UPDATED`|
|user_id|string|true|none|The `user_id` associated with the user whose data is being requested. This is received by calling `/user/create`.|
|client_user_id|string|true|none|The `client_user_id` you supplied for this user when calling `/user/create`.|
|report_id|string \| null|false|none|The identifier of the Consumer Report that was updated. Pass this value to the relevant product `/get` endpoint to retrieve the updated report.|
|scope|[CraReportScope](#schemacrareportscope)|true|none|Determines whose items are used. `PLAID_NETWORK` (default) uses the Plaid Network view of the user's profile. `CLIENT_USER` uses only the items linked by this client.|
|successful_products|[[CreditProduct](#schemacreditproduct)]|true|none|Specifies a list of products that have successfully been updated for the report. Call the product `/get` endpoint to retrieve them.|
|failed_products|[[CreditProduct](#schemacreditproduct)]|true|none|Specifies a list of products that have failed to update for the report. Additional detail on what caused the failure can be found by calling the product `/get` endpoint.|
|generated_time|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The timestamp when the products were generated, in ISO 8601 format. Null if there are no successful products.|
|error_code|string \| null|false|none|The reason all products failed to update. Populated only when every requested product failed; null if any product succeeded. For example, `PRODUCT_GENERATION_FAILED`.|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|PLAID_NETWORK|
|scope|CLIENT_USER|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

```json
      "product": {},
      "version": "string"
    }
  ],
  "failed_products": [
    {
      "product": {},
      "version": "string"
    }
  ],
  "generated_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "error_code": "DATA_UNAVAILABLE",
  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

Fired when generation finishes for a Consumer Report requested via `/cra/report/create` or a Link session configured with `cra_report_parameter`, whether every requested product was generated, only some were, or none were. `successful_products` and `failed_products` indicate which products were generated, and `error_code` is populated when every product failed. Call `/cra/report/get` for the generated products and for error details on failed products.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`CRA_REPORT`|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`CRA_REPORT_READY`|
|user_id|string|true|none|The `user_id` associated with the user whose data is being requested. This is received by calling `/user/create`.|
|client_user_id|string \| null|true|none|The `client_user_id` you supplied for this user when calling `/user/create`. `null` if no `client_user_id` is associated with the user.|
|report_id|object \| null|true|none|none|
|client_report_id|string \| null|true|none|The `client_report_id` you supplied when requesting the report, if any.|
|scope|[CraReportScope](#schemacrareportscope)|true|none|Determines whose items are used. `PLAID_NETWORK` (default) uses the Plaid Network view of the user's profile. `CLIENT_USER` uses only the items linked by this client.|
|successful_products|[[CreditProduct](#schemacreditproduct)]|true|none|Specifies a list of products that have successfully been generated for the report.|
|failed_products|[[CreditProduct](#schemacreditproduct)]|true|none|Specifies a list of products that have failed to generate for the report. Additional detail on what caused the failure can be found in the product's `errors` when calling `/cra/report/get`.|
|generated_time|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|The timestamp when the products were generated, in ISO 8601 format. Null if there are no successful products.|
|error_code|[CraReportErrorCode](#schemacrareporterrorcode)|true|none|The reason every product in a Consumer Report failed to generate. `null` when at least one product succeeded.<br><br>`DATA_UNAVAILABLE`: Plaid could not retrieve enough data from the user's Items to generate any of the requested products. Sending the user through Link to add or repair Items may resolve this.<br><br>`INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`: Plaid encountered an unexpected error while generating the report.|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|

|environment|production|

<h2 id="tocS_LinkEventsWebhook">LinkEventsWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalinkeventswebhook"></a>
<a id="schema_LinkEventsWebhook"></a>
<a id="tocSlinkeventswebhook"></a>
<a id="tocslinkeventswebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "webhook_type": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "events": [
    {
      "event_name": "string",
      "timestamp": "string",
      "event_id": "string",
      "event_metadata": {
        "error_code": "string",
        "error_message": "string",
        "error_type": "string",
        "exit_status": "string",
        "institution_id": "string",
        "institution_name": "string",
        "institution_search_query": "string",
        "request_id": "string",
        "mfa_type": "string",
        "view_name": "string",
        "selection": "string",
        "brand_name": "string",
        "match_reason": "string",
        "routing_number": "string",
        "account_number_mask": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "link_session_id": "string",
  "link_token": "string",
  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

This webhook contains a summary of the events from a Link session and will be fired after the user finishes going through Link. If the user abandons the Link flow (i.e., closes the hosted link webpage or leaves Link open for too long without taking any action), the webhook will be fired 15-25 minutes after the last user interaction. A single Link session may occasionally generate multiple `EVENTS` webhooks. If this occurs, the new webhook will contain all previous events for the session, as well as new events that occurred since the previous `EVENTS` webhook was sent. If this occurs, events can be grouped using the `link_session_id` field and, if necessary, de-duplicated using the `event_id` field.

By default, the `EVENTS` webhook is sent only for sessions where the end user goes through a Hosted Link flow (including Link Recovery flows). If you would like to receive this webhook for sessions not using Hosted Link, contact your account manager or support. This enablement will also cause you to receive the `SESSION_FINISHED` webhook for non-Hosted-Link sessions and to be able to use `/link/token/get` to receive events data for non-Hosted Link sessions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`LINK`|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`EVENTS`|
|events|[[LinkEvent](#schemalinkevent)]|true|none|The Link events emitted during the Link session|
|link_session_id|string|true|none|An identifier for the Link session these events occurred in|
|link_token|string|true|none|The Link token used to create the Link session these events are from|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

By default, this webhook is sent only for sessions enabled for the Hosted Link flow (including Link Recovery flows), a Multi-Item Link flow, or a Layer flow.
