The payment is awaiting user input to continue processing. It may re-enter this state if additional input is required.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_AUTHORISING`:** Transitional. The payment is being authorised by the financial institution. It will automatically move on once authorisation completes.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED`:** The payment has been authorised and accepted by the financial institution. In many EU markets, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not supported, and a payment will remain in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` until the funds settle, making this a terminal success state in those cases. A payment in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` should be treated as a successfully submitted payment; do not gate downstream processing on reaching `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`. For a full explanation of payment statuses and how to handle each, see the [Payment Status guide](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/payment-status/).<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`: Terminal.** The funds have left the payer's account and the payment is en route to settlement. Note that this status does not confirm that funds have arrived in the recipient's account; do not use it as proof of fund receipt. Support is more common in the UK than in the EU; where unsupported, a successful payment remains in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` before settling. When using Plaid Virtual Accounts, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not terminal -- the payment will continue to `PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED` once funds are available.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED`: Terminal.** The funds are available in the recipient's account. Only available to customers using [Plaid Virtual Accounts](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/virtual-accounts/).<br><br>Failure statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: Terminal.** The payment failed due to insufficient funds. No further retries will succeed until the payer's balance is replenished.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_FAILED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment could not be initiated due to a system error or outage. Retry once the root cause is resolved.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_BLOCKED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment was blocked by Plaid (e.g., flagged as risky). Resolve any compliance or risk issues and retry.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_REJECTED`: Terminal.** The payment was rejected by the financial institution. No automatic retry is possible.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_CANCELLED`: Terminal.** The end user cancelled the payment during authorisation.<br><br>Standing-order statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_ESTABLISHED`: Terminal.** A recurring/standing order has been successfully created.<br><br>Deprecated (to be removed in a future release):<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_UNKNOWN`: The payment status is unknown.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_PROCESSING`: The payment is currently being processed.<br><br>`PAYMENT_STATUS_COMPLETED`: Indicates that the standing order has been successfully established.|

In many EU markets, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not supported, and a payment will remain in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` until the funds settle, making this a terminal success state in those cases. A payment in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` should be treated as a successfully submitted payment; do not gate downstream processing on reaching `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`. For a full explanation of payment statuses and how to handle each, see the [Payment Status guide](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/payment-status/).<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED`: Terminal.** The funds have left the payer's account and the payment is en route to settlement. Note that this status does not confirm that funds have arrived in the recipient's account; do not use it as proof of fund receipt. Support is more common in the UK than in the EU; where unsupported, a successful payment remains in `PAYMENT_STATUS_INITIATED` before settling. When using Plaid Virtual Accounts, `PAYMENT_STATUS_EXECUTED` is not terminal -- the payment will continue to `PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED` once funds are available.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_SETTLED`: Terminal.** The funds are available in the recipient's account. Only available to customers using [Plaid Virtual Accounts](https://plaid.com/docs/payment-initiation/virtual-accounts/).<br><br>Failure statuses:<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: Terminal.** The payment failed due to insufficient funds. No further retries will succeed until the payer's balance is replenished.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_FAILED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment could not be initiated due to a system error or outage. Retry once the root cause is resolved.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_BLOCKED`: Terminal (retryable).** The payment was blocked by Plaid (e.g., flagged as risky). Resolve any compliance or risk issues and retry.<br><br>**`PAYMENT_STATUS_REJECTED`: Terminal.** The payment was rejected by the financial institution.     ],

```json
  }
```

AssetReportCreateRequest defines the request schema for `/asset_report/create`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|access_tokens|[[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)]|false|none|An array of access tokens corresponding to the Items that will be included in the report. The `assets` product must have been initialized for the Items during Link; the Assets product cannot be added after initialization.|
|days_requested|integer|true|none|The maximum integer number of days of history to include in the Asset Report. If using Fannie Mae Day 1 Certainty, `days_requested` must be at least 61 for new originations or at least 31 for refinancings.<br><br>An Asset Report requested with "Additional History" (that is, with more than 61 days of transaction history) will incur an Additional History fee.|
|options|[AssetReportCreateRequestOptions](#schemaassetreportcreaterequestoptions)|false|none|An optional object to filter `/asset_report/create` results. If provided, must be non-`null`. The optional `user` object is required for the report to be eligible for Fannie Mae's Day 1 Certainty program.|

<h2 id="tocS_AssetReportCreateRequestOptions">AssetReportCreateRequestOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaassetreportcreaterequestoptions"></a>
<a id="schema_AssetReportCreateRequestOptions"></a>
<a id="tocSassetreportcreaterequestoptions"></a>
<a id="tocsassetreportcreaterequestoptions"></a>

```json
{
  "client_report_id": "string",
  "webhook": "http://example.com",
  "include_fast_report": true,
  "products": [
    "string"
  ],
  "add_ons": [
    "investments"
  ],
  "user": {
    "client_user_id": "string",
    "first_name": "string",
    "middle_name": "string",
    "last_name": "string",
    "ssn": "string",
    "phone_number": "string",
    "email": "string"
  },
  "require_all_items": true
}
```

An optional object to filter `/asset_report/create` results. If provided, must be non-`null`. The optional `user` object is required for the report to be eligible for Fannie Mae's Day 1 Certainty program.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_report_id|string \| null|false|none|Client-generated identifier, which can be used by lenders to track loan applications.|
|webhook|string(url) \| null|false|none|URL to which Plaid will send Assets webhooks, for example when the requested Asset Report is ready.|
|include_fast_report|boolean \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** true to return balance and identity earlier as a fast report. Defaults to false if omitted.|
|products|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Additional information that can be included in the asset report. Possible values: `"investments"`|
|add_ons|[[AssetReportAddOns](#schemaassetreportaddons)]|false|none|A list of add-ons that should be included in the Asset Report.<br><br>When Fast Assets is requested, Plaid will create two versions of the Asset Report: the Fast Asset Report, which will contain only Identity and Balance information, and the Full Asset Report, which will also contain Transactions information. A `PRODUCT_READY` webhook will be fired for each Asset Report when it is ready, and the `report_type` field will indicate whether the webhook is firing for the `FULL` or `FAST` Asset Report. To retrieve the Fast Asset Report, call `/asset_report/get` with `fast_report` set to `true`. There is no additional charge for using Fast Assets. To create a Fast Asset Report, Plaid must successfully retrieve both Identity and Balance data; if Plaid encounters an error obtaining this data, the Fast Asset Report will not be created. However, as long as Plaid can obtain Transactions data, the Full Asset Report will still be available.<br><br>When Investments is requested, `investments` must be specified in the `optional_products` array when initializing Link.|
|user|[AssetReportUser](#schemaassetreportuser)|false|none|The user object allows you to provide additional information about the user to be appended to the Asset Report. All fields are optional. The `first_name`, `last_name`, and `ssn` fields are required if you would like the Report to be eligible for Fannie Mae's Day 1 Certainty™ program.|
|require_all_items|boolean \| null|false|none|By default (`true`), the asynchronous report generation fails unless all Items extract successfully. If set to `false`, the report will still be generated as long as at least one Item extracts successfully; extraction failures on the remaining Items are tolerated. This setting applies only to failures that occur during asynchronous extraction. It does not relax the synchronous check at call time: if any Item is already unhealthy when `/asset_report/create` is invoked, the request fails immediately regardless of this value.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|add_ons|investments|
|add_ons|fast_assets|

|user_token|string|false|none|The user token associated with the User for which to create an asset report for. The latest asset report associated with the User will be returned|
|include_insights|boolean|false|none|`true` if you would like to retrieve the Asset Report with Insights, `false` otherwise. This field defaults to `false` if omitted.|
|fast_report|boolean|false|none|`true` to fetch "fast" version of asset report. Defaults to false if omitted. Can only be used if `/asset_report/create` was called with `options.add_ons` set to `["fast_assets"]`.|
|options|[AssetReportGetRequestOptions](#schemaassetreportgetrequestoptions)|false|none|An optional object to filter or add data to `/asset_report/get` results. If provided, must be non-`null`.|

```json
{
  "days_to_include": 0
}
```

An optional object to filter or add data to `/asset_report/get` results. If provided, must be non-`null`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|days_to_include|integer \| null|false|none|The maximum number of days of history to include in the Asset Report.|

An object representing a Monitoring Insights Item

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|date_generated|string(date-time)|true|none|The date and time when the specific insights were generated (per-item), in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (e.g. "2018-04-12T03:32:11Z").|
|item_id|string|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with the insights|
|institution_id|string|true|none|The id of the financial institution associated with the Item.|
|institution_name|string|true|none|The full financial institution name associated with the Item.|
|status|[MonitoringInsightsItemStatus](#schemamonitoringinsightsitemstatus)|true|none|An object with details of the Monitoring Insights Item's status.|
|insights|[MonitoringInsights](#schemamonitoringinsights)|true|none|An object representing the Monitoring Insights for the given Item|
|accounts|[[BaseReportAccount](#schemabasereportaccount)]|false|none|Data about each of the accounts open on the Item.|

<h2 id="tocS_MonitoringConsumerReportPermissiblePurpose">MonitoringConsumerReportPermissiblePurpose</h2>

<a id="tocSmonitoringconsumerreportpermissiblepurpose"></a>
<a id="tocsmonitoringconsumerreportpermissiblepurpose"></a>

```json
"ACCOUNT_REVIEW_CREDIT"
```

Describes the reason you are generating a Consumer Report for this user.

`ACCOUNT_REVIEW_CREDIT`: In connection with a consumer credit transaction for the review or collection of an account pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(3)(A).

`WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION_OTHER`: In accordance with the written instructions of the consumer pursuant to FCRA Section 604(a)(2), such as when an individual agrees to act as a guarantor or assumes personal liability for a consumer, business, or commercial loan.

An object representing an income source

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|income_source_id|string|true|none|A unique identifier for an income source|
|income_description|string|true|none|The most common name or original description for the underlying income transactions|
|income_category|[CreditBankIncomeCategory](#schemacreditbankincomecategory)|true|none|The income category.<br><br>`BANK_INTEREST`: Interest earned from a bank account.<br><br>`BENEFIT_OTHER`: Government benefits other than retirement, unemployment, child support, or disability. Currently used only in the UK, to represent benefits such as Cost of Living Payments.<br><br>`CASH`: Deprecated and used only for existing legacy implementations. Has been replaced by `CASH_DEPOSIT` and `TRANSFER_FROM_APPLICATION`.<br><br>`CASH_DEPOSIT`: A cash or check deposit.<br><br>`CHILD_SUPPORT`: Child support payments received.<br><br>`GIG_ECONOMY`: Income earned as a gig economy worker, e.g. driving for Uber, Lyft, Postmates, DoorDash, etc.<br><br>`LONG_TERM_DISABILITY`: Disability payments, including Social Security disability benefits.<br><br>`OTHER`: Income that could not be categorized as any other income category.<br><br>`MILITARY`: Veterans benefits. Income earned as salary for serving in the military (e.g. through DFAS) will be classified as `SALARY` rather than `MILITARY`.<br><br>`RENTAL`: Income earned from a rental property. Income may be identified as rental when the payment is received through a rental platform, e.g. Airbnb; rent paid directly by the tenant to the property owner (e.g. via cash, check, or ACH) will typically not be classified as rental income.<br><br>`RETIREMENT`: Payments from private retirement systems, pensions, and government retirement programs, including Social Security retirement benefits.<br><br>`SALARY`: Payment from an employer to an earner or other form of permanent employment.<br><br>`TAX_REFUND`: A tax refund.<br><br>`TRANSFER_FROM_APPLICATION`: Deposits from a money transfer app, such as Venmo, Cash App, or Zelle.<br><br>`UNEMPLOYMENT`: Unemployment benefits. In the UK, includes certain low-income benefits such as the Universal Credit.|
|last_transaction_date|string(date)|true|none|The last detected transaction date for this income source|

It is possible for a Base Report to be returned with missing account owner information. In such cases, the Base Report will contain warning data in the response, indicating why obtaining the owner information failed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|warning_type|string|true|none|The warning type, which will always be `BASE_REPORT_WARNING`|
|warning_code|[BaseReportWarningCode](#schemabasereportwarningcode)|true|none|The warning code identifies a specific kind of warning.<br><br>`IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE`: Account-owner information is not available.<br><br>`TRANSACTIONS_UNAVAILABLE`: Transactions information associated with Credit and Depository accounts are unavailable.<br><br>`USER_FRAUD_ALERT`: The User has placed a fraud alert on their Plaid Check consumer report due to suspected fraud. Note: when a fraud alert is in place, the recipient of the consumer report has an obligation to verify the consumer's identity.|
|cause|[Cause](#schemacause)|true|none|An error object and associated `item_id` used to identify a specific Item and error when a batch operation operating on multiple Items has encountered an error in one of the Items.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|warning_code|IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE|
|warning_code|TRANSACTIONS_UNAVAILABLE|
|warning_code|USER_FRAUD_ALERT|

```json
"IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE"
```

The warning code identifies a specific kind of warning.

`IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE`: Account-owner information is not available.

`TRANSACTIONS_UNAVAILABLE`: Transactions information associated with Credit and Depository accounts are unavailable.

`USER_FRAUD_ALERT`: The User has placed a fraud alert on their Plaid Check consumer report due to suspected fraud. Note: when a fraud alert is in place, the recipient of the consumer report has an obligation to verify the consumer's identity.

An object representing a balance held by an account in the past

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|date|string(date)|true|none|The date of the calculated historical balance, in an [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD)|
|current|number(double)|true|none|The total amount of funds in the account, calculated from the `current` balance in the `balance` object by subtracting inflows and adding back outflows according to the posted date of each transaction.<br><br>If the account has any pending transactions, historical balance amounts on or before the date of the earliest pending transaction may differ if retrieved in subsequent reports as a result of those pending transactions posting.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the balance. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the balance. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|

<h2 id="tocS_HistoricalBalance">HistoricalBalance</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemahistoricalbalance"></a>
<a id="schema_HistoricalBalance"></a>
<a id="tocShistoricalbalance"></a>
<a id="tocshistoricalbalance"></a>

```json
{
  "date": "1970-01-01",
  "current": 0,
  "iso_currency_code": "string",
  "unofficial_currency_code": "string"
}
```

An object representing a balance held by an account in the past

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|date|string(date)|true|none|The date of the calculated historical balance, in an [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (YYYY-MM-DD)|
|current|number(double)|true|none|The total amount of funds in the account, calculated from the `current` balance in the `balance` object by subtracting inflows and adding back outflows according to the posted date of each transaction.<br><br>If the account has any pending transactions, historical balance amounts on or before the date of the earliest pending transaction may differ if retrieved in subsequent Asset Reports as a result of those pending transactions posting.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the balance. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the balance. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|

<h2 id="tocS_AssetsProductReadyWebhook">AssetsProductReadyWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaassetsproductreadywebhook"></a>
<a id="schema_AssetsProductReadyWebhook"></a>
<a id="tocSassetsproductreadywebhook"></a>
<a id="tocsassetsproductreadywebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "webhook_type": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "asset_report_id": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "report_type": "FULL",
  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

Fired when the Asset Report has been generated and `/asset_report/get` is ready to be called.  If you attempt to retrieve an Asset Report before this webhook has fired, you'll receive a response with the HTTP status code 400 and a Plaid error code of `PRODUCT_NOT_READY`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`ASSETS`|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`PRODUCT_READY`|
|asset_report_id|string|true|none|The `asset_report_id` corresponding to the Asset Report the webhook has fired for.|
|user_id|string|false|none|The `user_id` corresponding to the User ID the webhook has fired for.|
|report_type|[AssetReportType](#schemaassetreporttype)|false|none|Indicates either a Fast Asset Report, which will contain only current identity and balance information, or a Full Asset Report, which will also contain historical balance information and transaction data.|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|report_type|FULL|
|report_type|FAST|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

<h2 id="tocS_AssetsErrorWebhook">AssetsErrorWebhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaassetserrorwebhook"></a>
<a id="schema_AssetsErrorWebhook"></a>
<a id="tocSassetserrorwebhook"></a>
<a id="tocsassetserrorwebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "webhook_type": "string",
  "webhook_code": "string",
  "error": {
    "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "error_code": "string",
    "error_code_reason": "string",
    "error_message": "string",
    "display_message": "string",
    "request_id": "string",
    "causes": [
      null
    ],
    "status": 0,
    "documentation_url": "string",
    "suggested_action": "string",
    "required_account_subtypes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "provided_account_subtypes": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "asset_report_id": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "environment": "sandbox"
}
```

Fired when Asset Report generation has failed. The resulting `error` will have an `error_type` of `ASSET_REPORT_ERROR`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_type|string|true|none|`ASSETS`|
|webhook_code|string|true|none|`ERROR`|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|true|none|Errors are identified by `error_code` and categorized by `error_type`. Use these in preference to HTTP status codes to identify and handle specific errors. HTTP status codes are set and provide the broadest categorization of errors: 4xx codes are for developer- or user-related errors, and 5xx codes are for Plaid-related errors, and the status will be 2xx in non-error cases. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|asset_report_id|string|true|none|The ID associated with the Asset Report.|
|user_id|string|false|none|The `user_id` corresponding to the User ID the webhook has fired for.|
|environment|[WebhookEnvironmentValues](#schemawebhookenvironmentvalues)|true|none|The Plaid environment the webhook was sent from|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|environment|sandbox|
|environment|production|

<h2 id="tocS_Warning">Warning</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawarning"></a>
<a id="schema_Warning"></a>
<a id="tocSwarning"></a>
<a id="tocswarning"></a>

```json
{
  "warning_type": "string",
  "warning_code": "OWNERS_UNAVAILABLE",
  "cause": {
    "error_type": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "error_code": "string",
    "error_code_reason": "string",
    "error_message": "string",
    "display_message": "string",
    "request_id": "string",
    "causes": [
      null
    ],
    "status": 0,
    "documentation_url": "string",
    "suggested_action": "string",
    "required_account_subtypes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "provided_account_subtypes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "item_id": "string"
  }
}
```

It is possible for an Asset Report to be returned with missing account owner information. In such cases, the Asset Report will contain warning data in the response, indicating why obtaining the owner information failed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|warning_type|string|true|none|The warning type, which will always be `ASSET_REPORT_WARNING`|
|warning_code|string|true|none|The warning code identifies a specific kind of warning. `OWNERS_UNAVAILABLE` indicates that account-owner information is not available. `INVESTMENTS_UNAVAILABLE` indicates that Investments specific information is not available. `TRANSACTIONS_UNAVAILABLE` indicates that transactions information associated with Credit and Depository accounts are unavailable. The `BANK_INCOME_INSIGHTS_*` codes apply to the Bank Income add-on: `BANK_INCOME_INSIGHTS_INSUFFICIENT_DATA` indicates there was not enough data to compute Bank Income Insights; `BANK_INCOME_INSIGHTS_INCOMPLETE` indicates the Bank Income Insights flow was not completed; `BANK_INCOME_INSIGHTS_STATUS_IN_PROGRESS` indicates Bank Income Insights are still being computed; `BANK_INCOME_INSIGHTS_INTERNAL_ERROR` indicates an internal error occurred while computing Bank Income Insights; `BANK_INCOME_INSIGHTS_MISMATCHED_DAYS_REQUESTED` indicates the days requested for Bank Income Insights did not match that of the Asset Report.|
|cause|[Cause](#schemacause)|true|none|An error object and associated `item_id` used to identify a specific Item and error when a batch operation operating on multiple Items has encountered an error in one of the Items.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|warning_code|OWNERS_UNAVAILABLE|
|warning_code|INVESTMENTS_UNAVAILABLE|
|warning_code|TRANSACTIONS_UNAVAILABLE|
|warning_code|BANK_INCOME_INSIGHTS_INSUFFICIENT_DATA|
|warning_code|BANK_INCOME_INSIGHTS_INCOMPLETE|
|warning_code|BANK_INCOME_INSIGHTS_STATUS_IN_PROGRESS|
|warning_code|BANK_INCOME_INSIGHTS_INTERNAL_ERROR|
|warning_code|BANK_INCOME_INSIGHTS_MISMATCHED_DAYS_REQUESTED|

<h2 id="tocS_AssetReportUser">AssetReportUser</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaassetreportuser"></a>
<a id="schema_AssetReportUser"></a>
<a id="tocSassetreportuser"></a>
<a id="tocsassetreportuser"></a>

```json
{
  "client_user_id": "string",
  "first_name": "string",
  "middle_name": "string",
  "last_name": "string",
  "ssn": "string",
  "phone_number": "string",
  "email": "string"
}
```

The user object allows you to provide additional information about the user to be appended to the Asset Report. All fields are optional. The `first_name`, `last_name`, and `ssn` fields are required if you would like the Report to be eligible for Fannie Mae's Day 1 Certainty™ program.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_user_id|string \| null|false|none|An identifier you determine and submit for the user.|
|first_name|string \| null|false|none|The user's first name. Required for the Fannie Mae Day 1 Certainty™ program.|
|middle_name|string \| null|false|none|The user's middle name|
|last_name|string \| null|false|none|The user's last name.  Required for the Fannie Mae Day 1 Certainty™ program.|
|ssn|string \| null|false|none|The user's Social Security Number. Required for the Fannie Mae Day 1 Certainty™ program.<br><br>Format: "ddd-dd-dddd"|
|phone_number|string \| null|false|none|The user's phone number, in E.164 format: +{countrycode}{number}. For example: "+14151234567". Phone numbers provided in other formats will be parsed on a best-effort basis.|
|email|string \| null|false|none|The user's email address.|


An object representing an Asset Report

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|asset_report_id|[AssetReportId](#schemaassetreportid)|true|none|A unique ID identifying an Asset Report. Like all Plaid identifiers, this ID is case sensitive.|
|insights|object|false|none|none|
|client_report_id|string \| null|true|none|An identifier you determine and submit for the Asset Report.|
|date_generated|string(date-time)|true|none|The date and time when the Asset Report was created, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (e.g. "2018-04-12T03:32:11Z").|
|days_requested|number|true|none|The duration of transaction history you requested|
|user|[AssetReportUser](#schemaassetreportuser)|true|none|The user object allows you to provide additional information about the user to be appended to the Asset Report. All fields are optional. The `first_name`, `last_name`, and `ssn` fields are required if you would like the Report to be eligible for Fannie Mae's Day 1 Certainty™ program.|
|items|[[AssetReportItem](#schemaassetreportitem)]|true|none|Data returned by Plaid about each of the Items included in the Asset Report.|

A representation of an Item within an Asset Report.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|item_id|[ItemId](#schemaitemid)|true|none|The `item_id` of the Item associated with this webhook, warning, or error|
|institution_name|string|true|none|The full financial institution name associated with the Item.|
|institution_id|string|true|none|The id of the financial institution associated with the Item.|
|date_last_updated|string(date-time)|true|none|The date and time when this Item's data was last retrieved from the financial institution, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|accounts|[[AccountAssets](#schemaaccountassets)]|true|none|Data about each of the accounts open on the Item.|

Asset information about an account

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|Plaid's unique identifier for the account. This value will not change unless Plaid can't reconcile the account with the data returned by the financial institution. This may occur, for example, when the name of the account changes. If this happens a new `account_id` will be assigned to the account.<br><br>The `account_id` can also change if the `access_token` is deleted and the same credentials that were used to generate that `access_token` are used to generate a new `access_token` on a later date. In that case, the new `account_id` will be different from the old `account_id`.<br><br>If an account with a specific `account_id` disappears instead of changing, the account is likely closed. Closed accounts are not returned by the Plaid API.<br><br>Like all Plaid identifiers, the `account_id` is case sensitive.|
|balances|[AssetReportAccountBalance](#schemaassetreportaccountbalance)|true|none|A set of fields describing the balance for an account. Balance information may be cached unless the balance object was returned by `/accounts/balance/get`.|
|mask|string \| null|true|none|The last 2-4 alphanumeric characters of an account's official account number. Note that the mask may be non-unique between an Item's accounts, and it may also not match the mask that the bank displays to the user.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the account, either assigned by the user or by the financial institution itself|
|official_name|string \| null|true|none|The official name of the account as given by the financial institution|
|type|[AccountType](#schemaaccounttype)|true|none|`investment:` Investment account. In API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier, this type is called `brokerage` instead.<br><br>`credit:` Credit card<br><br>`depository:` Depository account<br><br>`loan:` Loan account<br><br>`other:` Non-specified account type<br><br>See the [Account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema) for a full listing of account types and corresponding subtypes.|
|subtype|[AccountSubtype](#schemaaccountsubtype)|true|none|See the [Account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#account-type-schema) for a full listing of account types and corresponding subtypes.|
|verification_status|string|false|none|The current verification status of an Auth Item initiated through Automated or Manual micro-deposits.  Returned for Auth Items only.<br><br>`pending_automatic_verification`: The Item is pending automatic verification.<br><br>`pending_manual_verification`: The Item is pending manual micro-deposit verification. Items remain in this state until the user successfully verifies the micro-deposit.<br><br>`automatically_verified`: The Item has successfully been automatically verified.<br><br>`manually_verified`: The Item has successfully been manually verified.<br><br>`verification_expired`: Plaid was unable to automatically verify the deposit within 7 calendar days and will no longer attempt to validate the Item. Users may retry by submitting their information again through Link.<br><br>`verification_failed`: The Item failed manual micro-deposit verification because the user exhausted all 3 verification attempts. Users may retry by submitting their information again through Link.<br><br>`database_matched`: (deprecated) The Item has successfully been verified using Plaid's data sources. Only returned for Auth Items created via Database Match.|
|persistent_account_id|string|false|none|A unique and persistent identifier for accounts that can be used to trace multiple instances of the same account across different Items for depository accounts. This is currently an opt-in field and only supported for Chase Items.|
|days_available|number|true|none|The duration of transaction history available within this report for this Item, typically defined as the time since the date of the earliest transaction in that account.|
|transactions|[[AssetReportTransaction](#schemaassetreporttransaction)]|true|none|Transaction history associated with the account.|
|investments|[AssetReportInvestments](#schemaassetreportinvestments)|false|none|A set of fields describing the investments data on an account.|
|owners|[[Owner](#schemaowner)]|true|none|Data returned by the financial institution about the account owner or owners. For business accounts, the name reported may be either the name of the individual or the name of the business, depending on the institution. Multiple owners on a single account will be represented in the same `owner` object, not in multiple owner objects within the array. In API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier, the `owners` object is not returned, and instead identity information is returned in the top level `identity` object. For more details, see [Plaid API versioning](https://plaid.com/docs/api/versioning/#version-2019-05-29)|
|ownership_type|[OwnershipType](#schemaownershiptype)|false|none|How an asset is owned.<br><br>`association`: Ownership by a corporation, partnership, or unincorporated association, including for-profit and not-for-profit organizations.<br><br>`individual`: Ownership by an individual.<br><br>`joint`: Joint ownership by multiple parties.<br><br>`trust`: Ownership by a revocable or irrevocable trust.|
|historical_balances|[[HistoricalBalance](#schemahistoricalbalance)]|true|none|Calculated data about the historical balances on the account.<br><br>Available for `credit` and `depository` type accounts.|
|account_insights|[AccountInsights](#schemaaccountinsights)|false|none|This is a container object for all lending-related insights. This field will be returned only for European customers.|

<h2 id="tocS_AssetReportAccountBalance">AssetReportAccountBalance</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaassetreportaccountbalance"></a>
<a id="schema_AssetReportAccountBalance"></a>
<a id="tocSassetreportaccountbalance"></a>
<a id="tocsassetreportaccountbalance"></a>

```json
{
  "available": 0,
  "current": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "margin_loan_amount": 0,
  "iso_currency_code": "string",
  "unofficial_currency_code": "string",
  "last_updated_datetime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

A set of fields describing the balance for an account. Balance information may be cached unless the balance object was returned by `/accounts/balance/get`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|available|number(double) \| null|true|none|The amount of funds available to be withdrawn from the account, as determined by the financial institution.<br><br>For `credit`-type accounts, the `available` balance typically equals the `limit` less the `current` balance, less any pending outflows plus any pending inflows.<br><br>For `depository`-type accounts, the `available` balance typically equals the `current` balance less any pending outflows plus any pending inflows. For `depository`-type accounts, the `available` balance does not include the overdraft limit.<br><br>For `investment`-type accounts (or `brokerage`-type accounts for API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier), the `available` balance is the total cash available to withdraw as presented by the institution.<br><br>Note that not all institutions calculate the `available`  balance. In the event that `available` balance is unavailable, Plaid will return an `available` balance value of `null`.<br><br>Available balance may be cached and is not guaranteed to be up-to-date in real-time unless the value was returned by `/accounts/balance/get`.<br><br>If `current` is `null` this field is guaranteed not to be `null`.|
|current|number(double) \| null|true|none|The total amount of funds in or owed by the account.<br><br>For `credit`-type accounts, a positive balance indicates the amount owed; a negative amount indicates the lender owing the account holder.<br><br>For `loan`-type accounts, the current balance is the principal remaining on the loan, except in the case of student loan accounts at Sallie Mae (`ins_116944`). For Sallie Mae student loans, the account's balance includes both principal and any outstanding interest.<br><br>For `investment`-type accounts (or `brokerage`-type accounts for API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier), the current balance is the total value of assets as presented by the institution.<br><br>Note that balance information may be cached unless the value was returned by `/accounts/balance/get`; if the Item is enabled for Transactions, the balance will be at least as recent as the most recent Transaction update. If you require real-time balance information, use the `available` balance as provided by `/accounts/balance/get`.<br><br>When returned by `/accounts/balance/get`, this field may be `null`. When this happens, `available` is guaranteed not to be `null`.|
|limit|number(double) \| null|true|none|For `credit`-type accounts, this represents the credit limit.<br><br>For `depository`-type accounts, this represents the pre-arranged overdraft limit, which is common for current (checking) accounts in Europe.<br><br>In North America, this field is typically only available for `credit`-type accounts.|
|margin_loan_amount|number(double) \| null|true|none|The total amount of borrowed funds in the account, as determined by the financial institution.<br>For investment-type accounts, the margin balance is the total value of borrowed assets in the account, as presented by the institution.<br>This is commonly referred to as margin or a loan.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the balance. Always null if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-null.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the balance. Always null if `iso_currency_code` is non-null. Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|
|last_updated_datetime|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`) indicating the oldest acceptable balance when making a request to `/accounts/balance/get`.<br><br>This field is only used and expected when the institution is `ins_128026` (Capital One) and the Item contains one or more accounts with a non-depository account type, in which case a value must be provided or an `INVALID_REQUEST` error with the code of `INVALID_FIELD` will be returned. For Capital One depository accounts as well as all other account types on all other institutions, this field is ignored. See [account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#account-type-schema) for a full list of account types.<br><br>If the balance that is pulled is older than the given timestamp for Items with this field required, an `INVALID_RESULT` error with the code of `LAST_UPDATED_DATETIME_OUT_OF_RANGE` will be returned with the most recent timestamp for the requested account contained in the response.|

A transaction within an investment account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|investment_transaction_id|string|true|none|The ID of the Investment transaction, unique across all Plaid transactions. Like all Plaid identifiers, the `investment_transaction_id` is case sensitive.|
|account_id|string|true|none|The `account_id` of the account against which this transaction posted.|
|security_id|string \| null|true|none|The `security_id` to which this transaction is related.|
|date|string(date)|true|none|The [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) posting date for the transaction.|
|name|string|true|none|The institution's description of the transaction.|
|quantity|number(double)|true|none|The number of units of the security involved in this transaction. Positive for buy transactions; negative for sell transactions.|
|amount|number(double)|true|none|The complete value of the transaction. Positive values when cash is debited, e.g. purchases of stock; negative values when cash is credited, e.g. sales of stock. Treatment remains the same for cash-only movements unassociated with securities. For transactions representing a simultaneous cash contribution and purchase of a security, the portion of the transaction representing the purchase takes precedence, and the `amount` is represented as positive.|
|price|number(double)|true|none|The price of the security at which this transaction occurred.|
|fees|number(double) \| null|true|none|The combined value of all fees applied to this transaction|
|type|[InvestmentTransactionType](#schemainvestmenttransactiontype)|true|none|Value is one of the following:<br><br>`buy`: Buying an investment<br><br>`sell`: Selling an investment<br><br>`cancel`: A cancellation of a pending transaction<br><br>`cash`: Activity that modifies a cash position<br><br>`fee`: A fee on the account<br><br>`transfer`: Activity which modifies a position, but not through buy/sell activity e.g. options exercise, portfolio transfer<br><br>For descriptions of possible transaction types and subtypes, see the [Investment transaction types schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#investment-transaction-types-schema).|
|subtype|[InvestmentTransactionSubtype](#schemainvestmenttransactionsubtype)|true|none|For descriptions of possible transaction types and subtypes, see the [Investment transaction types schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#investment-transaction-types-schema).|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the transaction. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the transaction. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`. Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|The Plaid `account_id` associated with the holding.|
|security_id|string|true|none|The Plaid `security_id` associated with the holding. Security data is not specific to a user's account; any user who held the same security at the same financial institution at the same time would have identical security data. The `security_id` for the same security will typically be the same across different institutions, but this is not guaranteed. The `security_id` does not typically change, but may change if inherent details of the security change due to a corporate action, for example, in the event of a ticker symbol change or CUSIP change.|
|ticker_symbol|string \| null|true|none|The holding's trading symbol for publicly traded holdings, and otherwise a short identifier if available.|
|institution_price|number(double)|true|none|The last price given by the institution for this security.|
|institution_price_as_of|string(date) \| null|false|none|The date at which `institution_price` was current.|
|institution_value|number(double)|true|none|The value of the holding, as reported by the institution.|
|quantity|number(double)|true|none|The total quantity of the asset held, as reported by the financial institution. If the security is an option, `quantity` will reflect the total number of options (typically the number of contracts multiplied by 100), not the number of contracts.|
|vested_quantity|number(double) \| null|false|none|The total quantity of vested assets held, as reported by the financial institution. Vested assets are only associated with [equities](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/investments/#investments-holdings-get-response-securities-type).|
|vested_value|number(double) \| null|false|none|The value of the vested holdings as reported by the institution.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the holding. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the holding. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`. Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.<br>|
|tax_lots|[[HoldingTaxLot](#schemaholdingtaxlot)]|false|none|Per-lot acquisition data for this holding. This field is absent when lot-level data is not available for the holding — either the institution does not provide it, or the report was generated before lot-level data was supported. Refresh the report if you expect lots.|

A transaction on the asset report

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|The ID of the account in which this transaction occurred.|
|amount|number(double)|true|none|The settled value of the transaction, denominated in the transaction's currency, as stated in `iso_currency_code` or `unofficial_currency_code`. Positive values when money moves out of the account; negative values when money moves in. For example, debit card purchases are positive; credit card payments, direct deposits, and refunds are negative.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the transaction. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-null.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the transaction. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`. Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|
|original_description|string \| null|true|none|The string returned by the financial institution to describe the transaction.|
|category|[string]|false|none|A hierarchical array of the categories to which this transaction belongs. For a full list of categories, see [`/categories/get`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#categoriesget).<br><br>This field will only appear in an Asset Report with Insights.|
|category_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the category to which this transaction belongs. For a full list of categories, see [`/categories/get`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#categoriesget).<br><br>This field will only appear in an Asset Report with Insights.|
|credit_category|[CreditCategory](#schemacreditcategory)|false|none|Information describing the intent of the transaction. Most relevant for credit use cases, but not limited to such use cases.<br><br>See the [`taxonomy csv file`](https://plaid.com/documents/credit-category-taxonomy.csv) for a full list of credit categories.|
|check_number|string \| null|false|none|The check number of the transaction. This field is only populated for check transactions.|
|date|string(date)|true|none|For pending transactions, the date that the transaction occurred; for posted transactions, the date that the transaction posted. Both dates are returned in an [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format ( `YYYY-MM-DD` ).|
|date_transacted|string \| null|false|none|The date on which the transaction took place, in ISO 8601 format.|
|location|[Location](#schemalocation)|false|none|A representation of where a transaction took place. Location data is provided only for transactions at physical locations, not for online transactions. Location data availability depends primarily on the merchant and is most likely to be populated for transactions at large retail chains; small, local businesses are less likely to have location data available.|
|name|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** The merchant name or transaction description. This is a legacy field that is no longer maintained. For merchant name, use the `merchant_name` field. For description, use the `original_description` field.<br><br>This field will only appear in an Asset Report with Insights.|
|merchant_name|string \| null|false|none|The merchant name, as enriched by Plaid. This is typically a more human-readable version of the merchant counterparty in the transaction. For some bank transactions (such as checks or account transfers) where there is no meaningful merchant name, this value will be `null`.|
|payment_meta|[PaymentMeta](#schemapaymentmeta)|false|none|Transaction information specific to inter-bank transfers. If the transaction was not an inter-bank transfer, all fields will be `null`.<br><br>If the `transactions` object was returned by a Transactions endpoint such as `/transactions/sync` or `/transactions/get`, the `payment_meta` key will always appear, but no data elements are guaranteed. If the `transactions` object was returned by an Assets endpoint such as `/asset_report/get` or `/asset_report/pdf/get`, this field will only appear in an Asset Report with Insights.|
|pending|boolean|true|none|When `true`, identifies the transaction as pending or unsettled. Pending transaction details (name, type, amount, category ID) may change before they are settled.|
|pending_transaction_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of a posted transaction's associated pending transaction, where applicable.|
|account_owner|string \| null|false|none|The name of the account owner. This field is not typically populated and only relevant when dealing with sub-accounts.|
|transaction_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the transaction. Like all Plaid identifiers, the `transaction_id` is case sensitive.|
|transaction_type|[AssetReportTransactionType](#schemaassetreporttransactiontype)|false|none|`digital:` transactions that took place online.<br><br>`place:` transactions that were made at a physical location.<br><br>`special:` transactions that relate to banks, e.g. fees or deposits.<br><br>`unresolved:` transactions that do not fit into the other three types.<br>|
|income_source_id|string|false|none|A unique identifier for an income source.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|transaction_type|place|
|transaction_type|special|
|transaction_type|unresolved|

This is a container object for all lending-related insights. This field will be returned only for European customers.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|risk|[RiskIndicators](#schemariskindicators)|false|none|Risk indicators focus on providing signal on the possibility of a borrower defaulting on their loan repayments by providing data points related to its payment behavior, debt, and other relevant financial information, helping lenders gauge the level of risk involved in a certain operation.|
|affordability|[AffordabilityInsights](#schemaaffordabilityinsights)|false|none|Affordability insights focus on providing signal on the ability of a borrower to repay their loan without experiencing financial strain. It provides insights on factors such as a user's monthly income and expenses, disposable income, average expenditure, etc., helping lenders gauge the level of affordability of a borrower.|

Affordability insights focus on providing signal on the ability of a borrower to repay their loan without experiencing financial strain. It provides insights on factors such as a user's monthly income and expenses, disposable income, average expenditure, etc., helping lenders gauge the level of affordability of a borrower.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expenditure|[ExpenditureInsights](#schemaexpenditureinsights)|false|none|Comprehensive analysis of spending patterns, categorizing expenses into essential, non-essential, and other categories.|
|income|[IncomeInsights](#schemaincomeinsights)|false|none|Comprehensive income analysis including total income, income excluding transfers, and inbound transfer amounts.|

Risk indicators focus on providing signal on the possibility of a borrower defaulting on their loan repayments by providing data points related to its payment behavior, debt, and other relevant financial information, helping lenders gauge the level of risk involved in a certain operation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bank_penalties|[BankPenaltiesIndicators](#schemabankpenaltiesindicators)|false|none|Insights into bank penalties and fees, including overdraft fees, NSF fees, and other bank-imposed charges.|
|gambling|[GamblingIndicators](#schemagamblingindicators)|false|none|Insights into gambling-related transactions, including frequency, amounts, and top merchants.|
|loan_disbursements|[LoanDisbursementsIndicators](#schemaloandisbursementsindicators)|false|none|Insights into loan disbursement transactions received by the user, tracking incoming funds from loan providers.|
|loan_payments|[LoanPaymentsIndicators](#schemaloanpaymentsindicators)|false|none|Insights into loan payment transactions made by the user, tracking outgoing payments to loan providers.|
|negative_balance|[NegativeBalanceInsights](#schemanegativebalanceinsights)|false|none|Insights into negative balance occurrences, including frequency, duration, and minimum balance details.|

Insights into bank penalties and fees, including overdraft fees, NSF fees, and other bank-imposed charges.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|number(double) \| null|false|none|The total value of outflow transactions categorized as `BANK_PENALTIES`, across all the accounts in the report within the requested time window.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the amount. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the amount. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|
|monthly_average|[MonthlyAverage](#schemamonthlyaverage)|false|none|The monthly average amount calculated by dividing the total by the number of calendar months in the time period.|
|category_details|[[CategoryExpenses](#schemacategoryexpenses)]|false|none|Detailed categories view of all the transactions that fall into the `BANK_PENALTIES` credit category within the given time window, across all the accounts in the report.|
|transactions_count|integer \| null|false|none|The total number of transactions that fall into the `BANK_PENALTIES` credit category, across all the accounts in the report.|

|iso_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the amount. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the amount. |amount|number(double) \| null|false|none|The monthly average amount of all the aggregated transactions of the given category, across all the accounts for the given time window.<br><br>The average is calculated by dividing the total amount of the transactions by the number of calendar months in the given time window.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the amount. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the amount. Summary statistics for a specific expenditure category, including total amount, monthly average, and percentage of income.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|number(double) \| null|false|none|The total value of all the aggregated transactions in this expenditure category.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the amount. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the amount. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|
|monthly_average|[MonthlyAverage](#schemamonthlyaverage)|false|none|The monthly average amount calculated by dividing the total by the number of calendar months in the time period.|
|transactions_count|integer \| null|false|none|The total number of outflow transactions in this expenses group, within the given time window across all the accounts in the report.|
|percentage_of_income|number(double) \| null|false|none|The percentage of the total inflows that was spent in this expenses group, within the given time window across all the accounts in the report.<br>For example, a value of 100 represents that 100% of the inflows were spent on transactions that fall into this expenditure group.<br>If there's no available income for the given time period, this field value will be `-1`.|
|top_categories|[[CategoryExpenses](#schemacategoryexpenses)]|false|none|The primary credit categories of the expenses within the given time window, across all the accounts in the report.<br><br>The categories are sorted in descending order by the total value spent.<br>See the [category taxonomy](https://plaid.com/documents/credit-category-taxonomy.csv) for a full listing of category IDs.|

A monetary amount with its associated currency information, supporting both official and unofficial currency codes.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|number(double) \| null|false|none|If the parent object represents a category of transactions, such as `total_amount`, `transfers_in`, `total_income`, etc. the `amount` represents the sum of all of the transactions in the group.<br><br>If the parent object is `cash_flow`, the `amount` represents the total value of all the inflows minus all the outflows across all the accounts in the report in the given time window.<br><br>If the parent object is `minimum_balance`, the `amount` represents the lowest balance of the account during the given time window.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the amount. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|false|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the amount. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|

Calculated attributes derived from transaction-level data, aggregated across accounts.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|nsf_overdraft_transactions_count|integer|false|none|The number of net NSF fee transactions in the time range for the report (not counting any fees that were reversed within that time range).|
|nsf_overdraft_transactions_count_30d|integer|false|none|The number of net NSF fee transactions in the last 30 days in the report (not counting any fees that were reversed within that time range).|
|nsf_overdraft_transactions_count_60d|integer|false|none|The number of net NSF fee transactions in the last 60 days in the report (not counting any fees that were reversed within that time range).|
|nsf_overdraft_transactions_count_90d|integer|false|none|The number of net NSF fee transactions in the last 90 days in the report (not counting any fees that were reversed within that time range).|
|total_inflow_amount|[TotalReportInflowAmount](#schematotalreportinflowamount)|false|none|Total amount of money into the report's accounts in the time period of the report. This field only takes into account USD transactions from the accounts.|
|total_inflow_amount_30d|[TotalReportInflowAmount30d](#schematotalreportinflowamount30d)|false|none|Total amount of money into the report's accounts in the last 30 days. This field only takes into account USD transactions from the accounts.|
|total_inflow_amount_60d|[TotalReportInflowAmount60d](#schematotalreportinflowamount60d)|false|none|Total amount of money into the report's accounts in the last 60 days. This field only takes into account USD transactions from the accounts.|
|total_inflow_amount_90d|[TotalReportInflowAmount90d](#schematotalreportinflowamount90d)|false|none|Total amount of money into the report's accounts in the last 90 days. This field only takes into account USD transactions from the accounts.|
|total_outflow_amount|[TotalReportOutflowAmount](#schematotalreportoutflowamount)|false|none|Total amount of money out of the report's accounts in the time period of the report. This field only takes into account USD transactions from the accounts.|
|total_outflow_amount_30d|[TotalReportOutflowAmount30d](#schematotalreportoutflowamount30d)|false|none|Total amount of money out of the report's accounts in the last 30 days. This field only takes into account USD transactions from the accounts.|
|total_outflow_amount_60d|[TotalReportOutflowAmount60d](#schematotalreportoutflowamount60d)|false|none|Total amount of money out of the report's accounts in the last 60 days. This field only takes into account USD transactions from the accounts.|
|total_outflow_amount_90d|[TotalReportOutflowAmount90d](#schematotalreportoutflowamount90d)|false|none|Total amount of money out of the report's accounts in the last 90 days. This field only takes into account USD transactions from the accounts.|

|accounts|[[BaseReportAccount](#schemabasereportaccount)]|true|none|Data about each of the accounts open on the Item.|

Base Report information about an account

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|Plaid's unique identifier for the account. This value will not change unless Plaid can't reconcile the account with the data returned by the financial institution. This may occur, for example, when the name of the account changes. If this happens a new `account_id` will be assigned to the account.<br><br>If an account with a specific `account_id` disappears instead of changing, the account is likely closed. Closed accounts are not returned by the Plaid API.<br><br>Like all Plaid identifiers, the `account_id` is case sensitive.|
|balances|[BaseReportAccountBalances](#schemabasereportaccountbalances)|true|none|Information about an account's balances.|
|consumer_disputes|[[ConsumerDispute](#schemaconsumerdispute)]|true|none|The information about previously submitted valid dispute statements by the consumer|
|mask|string \| null|true|none|The last 2-4 alphanumeric characters of an account's official account number. Note that the mask may be non-unique between an Item's accounts, and it may also not match the mask that the bank displays to the user.|
|metadata|[BaseReportAccountMetadata](#schemabasereportaccountmetadata)|true|none|Metadata about the extracted account.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the account, either assigned by the user or by the financial institution itself|
|official_name|string \| null|true|none|The official name of the account as given by the financial institution|
|type|[AccountType](#schemaaccounttype)|true|none|`investment:` Investment account. In API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier, this type is called `brokerage` instead.<br><br>`credit:` Credit card<br><br>`depository:` Depository account<br><br>`loan:` Loan account<br><br>`other:` Non-specified account type<br><br>See the [Account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#account-type-schema) for a full listing of account types and corresponding subtypes.|
|subtype|[AccountSubtype](#schemaaccountsubtype)|true|none|See the [Account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#account-type-schema) for a full listing of account types and corresponding subtypes.|
|days_available|number|true|none|The duration of transaction history available within this report for this Item, typically defined as the time since the date of the earliest transaction in that account.|
|transactions|[[BaseReportTransaction](#schemabasereporttransaction)]|true|none|Transaction history associated with the account. Transaction history returned by endpoints such as `/transactions/get` or `/investments/transactions/get` will be returned in the top-level `transactions` field instead. Some transactions may have their details masked in accordance with the FCRA. These will appear with a `credit_category` of `MASKED_TRANSACTION_CATEGORY`.|
|owners|[[Owner](#schemaowner)]|true|none|Data returned by the financial institution about the account owner or owners. For business accounts, the name reported may be either the name of the individual or the name of the business, depending on the institution. Multiple owners on a single account will be represented in the same `owner` object, not in multiple owner objects within the array. This array can also be empty if no owners are found.|
|ownership_type|[OwnershipType](#schemaownershiptype)|true|none|How an asset is owned.<br><br>`association`: Ownership by a corporation, partnership, or unincorporated association, including for-profit and not-for-profit organizations.<br><br>`individual`: Ownership by an individual.<br><br>`joint`: Joint ownership by multiple parties.<br><br>`trust`: Ownership by a revocable or irrevocable trust.|
|historical_balances|[[BaseReportHistoricalBalance](#schemabasereporthistoricalbalance)]|false|none|Calculated data about the historical balances on the account. Currently not supported by `brokerage` or `investment` accounts.|
|account_insights|[BaseReportAccountInsights](#schemabasereportaccountinsights)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Calculated insights derived from transaction-level data. This field has been deprecated in favor of [Base Report attributes aggregated across accounts](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/check-legacy/#cra-check_report-base_report-get-response-report-attributes) and will be removed in a future release.|
|attributes|[BaseReportAttributes](#schemabasereportattributes)|false|none|Calculated attributes derived from transaction-level data.|

<h2 id="tocS_BaseReportAccountBalances">BaseReportAccountBalances</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabasereportaccountbalances"></a>
<a id="schema_BaseReportAccountBalances"></a>
<a id="tocSbasereportaccountbalances"></a>
<a id="tocsbasereportaccountbalances"></a>

```json
{
  "available": 0,
  "current": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "iso_currency_code": "string",
  "unofficial_currency_code": "string",
  "last_updated_datetime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "average_balance": 0,
  "average_monthly_balances": [
    {
      "start_date": "string",
      "end_date": "string",
      "average_balance": {
        "amount": 0,
        "iso_currency_code": "string",
        "unofficial_currency_code": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "most_recent_thirty_day_average_balance": 0
}
```

Information about an account's balances.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|available|number(double) \| null|true|none|The amount of funds available to be withdrawn from the account, as determined by the financial institution.<br><br>For `credit`-type accounts, the `available` balance typically equals the `limit` less the `current` balance, less any pending outflows plus any pending inflows.<br><br>For `depository`-type accounts, the `available` balance typically equals the `current` balance less any pending outflows plus any pending inflows. For `depository`-type accounts, the `available` balance does not include the overdraft limit.<br><br>For `investment`-type accounts (or `brokerage`-type accounts for API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier), the `available` balance is the total cash available to withdraw as presented by the institution.<br><br>Note that not all institutions calculate the `available`  balance. In the event that `available` balance is unavailable, Plaid will return an `available` balance value of `null`.<br><br>Available balance may be cached and is not guaranteed to be up-to-date in real-time unless the value was returned by `/accounts/balance/get`.<br><br>If `current` is `null` this field is guaranteed not to be `null`.|
|current|number(double) \| null|true|none|The total amount of funds in or owed by the account.<br><br>For `credit`-type accounts, a positive balance indicates the amount owed; a negative amount indicates the lender owing the account holder.<br><br>For `loan`-type accounts, the current balance is the principal remaining on the loan, except in the case of student loan accounts at Sallie Mae (`ins_116944`). For Sallie Mae student loans, the account's balance includes both principal and any outstanding interest.<br><br>For `investment`-type accounts (or `brokerage`-type accounts for API versions 2018-05-22 and earlier), the current balance is the total value of assets as presented by the institution.<br><br>Note that balance information may be cached unless the value was returned by `/accounts/balance/get`; if the Item is enabled for Transactions, the balance will be at least as recent as the most recent Transaction update. If you require real-time balance information, use the `available` balance as provided by `/accounts/balance/get`.<br><br>When returned by `/accounts/balance/get`, this field may be `null`. When this happens, `available` is guaranteed not to be `null`.|
|limit|number(double) \| null|true|none|For `credit`-type accounts, this represents the credit limit.<br><br>For `depository`-type accounts, this represents the pre-arranged overdraft limit, which is common for current (checking) accounts in Europe.<br><br>In North America, this field is typically only available for `credit`-type accounts.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the balance. Always null if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-null.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the balance. Always null if `iso_currency_code` is non-null. Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|
|last_updated_datetime|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`) indicating the oldest acceptable balance when making a request to `/accounts/balance/get`.<br><br>This field is only used and expected when the institution is `ins_128026` (Capital One) and the Item contains one or more accounts with a non-depository account type, in which case a value must be provided or an `INVALID_REQUEST` error with the code of `INVALID_FIELD` will be returned. For Capital One depository accounts as well as all other account types on all other institutions, this field is ignored. See [account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#account-type-schema) for a full list of account types.<br><br>If the balance that is pulled is older than the given timestamp for Items with this field required, an `INVALID_RESULT` error with the code of `LAST_UPDATED_DATETIME_OUT_OF_RANGE` will be returned with the most recent timestamp for the requested account contained in the response.|
|average_balance|number(double) \| null|false|none|The average historical balance for the entire report|
|average_monthly_balances|[[BaseReportAverageMonthlyBalances](#schemabasereportaveragemonthlybalances)]|false|none|The average historical balance of each calendar month|
|most_recent_thirty_day_average_balance|number(double) \| null|false|none|The average historical balance from the most recent 30 days|

A transaction on the Base Report

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|The ID of the account in which this transaction occurred.|
|amount|number(double)|true|none|The settled value of the transaction, denominated in the transaction's currency, as stated in `iso_currency_code` or `unofficial_currency_code`. Positive values when money moves out of the account; negative values when money moves in. For example, debit card purchases are positive; credit card payments, direct deposits, and refunds are negative.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the transaction. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-null.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the transaction. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`. Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The merchant name or transaction description.<br><br>Note: This is a legacy field that is not actively maintained. Use `merchant_name` instead for the merchant name.|
|original_description|string \| null|true|none|The string returned by the financial institution to describe the transaction.|
|credit_category|[CreditCategory](#schemacreditcategory)|false|none|Information describing the intent of the transaction. Most relevant for credit use cases, but not limited to such use cases.<br><br>See the [`taxonomy csv file`](https://plaid.com/documents/credit-category-taxonomy.csv) for a full list of credit categories.|
|check_number|string \| null|false|none|The check number of the transaction. This field is only populated for check transactions.|
|date|string(date)|true|none|For pending transactions, the date that the transaction occurred; for posted transactions, the date that the transaction posted. Both dates are returned in an [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format ( `YYYY-MM-DD` ).|
|date_transacted|string \| null|false|none|The date on which the transaction took place, in ISO 8601 format.|
|location|[Location](#schemalocation)|false|none|A representation of where a transaction took place. Location data is provided only for transactions at physical locations, not for online transactions. Location data availability depends primarily on the merchant and is most likely to be populated for transactions at large retail chains; small, local businesses are less likely to have location data available.|
|merchant_name|string \| null|false|none|The merchant name, as enriched by Plaid from the `name` field. This is typically a more human-readable version of the merchant counterparty in the transaction. For some bank transactions (such as checks or account transfers) where there is no meaningful merchant name, this value will be `null`.|
|pending|boolean|true|none|When `true`, identifies the transaction as pending or unsettled. Pending transaction details (name, type, amount, category ID) may change before they are settled.|
|account_owner|string \| null|false|none|The name of the account owner. This field is not typically populated and only relevant when dealing with sub-accounts.|
|transaction_id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the transaction. Like all Plaid identifiers, the `transaction_id` is case sensitive.|
|transaction_type|[BaseReportTransactionType](#schemabasereporttransactiontype)|false|none|`digital:` transactions that took place online.<br><br>`place:` transactions that were made at a physical location.<br><br>`special:` transactions that relate to banks, e.g. fees or deposits.<br><br>`unresolved:` transactions that do not fit into the other types.<br>|
|category|[string]|false|none|A hierarchical array of the categories to which this transaction belongs. For a full list of categories, see [`/categories/get`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#categoriesget).|
|category_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the category to which this transaction belongs. For a full list of categories, see [`/categories/get`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#categoriesget).|
|personal_finance_category|object|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|transaction_type|digital|
|transaction_type|place|
|transaction_type|special|
|transaction_type|unresolved|
