```json
}
```

A transaction within an investment account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|investment_transaction_id|string|true|none|The ID of the Investment transaction, unique across all Plaid transactions. Like all Plaid identifiers, the `investment_transaction_id` is case sensitive.|
|account_id|string|true|none|The `account_id` of the account against which this transaction posted.|
|security_id|string \| null|true|none|The `security_id` to which this transaction is related.|
|date|string(date)|true|none|The [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) posting date for the transaction.|
|name|string|true|none|The institution's description of the transaction.|
|quantity|number(double)|true|none|The number of units of the security involved in this transaction. Positive for buy transactions; negative for sell transactions.|
|amount|number(double)|true|none|The complete value of the transaction. Positive values when cash is debited, e.g. purchases of stock; negative values when cash is credited, e.g. sales of stock. Treatment remains the same for cash-only movements unassociated with securities. For transactions representing a simultaneous cash contribution and purchase of a security, the portion of the transaction representing the purchase takes precedence, and the `amount` is represented as positive.|
|price|number(double)|true|none|The price of the security at which this transaction occurred.|
|fees|number(double) \| null|true|none|The combined value of all fees applied to this transaction|
|type|[InvestmentTransactionType](#schemainvestmenttransactiontype)|true|none|Value is one of the following:<br><br>`buy`: Buying an investment<br><br>`sell`: Selling an investment<br><br>`cancel`: A cancellation of a pending transaction<br><br>`cash`: Activity that modifies a cash position<br><br>`fee`: A fee on the account<br><br>`transfer`: Activity which modifies a position, but not through buy/sell activity e.g. options exercise, portfolio transfer<br><br>For descriptions of possible transaction types and subtypes, see the [Investment transaction types schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#investment-transaction-types-schema).|
|subtype|[InvestmentTransactionSubtype](#schemainvestmenttransactionsubtype)|true|none|For descriptions of possible transaction types and subtypes, see the [Investment transaction types schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#investment-transaction-types-schema).|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the transaction. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the transaction. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`. Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.|

A securities holding at an institution.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string|true|none|The Plaid `account_id` associated with the holding.|
|security_id|string|true|none|The Plaid `security_id` associated with the holding. Security data is not specific to a user's account; any user who held the same security at the same financial institution at the same time would have identical security data. The `security_id` for the same security will typically be the same across different institutions, but this is not guaranteed. The `security_id` does not typically change, but may change if inherent details of the security change due to a corporate action, for example, in the event of a ticker symbol change or CUSIP change.|
|institution_price|number(double)|true|none|The last price given by the institution for this security.|
|institution_price_as_of|string(date) \| null|false|none|The date at which `institution_price` was current.|
|institution_value|number(double)|true|none|The value of the holding, as reported by the institution.|
|cost_basis|number(double) \| null|true|none|The original total value of the holding. This field is calculated by Plaid as the sum of the purchase price of all of the shares in the holding.|
|quantity|number(double)|true|none|The total quantity of the asset held, as reported by the financial institution. If the security is an option, `quantity` will reflect the total number of options (typically the number of contracts multiplied by 100), not the number of contracts.|
|iso_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-4217 currency code of the holding. Always `null` if `unofficial_currency_code` is non-`null`.|
|unofficial_currency_code|string \| null|true|none|The unofficial currency code associated with the holding. Always `null` if `iso_currency_code` is non-`null`. Unofficial currency codes are used for currencies that do not have official ISO currency codes, such as cryptocurrencies and the currencies of certain countries.<br><br>See the [currency code schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts#currency-code-schema) for a full listing of supported `unofficial_currency_code`s.<br>|
|tax_lots|[[HoldingTaxLot](#schemaholdingtaxlot)]|false|none|Per-lot acquisition data for this holding. This field is absent when lot-level data is not available for the holding — either the institution does not provide it, or the report was generated before lot-level data was supported. Refresh the report if you expect lots.|

|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|access_token|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|false|none|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|
|options|[BeaconAccountRiskEvaluateRequestOptions](#schemabeaconaccountriskevaluaterequestoptions)|false|none|An optional object to filter `/beacon/account_risk/v1/evaluate` results to a subset of the accounts on the linked Item.|
|client_user_id|string|false|none|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. This ID is used to correlate requests by a user with multiple evaluations and/or multiple linked accounts. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|client_evaluation_id|string|false|none|Unique identifier of what you are looking to evaluate (account add, information change, etc.) to allow us to tie the activity to the decisions and possible fraud outcome sent via our feedback endpoints. You can use your internal request ID or similar.|
|evaluation_reason|[BeaconAccountRiskEvaluateEvaluationReason](#schemabeaconaccountriskevaluateevaluationreason)|false|none|Description of the reason you want to evaluate risk.<br><br>`ONBOARDING`: user links a first bank account as part of the onboarding flow of your platform.<br><br>`NEW_ACCOUNT`: user links another bank account or replaces the currently linked bank account on your platform.<br><br>`INFORMATION_CHANGE`: user changes their information on your platform, e.g., updating their phone number.<br><br>`DORMANT_USER`:  you decide to re-evaluate a user that becomes active after a period of inactivity.<br><br>`OTHER`: any other reasons not listed here<br><br>Possible values:  `ONBOARDING`, `NEW_ACCOUNT`, `INFORMATION_CHANGE`, `DORMANT_USER`, `OTHER`<br>|
|device|[SignalDevice](#schemasignaldevice)|false|none|Details about the end user's device. These fields are optional, but strongly recommended to increase the accuracy of results when using Signal Transaction Scores. When using a Balance-only Ruleset, these fields are ignored if the Signal Addendum has been signed; if it has not been signed, using these fields will result in an error.|
|evaluate_time|string|false|none|The time the event for evaluation has occurred. Populate this field for backfilling data. If you don't populate this field, we'll use the timestamp at the time of receipt. Use ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ).|

|evaluation_reason|OTHER|


Description of the reason you want to evaluate risk.

`ONBOARDING`: user links a first bank account as part of the onboarding flow of your platform.

`NEW_ACCOUNT`: user links another bank account or replaces the currently linked bank account on your platform.

`INFORMATION_CHANGE`: user changes their information on your platform, e.g., updating their phone number.

`DORMANT_USER`:  you decide to re-evaluate a user that becomes active after a period of inactivity.

`OTHER`: any other reasons not listed here

Possible values:  `ONBOARDING`, `NEW_ACCOUNT`, `INFORMATION_CHANGE`, `DORMANT_USER`, `OTHER`

The attributes object contains data that can be used to assess account risk. Examples of data include:

`days_since_first_plaid_connection`: The number of days since the first time the Item was connected to an application via Plaid

`plaid_connections_count_7d`: The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid over the past 7 days

`plaid_connections_count_30d`: The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid over the past 30 days

`total_plaid_connections_count`: The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid

For the full list and detailed documentation of core attributes available, or to request that core attributes not be returned, contact sales or your Plaid account manager

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|

|is_account_closed|boolean \| null|false|none|Indicates if the account has been closed by the financial institution or the consumer, or is at risk of being closed|
|is_account_frozen_or_restricted|boolean \| null|false|none|Indicates whether the account has withdrawals and transfers disabled or if access to the account is restricted. This could be due to a freeze by the credit issuer, legal restrictions (e.g., sanctions), or regulatory requirements limiting monthly withdrawals, among other reasons|
|total_plaid_connections_count|integer \| null|false|none|The total number of times the item has been connected to applications via Plaid|
|plaid_connections_count_7d|integer \| null|false|none|The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid over the past 7 days|
|plaid_connections_count_30d|integer \| null|false|none|The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid over the past 30 days|
|failed_plaid_non_oauth_authentication_attempts_count_3d|integer \| null|false|none|The number of failed non-OAuth authentication attempts via Plaid for this bank account over the past 3 days|

The attributes object contains data that can be used to assess account risk. Examples of data include:

`days_since_first_plaid_connection`: The number of days since the first time the Item was connected to an application via Plaid

`plaid_connections_count_7d`: The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid over the past 7 days

`plaid_connections_count_30d`: The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid over the past 30 days

`total_plaid_connections_count`: The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid

For the full list and detailed documentation of core attributes available, or to request that core attributes not be returned, contact sales or your Plaid account manager

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|days_since_first_plaid_connection|integer \| null|true|none|The number of days since the first time the Item was connected to an application via Plaid|
|is_account_closed|boolean \| null|true|none|Indicates if the account has been closed by the financial institution or the consumer, or is at risk of being closed|
|is_account_frozen_or_restricted|boolean \| null|true|none|Indicates whether the account has withdrawals and transfers disabled or if access to the account is restricted. This could be due to a freeze by the credit issuer, legal restrictions (e.g., sanctions), or regulatory requirements limiting monthly withdrawals, among other reasons|
|total_plaid_connections_count|integer \| null|true|none|The total number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid|
|plaid_connections_count_7d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid over the past 7 days|
|plaid_connections_count_30d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid over the past 30 days|
|failed_plaid_non_oauth_authentication_attempts_count_3d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of failed non-OAuth authentication attempts via Plaid for this bank account over the past 3 days|
|plaid_non_oauth_authentication_attempts_count_3d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of non-OAuth authentication attempts via Plaid for this bank account over the past 3 days|
|failed_plaid_non_oauth_authentication_attempts_count_7d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of failed non-OAuth authentication attempts via Plaid for this bank account over the past 7 days|
|plaid_non_oauth_authentication_attempts_count_7d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of non-OAuth authentication attempts via Plaid for this bank account over the past 7 days|
|failed_plaid_non_oauth_authentication_attempts_count_30d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of failed non-OAuth authentication attempts via Plaid for this bank account over the past 30 days|
|plaid_non_oauth_authentication_attempts_count_30d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of non-OAuth authentication attempts via Plaid for this bank account over the past 30 days|
|distinct_ip_addresses_count_3d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of distinct IP addresses linked to the same bank account during Plaid authentication in the last 3 days|
|distinct_ip_addresses_count_7d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of distinct IP addresses linked to the same bank account during Plaid authentication in the last 7 days|
|distinct_ip_addresses_count_30d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of distinct IP addresses linked to the same bank account during Plaid authentication in the last 30 days|
|distinct_ip_addresses_count_90d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of distinct IP addresses linked to the same bank account during Plaid authentication in the last 90 days|
|distinct_user_agents_count_3d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of distinct user agents linked to the same bank account during Plaid authentication in the last 3 days|
|distinct_user_agents_count_7d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of distinct user agents linked to the same bank account during Plaid authentication in the last 7 days|
|distinct_user_agents_count_30d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of distinct user agents linked to the same bank account during Plaid authentication in the last 30 days|
|distinct_user_agents_count_90d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of distinct user agents linked to the same bank account during Plaid authentication in the last 90 days|
|address_change_count_28d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of times the account's addresses on file have changed over the past 28 days|
|email_change_count_28d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of times the account's email addresses on file have changed over the past 28 days|
|phone_change_count_28d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of times the account's phone numbers on file have changed over the past 28 days|
|address_change_count_90d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of times the account's addresses on file have changed over the past 90 days|
|email_change_count_90d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of times the account's email addresses on file have changed over the past 90 days|
|phone_change_count_90d|integer \| null|true|none|The number of times the account's phone numbers on file have changed over the past 90 days|
|days_since_account_opening|integer \| null|true|none|The number of days since the bank account was opened, as reported by the financial institution|
|days_since_first_observed_transaction|integer \| null|true|none|The number of days since the oldest transaction available to Plaid for this account. This measure, combined with Plaid connection history, can be used to infer the age of the account|

For example, if another business using Plaid Beacon created a fraud report that matched one of your users, your matching user's status would automatically be updated and the audit trail source would be `system`.<br><br>`bulk_import` - The resource was created or updated as part of a bulk import process. A type indicating what caused a resource to be changed or updated.


`dashboard` - The resource was created or updated by a member of your team via the Plaid dashboard.

`api` - The resource was created or updated via the Plaid API.

`system` - The resource was created or updated automatically by a part of the Plaid Beacon system. For example, if another business using Plaid Beacon created a fraud report that matched one of your users, your matching user's status would automatically be updated and the audit trail source would be `system`.

`bulk_import` - The resource was created or updated as part of a bulk import process. For example, if your company provided a CSV of user data as part of your initial onboarding, the audit trail source would be `bulk_import`.

<h2 id="tocS_BeaconMatchSummaryCode">BeaconMatchSummaryCode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabeaconmatchsummarycode"></a>
<a id="schema_BeaconMatchSummaryCode"></a>
<a id="tocSbeaconmatchsummarycode"></a>
<a id="tocsbeaconmatchsummarycode"></a>

```json
"match"
```

An enum indicating the match type between two Beacon Users.


`match` indicates that the provided input data was a strong match against the other Beacon User.

`partial_match` indicates the data approximately matched the other Beacon User. For example, "Knope" vs. "Knope-Wyatt" for last name.

`no_match` indicates that Plaid was able to compare this field against the other Beacon User and it did not match the provided input data.

`no_data` indicates that Plaid was unable to compare this field against the original Beacon User because the field was not present in one of the Beacon Users.

<h2 id="tocS_BeaconReport">BeaconReport</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabeaconreport"></a>
<a id="schema_BeaconReport"></a>
<a id="tocSbeaconreport"></a>
<a id="tocsbeaconreport"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "becrpt_11111111111111",
  "beacon_user_id": "becusr_42cF1MNo42r9Xj",
  "created_at": "2020-07-24T03:26:02Z",
  "type": "first_party",
  "fraud_date": "1990-05-29",
  "event_date": "1990-05-29",
  "fraud_amount": {
    "iso_currency_code": "USD",
    "value": 100
  },
  "audit_trail": {
    "source": "dashboard",
    "dashboard_user_id": "54350110fedcbaf01234ffee",
    "timestamp": "2020-07-24T03:26:02Z"
  }
}
```

A Beacon Report describes the type of fraud committed by a user as well as the date the fraud was committed and the total amount of money lost due to the fraud incident.

This information is used to block similar fraud attempts on your platform as well as alert other companies who screen a user with matching identity information.
Other companies will not receive any new identity information, just what matched, plus information such as industry, type of fraud, and date of fraud.

You can manage your fraud reports by adding, deleting, or editing reports as you get additional information on fraudulent users.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[BeaconReportID](#schemabeaconreportid)|true|none|ID of the associated Beacon Report.|
|beacon_user_id|[BeaconUserID](#schemabeaconuserid)|true|none|ID of the associated Beacon User.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|type|[BeaconReportType](#schemabeaconreporttype)|true|none|The type of Beacon Report.<br><br>`first_party`: If this is the same individual as the one who submitted the KYC.<br><br>`stolen`: If this is a different individual from the one who submitted the KYC.<br><br>`synthetic`: If this is an individual using fabricated information.<br><br>`account_takeover`: If this individual's account was compromised.<br><br>`data_breach`: If this individual's data was compromised in a breach.<br><br>`unknown`: If you aren't sure who committed the fraud.|
|fraud_date|[ISO8601DateNullable](#schemaiso8601datenullable)|true|none|A date in the format YYYY-MM-DD (RFC 3339 Section 5.6).|
|event_date|[ISO8601Date](#schemaiso8601date)|true|none|A date in the format YYYY-MM-DD (RFC 3339 Section 5.6).|
|fraud_amount|[FraudAmount](#schemafraudamount)|true|none|The amount and currency of the fraud or attempted fraud.<br>`fraud_amount` should be omitted to indicate an unknown fraud amount.|
|audit_trail|[BeaconAuditTrail](#schemabeaconaudittrail)|true|none|Information about the last change made to the parent object specifying what caused the change as well as when it occurred.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|first_party|
|type|stolen|
|type|synthetic|
|type|account_takeover|
|type|data_breach|
|type|unknown|

<h2 id="tocS_BeaconReportSyndication">BeaconReportSyndication</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabeaconreportsyndication"></a>
<a id="schema_BeaconReportSyndication"></a>
<a id="tocSbeaconreportsyndication"></a>
<a id="tocsbeaconreportsyndication"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "becrsn_11111111111111",
  "beacon_user_id": "becusr_42cF1MNo42r9Xj",
  "report": {
    "id": "becrpt_11111111111111",
    "created_at": "2020-07-24T03:26:02Z",
    "type": "first_party",
    "fraud_date": "1990-05-29",
    "event_date": "1990-05-29"
  },
  "analysis": {
    "address": "match",
    "date_of_birth": "match",
    "email_address": "match",
    "name": "match",
    "id_number": "match",
    "ip_address": "match",
    "phone_number": "match",
    "depository_accounts": [
      {
        "account_mask": "4000",
        "routing_number": "021000021",
        "match_status": "match"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

A Beacon Report Syndication represents a Beacon Report created either by your organization or another Beacon customer that matches a specific Beacon User you've created.

The `analysis` field in the response indicates which fields matched between the originally reported Beacon User and the Beacon User that the report was syndicated to.

The `report` field in the response contains a subset of information from the original report.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[BeaconReportSyndicationID](#schemabeaconreportsyndicationid)|true|none|ID of the associated Beacon Report Syndication.|
|beacon_user_id|[BeaconUserID](#schemabeaconuserid)|true|none|ID of the associated Beacon User.|
|report|[BeaconReportSyndicationOriginalReport](#schemabeaconreportsyndicationoriginalreport)|true|none|A subset of information from a Beacon Report that has been syndicated to a matching Beacon User in your program.<br><br>The `id` field in the response is the ID of the original report that was syndicated. If the original report was created by your organization, the field will be filled with the ID of the report. Otherwise, the field will be `null` indicating that the original report was created by another Beacon customer.|
|analysis|[BeaconReportSyndicationAnalysis](#schemabeaconreportsyndicationanalysis)|true|none|Analysis of which fields matched between the originally reported Beacon User and the Beacon User that the report was syndicated to.|

<h2 id="tocS_BeaconReportSyndicationAnalysis">BeaconReportSyndicationAnalysis</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

A Beacon Report Syndication represents a Beacon Report created either by your organization or another Beacon customer that matches a specific Beacon User you've created.

The `analysis` field in the response indicates which fields matched between the originally reported Beacon User and the Beacon User that the report was syndicated to.

The `report` field in the response contains a subset of information from the original report.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[BeaconReportSyndicationID](#schemabeaconreportsyndicationid)|true|none|ID of the associated Beacon Report Syndication.|
|beacon_user_id|[BeaconUserID](#schemabeaconuserid)|true|none|ID of the associated Beacon User.|
|report|[BeaconReportSyndicationOriginalReport](#schemabeaconreportsyndicationoriginalreport)|true|none|A subset of information from a Beacon Report that has been syndicated to a matching Beacon User in your program.<br><br>The `id` field in the response is the ID of the original report that was syndicated. If the original report was created by your organization, the field will be filled with the ID of the report. Otherwise, the field will be `null` indicating that the original report was created by another Beacon customer.|
|analysis|[BeaconReportSyndicationAnalysis](#schemabeaconreportsyndicationanalysis)|true|none|Analysis of which fields matched between the originally reported Beacon User and the Beacon User that the report was syndicated to.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

<h2 id="tocS_BeaconReportSyndicationOriginalReport">BeaconReportSyndicationOriginalReport</h2>

```json
  "created_at": "2020-07-24T03:26:02Z",
  "type": "first_party",
  "fraud_date": "1990-05-29",
  "event_date": "1990-05-29"
}
```

A subset of information from a Beacon Report that has been syndicated to a matching Beacon User in your program.

The `id` field in the response is the ID of the original report that was syndicated. If the original report was created by your organization, the field will be filled with the ID of the report. Otherwise, the field will be `null` indicating that the original report was created by another Beacon customer.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[BeaconReportIDNullable](#schemabeaconreportidnullable)|true|none|ID of the associated Beacon Report.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|type|[BeaconReportType](#schemabeaconreporttype)|true|none|The type of Beacon Report.<br><br>`first_party`: If this is the same individual as the one who submitted the KYC.<br><br>`stolen`: If this is a different individual from the one who submitted the KYC.<br><br>`synthetic`: If this is an individual using fabricated information.<br><br>`account_takeover`: If this individual's account was compromised.<br><br>`data_breach`: If this individual's data was compromised in a breach.<br><br>`unknown`: If you aren't sure who committed the fraud.|
|fraud_date|[ISO8601DateNullable](#schemaiso8601datenullable)|true|none|A date in the format YYYY-MM-DD (RFC 3339 Section 5.6).|
|event_date|[ISO8601Date](#schemaiso8601date)|true|none|A date in the format YYYY-MM-DD (RFC 3339 Section 5.6).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|first_party|
|type|stolen|
|type|synthetic|
|type|account_takeover|
|type|data_breach|
|type|unknown|

<a id="schema_BeaconReportType"></a>
<a id="tocSbeaconreporttype"></a>
<a id="tocsbeaconreporttype"></a>

```json
"first_party"
```

The type of Beacon Report.

`first_party`: If this is the same individual as the one who submitted the KYC.

`stolen`: If this is a different individual from the one who submitted the KYC.

`synthetic`: If this is an individual using fabricated information.

`account_takeover`: If this individual's account was compromised.

`data_breach`: If this individual's data was compromised in a breach.

`unknown`: If you aren't sure who committed the fraud.

A Beacon User represents an end user that has been scanned against the Beacon Network.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|id|[BeaconUserID](#schemabeaconuserid)|true|none|ID of the associated Beacon User.|
|version|integer|true|none|The `version` field begins with 1 and increments each time the user is updated.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|updated_at|[UpdatedAtTimestamp](#schemaupdatedattimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp. This field indicates the last time the resource was modified.|
|status|[BeaconUserStatus](#schemabeaconuserstatus)|true|none|A status of a Beacon User.<br><br>`rejected`: The Beacon User has been rejected for fraud. Users can be automatically or manually rejected.<br><br>`pending_review`: The Beacon User has been marked for review.<br><br>`cleared`: The Beacon User has been cleared of fraud.|
|program_id|[BeaconProgramID](#schemabeaconprogramid)|true|none|ID of the associated Beacon Program.|
|client_user_id|[ClientUserID](#schemaclientuserid)|true|none|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. This ID can also be used to associate user-specific data from other Plaid products. Financial Account Matching requires this field and the `/link/token/create` `client_user_id` to be consistent. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|user|[BeaconUserData](#schemabeaconuserdata)|true|none|A Beacon User's data and resulting analysis when checked against duplicate records and the Beacon Fraud Network.|
|audit_trail|[BeaconAuditTrail](#schemabeaconaudittrail)|true|none|Information about the last change made to the parent object specifying what caused the change as well as when it occurred.|

|Property|Value|

|status|pending_review|
|status|cleared|

Even if an address has been collected, some fields may be null depending on the region's addressing system. For example:


Addresses from the United Kingdom will not include a region


Addresses from Hong Kong will not include a postal code

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|street|[Street](#schemastreet)|true|none|The primary street portion of an address. If an address is provided, this field will always be filled. A string with at least one non-whitespace alphabetical character, with a max length of 80 characters.|
|street2|[Street2](#schemastreet2)|true|none|Extra street information, like an apartment or suite number. If provided, a string with at least one non-whitespace character, with a max length of 50 characters.|
|city|[City](#schemacity)|true|none|City from the address. A string with at least one non-whitespace alphabetical character, with a max length of 100 characters.|
|region|[Region](#schemaregion)|true|none|A subdivision code. "Subdivision" is a generic term for "state", "province", "prefecture", "zone", etc. For the list of valid codes, see [country subdivision codes](https://plaid.com/documents/country_subdivision_codes.json). Country prefixes are omitted, since they are inferred from the `country` field.|
|postal_code|[PostalCode](#schemapostalcode)|true|none|The postal code for the associated address. Between 2 and 10 alphanumeric characters. For US-based addresses this must be 5 numeric digits.|
|country|[GenericCountryCode](#schemagenericcountrycode)|true|none|Valid, capitalized, two-letter ISO code representing the country of this object. Must be in ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 form.|

Request input for creating a Beacon User.

The primary use for this endpoint is to add a new end user to Beacon for fraud and duplicate scanning.

Some fields are optional, but it is recommended to provide as much information as possible to improve
the accuracy of the fraud and duplicate scanning.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|program_id|[BeaconProgramID](#schemabeaconprogramid)|true|none|ID of the associated Beacon Program.|
|client_user_id|[ClientUserID](#schemaclientuserid)|true|none|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. This ID can also be used to associate user-specific data from other Plaid products. Financial Account Matching requires this field and the `/link/token/create` `client_user_id` to be consistent. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|user|[BeaconUserRequestData](#schemabeaconuserrequestdata)|true|none|A Beacon User's data which is used to check against duplicate records and the Beacon Fraud Network.<br><br>In order to create a Beacon User, in addition to the `name`, _either_ the `date_of_birth` _or_ the `depository_accounts` field must be provided.|
|access_tokens|[[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)]|false|none|Send this array of access tokens to link accounts to the Beacon User and have them evaluated for Account Insights.<br>A maximum of 50 accounts total can be added to a single Beacon User.|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

A Beacon User's data which is used to check against duplicate records and the Beacon Fraud Network.

In order to create a Beacon User, in addition to the `name`, _either_ the `date_of_birth` _or_ the `depository_accounts` field must be provided.

|address|[BeaconUserRequestAddress](#schemabeaconuserrequestaddress)|false|none|Home address for the associated user. For more context on this field, see [Input Validation by Country](https://plaid.com/docs/identity-verification/hybrid-input-validation/#input-validation-by-country).|
|email_address|[EmailAddress](#schemaemailaddress)|false|none|A valid email address. Must not have leading or trailing spaces and address must be RFC compliant. For more information, see [RFC 3696](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3696).|
|phone_number|[BeaconUserPhoneNumber](#schemabeaconuserphonenumber)|false|none|A phone number in E.164 format.|
|id_number|[BeaconUserIDNumber](#schemabeaconuseridnumber)|false|none|The ID number associated with a Beacon User.|
|ip_address|[IPAddress](#schemaipaddress)|false|none|An IPv4 or IPv6 address.|
|depository_accounts|[[BeaconUserRequestDepositoryAccount](#schemabeaconuserrequestdepositoryaccount)]|false|none|Provide a list of bank accounts that are associated with this Beacon User. These accounts will be scanned across the Beacon Network and used to find duplicate records.<br><br>Note: These accounts will not have Bank Account Insights. To receive Bank Account Insights please supply `access_tokens`.|

A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. This ID can also be used to associate user-specific data from other Plaid products. Financial Account Matching requires this field and the `/link/token/create` `client_user_id` to be consistent. High level descriptions of how the associated document was processed. If a document fails verification, the details in the `analysis` object should help clarify why the document was rejected.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authenticity|[DocumentAuthenticityMatchCode](#schemadocumentauthenticitymatchcode)|true|none|High level summary of whether the document in the provided image matches the formatting rules and security checks for the associated jurisdiction.<br><br>For example, most identity documents have formatting rules like the following:<br><br><br>The image of the person's face must have a certain contrast in order to highlight skin tone<br><br><br>The subject in the document's image must remove eye glasses and pose in a certain way<br><br><br>The informational fields (name, date of birth, ID number, etc.) must be colored and aligned according to specific rules<br><br><br>Security features like watermarks and background patterns must be present<br><br>So a `match` status for this field indicates that the document in the provided image seems to conform to the various formatting and security rules associated with the detected document.|
|image_quality|[ImageQuality](#schemaimagequality)|true|none|A high level description of the quality of the image the user submitted.<br><br>For example, an image that is blurry, distorted by glare from a nearby light source, or improperly framed might be marked as low or medium quality. Poor quality images are more likely to fail OCR and/or template conformity checks.<br><br>Note: By default, Plaid will let a user recapture document images twice before failing the entire session if we attribute the failure to low image quality.|
|extracted_data|[PhysicalDocumentExtractedDataAnalysis](#schemaphysicaldocumentextracteddataanalysis)|true|none|Analysis of the data extracted from the submitted document.|
|fraud_analysis_details|[FraudAnalysisDetails](#schemafraudanalysisdetails)|true|none|Details about the fraud analysis performed on the document.|
|image_quality_details|[ImageQualityDetails](#schemaimagequalitydetails)|true|none|Details about the image quality of the document.|
|human_review|[HumanReview](#schemahumanreview)|false|none|Details about the human review check, which refers to a check that is performed by a document specialist.|
|aamva_verification|[AAMVAAnalysis](#schemaaamvaanalysis)|true|none|Analyzed AAMVA data for the associated hit.<br><br>Note: This field is only available for U.S. driver's licenses issued by participating states.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|authenticity|match|
|authenticity|partial_match|
|authenticity|no_match|
|authenticity|no_data|
|image_quality|high|
|image_quality|medium|
|image_quality|low|


High level summary of whether the document in the provided image matches the formatting rules and security checks for the associated jurisdiction.

For example, most identity documents have formatting rules like the following:


The image of the person's face must have a certain contrast in order to highlight skin tone


The subject in the document's image must remove eye glasses and pose in a certain way


The informational fields (name, date of birth, ID number, etc.) must be colored and aligned according to specific rules


Security features like watermarks and background patterns must be present

So a `match` status for this field indicates that the document in the provided image seems to conform to the various formatting and security rules associated with the detected document.

Data, images, analysis, and results from the `documentary_verification` step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.documentary_verification` has reached a terminal state of `success`, `failed`, `manually_approved`, or `manually_rejected`. It is also returned while the user is being asked to retry after a failed document attempt.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|string|true|none|The outcome status for the associated Identity Verification attempt's `documentary_verification` step. This field will be `success` if `steps.documentary_verification` is `success` or `manually_approved`, and `failed` if `steps.documentary_verification` is `failed` or `manually_rejected`.|
|documents|[[DocumentaryVerificationDocument](#schemadocumentaryverificationdocument)]|true|none|An array of documents submitted to the `documentary_verification` step. Each entry represents one user submission, where each submission will contain both a front and back image, or just a front image, depending on the document type.<br><br>Note: Plaid will automatically let a user submit a new set of document images up to three times if we detect that a previous attempt might have failed due to user error. For example, if the first set of document images are blurry or obscured by glare, the user will be asked to capture their documents again, resulting in at least two separate entries within `documents`. If the overall `documentary_verification` is `failed`, the user has exhausted their retry attempts.|

|images|[PhysicalDocumentImages](#schemaphysicaldocumentimages)|true|none|URLs for downloading original and cropped images for this document submission. The URLs are designed to only allow downloading, not hot linking, so the URL will only serve the document image for 60 seconds before expiring. The expiration time is 60 seconds after the `GET` request for the associated Identity Verification attempt. A new expiring URL is generated with each request, so you can always rerequest the Identity Verification attempt if one of your URLs expires.|
|extracted_data|[PhysicalDocumentExtractedData](#schemaphysicaldocumentextracteddata)|true|none|Data extracted from a user-submitted document.|
|analysis|[DocumentAnalysis](#schemadocumentanalysis)|true|none|High level descriptions of how the associated document was processed. If a document fails verification, the details in the `analysis` object should help clarify why the document was rejected.|

Shorthand identifier for a specific screening list for entities.

 `AU_CON`: Australia Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Consolidated List

 `CA_CON`: Government of Canada Consolidated List of Sanctions

 `EU_CON`: European External Action Service Consolidated List

 `IZ_SOE`: State Owned Enterprise List

 `IZ_UNC`: United Nations Consolidated Sanctions

 `IZ_WBK`: World Bank Listing of Ineligible Firms and Individuals

 `US_CAP`: US OFAC Correspondent Account or Payable-Through Account Sanctions

 `US_FSE`: US OFAC Foreign Sanctions Evaders

 `US_MBS`: US Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions

 `US_SDN`: US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List

 `US_SSI`: US OFAC Sectoral Sanctions Identifications

 `US_CMC`: US OFAC Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex List

 `US_UVL`: Bureau of Industry and Security Unverified List

 `US_SAM`: US System for Award Management Exclusion List

 `US_TEL`: US Terrorist Exclusion List

 `UK_HMC`: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office UK Sanctions List

```json
{
  "id": "entprg_2eRPsDnL66rZ7H",
  "created_at": "2020-07-24T03:26:02Z",
  "is_rescanning_enabled": true,
  "lists_enabled": [
    "EU_CON"
  ],
  "name": "Sample Program",
  "name_sensitivity": "balanced",
  "audit_trail": {
    "source": "dashboard",
    "dashboard_user_id": "54350110fedcbaf01234ffee",
    "timestamp": "2020-07-24T03:26:02Z"
  },
  "is_archived": false
}
```

A program that configures the active lists, search parameters, and other behavior for initial and ongoing screening of entities.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[EntityWatchlistProgramID](#schemaentitywatchlistprogramid)|true|none|ID of the associated entity program.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|is_rescanning_enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicator specifying whether the program is enabled and will perform daily rescans.|
|lists_enabled|[[EntityWatchlistCode](#schemaentitywatchlistcode)]|true|none|Watchlists enabled for the associated program|
|name|[EntityWatchlistScreeningProgramName](#schemaentitywatchlistscreeningprogramname)|true|none|A name for the entity program to define its purpose. For example, "High Risk Organizations" or "Applicants".|
|name_sensitivity|[ProgramNameSensitivity](#schemaprogramnamesensitivity)|true|none|The valid name matching sensitivity configurations for a screening program. Note that while certain matching techniques may be more prevalent on less strict settings, all matching algorithms are enabled for every sensitivity.<br><br>`coarse` - See more potential matches. This sensitivity will see more broad phonetic matches across alphabets that make missing a potential hit very unlikely. This setting is noisier and will require more manual review.<br><br>`balanced` - A good default for most companies. This sensitivity is balanced to show high quality hits with reduced noise.<br><br>`strict` - Aggressive false positive reduction. This sensitivity will require names to be more similar than `coarse` and `balanced` settings, relying less on phonetics, while still accounting for character transpositions, missing tokens, and other common permutations.<br><br>`exact` - Matches must be nearly exact. This sensitivity will only show hits with exact or nearly exact name matches with only basic correction such as extraneous symbols and capitalization. This setting is generally not recommended unless you have a very specific use case.|
|audit_trail|[WatchlistScreeningAuditTrail](#schemawatchlistscreeningaudittrail)|true|none|Information about the last change made to the parent object specifying what caused the change as well as when it occurred.|
|is_archived|[ProgramArchived](#schemaprogramarchived)|true|none|Archived programs are read-only and cannot screen new customers nor participate in ongoing monitoring.|

|lists_enabled|US_TEL|
|lists_enabled|AU_CON|
|lists_enabled|UK_HMC|
|name_sensitivity|coarse|
|name_sensitivity|balanced|
|name_sensitivity|strict|
|name_sensitivity|exact|

The entity screening object allows you to represent an entity in your system, update its profile, and search for it on various watchlists. Note: Rejected entity screenings will not receive new hits, regardless of entity program configuration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[EntityWatchlistScreeningID](#schemaentitywatchlistscreeningid)|true|none|ID of the associated entity screening.|
|search_terms|[EntityWatchlistScreeningSearchTerms](#schemaentitywatchlistscreeningsearchterms)|true|none|Search terms associated with an entity used for searching against watchlists|
|assignee|[DashboardUserIDNullable](#schemadashboarduseridnullable)|true|none|ID of the associated user. To retrieve the email address or other details of the person corresponding to this ID, use `/dashboard_user/get`.|
|status|[WatchlistScreeningStatus](#schemawatchlistscreeningstatus)|true|none|A status enum indicating whether a screening is still pending review, has been rejected, or has been cleared.|
|client_user_id|[ClientUserIDNullable](#schemaclientuseridnullable)|true|none|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. This ID can also be used to associate user-specific data from other Plaid products. Financial Account Matching requires this field and the `/link/token/create` `client_user_id` to be consistent. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|audit_trail|[WatchlistScreeningAuditTrail](#schemawatchlistscreeningaudittrail)|true|none|Information about the last change made to the parent object specifying what caused the change as well as when it occurred.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|rejected|
|status|pending_review|
|status|cleared|

Data from a government watchlist that has been attached to the screening.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[EntityWatchlistScreeningHitID](#schemaentitywatchlistscreeninghitid)|true|none|ID of the associated entity screening hit.|
|review_status|[WatchlistScreeningHitStatus](#schemawatchlistscreeninghitstatus)|true|none|The current state of review. All watchlist screening hits begin in a `pending_review` state but can be changed by creating a review. When a hit is in the `pending_review` state, it will always show the latest version of the watchlist data Plaid has available and be compared against the latest customer information saved in the watchlist screening. Once a hit has been marked as `confirmed` or `dismissed` it will no longer be updated so that the state is as it was when the review was first conducted.|
|first_active|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|inactive_since|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|historical_since|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|list_code|[EntityWatchlistCode](#schemaentitywatchlistcode)|true|none|Shorthand identifier for a specific screening list for entities.<br><br> `AU_CON`: Australia Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Consolidated List<br><br> `CA_CON`: Government of Canada Consolidated List of Sanctions<br><br> `EU_CON`: European External Action Service Consolidated List<br><br> `IZ_SOE`: State Owned Enterprise List<br><br> `IZ_UNC`: United Nations Consolidated Sanctions<br><br> `IZ_WBK`: World Bank Listing of Ineligible Firms and Individuals<br><br> `US_CAP`: US OFAC Correspondent Account or Payable-Through Account Sanctions<br><br> `US_FSE`: US OFAC Foreign Sanctions Evaders<br><br> `US_MBS`: US Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions<br><br> `US_SDN`: US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List<br><br> `US_SSI`: US OFAC Sectoral Sanctions Identifications<br><br> `US_CMC`: US OFAC Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex List<br><br> `US_UVL`: Bureau of Industry and Security Unverified List<br><br> `US_SAM`: US System for Award Management Exclusion List<br><br> `US_TEL`: US Terrorist Exclusion List<br><br> `UK_HMC`: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office UK Sanctions List|
|plaid_uid|[InternalUID](#schemainternaluid)|true|none|A universal identifier for a watchlist individual that is stable across searches and updates.|
|source_uid|[SourceUID](#schemasourceuid)|true|none|The identifier provided by the source sanction or watchlist. When one is not provided by the source, this is `null`.|
|sub_programs|[string]|true|none|Sub-program designations that may be attached to the watchlist entry by the issuing authority. For OFAC SDN<br>entries these are the program codes published in the SDN list (for example `SDGT` for Specially<br>Designated Global Terrorists, `SDNTK` for Specially Designated Narcotics Trafficking Kingpins,<br>`IRAN`, `RUSSIA-EO14024`). New codes are added by sanctioning authorities without prior notice,<br>so callers should treat unknown values as opaque strings rather than enum members.<br>|
|analysis|[EntityScreeningHitAnalysis](#schemaentityscreeninghitanalysis)|false|none|Analysis information describing why a screening hit matched the provided entity information|
|data|[EntityScreeningHitData](#schemaentityscreeninghitdata)|false|none|Information associated with the entity watchlist hit|

Details about the fraud analysis performed on the document.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type_supported|object|true|none|Whether the submitted document type is supported for fraud analysis.<br><br>`success` - The document type is supported.<br><br>`failed` - The document type is not supported.|
|portrait_presence_check|object|true|none|The outcome of the portrait presence check.<br><br>`success` - A portrait was detected.<br><br>`failed` - No portrait was detected.|
|portrait_details_check|object|true|none|The outcome of the portrait details check including photo embedding and face landmark checks.<br><br>`success` - The portrait passed all validity checks.<br><br>`failed` - The portrait did not pass one or more validity checks.|
|image_composition_check|object|true|none|The outcome of the image composition check.<br><br>`success` - The image is a valid physical document capture.<br><br>`failed` - The image appears to be a photograph of a screen or a digital forgery.|
|integrity_check|object|true|none|The outcome of the integrity check for document security elements.<br><br>`success` - Data is consistent across all checked security elements.<br><br>`failed` - Inconsistencies were detected across one or more security elements.|
|detail_check|object|true|none|The outcome of the document detail check for correct styling and layout.<br><br>`success` - The document passed all authenticity checks.<br><br>`failed` - The document did not pass one or more authenticity checks.|
|issue_date_check|object|true|none|The outcome of the issue date validity check.<br><br>`success` - The issue date is valid.<br><br>`failed` - The issue date is invalid or could not be verified.<br><br>`no_data` - The check could not be performed due to insufficient data.|

<h2 id="tocS_HiddenMatchSummaryCode">HiddenMatchSummaryCode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemahiddenmatchsummarycode"></a>
<a id="schema_HiddenMatchSummaryCode"></a>
<a id="tocShiddenmatchsummarycode"></a>
<a id="tocshiddenmatchsummarycode"></a>

```json
"match"
```

An enum indicating the match type between data provided by user and data checked against an external data source.


`match` indicates that the provided input data was a strong match against external data.

`partial_match` indicates the data approximately matched against external data. For example, "Knope" vs. "Knope-Wyatt" for last name.

`no_match` indicates that Plaid was able to perform a check against an external data source and it did not match the provided input data.

`no_data` indicates that Plaid was unable to find external data to compare against the provided input data.

`no_input` indicates that Plaid was unable to perform a check because no information was provided for this field by the end user.

<a id="schemaidempotencyflag"></a>
<a id="schema_IdempotencyFlag"></a>
<a id="tocSidempotencyflag"></a>
<a id="tocsidempotencyflag"></a>

```json
true
```

An optional flag specifying how you would like Plaid to handle attempts to create an Identity Verification when an Identity Verification already exists for the provided `client_user_id` and/or `user_id`, and `template_id`.
If idempotency is enabled, Plaid will return the existing Identity Verification. If idempotency is disabled, Plaid will reject the request with a `400 Bad Request` status code if an Identity Verification already exists for the supplied `client_user_id` and/or `user_id`, and `template_id`.

An identity verification attempt represents a customer's attempt to verify their identity, reflecting the required steps for completing the session, the results for each step, and information collected in the process.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[IdentityVerificationID](#schemaidentityverificationid)|true|none|ID of the associated Identity Verification attempt.|
|client_user_id|[ClientUserID](#schemaclientuserid)|true|none|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. This ID can also be used to associate user-specific data from other Plaid products. Financial Account Matching requires this field and the `/link/token/create` `client_user_id` to be consistent. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|completed_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|previous_attempt_id|[PreviousIdentityVerificationAttemptID](#schemapreviousidentityverificationattemptid)|true|none|The ID for the Identity Verification preceding this session. This field will only be filled if the current Identity Verification is a retry of a previous attempt.|
|shareable_url|[ShareableURL](#schemashareableurl)|true|none|A shareable URL that can be sent directly to the user to complete verification|
|template|[IdentityVerificationTemplateReference](#schemaidentityverificationtemplatereference)|true|none|The resource ID and version number of the template configuring the behavior of a given Identity Verification.|
|user|[IdentityVerificationUserData](#schemaidentityverificationuserdata)|true|none|The identity data that was either collected from the user or provided via API in order to perform an Identity Verification.|
|status|[IdentityVerificationStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstatus)|true|none|The status of this Identity Verification attempt.<br><br><br>`active` - The Identity Verification attempt is incomplete. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed nor passed.<br><br>`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed, passing all steps defined to the associated Identity Verification template.<br><br>`failed` - The user failed one or more steps in the session and was told to contact support.<br><br>`expired` - The Identity Verification attempt was active for a long period of time without being completed and was automatically marked as expired. Note that sessions currently do not expire. Automatic expiration is expected to be enabled in the future.<br><br>`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled, either via the dashboard by a user, or via API. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed nor passed.<br><br>`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.|
|steps|[IdentityVerificationStepSummary](#schemaidentityverificationstepsummary)|true|none|Each step will be one of the following values:<br><br><br>`active` - This step is the user's current step. They are either in the process of completing this step, or they recently closed their Identity Verification attempt while in the middle of this step. Only one step will be marked as `active` at any given point.<br><br>`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed this step.<br><br>`failed` - The user failed this step. This can either cause the user to fail the session as a whole, or cause them to fall back to another step depending on how the Identity Verification template is configured. A failed step does not imply a failed session.<br><br>`waiting_for_prerequisite` - The user needs to complete another step first, before they progress to this step. This step may never run, depending on if the user fails an earlier step or if the step is only run as a fallback.<br><br>`not_applicable` - This step will not be run for this session.<br><br>`skipped` - This step was skipped, for example because the retry instructions that created this Identity Verification attempt specified that it should be skipped, because your template configuration skips it, or, for `accept_tos`, because `gave_consent` was `true`.<br><br>`expired` - This step had not yet been completed when the Identity Verification attempt as a whole expired.<br><br>`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled before the user completed this step.<br><br>`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.<br><br>`manually_approved` - The step was manually overridden to pass by a team member in the dashboard.<br><br>`manually_rejected` - The step was manually overridden to fail by a team member in the dashboard.|
|documentary_verification|[DocumentaryVerification](#schemadocumentaryverification)|true|none|Data, images, analysis, and results from the `documentary_verification` step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.documentary_verification` has reached a terminal state of `success`, `failed`, `manually_approved`, or `manually_rejected`. It is also returned while the user is being asked to retry after a failed document attempt.|
|selfie_check|[SelfieCheck](#schemaselfiecheck)|true|none|Additional information for the `selfie_check` step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.selfie_check` has reached a terminal state of `success`, `failed`, `manually_approved`, or `manually_rejected`.|
|kyc_check|[KYCCheckDetails](#schemakyccheckdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `kyc_check` (Data Source Verification) step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.kyc_check` has reached a terminal state of `success`, `failed`, `manually_approved`, or `manually_rejected`.|
|risk_check|[RiskCheckDetails](#schemariskcheckdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `risk_check` step.|
|verify_sms|[VerifySMSDetails](#schemaverifysmsdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `verify_sms` step.|
|watchlist_screening_id|[WatchlistScreeningIndividualIDNullable](#schemawatchlistscreeningindividualidnullable)|true|none|ID of the associated screening.|
|beacon_user_id|[BeaconUserIDNullable](#schemabeaconuseridnullable)|true|none|**Deprecated.** Beacon is deprecated in favor of Plaid Protect. This field is only populated for users of the deprecated Beacon product.|
|user_id|[PlaidUserIDNullable](#schemaplaiduseridnullable)|true|none|Unique user identifier, created by calling `/user/create`. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. The `user_id` may only be used instead of the `client_user_id` if you were not a pre-existing user of `/user/create` as of December 10, 2025, or if you have since [migrated to the new User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/migrate-to-new-user-apis); for more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis). If both this field and a `client_user_id` are present in a request, the `user_id` must have been created from the provided `client_user_id`.|
|redacted_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|latest_scored_protect_event|[IDVProtectEvent](#schemaidvprotectevent)|false|none|Information about a Protect event including Trust Index score and fraud attributes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|success|
|status|failed|
|status|expired|
|status|canceled|
|status|pending_review|

Even if an address has been autofilled, some fields may be null depending on the region's addressing system. For example:

Addresses from the United Kingdom will not include a region

Addresses from Hong Kong will not include postal code

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|street|[Street](#schemastreet)|true|none|The primary street portion of an address. If an address is provided, this field will always be filled. A string with at least one non-whitespace alphabetical character, with a max length of 80 characters.|
|street2|[Street2](#schemastreet2)|true|none|Extra street information, like an apartment or suite number. If provided, a string with at least one non-whitespace character, with a max length of 50 characters.|
|city|[CityNullable](#schemacitynullable)|true|none|City from the address. A string with at least one non-whitespace alphabetical character, with a max length of 100 characters.|
|region|[Region](#schemaregion)|true|none|A subdivision code. "Subdivision" is a generic term for "state", "province", "prefecture", "zone", etc. For the list of valid codes, see [country subdivision codes](https://plaid.com/documents/country_subdivision_codes.json). Country prefixes are omitted, since they are inferred from the `country` field.|
|postal_code|[PostalCode](#schemapostalcode)|true|none|The postal code for the associated address. Between 2 and 10 alphanumeric characters. For US-based addresses this must be 5 numeric digits.|
|country|[GenericCountryCode](#schemagenericcountrycode)|true|none|Valid, capitalized, two-letter ISO code representing the country of this object. Must be in ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 form.|
|po_box|[POBoxStatus](#schemapoboxstatus)|true|none|Field describing whether the associated address is a post office box. Will be `yes` when a P.O. box is detected, `no` when Plaid confirmed the address is not a P.O. box, and `no_data` when Plaid was not able to determine if the address is a P.O. box.|
|type|[AddressPurposeLabel](#schemaaddresspurposelabel)|true|none|Field describing whether the associated address is being used for commercial or residential purposes.<br><br>Note: This value will be `no_data` when Plaid does not have sufficient data to determine the address's use.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|po_box|yes|
|po_box|no|
|po_box|no_data|
|type|residential|
|type|commercial|
|type|no_data|

A flag specifying whether the end user has already agreed to a privacy policy specifying that their data will be shared with Plaid for verification purposes.

If `gave_consent` is set to `true`, the `accept_tos` step will be marked as `skipped` and the end user's session will start at the next step requirement.

Request schema for `/identity_verification/create`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_user_id|[ClientUserID](#schemaclientuserid)|false|none|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. This ID can also be used to associate user-specific data from other Plaid products. Financial Account Matching requires this field and the `/link/token/create` `client_user_id` to be consistent. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|user_id|[PlaidUserID](#schemaplaiduserid)|false|none|Unique user identifier, created by calling `/user/create`. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. The `user_id` may only be used instead of the `client_user_id` if you were not a pre-existing user of `/user/create` as of December 10, 2025, or if you have since [migrated to the new User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/migrate-to-new-user-apis); for more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis). If both this field and a `client_user_id` are present in a request, the `user_id` must have been created from the provided `client_user_id`.|
|is_shareable|boolean|true|none|A flag specifying whether you would like Plaid to expose a shareable URL for the verification being created.|
|template_id|[IdentityVerificationTemplateID](#schemaidentityverificationtemplateid)|true|none|ID of the associated Identity Verification template. Like all Plaid identifiers, this is case-sensitive.|
|language|[IdentityVerificationLanguage](#schemaidentityverificationlanguage)|false|none|The language shown when the user starts this identity verification. If omitted or null, the language is detected from the user's browser settings, with English as the fallback. The user can select a different language during the session. An idempotent request that returns an existing identity verification does not change its language.<br><br>Use a supported BCP 47 language tag, such as `fr-CA`. Unlike `/link/token/create`, this field requires a region-specific value rather than a two-letter language code such as `fr`.|
|gave_consent|[IdentityVerificationConsent](#schemaidentityverificationconsent)|true|none|A flag specifying whether the end user has already agreed to a privacy policy specifying that their data will be shared with Plaid for verification purposes.<br><br>If `gave_consent` is set to `true`, the `accept_tos` step will be marked as `skipped` and the end user's session will start at the next step requirement.|
|user|[IdentityVerificationCreateRequestUser](#schemaidentityverificationcreaterequestuser)|false|none|User information collected outside of Link, most likely via your own onboarding process.<br><br>Each of the following identity fields are optional:<br><br>`email_address`<br><br>`phone_number`<br><br>`date_of_birth`<br><br>`name`<br><br>`address`<br><br>`id_number`<br><br>Specifically, these fields are optional in that they can either be fully provided (satisfying every required field in their subschema) or omitted from the request entirely by not providing the key or value.<br>Providing these fields via the API will result in Link skipping the data collection process for the associated user. All verification steps enabled in the associated Identity Verification Template will still be run. Verification steps will either be run immediately, or once the user completes the `accept_tos` step, depending on the value provided to the `gave_consent` field.<br>If you are not using the shareable URL feature, you can optionally provide these fields via `/link/token/create` instead; both `/identity_verification/create` and `/link/token/create` are valid ways to provide this information. Note that if you provide a non-`null` user data object via `/identity_verification/create`, any user data fields entered via `/link/token/create` for the same `client_user_id` will be ignored when prefilling Link.<br><br>The `ip_address` field is optional. Provide the end user's IP address to enable IP-based risk checks for backend-only integrations that do not use the Link SDK; when the Link SDK is used, the IP address is collected automatically. Unlike the identity fields above, `ip_address` cannot be provided via `/link/token/create`.|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|is_idempotent|[IdempotencyFlag](#schemaidempotencyflag)|false|none|An optional flag specifying how you would like Plaid to handle attempts to create an Identity Verification when an Identity Verification already exists for the provided `client_user_id` and/or `user_id`, and `template_id`.<br>If idempotency is enabled, Plaid will return the existing Identity Verification. If idempotency is disabled, Plaid will reject the request with a `400 Bad Request` status code if an Identity Verification already exists for the supplied `client_user_id` and/or `user_id`, and `template_id`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|language|en-US|
|language|es-ES|
|language|es-US|
|language|fr-CA|
|language|ja-JP|
|language|pt-BR|
|language|pt-PT|
|language|null|

<h2 id="tocS_IdentityVerificationCreateRequestUser">IdentityVerificationCreateRequestUser</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaidentityverificationcreaterequestuser"></a>
<a id="schema_IdentityVerificationCreateRequestUser"></a>
<a id="tocSidentityverificationcreaterequestuser"></a>
<a id="tocsidentityverificationcreaterequestuser"></a>

```json
{
  "email_address": "user@example.com",
  "phone_number": "+12345678909",
  "date_of_birth": "1990-05-29",
  "name": {
    "given_name": "Leslie",
    "family_name": "Knope"
  },
  "address": {
    "street": "123 Main St.",
    "street2": "Unit 42",
    "city": "Pawnee",
    "region": "IN",
    "postal_code": "46001",
    "country": "US"
  },
  "id_number": {
    "value": "123456789",
    "type": "us_ssn"
  },
  "client_user_id": "your-db-id-3b24110",
  "ip_address": "192.0.2.42"
}
```

User information collected outside of Link, most likely via your own onboarding process.

Each of the following identity fields are optional:

`email_address`

`phone_number`

`date_of_birth`

`name`

`address`

`id_number`

Specifically, these fields are optional in that they can either be fully provided (satisfying every required field in their subschema) or omitted from the request entirely by not providing the key or value.
Providing these fields via the API will result in Link skipping the data collection process for the associated user. All verification steps enabled in the associated Identity Verification Template will still be run. Verification steps will either be run immediately, or once the user completes the `accept_tos` step, depending on the value provided to the `gave_consent` field.
If you are not using the shareable URL feature, you can optionally provide these fields via `/link/token/create` instead; both `/identity_verification/create` and `/link/token/create` are valid ways to provide this information. Note that if you provide a non-`null` user data object via `/identity_verification/create`, any user data fields entered via `/link/token/create` for the same `client_user_id` will be ignored when prefilling Link.

The `ip_address` field is optional. Provide the end user's IP address to enable IP-based risk checks for backend-only integrations that do not use the Link SDK; when the Link SDK is used, the IP address is collected automatically. Unlike the identity fields above, `ip_address` cannot be provided via `/link/token/create`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email_address|[EmailAddress](#schemaemailaddress)|false|none|A valid email address. Must not have leading or trailing spaces and address must be RFC compliant. For more information, see [RFC 3696](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3696).|
|phone_number|[IdentityVerificationUserPhoneNumber](#schemaidentityverificationuserphonenumber)|false|none|A valid phone number in E.164 format.|
|date_of_birth|[ISO8601Date](#schemaiso8601date)|false|none|A date in the format YYYY-MM-DD (RFC 3339 Section 5.6).|
|name|[IdentityVerificationRequestUserName](#schemaidentityverificationrequestusername)|false|none|You can use this field to pre-populate the user's legal name; if it is provided here, they will not be prompted to enter their name in the identity verification attempt.|
|address|[UserAddress](#schemauseraddress)|false|none|Home address for the user. Supported values are: not provided, address with only country code or full address.<br><br>For more context on this field, see [Input Validation by Country](https://plaid.com/docs/identity-verification/hybrid-input-validation/#input-validation-by-country).|
|id_number|[UserIDNumber](#schemauseridnumber)|false|none|ID number submitted by the user. If the user has not submitted this data yet, this field will be `null`. Otherwise, both fields are guaranteed to be filled.|
|client_user_id|[DeprecatedClientUserID](#schemadeprecatedclientuserid)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Specifying `user.client_user_id` is deprecated. Please provide `client_user_id` at the root level instead.|
|ip_address|[IPAddress](#schemaipaddress)|false|none|An IPv4 or IPv6 address.|
