An identity verification attempt represents a customer's attempt to verify their identity, reflecting the required steps for completing the session, the results for each step, and information collected in the process.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[IdentityVerificationID](#schemaidentityverificationid)|true|none|ID of the associated Identity Verification attempt.|
|client_user_id|[ClientUserID](#schemaclientuserid)|true|none|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. This ID can also be used to associate user-specific data from other Plaid products. Financial Account Matching requires this field and the `/link/token/create` `client_user_id` to be consistent. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|completed_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|previous_attempt_id|[PreviousIdentityVerificationAttemptID](#schemapreviousidentityverificationattemptid)|true|none|The ID for the Identity Verification preceding this session. This field will only be filled if the current Identity Verification is a retry of a previous attempt.|
|shareable_url|[ShareableURL](#schemashareableurl)|true|none|A shareable URL that can be sent directly to the user to complete verification|
|template|[IdentityVerificationTemplateReference](#schemaidentityverificationtemplatereference)|true|none|The resource ID and version number of the template configuring the behavior of a given Identity Verification.|
|user|[IdentityVerificationUserData](#schemaidentityverificationuserdata)|true|none|The identity data that was either collected from the user or provided via API in order to perform an Identity Verification.|
|status|[IdentityVerificationStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstatus)|true|none|The status of this Identity Verification attempt.<br><br><br>`active` - The Identity Verification attempt is incomplete. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed nor passed.<br><br>`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed, passing all steps defined to the associated Identity Verification template.<br><br>`failed` - The user failed one or more steps in the session and was told to contact support.<br><br>`expired` - The Identity Verification attempt was active for a long period of time without being completed and was automatically marked as expired. Note that sessions currently do not expire. Automatic expiration is expected to be enabled in the future.<br><br>`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled, either via the dashboard by a user, or via API. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed nor passed.<br><br>`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.|
|steps|[IdentityVerificationStepSummary](#schemaidentityverificationstepsummary)|true|none|Each step will be one of the following values:<br><br><br>`active` - This step is the user's current step. They are either in the process of completing this step, or they recently closed their Identity Verification attempt while in the middle of this step. Only one step will be marked as `active` at any given point.<br><br>`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed this step.<br><br>`failed` - The user failed this step. This can either cause the user to fail the session as a whole, or cause them to fall back to another step depending on how the Identity Verification template is configured. A failed step does not imply a failed session.<br><br>`waiting_for_prerequisite` - The user needs to complete another step first, before they progress to this step. This step may never run, depending on if the user fails an earlier step or if the step is only run as a fallback.<br><br>`not_applicable` - This step will not be run for this session.<br><br>`skipped` - This step was skipped, for example because the retry instructions that created this Identity Verification attempt specified that it should be skipped, because your template configuration skips it, or, for `accept_tos`, because `gave_consent` was `true`.<br><br>`expired` - This step had not yet been completed when the Identity Verification attempt as a whole expired.<br><br>`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled before the user completed this step.<br><br>`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.<br><br>`manually_approved` - The step was manually overridden to pass by a team member in the dashboard.<br><br>`manually_rejected` - The step was manually overridden to fail by a team member in the dashboard.|
|documentary_verification|[DocumentaryVerification](#schemadocumentaryverification)|true|none|Data, images, analysis, and results from the `documentary_verification` step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.documentary_verification` has reached a terminal state of `success`, `failed`, `manually_approved`, or `manually_rejected`. It is also returned while the user is being asked to retry after a failed document attempt.|
|selfie_check|[SelfieCheck](#schemaselfiecheck)|true|none|Additional information for the `selfie_check` step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.selfie_check` has reached a terminal state of `success`, `failed`, `manually_approved`, or `manually_rejected`.|
|kyc_check|[KYCCheckDetails](#schemakyccheckdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `kyc_check` (Data Source Verification) step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.kyc_check` has reached a terminal state of `success`, `failed`, `manually_approved`, or `manually_rejected`.|
|risk_check|[RiskCheckDetails](#schemariskcheckdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `risk_check` step.|
|verify_sms|[VerifySMSDetails](#schemaverifysmsdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `verify_sms` step.|
|watchlist_screening_id|[WatchlistScreeningIndividualIDNullable](#schemawatchlistscreeningindividualidnullable)|true|none|ID of the associated screening.|
|beacon_user_id|[BeaconUserIDNullable](#schemabeaconuseridnullable)|true|none|**Deprecated.** Beacon is deprecated in favor of Plaid Protect. This field is only populated for users of the deprecated Beacon product.|
|user_id|[PlaidUserIDNullable](#schemaplaiduseridnullable)|true|none|Unique user identifier, created by calling `/user/create`. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. The `user_id` may only be used instead of the `client_user_id` if you were not a pre-existing user of `/user/create` as of December 10, 2025, or if you have since [migrated to the new User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/migrate-to-new-user-apis); for more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis). If both this field and a `client_user_id` are present in a request, the `user_id` must have been created from the provided `client_user_id`.|
|redacted_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|latest_scored_protect_event|[IDVProtectEvent](#schemaidvprotectevent)|false|none|Information about a Protect event including Trust Index score and fraud attributes.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|success|
|status|failed|
|status|expired|
|status|canceled|
|status|pending_review|

<h2 id="tocS_IdentityVerificationDocumentAddressResponse">IdentityVerificationDocumentAddressResponse</h2>

```json
{
  "street": "123 Main St. Unit 42",
  "city": "Pawnee",
  "region": "IN",
  "postal_code": "46001",
  "country": "US"
}
```

The address extracted from the document. The address must at least contain the following fields to be a valid address: `street`, `city`, `country`. If any are missing or unable to be extracted, the address will be null.

`region`, and `postal_code` may be null based on the addressing system. For example:

Addresses from the United Kingdom will not include a region

Addresses from Hong Kong will not include postal code

Note: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology may sometimes extract incorrect data from a document.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|street|[IdentityVerificationDocumentStreet](#schemaidentityverificationdocumentstreet)|true|none|The full street address extracted from the document.|
|city|[IdentityVerificationDocumentCity](#schemaidentityverificationdocumentcity)|true|none|City extracted from the document.|
|region|[IdentityVerificationDocumentRegion](#schemaidentityverificationdocumentregion)|true|none|A subdivision code extracted from the document. Related terms would be "state", "province", "prefecture", "zone", "subdivision", etc. For a full list of valid codes, see [country subdivision codes](https://plaid.com/documents/country_subdivision_codes.json). Country prefixes are omitted, since they can be inferred from the `country` field.|
|postal_code|[IdentityVerificationDocumentPostalCode](#schemaidentityverificationdocumentpostalcode)|true|none|The postal code extracted from the document. Between 2 and 10 alphanumeric characters. For US-based addresses this must be 5 numeric digits.|
|country|[IdentityVerificationDocumentCountryCode](#schemaidentityverificationdocumentcountrycode)|true|none|Valid, capitalized, two-letter ISO code representing the country extracted from the document. Must be in ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 form.|

An identity verification attempt represents a customer's attempt to verify their identity, reflecting the required steps for completing the session, the results for each step, and information collected in the process.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[IdentityVerificationID](#schemaidentityverificationid)|true|none|ID of the associated Identity Verification attempt.|
|client_user_id|[ClientUserID](#schemaclientuserid)|true|none|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. This ID can also be used to associate user-specific data from other Plaid products. Financial Account Matching requires this field and the `/link/token/create` `client_user_id` to be consistent. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|completed_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|previous_attempt_id|[PreviousIdentityVerificationAttemptID](#schemapreviousidentityverificationattemptid)|true|none|The ID for the Identity Verification preceding this session. This field will only be filled if the current Identity Verification is a retry of a previous attempt.|
|shareable_url|[ShareableURL](#schemashareableurl)|true|none|A shareable URL that can be sent directly to the user to complete verification|
|template|[IdentityVerificationTemplateReference](#schemaidentityverificationtemplatereference)|true|none|The resource ID and version number of the template configuring the behavior of a given Identity Verification.|
|user|[IdentityVerificationUserData](#schemaidentityverificationuserdata)|true|none|The identity data that was either collected from the user or provided via API in order to perform an Identity Verification.|
|status|[IdentityVerificationStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstatus)|true|none|The status of this Identity Verification attempt.<br><br><br>`active` - The Identity Verification attempt is incomplete. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed nor passed.<br><br>`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed, passing all steps defined to the associated Identity Verification template.<br><br>`failed` - The user failed one or more steps in the session and was told to contact support.<br><br>`expired` - The Identity Verification attempt was active for a long period of time without being completed and was automatically marked as expired. Note that sessions currently do not expire. Automatic expiration is expected to be enabled in the future.<br><br>`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled, either via the dashboard by a user, or via API. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed nor passed.<br><br>`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.|
|steps|[IdentityVerificationStepSummary](#schemaidentityverificationstepsummary)|true|none|Each step will be one of the following values:<br><br><br>`active` - This step is the user's current step. They are either in the process of completing this step, or they recently closed their Identity Verification attempt while in the middle of this step. Only one step will be marked as `active` at any given point.<br><br>`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed this step.<br><br>`failed` - The user failed this step. This can either cause the user to fail the session as a whole, or cause them to fall back to another step depending on how the Identity Verification template is configured. A failed step does not imply a failed session.<br><br>`waiting_for_prerequisite` - The user needs to complete another step first, before they progress to this step. This step may never run, depending on if the user fails an earlier step or if the step is only run as a fallback.<br><br>`not_applicable` - This step will not be run for this session.<br><br>`skipped` - This step was skipped, for example because the retry instructions that created this Identity Verification attempt specified that it should be skipped, because your template configuration skips it, or, for `accept_tos`, because `gave_consent` was `true`.<br><br>`expired` - This step had not yet been completed when the Identity Verification attempt as a whole expired.<br><br>`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled before the user completed this step.<br><br>`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.<br><br>`manually_approved` - The step was manually overridden to pass by a team member in the dashboard.<br><br>`manually_rejected` - The step was manually overridden to fail by a team member in the dashboard.|
|documentary_verification|[DocumentaryVerification](#schemadocumentaryverification)|true|none|Data, images, analysis, and results from the `documentary_verification` step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.documentary_verification` has reached a terminal state of `success`, `failed`, `manually_approved`, or `manually_rejected`. It is also returned while the user is being asked to retry after a failed document attempt.|
|selfie_check|[SelfieCheck](#schemaselfiecheck)|true|none|Additional information for the `selfie_check` step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.selfie_check` has reached a terminal state of `success`, `failed`, `manually_approved`, or `manually_rejected`.|
|kyc_check|[KYCCheckDetails](#schemakyccheckdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `kyc_check` (Data Source Verification) step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.kyc_check` has reached a terminal state of `success`, `failed`, `manually_approved`, or `manually_rejected`.|
|risk_check|[RiskCheckDetails](#schemariskcheckdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `risk_check` step.|
|verify_sms|[VerifySMSDetails](#schemaverifysmsdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `verify_sms` step.|
|watchlist_screening_id|[WatchlistScreeningIndividualIDNullable](#schemawatchlistscreeningindividualidnullable)|true|none|ID of the associated screening.|
|beacon_user_id|[BeaconUserIDNullable](#schemabeaconuseridnullable)|true|none|**Deprecated.** Beacon is deprecated in favor of Plaid Protect. This field is only populated for users of the deprecated Beacon product.|
|user_id|[PlaidUserIDNullable](#schemaplaiduseridnullable)|true|none|Unique user identifier, created by calling `/user/create`. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. The `user_id` may only be used instead of the `client_user_id` if you were not a pre-existing user of `/user/create` as of December 10, 2025, or if you have since [migrated to the new User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/migrate-to-new-user-apis); for more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis). If both this field and a `client_user_id` are present in a request, the `user_id` must have been created from the provided `client_user_id`.|
|redacted_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|latest_scored_protect_event|[IDVProtectEvent](#schemaidvprotectevent)|false|none|Information about a Protect event including Trust Index score and fraud attributes.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|success|
|status|failed|
|status|expired|
|status|canceled|
|status|pending_review|

<h2 id="tocS_IdentityVerificationLanguage">IdentityVerificationLanguage</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaidentityverificationlanguage"></a>
<a id="schema_IdentityVerificationLanguage"></a>
<a id="tocSidentityverificationlanguage"></a>
<a id="tocsidentityverificationlanguage"></a>

```json
"fr-CA"
```

The language shown when the user starts this identity verification. If omitted or null, the language is detected from the user's browser settings, with English as the fallback. The user can select a different language during the session. An idempotent request that returns an existing identity verification does not change its language.

Use a supported BCP 47 language tag, such as `fr-CA`. Unlike `/link/token/create`, this field requires a region-specific value rather than a two-letter language code such as `fr`.

User information collected outside of Link, most likely via your own onboarding process.

Each of the following identity fields are optional:

`email_address`

`phone_number`

`date_of_birth`

`name`

`address`

`id_number`

Specifically, these fields are optional in that they can either be fully provided (satisfying every required field in their subschema) or omitted from the request entirely by not providing the key or value.
Providing these fields via the API will result in Link skipping the data collection process for the associated user. All verification steps enabled in the associated Identity Verification Template will still be run. Verification steps will either be run immediately, or once the user completes the `accept_tos` step, depending on the value provided to the `gave_consent` field.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email_address|[EmailAddress](#schemaemailaddress)|false|none|A valid email address. Must not have leading or trailing spaces and address must be RFC compliant. For more information, see [RFC 3696](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3696).|
|phone_number|[IdentityVerificationUserPhoneNumber](#schemaidentityverificationuserphonenumber)|false|none|A valid phone number in E.164 format.|
|date_of_birth|[ISO8601Date](#schemaiso8601date)|false|none|A date in the format YYYY-MM-DD (RFC 3339 Section 5.6).|
|name|[IdentityVerificationRequestUserName](#schemaidentityverificationrequestusername)|false|none|You can use this field to pre-populate the user's legal name; if it is provided here, they will not be prompted to enter their name in the identity verification attempt.|
|address|[UserAddress](#schemauseraddress)|false|none|Home address for the user. Supported values are: not provided, address with only country code or full address.<br><br>For more context on this field, see [Input Validation by Country](https://plaid.com/docs/identity-verification/hybrid-input-validation/#input-validation-by-country).|
|id_number|[UserIDNumber](#schemauseridnumber)|false|none|ID number submitted by the user. If the user has not submitted this data yet, this field will be `null`. Otherwise, both fields are guaranteed to be filled.|

Request input for retrying an identity verification attempt

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_user_id|[ClientUserID](#schemaclientuserid)|true|none|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. This ID can also be used to associate user-specific data from other Plaid products. Financial Account Matching requires this field and the `/link/token/create` `client_user_id` to be consistent. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|template_id|[IdentityVerificationTemplateID](#schemaidentityverificationtemplateid)|true|none|ID of the associated Identity Verification template. Like all Plaid identifiers, this is case-sensitive.|
|strategy|[Strategy](#schemastrategy)|true|none|An instruction specifying what steps the new Identity Verification attempt should require the user to complete:<br><br><br>`reset` - Restart the user at the beginning of the session, regardless of whether they successfully completed part of their previous session.<br><br>`incomplete` - Start the new session at the step that the user failed in the previous session, skipping steps that have already been successfully completed.<br><br>`infer` - If the most recent Identity Verification attempt associated with the given `client_user_id` has a status of `failed`, `expired`, or `canceled`, retry using the `incomplete` strategy, unless that attempt was created as part of a bulk import, its `watchlist_screening` step is `failed`, `expired`, or `canceled`, or its `risk_check` step is `failed`, `expired`, `canceled`, or `manually_rejected`. Otherwise, use the `reset` strategy.<br><br>`custom` - Start the new session with a custom configuration, specified by the value of the `steps` field<br><br>Note:<br><br>The `incomplete` strategy cannot be applied if the session's failing step is `watchlist_screening` or `risk_check`.<br><br>The `infer` strategy cannot be applied if the session's status is still `active`|
|user|[IdentityVerificationRequestUser](#schemaidentityverificationrequestuser)|false|none|User information collected outside of Link, most likely via your own onboarding process.<br><br>Each of the following identity fields are optional:<br><br>`email_address`<br><br>`phone_number`<br><br>`date_of_birth`<br><br>`name`<br><br>`address`<br><br>`id_number`<br><br>Specifically, these fields are optional in that they can either be fully provided (satisfying every required field in their subschema) or omitted from the request entirely by not providing the key or value.<br>Providing these fields via the API will result in Link skipping the data collection process for the associated user. All verification steps enabled in the associated Identity Verification Template will still be run. Verification steps will either be run immediately, or once the user completes the `accept_tos` step, depending on the value provided to the `gave_consent` field.|
|steps|[IdentityVerificationRetryRequestStepsObject](#schemaidentityverificationretryrequeststepsobject)|false|none|Instructions for the `custom` retry strategy specifying which steps should be required or skipped.<br><br><br>Note:<br><br><br>This field must be provided when the retry strategy is `custom` and must be omitted otherwise.<br><br>Custom retries override settings in your Plaid Template. For example, if your Plaid Template has `verify_sms` disabled, a custom retry with `verify_sms` enabled will still require the step.<br><br>The `selfie_check` step is currently not supported on the sandbox server. Sandbox requests will silently disable the `selfie_check` step when provided.|
|is_shareable|boolean \| null|false|none|A flag specifying whether you would like Plaid to expose a shareable URL for the verification being retried. If a value for this flag is not specified, the `is_shareable` setting from the original verification attempt will be used.|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|strategy|reset|
|strategy|incomplete|
|strategy|infer|
|strategy|custom|

<h2 id="tocS_IdentityVerificationRetryRequestStepsObject">IdentityVerificationRetryRequestStepsObject</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaidentityverificationretryrequeststepsobject"></a>
<a id="schema_IdentityVerificationRetryRequestStepsObject"></a>
<a id="tocSidentityverificationretryrequeststepsobject"></a>
<a id="tocsidentityverificationretryrequeststepsobject"></a>

```json
{
  "verify_sms": true,
  "kyc_check": true,
  "documentary_verification": true,
  "selfie_check": true
}
```

Instructions for the `custom` retry strategy specifying which steps should be required or skipped.


Note:


This field must be provided when the retry strategy is `custom` and must be omitted otherwise.

Custom retries override settings in your Plaid Template. For example, if your Plaid Template has `verify_sms` disabled, a custom retry with `verify_sms` enabled will still require the step.

The `selfie_check` step is currently not supported on the sandbox server. Sandbox requests will silently disable the `selfie_check` step when provided.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|verify_sms|boolean|true|none|A boolean field specifying whether the new session should require or skip the `verify_sms` step.|
|kyc_check|boolean|true|none|A boolean field specifying whether the new session should require or skip the `kyc_check` (Data Source Verification) step.|
|documentary_verification|boolean|true|none|A boolean field specifying whether the new session should require or skip the `documentary_verification` step.|
|selfie_check|boolean|true|none|A boolean field specifying whether the new session should require or skip the `selfie_check` step. If a previous session has already passed the `selfie_check` step, the new selfie check will be a Selfie Reauthentication check, in which the selfie is tested for liveness and for consistency with the previous selfie.|

An identity verification attempt represents a customer's attempt to verify their identity, reflecting the required steps for completing the session, the results for each step, and information collected in the process.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[IdentityVerificationID](#schemaidentityverificationid)|true|none|ID of the associated Identity Verification attempt.|
|client_user_id|[ClientUserID](#schemaclientuserid)|true|none|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. This ID can also be used to associate user-specific data from other Plaid products. Financial Account Matching requires this field and the `/link/token/create` `client_user_id` to be consistent. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|completed_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|previous_attempt_id|[PreviousIdentityVerificationAttemptID](#schemapreviousidentityverificationattemptid)|true|none|The ID for the Identity Verification preceding this session. This field will only be filled if the current Identity Verification is a retry of a previous attempt.|
|shareable_url|[ShareableURL](#schemashareableurl)|true|none|A shareable URL that can be sent directly to the user to complete verification|
|template|[IdentityVerificationTemplateReference](#schemaidentityverificationtemplatereference)|true|none|The resource ID and version number of the template configuring the behavior of a given Identity Verification.|
|user|[IdentityVerificationUserData](#schemaidentityverificationuserdata)|true|none|The identity data that was either collected from the user or provided via API in order to perform an Identity Verification.|
|status|[IdentityVerificationStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstatus)|true|none|The status of this Identity Verification attempt.<br><br><br>`active` - The Identity Verification attempt is incomplete. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed nor passed.<br><br>`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed, passing all steps defined to the associated Identity Verification template.<br><br>`failed` - The user failed one or more steps in the session and was told to contact support.<br><br>`expired` - The Identity Verification attempt was active for a long period of time without being completed and was automatically marked as expired. Note that sessions currently do not expire. Automatic expiration is expected to be enabled in the future.<br><br>`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled, either via the dashboard by a user, or via API. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed nor passed.<br><br>`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.|
|steps|[IdentityVerificationStepSummary](#schemaidentityverificationstepsummary)|true|none|Each step will be one of the following values:<br><br><br>`active` - This step is the user's current step. They are either in the process of completing this step, or they recently closed their Identity Verification attempt while in the middle of this step. Only one step will be marked as `active` at any given point.<br><br>`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed this step.<br><br>`failed` - The user failed this step. This can either cause the user to fail the session as a whole, or cause them to fall back to another step depending on how the Identity Verification template is configured. A failed step does not imply a failed session.<br><br>`waiting_for_prerequisite` - The user needs to complete another step first, before they progress to this step. This step may never run, depending on if the user fails an earlier step or if the step is only run as a fallback.<br><br>`not_applicable` - This step will not be run for this session.<br><br>`skipped` - This step was skipped, for example because the retry instructions that created this Identity Verification attempt specified that it should be skipped, because your template configuration skips it, or, for `accept_tos`, because `gave_consent` was `true`.<br><br>`expired` - This step had not yet been completed when the Identity Verification attempt as a whole expired.<br><br>`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled before the user completed this step.<br><br>`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.<br><br>`manually_approved` - The step was manually overridden to pass by a team member in the dashboard.<br><br>`manually_rejected` - The step was manually overridden to fail by a team member in the dashboard.|
|documentary_verification|[DocumentaryVerification](#schemadocumentaryverification)|true|none|Data, images, analysis, and results from the `documentary_verification` step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.documentary_verification` has reached a terminal state of `success`, `failed`, `manually_approved`, or `manually_rejected`. It is also returned while the user is being asked to retry after a failed document attempt.|
|selfie_check|[SelfieCheck](#schemaselfiecheck)|true|none|Additional information for the `selfie_check` step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.selfie_check` has reached a terminal state of `success`, `failed`, `manually_approved`, or `manually_rejected`.|
|kyc_check|[KYCCheckDetails](#schemakyccheckdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `kyc_check` (Data Source Verification) step. This field will be `null` unless `steps.kyc_check` has reached a terminal state of `success`, `failed`, `manually_approved`, or `manually_rejected`.|
|risk_check|[RiskCheckDetails](#schemariskcheckdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `risk_check` step.|
|verify_sms|[VerifySMSDetails](#schemaverifysmsdetails)|true|none|Additional information for the `verify_sms` step.|
|watchlist_screening_id|[WatchlistScreeningIndividualIDNullable](#schemawatchlistscreeningindividualidnullable)|true|none|ID of the associated screening.|
|beacon_user_id|[BeaconUserIDNullable](#schemabeaconuseridnullable)|true|none|**Deprecated.** Beacon is deprecated in favor of Plaid Protect. This field is only populated for users of the deprecated Beacon product.|
|user_id|[PlaidUserIDNullable](#schemaplaiduseridnullable)|true|none|Unique user identifier, created by calling `/user/create`. Either a `user_id` or the `client_user_id` must be provided. The `user_id` may only be used instead of the `client_user_id` if you were not a pre-existing user of `/user/create` as of December 10, 2025, or if you have since [migrated to the new User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/migrate-to-new-user-apis); for more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis). If both this field and a `client_user_id` are present in a request, the `user_id` must have been created from the provided `client_user_id`.|
|redacted_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|latest_scored_protect_event|[IDVProtectEvent](#schemaidvprotectevent)|false|none|Information about a Protect event including Trust Index score and fraud attributes.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|success|
|status|failed|
|status|expired|
|status|canceled|
|status|pending_review|

<h2 id="tocS_IdentityVerificationStatus">IdentityVerificationStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="schema_IdentityVerificationStatus"></a>

<a id="tocsidentityverificationstatus"></a>

```json
"success"
```

The status of this Identity Verification attempt.


`active` - The Identity Verification attempt is incomplete. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed nor passed.

`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed, passing all steps defined to the associated Identity Verification template.

`failed` - The user failed one or more steps in the session and was told to contact support.

`expired` - The Identity Verification attempt was active for a long period of time without being completed and was automatically marked as expired. Note that sessions currently do not expire. Automatic expiration is expected to be enabled in the future.

`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled, either via the dashboard by a user, or via API. The user may have completed part of the session, but has neither failed nor passed.

`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.

<h2 id="tocS_IdentityVerificationStepSummary">IdentityVerificationStepSummary</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaidentityverificationstepsummary"></a>

<a id="tocsidentityverificationstepsummary"></a>

```json
{
  "accept_tos": "success",
  "verify_sms": "success",
  "kyc_check": "success",
  "documentary_verification": "success",
  "selfie_check": "success",
  "watchlist_screening": "success",
  "risk_check": "success"
}
```

Each step will be one of the following values:


`active` - This step is the user's current step. They are either in the process of completing this step, or they recently closed their Identity Verification attempt while in the middle of this step. Only one step will be marked as `active` at any given point.

`success` - The Identity Verification attempt has completed this step.

`failed` - The user failed this step. This can either cause the user to fail the session as a whole, or cause them to fall back to another step depending on how the Identity Verification template is configured. A failed step does not imply a failed session.

`waiting_for_prerequisite` - The user needs to complete another step first, before they progress to this step. This step may never run, depending on if the user fails an earlier step or if the step is only run as a fallback.

`not_applicable` - This step will not be run for this session.

`skipped` - This step was skipped, for example because the retry instructions that created this Identity Verification attempt specified that it should be skipped, because your template configuration skips it, or, for `accept_tos`, because `gave_consent` was `true`.

`expired` - This step had not yet been completed when the Identity Verification attempt as a whole expired.

`canceled` - The Identity Verification attempt was canceled before the user completed this step.

`pending_review` - The Identity Verification attempt template was configured to perform a screening that had one or more hits needing review.

`manually_approved` - The step was manually overridden to pass by a team member in the dashboard.

`manually_rejected` - The step was manually overridden to fail by a team member in the dashboard.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accept_tos|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the Identity Verification process.|
|verify_sms|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the Identity Verification process.|
|kyc_check|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the Identity Verification process.|
|documentary_verification|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the Identity Verification process.|
|selfie_check|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the Identity Verification process.|
|watchlist_screening|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the Identity Verification process.|
|risk_check|[IdentityVerificationStepStatus](#schemaidentityverificationstepstatus)|true|none|The status of a step in the Identity Verification process.|

|city|[CityNullable](#schemacitynullable)|true|none|City from the address. A string with at least one non-whitespace alphabetical character, with a max length of 100 characters.|
|region|[Region](#schemaregion)|true|none|A subdivision code. "Subdivision" is a generic term for "state", "province", "prefecture", "zone", etc. For the list of valid codes, see [country subdivision codes](https://plaid.com/documents/country_subdivision_codes.json). Country prefixes are omitted, since they are inferred from the `country` field.|
|postal_code|[PostalCode](#schemapostalcode)|true|none|The postal code for the associated address. Between 2 and 10 alphanumeric characters. For US-based addresses this must be 5 numeric digits.|
|country|[GenericCountryCode](#schemagenericcountrycode)|true|none|Valid, capitalized, two-letter ISO code representing the country of this object. Must be in ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 form.|

A high level description of the quality of the image the user submitted.

For example, an image that is blurry, distorted by glare from a nearby light source, or improperly framed might be marked as low or medium quality. Poor quality images are more likely to fail OCR and/or template conformity checks.

Note: By default, Plaid will let a user recapture document images twice before failing the entire session if we attribute the failure to low image quality.

```json
  "blur_check": {}
```

Details about the image quality of the document.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|glare_check|object|true|none|The outcome of the glare check.<br><br>`success` - The image is free of glare.<br><br>`failed` - The image contains glare that may obscure document details.|
|dimensions_check|object|true|none|The outcome of the dimensions check.<br><br>`success` - The image meets the minimum size and resolution requirements.<br><br>`failed` - The image does not meet the minimum size or resolution requirements.|
|blur_check|object|true|none|The outcome of the blur check.<br><br>`success` - The image is sufficiently sharp.<br><br>`failed` - The image is too blurry for analysis.|

 `IZ_PEP`: Politically Exposed Persons List

 `IZ_UNC`: United Nations Consolidated Sanctions

 `IZ_WBK`: World Bank Listing of Ineligible Firms and Individuals

 `UK_HMC`: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office UK Sanctions List

 `US_DPL`: Bureau of Industry and Security Denied Persons List

 `US_DTC`: US Department of State AECA Debarred

 `US_FBI`: US Department of Justice FBI Wanted List

 `US_FSE`: US OFAC Foreign Sanctions Evaders

 `US_ISN`: US Department of State Nonproliferation Sanctions

 `US_MBS`: US Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions

 `US_PLC`: US OFAC Palestinian Legislative Council

 `US_SAM`: US System for Award Management Exclusion List

 `US_SDN`: US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List

 `US_SSI`: US OFAC Sectoral Sanctions Identifications

 `SG_SOF`: Government of Singapore Terrorists and Terrorist Entities

 `TR_TWL`: Government of Turkey Terrorist Wanted List

 `TR_DFD`: Government of Turkey Domestic Freezing Decisions

 `TR_FOR`: Government of Turkey Foreign Freezing Requests

 `TR_WMD`: Government of Turkey Weapons of Mass Destruction

```json
  "id": "prg_2eRPsDnL66rZ7H",
  "created_at": "2020-07-24T03:26:02Z",
  "is_rescanning_enabled": true,
  "lists_enabled": [
    "US_SDN"
  ],
  "name": "Sample Program",
  "name_sensitivity": "balanced",
  "audit_trail": {
    "source": "dashboard",
    "dashboard_user_id": "54350110fedcbaf01234ffee",
    "timestamp": "2020-07-24T03:26:02Z"
  },
  "is_archived": false
}
```

A program that configures the active lists, search parameters, and other behavior for initial and ongoing screening of individuals.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[WatchlistProgramID](#schemawatchlistprogramid)|true|none|ID of the associated program.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|is_rescanning_enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicator specifying whether the program is enabled and will perform daily rescans.|
|lists_enabled|[[IndividualWatchlistCode](#schemaindividualwatchlistcode)]|true|none|Watchlists enabled for the associated program|
|name|[IndividualWatchlistScreeningProgramName](#schemaindividualwatchlistscreeningprogramname)|true|none|A name for the program to define its purpose. For example, "High Risk Individuals", "US Cardholders", or "Applicants".|
|name_sensitivity|[ProgramNameSensitivity](#schemaprogramnamesensitivity)|true|none|The valid name matching sensitivity configurations for a screening program. Note that while certain matching techniques may be more prevalent on less strict settings, all matching algorithms are enabled for every sensitivity.<br><br>`coarse` - See more potential matches. This sensitivity will see more broad phonetic matches across alphabets that make missing a potential hit very unlikely. This setting is noisier and will require more manual review.<br><br>`balanced` - A good default for most companies. This sensitivity is balanced to show high quality hits with reduced noise.<br><br>`strict` - Aggressive false positive reduction. This sensitivity will require names to be more similar than `coarse` and `balanced` settings, relying less on phonetics, while still accounting for character transpositions, missing tokens, and other common permutations.<br><br>`exact` - Matches must be nearly exact. This sensitivity will only show hits with exact or nearly exact name matches with only basic correction such as extraneous symbols and capitalization. This setting is generally not recommended unless you have a very specific use case.|
|audit_trail|[WatchlistScreeningAuditTrail](#schemawatchlistscreeningaudittrail)|true|none|Information about the last change made to the parent object specifying what caused the change as well as when it occurred.|
|is_archived|[ProgramArchived](#schemaprogramarchived)|true|none|Archived programs are read-only and cannot screen new customers nor participate in ongoing monitoring.|


An enum indicating the match type between data provided by user and data checked against an external data source.


`match` indicates that the provided input data was a strong match against external data.

`partial_match` indicates the data approximately matched against external data. For example, "Knope" vs. "Knope-Wyatt" for last name.

`no_match` indicates that Plaid was able to perform a check against an external data source and it did not match the provided input data.

`no_data` indicates that Plaid was unable to find external data to compare against the provided input data.

`no_input` indicates that Plaid was unable to perform a check because no information was provided for this field by the end user.

<h2 id="tocS_PhysicalDocumentCategory">PhysicalDocumentCategory</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaphysicaldocumentcategory"></a>
<a id="schema_PhysicalDocumentCategory"></a>
<a id="tocSphysicaldocumentcategory"></a>
<a id="tocsphysicaldocumentcategory"></a>

```json
"drivers_license"
```

The type of identity document detected in the images provided. Will always be one of the following values:

  `drivers_license` - A driver's license issued by the associated country, establishing identity without any guarantee as to citizenship, and granting driving privileges

  `id_card` - A general national identification card, distinct from driver's licenses as it only establishes identity

  `passport` - A travel passport issued by the associated country for one of its citizens

  `residence_permit_card` - An identity document issued by the associated country permitting a foreign citizen to <em>temporarily</em> reside there

  `resident_card` - An identity document issued by the associated country permitting a foreign citizen to <em>permanently</em> reside there

  `visa` - An identity document issued by the associated country permitting a foreign citizen entry for a short duration and for a specific purpose, typically no longer than 6 months

Note: This value may be different from the ID type that the user selects within Link. For example, if they select "Driver's License" but then submit a picture of a passport, this field will say `passport`

For example, if they select "Driver's License" but then submit a picture of a passport, this field will say `passport`|

Country prefixes are omitted, since they are inferred from the `country` field.|

<h2 id="tocS_PhysicalDocumentImages">PhysicalDocumentImages</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaphysicaldocumentimages"></a>
<a id="schema_PhysicalDocumentImages"></a>
<a id="tocSphysicaldocumentimages"></a>
<a id="tocsphysicaldocumentimages"></a>

```json
{
  "original_front": "https://example.plaid.com/verifications/idv_52xR9LKo77r1Np/documents/1/original_front.jpeg",
  "original_back": "https://example.plaid.com/verifications/idv_52xR9LKo77r1Np/documents/1/original_back.jpeg",
  "cropped_front": "https://example.plaid.com/verifications/idv_52xR9LKo77r1Np/documents/1/cropped_front.jpeg",
  "cropped_back": "https://example.plaid.com/verifications/idv_52xR9LKo77r1Np/documents/1/cropped_back.jpeg",
  "face": "https://example.plaid.com/verifications/idv_52xR9LKo77r1Np/documents/1/face.jpeg"
}
```

URLs for downloading original and cropped images for this document submission. The URLs are designed to only allow downloading, not hot linking, so the URL will only serve the document image for 60 seconds before expiring. The expiration time is 60 seconds after the `GET` request for the associated Identity Verification attempt. A new expiring URL is generated with each request, so you can always rerequest the Identity Verification attempt if one of your URLs expires.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|original_front|[DocumentImage__Front](#schemadocumentimage__front)|true|none|Temporary URL that expires after 60 seconds for downloading the uncropped original image of the front of the document.|
|original_back|[DocumentImage__Back](#schemadocumentimage__back)|true|none|Temporary URL that expires after 60 seconds for downloading the original image of the back of the document. Might be null if the back of the document was not collected.|
|cropped_front|[DocumentImage__CroppedFront](#schemadocumentimage__croppedfront)|true|none|Temporary URL that expires after 60 seconds for downloading a cropped image containing just the front of the document.|
|cropped_back|[DocumentImage__CroppedBack](#schemadocumentimage__croppedback)|true|none|Temporary URL that expires after 60 seconds for downloading a cropped image containing just the back of the document. Might be null if the back of the document was not collected.|
|face|[DocumentImage__Face](#schemadocumentimage__face)|true|none|Temporary URL that expires after 60 seconds for downloading a crop of just the user's face from the document image. Might be null if the document does not contain a face photo.|

If both this field and a `client_user_id` are present in a request, the `user_id` must have been created from the provided `client_user_id`.

<h2 id="tocS_ProgramNameSensitivity">ProgramNameSensitivity</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaprogramnamesensitivity"></a>
<a id="schema_ProgramNameSensitivity"></a>
<a id="tocSprogramnamesensitivity"></a>
<a id="tocsprogramnamesensitivity"></a>

```json
"balanced"
```

The valid name matching sensitivity configurations for a screening program. Note that while certain matching techniques may be more prevalent on less strict settings, all matching algorithms are enabled for every sensitivity.

`coarse` - See more potential matches. This sensitivity will see more broad phonetic matches across alphabets that make missing a potential hit very unlikely. This setting is noisier and will require more manual review.

`balanced` - A good default for most companies. This sensitivity is balanced to show high quality hits with reduced noise.

`strict` - Aggressive false positive reduction. This sensitivity will require names to be more similar than `coarse` and `balanced` settings, relying less on phonetics, while still accounting for character transpositions, missing tokens, and other common permutations.

`exact` - Matches must be nearly exact. This sensitivity will only show hits with exact or nearly exact name matches with only basic correction such as extraneous symbols and capitalization. This setting is generally not recommended unless you have a very specific use case.

<h2 id="tocS_ProxyType">ProxyType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaproxytype"></a>
<a id="schema_ProxyType"></a>
<a id="tocSproxytype"></a>
<a id="tocsproxytype"></a>

```json
"none_detected"
```

An enum indicating whether a network proxy is present and if so what type it is.

`none_detected` indicates the user is not on a detectable proxy network.

`tor` indicates the user was using a Tor browser, which sends encrypted traffic on a decentralized network and is somewhat similar to a VPN (Virtual Private Network).

`vpn` indicates the user is on a VPN (Virtual Private Network)

`web_proxy` indicates the user is on a web proxy server, which may allow them to conceal information such as their IP address or other identifying information.

`public_proxy` indicates the user is on a public web proxy server, which is similar to a web proxy but can be shared by multiple users. This may allow multiple users to appear as if they have the same IP address for instance.

Field describing the overall user interaction signals of a behavior risk check. This value represents how familiar the user is with the personal data they provide, based on a number of signals that are collected during their session.

`genuine` indicates the user has high familiarity with the data they are providing, and that fraud is unlikely.

`neutral` indicates some signals are present in between `risky` and `genuine`, but there are not enough clear signals to determine an outcome.

`risky` indicates the user has low familiarity with the data they are providing, and that fraud is likely.

`no_data` indicates there is not sufficient information to give an accurate signal.

<h2 id="tocS_RiskCheckEmailName">RiskCheckEmailName</h2>

<a id="schemariskcheckemailname"></a>
<a id="schema_RiskCheckEmailName"></a>
<a id="tocSriskcheckemailname"></a>
<a id="tocsriskcheckemailname"></a>

```json
"match"
```

Indicates whether the provided name matches the email address according to the KYC name-matches-email inference result if known.

`match` - "The email's name identifiers match the user's name."

`partial_match` - "The email's name identifiers partially match the user's name."

`no_match` - "The email's name identifiers do not match the user's name."

`indeterminate` - "The email does not contain any name identifiers, and a match could not be determined."

`no_input` - "The user's profile does not contain the required user inputs to determine a match."

`no_data` - "Field could not be verified against available sources."

<h2 id="tocS_SMSVerification">SMSVerification</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasmsverification"></a>
<a id="schema_SMSVerification"></a>
<a id="tocSsmsverification"></a>
<a id="tocssmsverification"></a>

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "attempt": 1,
  "phone_number": "+12345678909",
  "delivery_attempt_count": 1,
  "solve_attempt_count": 1,
  "initially_sent_at": "2020-07-24T03:26:02Z",
  "last_sent_at": "2020-07-24T03:26:02Z",
  "redacted_at": "2020-07-24T03:26:02Z"
}
```

Additional information for the individual SMS verification.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|[SMSVerificationStatus](#schemasmsverificationstatus)|true|none|The outcome status for the individual SMS verification.|
|attempt|integer|true|none|The attempt field begins with 1 and increments with each subsequent SMS verification.|
|phone_number|string \| null|true|none|A phone number in E.164 format.|
|delivery_attempt_count|integer|true|none|The number of delivery attempts made within the verification to send the SMS code to the user. Each delivery attempt represents the user taking action from the front end UI to request creation and delivery of a new SMS verification code, or to resend an existing SMS verification code. There is a limit of 3 delivery attempts per verification.|
|solve_attempt_count|integer|true|none|The number of attempts made by the user within the verification to verify the SMS code by entering it into the front end UI. There is a limit of 3 solve attempts per verification.|
|initially_sent_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|last_sent_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|redacted_at|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|
|status|success|
|status|failed|
|status|canceled|

<h2 id="tocS_ScreeningHitAnalysis">ScreeningHitAnalysis</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemascreeninghitanalysis"></a>
<a id="schema_ScreeningHitAnalysis"></a>
<a id="tocSscreeninghitanalysis"></a>
<a id="tocsscreeninghitanalysis"></a>

```json
{
  "dates_of_birth": "match",
  "documents": "match",
  "locations": "match",
  "names": "match",
  "search_terms_version": 1
}
```

Analysis information describing why a screening hit matched the provided user information

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dates_of_birth|[MatchSummaryCode](#schemamatchsummarycode)|false|none|An enum indicating the match type between data provided by user and data checked against an external data source.<br><br><br>`match` indicates that the provided input data was a strong match against external data.<br><br>`partial_match` indicates the data approximately matched against external data. For example, "Knope" vs. "Knope-Wyatt" for last name.<br><br>`no_match` indicates that Plaid was able to perform a check against an external data source and it did not match the provided input data.<br><br>`no_data` indicates that Plaid was unable to find external data to compare against the provided input data.<br><br>`no_input` indicates that Plaid was unable to perform a check because no information was provided for this field by the end user.|
|documents|[MatchSummaryCode](#schemamatchsummarycode)|false|none|An enum indicating the match type between data provided by user and data checked against an external data source.<br><br><br>`match` indicates that the provided input data was a strong match against external data.<br><br>`partial_match` indicates the data approximately matched against external data. For example, "Knope" vs. "Knope-Wyatt" for last name.<br><br>`no_match` indicates that Plaid was able to perform a check against an external data source and it did not match the provided input data.<br><br>`no_data` indicates that Plaid was unable to find external data to compare against the provided input data.<br><br>`no_input` indicates that Plaid was unable to perform a check because no information was provided for this field by the end user.|
|locations|[MatchSummaryCode](#schemamatchsummarycode)|false|none|An enum indicating the match type between data provided by user and data checked against an external data source.<br><br><br>`match` indicates that the provided input data was a strong match against external data.<br><br>`partial_match` indicates the data approximately matched against external data. For example, "Knope" vs. "Knope-Wyatt" for last name.<br><br>`no_match` indicates that Plaid was able to perform a check against an external data source and it did not match the provided input data.<br><br>`no_data` indicates that Plaid was unable to find external data to compare against the provided input data.<br><br>`no_input` indicates that Plaid was unable to perform a check because no information was provided for this field by the end user.|
|names|[MatchSummaryCode](#schemamatchsummarycode)|false|none|An enum indicating the match type between data provided by user and data checked against an external data source.<br><br><br>`match` indicates that the provided input data was a strong match against external data.<br><br>`partial_match` indicates the data approximately matched against external data. For example, "Knope" vs. "Knope-Wyatt" for last name.<br><br>`no_match` indicates that Plaid was able to perform a check against an external data source and it did not match the provided input data.<br><br>`no_data` indicates that Plaid was unable to find external data to compare against the provided input data.<br><br>`no_input` indicates that Plaid was unable to perform a check because no information was provided for this field by the end user.|
|search_terms_version|integer|true|none|The version of the screening's `search_terms` that were compared when the screening hit was added. Screening hits are immutable once they have been reviewed. If changes are detected due to updates to the screening's `search_terms`, the associated program, or the list's source data prior to review, the screening hit will be updated to reflect those changes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|

|dates_of_birth|partial_match|
|dates_of_birth|no_match|
|dates_of_birth|no_data|
|dates_of_birth|no_input|

|documents|partial_match|
|documents|no_match|
|documents|no_data|
|documents|no_input|
|locations|match|
|locations|partial_match|
|locations|no_match|
|locations|no_data|
|locations|no_input|
|names|match|
|names|partial_match|
|names|no_match|
|names|no_data|
|names|no_input|

An enum indicating whether the reported age aligns with the estimated selfie capture age range.

`match` indicates that the reported age falls within the estimated selfie capture age range.

`warning` indicates that the reported age falls outside the estimated selfie capture age range, but is close enough that the result should be reviewed.

`no_match` indicates that the reported age falls far outside the estimated selfie capture age range.

`no_data` indicates that there was not enough data available at age-estimation time to compare the reported age against the estimated selfie capture age range.

<h2 id="tocS_SelfieCapture">SelfieCapture</h2>

```json
}
```

The image or video capture of a selfie. Only one of `image_url` or `video_url` will be populated per selfie. In the vast majority of sessions Plaid records a short video of the user, so `video_url` is populated and `image_url` is `null`. `image_url` is only populated in the rare passive-liveness fallback case, where the user's device could not complete the standard video liveness capture (for example, a camera or streaming error) and submitted a single still image instead.

This field is only populated when the session fell back to passive (image-based) liveness. For the majority of selfie checks this field is `null` and `video_url` is populated instead.|
|video_url|[SelfieCaptureVideoURL](#schemaselfiecapturevideourl)|true|none|Temporary URL for downloading a video selfie capture. This is the standard selfie capture for Identity Verification. Plaid records a short video of the user during the Selfie Check liveness step, so this field is populated for the vast majority of selfie checks.|

<h2 id="tocS_Strategy">Strategy</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemastrategy"></a>
<a id="schema_Strategy"></a>
<a id="tocSstrategy"></a>
<a id="tocsstrategy"></a>

```json
"reset"
```

An instruction specifying what steps the new Identity Verification attempt should require the user to complete:


`reset` - Restart the user at the beginning of the session, regardless of whether they successfully completed part of their previous session.

`incomplete` - Start the new session at the step that the user failed in the previous session, skipping steps that have already been successfully completed.

`infer` - If the most recent Identity Verification attempt associated with the given `client_user_id` has a status of `failed`, `expired`, or `canceled`, retry using the `incomplete` strategy, unless that attempt was created as part of a bulk import, its `watchlist_screening` step is `failed`, `expired`, or `canceled`, or its `risk_check` step is `failed`, `expired`, `canceled`, or `manually_rejected`. Otherwise, use the `reset` strategy.

`custom` - Start the new session with a custom configuration, specified by the value of the `steps` field

Note:

The `incomplete` strategy cannot be applied if the session's failing step is `watchlist_screening` or `risk_check`.

The `infer` strategy cannot be applied if the session's status is still `active`

A program that configures the active lists, search parameters, and other behavior for initial and ongoing screening of entities.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[EntityWatchlistProgramID](#schemaentitywatchlistprogramid)|true|none|ID of the associated entity program.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|is_rescanning_enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicator specifying whether the program is enabled and will perform daily rescans.|
|lists_enabled|[[EntityWatchlistCode](#schemaentitywatchlistcode)]|true|none|Watchlists enabled for the associated program|
|name|[EntityWatchlistScreeningProgramName](#schemaentitywatchlistscreeningprogramname)|true|none|A name for the entity program to define its purpose. For example, "High Risk Organizations" or "Applicants".|
|name_sensitivity|[ProgramNameSensitivity](#schemaprogramnamesensitivity)|true|none|The valid name matching sensitivity configurations for a screening program. Note that while certain matching techniques may be more prevalent on less strict settings, all matching algorithms are enabled for every sensitivity.<br><br>`coarse` - See more potential matches. This sensitivity will see more broad phonetic matches across alphabets that make missing a potential hit very unlikely. This setting is noisier and will require more manual review.<br><br>`balanced` - A good default for most companies. This sensitivity is balanced to show high quality hits with reduced noise.<br><br>`strict` - Aggressive false positive reduction. This sensitivity will require names to be more similar than `coarse` and `balanced` settings, relying less on phonetics, while still accounting for character transpositions, missing tokens, and other common permutations.<br><br>`exact` - Matches must be nearly exact. This sensitivity will only show hits with exact or nearly exact name matches with only basic correction such as extraneous symbols and capitalization. This setting is generally not recommended unless you have a very specific use case.|
|audit_trail|[WatchlistScreeningAuditTrail](#schemawatchlistscreeningaudittrail)|true|none|Information about the last change made to the parent object specifying what caused the change as well as when it occurred.|
|is_archived|[ProgramArchived](#schemaprogramarchived)|true|none|Archived programs are read-only and cannot screen new customers nor participate in ongoing monitoring.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

A review submitted by a team member for an entity watchlist screening. A review can be either a comment on the current screening state, actions taken
against hits attached to the watchlist screening, or both.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[EntityWatchlistScreeningReviewID](#schemaentitywatchlistscreeningreviewid)|true|none|ID of the associated entity review.|
|confirmed_hits|[[EntityWatchlistScreeningHitID](#schemaentitywatchlistscreeninghitid)]|true|none|Hits marked as a true positive after thorough manual review. These hits will never recur or be updated once confirmed. In most cases, confirmed hits indicate that the customer should be rejected.|

Data from a government watchlist or PEP list that has been attached to the screening.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[WatchlistScreeningHitID](#schemawatchlistscreeninghitid)|true|none|ID of the associated screening hit.|
|review_status|[WatchlistScreeningHitStatus](#schemawatchlistscreeninghitstatus)|true|none|The current state of review. All watchlist screening hits begin in a `pending_review` state but can be changed by creating a review. When a hit is in the `pending_review` state, it will always show the latest version of the watchlist data Plaid has available and be compared against the latest customer information saved in the watchlist screening. Once a hit has been marked as `confirmed` or `dismissed` it will no longer be updated so that the state is as it was when the review was first conducted.|
|first_active|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|inactive_since|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|historical_since|[TimestampNullable](#schematimestampnullable)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|list_code|[IndividualWatchlistCode](#schemaindividualwatchlistcode)|true|none|Shorthand identifier for a specific screening list for individuals.<br><br> `AU_CON`: Australia Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Consolidated List<br><br> `CA_CON`: Government of Canada Consolidated List of Sanctions<br><br> `EU_CON`: European External Action Service Consolidated List<br><br> `IZ_CIA`: CIA List of Chiefs of State and Cabinet Members<br><br> `IZ_IPL`: Interpol Red Notices for Wanted Persons List<br><br> `IZ_PEP`: Politically Exposed Persons List<br><br> `IZ_UNC`: United Nations Consolidated Sanctions<br><br> `IZ_WBK`: World Bank Listing of Ineligible Firms and Individuals<br><br> `UK_HMC`: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office UK Sanctions List<br><br> `US_DPL`: Bureau of Industry and Security Denied Persons List<br><br> `US_DTC`: US Department of State AECA Debarred<br><br> `US_FBI`: US Department of Justice FBI Wanted List<br><br> `US_FSE`: US OFAC Foreign Sanctions Evaders<br><br> `US_ISN`: US Department of State Nonproliferation Sanctions<br><br> `US_MBS`: US Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions<br><br> `US_PLC`: US OFAC Palestinian Legislative Council<br><br> `US_SAM`: US System for Award Management Exclusion List<br><br> `US_SDN`: US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List<br><br> `US_SSI`: US OFAC Sectoral Sanctions Identifications<br><br> `SG_SOF`: Government of Singapore Terrorists and Terrorist Entities<br><br> `TR_TWL`: Government of Turkey Terrorist Wanted List<br><br> `TR_DFD`: Government of Turkey Domestic Freezing Decisions<br><br> `TR_FOR`: Government of Turkey Foreign Freezing Requests<br><br> `TR_WMD`: Government of Turkey Weapons of Mass Destruction<br><br> `TR_CMB`: Government of Turkey Capital Markets Board|
|plaid_uid|[InternalUID](#schemainternaluid)|true|none|A universal identifier for a watchlist individual that is stable across searches and updates.|
|source_uid|[SourceUID](#schemasourceuid)|true|none|The identifier provided by the source sanction or watchlist. When one is not provided by the source, this is `null`.|
|sub_programs|[string]|true|none|Sub-program designations that may be attached to the watchlist entry by the issuing authority. For OFAC SDN<br>entries these are the program codes published in the SDN list (for example `SDGT` for Specially<br>Designated Global Terrorists, `SDNTK` for Specially Designated Narcotics Trafficking Kingpins,<br>`IRAN`, `RUSSIA-EO14024`). New codes are added by sanctioning authorities without prior notice,<br>so callers should treat unknown values as opaque strings rather than enum members.<br>|
|analysis|[ScreeningHitAnalysis](#schemascreeninghitanalysis)|false|none|Analysis information describing why a screening hit matched the provided user information|
|data|[ScreeningHitData](#schemascreeninghitdata)|false|none|Information associated with the watchlist hit|

|review_status|pending_review|
|review_status|dismissed|

A program that configures the active lists, search parameters, and other behavior for initial and ongoing screening of individuals.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[WatchlistProgramID](#schemawatchlistprogramid)|true|none|ID of the associated program.|
|created_at|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|true|none|An ISO8601 formatted timestamp.|
|is_rescanning_enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicator specifying whether the program is enabled and will perform daily rescans.|
|lists_enabled|[[IndividualWatchlistCode](#schemaindividualwatchlistcode)]|true|none|Watchlists enabled for the associated program|
|name|[IndividualWatchlistScreeningProgramName](#schemaindividualwatchlistscreeningprogramname)|true|none|A name for the program to define its purpose. For example, "High Risk Individuals", "US Cardholders", or "Applicants".|
|name_sensitivity|[ProgramNameSensitivity](#schemaprogramnamesensitivity)|true|none|The valid name matching sensitivity configurations for a screening program. Note that while certain matching techniques may be more prevalent on less strict settings, all matching algorithms are enabled for every sensitivity.<br><br>`coarse` - See more potential matches. This sensitivity will see more broad phonetic matches across alphabets that make missing a potential hit very unlikely. This setting is noisier and will require more manual review.<br><br>`balanced` - A good default for most companies. This sensitivity is balanced to show high quality hits with reduced noise.<br><br>`strict` - Aggressive false positive reduction. This sensitivity will require names to be more similar than `coarse` and `balanced` settings, relying less on phonetics, while still accounting for character transpositions, missing tokens, and other common permutations.<br><br>`exact` - Matches must be nearly exact. This sensitivity will only show hits with exact or nearly exact name matches with only basic correction such as extraneous symbols and capitalization. This setting is generally not recommended unless you have a very specific use case.|
|audit_trail|[WatchlistScreeningAuditTrail](#schemawatchlistscreeningaudittrail)|true|none|Information about the last change made to the parent object specifying what caused the change as well as when it occurred.|
|is_archived|[ProgramArchived](#schemaprogramarchived)|true|none|Archived programs are read-only and cannot screen new customers nor participate in ongoing monitoring.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|third_party_user_token|[ThirdPartyUserToken](#schemathirdpartyusertoken)|false|none|The third-party user token associated with the requested User data.|

Integrations that began using `/user/create` after December 10, 2025 use this field to identify a user instead of the `user_token`. For more details, see [New User APIs](https://plaid.com/docs/api/users/user-apis).|
|options|[CraCheckReportIncomeInsightsGetOptions](#schemacracheckreportincomeinsightsgetoptions)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. This field is no longer accepted for new clients (created on or after 2026-07-01). New clients should specify required products when creating the Consumer Report. Existing integrations may continue to pass `options`.|
|report_id|string|false|none|The CRA report token (formatted `cra-report-<env>-<uuid>`) identifying a specific consumer report. When provided alongside `consumer_report_permissible_purpose`, pins retrieval to that report and stamps its permissible purpose. If omitted, the most recently generated report for the user is returned.|
|consumer_report_permissible_purpose|object|false|none|The permissible purpose under which the consumer report is being retrieved.|

CraCheckReportIncomeInsightsGetResponse defines the response schema for `/cra/check_report/income_insights/get`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|report|[CraIncomeInsights](#schemacraincomeinsights)|false|none|The Check Income Insights Report for an end user.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|
|warnings|[[CheckReportWarning](#schemacheckreportwarning)]|false|none|If the Income Insights generation was successful but a subset of data could not be retrieved, this array will contain information about the errors causing information to be missing|

It is possible for a Check Report product to be returned with missing information. In such cases, the product will contain warning data in the response, indicating why some of the requested information could not be retrieved.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|warning_type|string|true|none|The warning type, which will always be `CHECK_REPORT_WARNING`|
|warning_code|[CheckReportWarningCode](#schemacheckreportwarningcode)|true|none|The warning code identifies a specific kind of warning.<br><br>`IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE`:  Account-owner information is not available.<br><br>`TRANSACTIONS_UNAVAILABLE`: Transactions information associated with Credit and Depository accounts are unavailable.<br><br>`USER_FRAUD_ALERT`: The user has placed a fraud alert on their Plaid Check consumer report due to suspected fraud. Please note that when a fraud alert is in place, the recipient of the consumer report has an obligation to verify the consumer's identity.|
|cause|[Cause](#schemacause)|true|none|An error object and associated `item_id` used to identify a specific Item and error when a batch operation operating on multiple Items has encountered an error in one of the Items.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|warning_code|IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE|
|warning_code|TRANSACTIONS_UNAVAILABLE|
|warning_code|USER_FRAUD_ALERT|

<h2 id="tocS_CheckReportWarningCode">CheckReportWarningCode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacheckreportwarningcode"></a>
<a id="schema_CheckReportWarningCode"></a>
<a id="tocScheckreportwarningcode"></a>
<a id="tocscheckreportwarningcode"></a>

```json
"IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE"
```

The warning code identifies a specific kind of warning.

`IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE`:  Account-owner information is not available.

`TRANSACTIONS_UNAVAILABLE`: Transactions information associated with Credit and Depository accounts are unavailable.

`USER_FRAUD_ALERT`: The user has placed a fraud alert on their Plaid Check consumer report due to suspected fraud. Please note that when a fraud alert is in place, the recipient of the consumer report has an obligation to verify the consumer's identity.
