Metadata about the Item.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|item_id|string|true|none|The Plaid Item ID. The `item_id` is always unique; linking the same account at the same institution twice will result in two Items with different `item_id` values. Like all Plaid identifiers, the `item_id` is case-sensitive.|
|institution_id|string \| null|false|none|The Plaid Institution ID associated with the Item. Field is omitted for Items created without an institution connection, such as Items created via Same-Day Micro-deposits.|
|institution_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the institution associated with the Item. Field is omitted for Items created without an institution connection, such as Items created via Same-Day Micro-deposits.|
|webhook|string \| null|true|none|The URL registered to receive webhooks for the Item. Empty string if no webhook is set.|
|auth_method|[ItemAuthMethod](#schemaitemauthmethod)|false|none|The method used to populate Auth data for the Item. This field is only populated for Items that have had Auth numbers data set on at least one of their accounts, and will be omitted otherwise. For info about the various flows, see our [Auth coverage documentation](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/coverage/).<br><br>`INSTANT_AUTH`: The Item's Auth data was provided directly by the user's institution connection.<br><br>`INSTANT_MATCH`: The Item's Auth data was provided via the Instant Match fallback flow.<br><br>`AUTOMATED_MICRODEPOSITS`: The Item's Auth data was provided via the Automated Micro-deposits flow.<br><br>`SAME_DAY_MICRODEPOSITS`: The Item's Auth data was provided via the Same-Day Micro-deposits flow.<br><br>`INSTANT_MICRODEPOSITS`: The Item's Auth data was provided via the Instant Micro-deposits flow.<br><br>`DATABASE_MATCH`: The Item's Auth data was provided via the Database Match flow.<br><br>`DATABASE_INSIGHTS`: The Item's Auth data was provided via the Database Insights flow.<br><br>`TRANSFER_MIGRATED`: The Item's Auth data was provided via [`/transfer/migrate_account`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transfer/account-linking/#migrate-account-into-transfers).<br><br>`INVESTMENTS_FALLBACK`: The Item's Auth data for Investments Move was provided via a [fallback flow](https://plaid.com/docs/investments-move/#fallback-flows).|
|error|[PlaidError](#schemaplaiderror)|true|none|Errors are identified by `error_code` and categorized by `error_type`. Use these in preference to HTTP status codes to identify and handle specific errors. HTTP status codes are set and provide the broadest categorization of errors: 4xx codes are for developer- or user-related errors, and 5xx codes are for Plaid-related errors, and the status will be 2xx in non-error cases. An Item with a non-`null` error object will only be part of an API response when calling `/item/get` to view Item status. Otherwise, error fields will be `null` if no error has occurred; if an error has occurred, an error code will be returned instead.|
|available_products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|true|none|A list of products available for the Item that have not yet been accessed. The contents of this array will be mutually exclusive with `billed_products`.|
|billed_products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|true|none|A list of products that have been billed for the Item. The contents of this array will be mutually exclusive with `available_products`. Note - `billed_products` is populated in all environments but only requests in Production are billed. Also note that products that are billed on a pay-per-call basis rather than a pay-per-Item basis, such as `balance`, will not appear here.<br>|
|products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|none|A list of products added to the Item. In almost all cases, this will be the same as the `billed_products` field. For some products, it is possible for the product to be added to an Item but not yet billed (e.g. Assets, before `/asset_report/create` has been called, or Auth or Identity when added as Optional Products but before their endpoints have been called), in which case the product may appear in `products` but not in `billed_products`.<br>|
|consented_products|[[Products](#schemaproducts)]|false|none|A list of products that the user has consented to for the Item via [Data Transparency Messaging](https://plaid.com/docs/link/data-transparency-messaging-migration-guide). This will consist of all products where both of the following are true: the user has consented to the required data scopes for that product and you have Production access for that product.<br>|
|consent_expiration_time|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|The date and time at which the Item's access consent will expire, in [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format. If the Item does not have consent expiration scheduled, this field will be `null`. Currently, only institutions in Europe and a small number of institutions in the US have expiring consent. For a list of US institutions that currently expire consent, see the [OAuth Guide](https://plaid.com/docs/link/oauth/#refreshing-item-consent).|
|update_type|string|true|none|Indicates whether an Item requires user interaction to be updated, which can be the case for Items with some forms of two-factor authentication.<br><br>`background` - Item can be updated in the background<br><br>`user_present_required` - Item requires user interaction to be updated|
|paired_item_id|string \| null|false|none|The `item_id` of the Item that was created alongside this one in a single Link session. Only present for Items created in a hybrid Link flow that produces separate Plaid Inc and Plaid Check items; `null` for every other Item.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|access_token|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|none|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|
|reason_code|[ProductsTerminateReasonCode](#schemaproductsterminatereasoncode)|true|none|The reason for terminating products.<br><br>`FRAUD_FIRST_PARTY`: The end user who owns the connected bank account committed fraud using their real identity<br><br>`FRAUD_FALSE_IDENTITY`: The connection was created using a false or stolen identity<br><br>`FRAUD_ABUSE`: The end user is abusing the client's service or platform (for example, automation or excessive retries) through their connected account<br><br>`FRAUD_OTHER`: Fraud-related, but not covered by the specific fraud categories above; `reason_note` should clarify<br><br>`FRAUD_TRANSACTION`: Fraud occurred at the transaction level, such as an unauthorized transaction, card testing, chargeback, ACH return, or dispute<br><br>`CONSUMER_LOAN_PAID_OFF`: The end user paid off their loan and no longer needs the product<br><br>`CONSUMER_ACCOUNT_CLOSED`: The end user closed their account with the client and no longer needs the product<br><br>`CONSUMER_CHARGE_OFF`: The end user's account has been charged off<br><br>`CONSUMER_PAYMENT_METHOD_SWITCHED`: The end user switched to a different payment method and no longer needs the product<br><br>`USER_OFFBOARDING`: The user is offboarding from the client's service or platform<br><br>`DUPLICATE_ITEM`: This Item is a duplicate of another active Item for the same user<br><br>`BILLING_TERMINATION`: The client's billing or subscription relationship with the end user has ended<br><br>`OTHER`: None of the above; `reason_note` should clarify<br>|
|reason_note|string \| null|false|none|Additional context or details about the reason for terminating products on the Item. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be included in the `reason_note`.|

<h2 id="tocS_ProductsTerminateReasonCode">ProductsTerminateReasonCode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaproductsterminatereasoncode"></a>
<a id="schema_ProductsTerminateReasonCode"></a>
<a id="tocSproductsterminatereasoncode"></a>
<a id="tocsproductsterminatereasoncode"></a>

```json
"FRAUD_FIRST_PARTY"
```

The reason for terminating products.

`FRAUD_FIRST_PARTY`: The end user who owns the connected bank account committed fraud using their real identity

`FRAUD_FALSE_IDENTITY`: The connection was created using a false or stolen identity

`FRAUD_ABUSE`: The end user is abusing the client's service or platform (for example, automation or excessive retries) through their connected account

`FRAUD_OTHER`: Fraud-related, but not covered by the specific fraud categories above; `reason_note` should clarify

`FRAUD_TRANSACTION`: Fraud occurred at the transaction level, such as an unauthorized transaction, card testing, chargeback, ACH return, or dispute

`CONSUMER_LOAN_PAID_OFF`: The end user paid off their loan and no longer needs the product

`CONSUMER_ACCOUNT_CLOSED`: The end user closed their account with the client and no longer needs the product

`CONSUMER_CHARGE_OFF`: The end user's account has been charged off

`CONSUMER_PAYMENT_METHOD_SWITCHED`: The end user switched to a different payment method and no longer needs the product

`USER_OFFBOARDING`: The user is offboarding from the client's service or platform

`DUPLICATE_ITEM`: This Item is a duplicate of another active Item for the same user

`BILLING_TERMINATION`: The client's billing or subscription relationship with the end user has ended

`OTHER`: None of the above; `reason_note` should clarify

A space-separated list of scopes associated with this token, in the format described in [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.3). Currently accepted values are:

`user:read` allows reading user data.

`user:write` allows writing user data.

`exchange` allows exchanging a token using the `urn:plaid:params:oauth:user-token` subject token type.

`mcp:dashboard` allows access to the MCP dashboard server.

<h2 id="tocS_OAuthGrantType">OAuthGrantType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaoauthgranttype"></a>
<a id="schema_OAuthGrantType"></a>
<a id="tocSoauthgranttype"></a>
<a id="tocsoauthgranttype"></a>

```json
"refresh_token"
```

The type of OAuth grant being requested:

`client_credentials` allows exchanging a client id and client secret for a refresh and access token.

`refresh_token` allows refreshing an access token using a refresh token. When using this grant type, only the `refresh_token` field is required (along with the `client_id` and `client_secret`).

`urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` allows exchanging a subject token for an OAuth token. When using this grant type, the `audience`, `subject_token` and `subject_token_type` fields are required.

These grants are defined in their respective RFCs. `refresh_token` and `client_credentials` are defined in RFC 6749 and `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` is defined in RFC 8693.

<h2 id="tocS_OAuthSubjectTokenType">OAuthSubjectTokenType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaoauthsubjecttokentype"></a>
<a id="schema_OAuthSubjectTokenType"></a>
<a id="tocSoauthsubjecttokentype"></a>
<a id="tocsoauthsubjecttokentype"></a>

```json
"urn:plaid:params:tokens:user"
```

The type of the subject token.

`urn:plaid:params:tokens:user` allows exchanging a Plaid-issued user token for an OAuth token. When using this token type, `audience` must be the same as the `client_id`. `subject_token` must be a Plaid-issued user token issued from the `/user/create` endpoint.

`urn:plaid:params:oauth:user-token` allows exchanging a refresh token for an OAuth token to another `client_id`. The other `client_id` is provided in `audience`. `subject_token` must be an OAuth refresh token issued from the `/oauth/token` endpoint.

`urn:plaid:params:credit:multi-user` allows exchanging a Plaid-issued user token for an OAuth token. When using this token type, `audience` may be a client id or a supported CRA partner URN. `audience` supports a comma-delimited list of clients. When multiple clients are specified in the `audience` a multi-party token is created which can be used by all parties in the audience in conjunction with their `client_id` and `client_secret`.

OAuth token introspect response

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Boolean indicator of whether or not the presented token is currently active. A `true` value indicates that the token has been issued, has not been revoked, and is within the time window of validity.|
|scope|[OAuthScope](#schemaoauthscope)|false|none|A space-separated list of scopes associated with this token, in the format described in [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.3). Currently accepted values are:<br><br>`user:read` allows reading user data.<br><br>`user:write` allows writing user data.<br><br>`exchange` allows exchanging a token using the `urn:plaid:params:oauth:user-token` subject token type.<br><br>`mcp:dashboard` allows access to the MCP dashboard server.|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|exp|integer|false|none|Expiration time as UNIX timestamp since January 1 1970 UTC|
|iat|integer|false|none|Issued at time as UNIX timestamp since January 1 1970 UTC|
|sub|string|false|none|Subject of the token|
|aud|string|false|none|Audience of the token|
|iss|string|false|none|Issuer of the token|
|token_type|string|false|none|Type of the token|
|user_id|string|false|none|User ID of the token|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

SignalEvaluateRequest defines the request schema for `/signal/evaluate`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|access_token|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|none|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|
|account_id|string|true|none|The Plaid `account_id` of the account that is the funding source for the proposed transaction. The `account_id` is returned in the `/accounts/get` endpoint as well as the [`onSuccess`](https://plaid.com/docs/link/ios/#link-ios-onsuccess-linkSuccess-metadata-accounts-id) callback metadata.<br><br>This will return an [`INVALID_ACCOUNT_ID`](https://plaid.com/docs/errors/invalid-input/#invalid_account_id) error if the account has been removed at the bank or if the `account_id` is no longer valid.|
|client_transaction_id|string|true|none|The unique ID that you would like to use to refer to this evaluation attempt - for example, a payment attempt ID. You will use this later to debug this evaluation, and/or report an ACH return, etc. The max length for this field is 36 characters. The `client_transaction_id` also functions as an idempotency key; calling `/signal/evaluate` with a previously used `client_transaction_id` will return the results of the previous evaluation rather than triggering a fresh evaluation.|
|amount|number(double)|true|none|The transaction amount, in USD (e.g. `102.05`)|
|user_present|boolean \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** `true` if the end user is present while initiating the ACH transfer and the endpoint is being called; `false` otherwise (for example, when the ACH transfer is scheduled and the end user is not present, or you call this endpoint after the ACH transfer but before submitting the Nacha file for ACH processing). When using a Balance-only ruleset, this field is ignored. This field is not currently used as part of Signal Transaction Score evaluations, but may be used in the future.|
|client_user_id|string|false|none|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. This ID is used to correlate requests by a user with multiple Items. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|is_recurring|boolean \| null|false|none|Use `true` if the ACH transaction is a part of recurring schedule (for example, a monthly repayment); `false` otherwise. When using a Balance-only ruleset, this field is ignored.|
|default_payment_method|string \| null|false|none|The default ACH payment method to complete the transaction. When using a Balance-only ruleset, this field is ignored.<br><br>`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH by Nacha. The debit transaction is processed and settled on the same day.<br><br>`STANDARD_ACH`: Standard ACH by Nacha.<br><br>`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: If there is no default debit rail or there are multiple payment methods.<br><br>Possible values:  `SAME_DAY_ACH`, `STANDARD_ACH`, `MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`|
|user|[SignalUser](#schemasignaluser)|false|none|Details about the end user initiating the transaction (i.e., the account holder). These fields are optional, but strongly recommended to increase the accuracy of results when using Signal Transaction Scores. When using a Balance-only ruleset, if the Signal Addendum has been signed, these fields are ignored; if the Addendum has not been signed, using these fields will result in an error.|
|device|[SignalDevice](#schemasignaldevice)|false|none|Details about the end user's device. These fields are optional, but strongly recommended to increase the accuracy of results when using Signal Transaction Scores. When using a Balance-only Ruleset, these fields are ignored if the Signal Addendum has been signed; if it has not been signed, using these fields will result in an error.|
|risk_profile_key|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** Specifying `risk_profile_key` is deprecated. Please provide `ruleset` instead.|
|ruleset_key|string \| null|false|none|The key of the ruleset to use for evaluating this transaction. You can create a ruleset using the Plaid Dashboard, under [Signal->Rules](https://dashboard.plaid.com/signal/risk-profiles). If not provided, for all new customers as of October 15, 2025, the `default` ruleset will be used. For existing Signal Transaction Scores customers as of October 15, 2025, by default, no ruleset will be used if the `ruleset_key` is not provided. For more information, or to opt out of using rulesets, see [Signal Rules](https://plaid.com/docs/signal/signal-rules/).|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

If using a Signal Transaction Scores ruleset, over 80 core attributes will be returned. Examples of attributes include:<br><br>`available_balance` and `current_balance`: The balance in the ACH transaction funding account<br><br>`days_since_first_plaid_connection`: The number of days since the first time the Item was connected to an application via Plaid<br><br>`plaid_connections_count_7d`: The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid over the past 7 days<br><br>`plaid_connections_count_30d`: The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid over the past 30 days<br><br>`total_plaid_connections_count`: The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid<br><br>`is_savings_or_money_market_account`: Indicates whether the ACH transaction funding account is a savings/money market account<br><br>For the full list and detailed documentation of core attributes available, or to request that core attributes not be returned, contact sales or your Plaid account manager.|

If a `ruleset_key` is not provided, for customers who began using Signal Transaction Scores before October 15, 2025, by default, this field will be omitted. To learn more, see [Signal Rules](https://plaid.com/docs/signal/signal-rules/).|
|warnings|[[SignalWarning](#schemasignalwarning)]|true|none|If bank information was not available to be used in the Signal Transaction Scores model, this array contains warnings describing why bank data is missing. SignalScheduleRequest defines the request schema for `/signal/schedule`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|access_token|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|none|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|
|account_id|string|true|none|The Plaid `account_id` of the account that is the funding source for the proposed transaction. The `account_id` is returned in the `/accounts/get` endpoint as well as the [`onSuccess`](https://plaid.com/docs/link/ios/#link-ios-onsuccess-linkSuccess-metadata-accounts-id) callback metadata.<br><br>This will return an [`INVALID_ACCOUNT_ID`](https://plaid.com/docs/errors/invalid-input/#invalid_account_id) error if the account has been removed at the bank or if the `account_id` is no longer valid.|
|client_transaction_id|string|true|none|The unique ID that you would like to use to refer to this transaction. For your convenience mapping your internal data, you could use your internal ID/identifier for this transaction. The max length for this field is 36 characters.|
|amount|number(double)|true|none|The transaction amount, in USD (e.g. `102.05`)|
|default_payment_method|[SignalScheduleDefaultPaymentMethod](#schemasignalscheduledefaultpaymentmethod)|false|none|The payment method specified in the `default_payment_method` field directly impacts the timing recommendations provided by the API for submitting the debit entry to your processor or ODFI. If unspecified, defaults to `STANDARD_ACH`.<br><br>`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH (as defined by Nacha). The API assumes the settlement will occur on the same business day as submission. Note: The actual cutoff time can vary depending on your payment processor or ODFI. Nacha has established three processing windows for Same Day ACH (Eastern Time): 10:30 AM, 2:45 PM, and 4:45 PM.<br><br>`STANDARD_ACH`: Standard ACH (as defined by Nacha), typically settled one to three business days after submission.<br><br>`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: Indicates that there is no default debit rail or multiple payment methods are available, and the transaction could use any of them based on customer policy or availability.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|default_payment_method|SAME_DAY_ACH|
|default_payment_method|STANDARD_ACH|
|default_payment_method|MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS|

SignalScheduleResponse defines the response schema for `/signal/schedule`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|optimal_date|string(date) \| null|true|none|The recommended optimal date to submit the debit entry, formatted in ISO 8601 "YYYY-MM-DD" (e.g., "2024-03-30"). The `optimal_date` is derived from the date with rank = 1 in the following recommendations array.<br><br>NOTE: The `default_payment_method` field specified in the request will affect the recommendation, since we're accounting for debit settlement time.<br><br>The debit scheduling evaluation covers the banking days within the seven calendar days after the /signal/schedule request is submitted; the day of the request is never recommended. If no date within this period is considered likely to result in a successful debit attempt, `null` will be returned for the `optimal_date`.|
|recommendations|[[SignalScheduleRecommendation](#schemasignalschedulerecommendation)]|true|none|This array provides a date-by-date evaluation of debit submission recommendations within the evaluation period. Each object in the array represents a retry recommendation for a specific date.|
|warnings|[[SignalWarning](#schemasignalwarning)]|true|none|If bank information was not available to be used in the Signal Transaction Scores model, this array contains warnings describing why bank data is missing. If you want to receive an API error instead of scores in the case of missing bank data, file a support ticket or contact your Plaid account manager.|
|request_id|[RequestID](#schemarequestid)|true|none|A unique identifier for the request, which can be used for troubleshooting. This identifier, like all Plaid identifiers, is case sensitive.|

```json
}
```

SignalDecisionReportRequest defines the request schema for `/signal/decision/report`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|client_transaction_id|string|true|none|Must be the same as the `client_transaction_id` supplied when calling `/signal/evaluate`|
|initiated|boolean|true|none|`true` if the ACH transaction was initiated, `false` otherwise.<br><br>This field must be returned as a boolean. If formatted incorrectly, this will result in an [`INVALID_FIELD`](https://plaid.com/docs/errors/invalid-request/#invalid_field) error.|
|days_funds_on_hold|integer \| null|false|none|The actual number of days (hold time) since the ACH debit transaction that you wait before making funds available to your customers. The holding time could affect the ACH return rate.<br><br>For example, use 0 if you make funds available to your customers instantly or the same day following the debit transaction, or 1 if you make funds available the next day following the debit initialization.|
|decision_outcome|[SignalDecisionOutcome](#schemasignaldecisionoutcome)|false|none|The payment decision from the risk assessment.<br><br>`APPROVE`: approve the transaction without requiring further actions from your customers. For example, use this field if you are placing a standard hold for all the approved transactions before making funds available to your customers. You should also use this field if you decide to accelerate the fund availability for your customers.<br><br>`REVIEW`: the transaction requires manual review<br><br>`REJECT`: reject the transaction<br><br>`TAKE_OTHER_RISK_MEASURES`: for example, placing a longer hold on funds than those approved transactions or introducing customer frictions such as step-up verification/authentication<br><br>`NOT_EVALUATED`: if only logging the results without using them<br>|
|payment_method|[SignalPaymentMethod](#schemasignalpaymentmethod)|false|none|The payment method to complete the transaction after the risk assessment. It may be different from the default payment method.<br><br>`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH by Nacha. The debit transaction is processed and settled on the same day.<br><br>`STANDARD_ACH`: Standard ACH by Nacha.<br><br>`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: if there is no default debit rail or there are multiple payment methods.<br>|
|amount_instantly_available|number(double) \| null|false|none|The amount (in USD) made available to your customers instantly following the debit transaction. It could be a partial amount of the requested transaction (example: 102.05).|
|submitted_at|string(date-time)|false|none|The date the ACH debit was submitted to the bank for processing (in ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`). This field should correspond to the attempt initiated after the `/signal/schedule` call.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|decision_outcome|APPROVE|
|decision_outcome|REVIEW|
|decision_outcome|REJECT|
|decision_outcome|TAKE_OTHER_RISK_MEASURES|
|decision_outcome|NOT_EVALUATED|
|payment_method|SAME_DAY_ACH|
|payment_method|NEXT_DAY_ACH|
|payment_method|STANDARD_ACH|
|payment_method|MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS|
|payment_method|null|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|processor_token|[ProcessorToken](#schemaprocessortoken)|true|none|The processor token obtained from the Plaid integration partner. Processor tokens are in the format: `processor-<environment>-<identifier>`|
|client_transaction_id|string|true|none|The unique ID that you would like to use to refer to this transaction. For your convenience mapping your internal data, you could use your internal ID/identifier for this transaction. The max length for this field is 36 characters.|
|amount|number(double)|true|none|The transaction amount, in USD (e.g. `102.05`)|
|user_present|boolean \| null|false|none|`true` if the end user is present while initiating the ACH transfer and the endpoint is being called; `false` otherwise (for example, when the ACH transfer is scheduled and the end user is not present, or you call this endpoint after the ACH transfer but before submitting the Nacha file for ACH processing).|
|client_user_id|string|false|none|A unique ID that identifies the end user in your system. This ID is used to correlate requests by a user with multiple Items. Personally identifiable information, such as an email address or phone number, should not be used in the `client_user_id`.|
|is_recurring|boolean \| null|false|none|**true** if the ACH transaction is a recurring transaction; **false** otherwise.|
|default_payment_method|string \| null|false|none|The default ACH payment method to complete the transaction.<br><br>`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH by Nacha. The debit transaction is processed and settled on the same day.<br><br>`STANDARD_ACH`: Standard ACH by Nacha.<br><br>`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: If there is no default debit rail or there are multiple payment methods.<br><br>Possible values:  `SAME_DAY_ACH`, `STANDARD_ACH`, `MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`|
|user|[SignalUser](#schemasignaluser)|false|none|Details about the end user initiating the transaction (i.e., the account holder). These fields are optional, but strongly recommended to increase the accuracy of results when using Signal Transaction Scores. When using a Balance-only ruleset, if the Signal Addendum has been signed, these fields are ignored; if the Addendum has not been signed, using these fields will result in an error.|
|device|[SignalDevice](#schemasignaldevice)|false|none|Details about the end user's device. These fields are optional, but strongly recommended to increase the accuracy of results when using Signal Transaction Scores. When using a Balance-only Ruleset, these fields are ignored if the Signal Addendum has been signed; if it has not been signed, using these fields will result in an error.|
|ruleset_key|string \| null|false|none|The key of the ruleset to use for this transaction. You can configure a ruleset using the Plaid Dashboard, under [Signal->Rules](https://dashboard.plaid.com/signal/risk-profiles). If not provided, for customers who began using Signal Transaction Scores before October 15, 2025, by default, no ruleset will be used; for customers who began using Signal Transaction Scores after that date, or for Balance customers, the `default` ruleset will be used. For more details, or to opt out of using a ruleset, see [Signal Rules](https://plaid.com/docs/signal/signal-rules/).|

The object contains a risk score and a risk tier that evaluate the transaction return risk of an unauthorized debit. Common return codes in this category include: "R05", "R07", "R10", "R11", "R29". These returns typically have a return time frame of up to 60 calendar days. During this period, customers of financial institutions can dispute a transaction as unauthorized.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|score|[SignalScore](#schemasignalscore)|true|none|A score from 1-99 that indicates the transaction return risk: a higher risk score suggests a higher return likelihood.|
|risk_tier|[CustomerInitiatedRiskTier](#schemacustomerinitiatedrisktier)|true|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED. Use Signal Rules instead to transform the `score` into a useful action.<br><br>A tier corresponding to the projected likelihood that the transaction, if initiated, will be subject to a return.<br><br>In the `customer_initiated_return_risk` object, there are five risk tiers corresponding to the scores:<br>  1: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate between 0.00% - 0.02%<br>  2: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate between 0.02% - 0.05%<br>  3: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate between 0.05% - 0.1%<br>  4: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate between 0.1% - 0.5%<br>  5: Predicted customer-initiated return incidence rate greater than 0.5%<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_SignalScheduleDefaultPaymentMethod">SignalScheduleDefaultPaymentMethod</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasignalscheduledefaultpaymentmethod"></a>
<a id="schema_SignalScheduleDefaultPaymentMethod"></a>
<a id="tocSsignalscheduledefaultpaymentmethod"></a>
<a id="tocssignalscheduledefaultpaymentmethod"></a>

```json
"SAME_DAY_ACH"
```

The payment method specified in the `default_payment_method` field directly impacts the timing recommendations provided by the API for submitting the debit entry to your processor or ODFI. If unspecified, defaults to `STANDARD_ACH`.

`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH (as defined by Nacha). The API assumes the settlement will occur on the same business day as submission. Note: The actual cutoff time can vary depending on your payment processor or ODFI. Nacha has established three processing windows for Same Day ACH (Eastern Time): 10:30 AM, 2:45 PM, and 4:45 PM.

`STANDARD_ACH`: Standard ACH (as defined by Nacha), typically settled one to three business days after submission.

`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: Indicates that there is no default debit rail or multiple payment methods are available, and the transaction could use any of them based on customer policy or availability.

Details about the end user's device. These fields are optional, but strongly recommended to increase the accuracy of results when using Signal Transaction Scores. When using a Balance-only Ruleset, these fields are ignored if the Signal Addendum has been signed; if it has not been signed, using these fields will result in an error.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ip_address|string \| null|false|none|The IP address of the device that initiated the transaction|
|user_agent|string \| null|false|none|The user agent of the device that initiated the transaction (e.g. "Mozilla/5.0")|

<h2 id="tocS_Ruleset">Ruleset</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaruleset"></a>
<a id="schema_Ruleset"></a>

```json
  "ruleset_key": "string",
  "result": "ACCEPT",
  "triggered_rule_details": {
    "internal_note": "string",
    "custom_action_key": "string"
  },
  "outcome": "string"
}
```

Details about the transaction result after evaluation by the requested Ruleset. If a `ruleset_key` is not provided, for customers who began using Signal Transaction Scores before October 15, 2025, by default, this field will be omitted. To learn more, see [Signal Rules](https://plaid.com/docs/signal/signal-rules/).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ruleset_key|string|false|none|The key of the Ruleset used for this transaction.|
|result|[RuleResult](#schemaruleresult)|true|none|The result of the rule that was triggered for this transaction.<br><br>`ACCEPT`: Accept the transaction for processing.<br><br>`REROUTE`: Reroute the transaction to a different payment method, as this transaction is too risky.<br><br>`REVIEW`: Review the transaction before proceeding.|
|triggered_rule_details|[RuleDetails](#schemaruledetails)|false|none|Rules are run in numerical order. The first rule with a logic match is triggered. These are the details of that rule.|
|outcome|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** The evaluated outcome for this transaction. This field is deprecated, use `result` or `triggered_rule_details.custom_action_key` instead.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|result|ACCEPT|
|result|REROUTE|
|result|REVIEW|

```json
  "internal_note": "string",
```

Rules are run in numerical order. The first rule with a logic match is triggered. These are the details of that rule.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|internal_note|string|false|none|An optional message attached to the triggered rule, defined within the Dashboard, for your internal use. Useful for debugging, such as "Account appears to be closed."|
|custom_action_key|string|false|none|A string key, defined within the Dashboard, used to trigger programmatic behavior for a certain result. For instance, you could optionally choose to define a "3-day-hold" `custom_action_key` for an ACCEPT result.|

<h2 id="tocS_RuleResult">RuleResult</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaruleresult"></a>
<a id="schema_RuleResult"></a>
<a id="tocSruleresult"></a>
<a id="tocsruleresult"></a>

```json
"ACCEPT"
```

The result of the rule that was triggered for this transaction.

`ACCEPT`: Accept the transaction for processing.

`REROUTE`: Reroute the transaction to a different payment method, as this transaction is too risky.

`REVIEW`: Review the transaction before proceeding.

<h2 id="tocS_SignalDecisionOutcome">SignalDecisionOutcome</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasignaldecisionoutcome"></a>
<a id="schema_SignalDecisionOutcome"></a>
<a id="tocSsignaldecisionoutcome"></a>
<a id="tocssignaldecisionoutcome"></a>

```json
"APPROVE"
```

The payment decision from the risk assessment.

`APPROVE`: approve the transaction without requiring further actions from your customers. For example, use this field if you are placing a standard hold for all the approved transactions before making funds available to your customers. You should also use this field if you decide to accelerate the fund availability for your customers.

`REVIEW`: the transaction requires manual review

`REJECT`: reject the transaction

`TAKE_OTHER_RISK_MEASURES`: for example, placing a longer hold on funds than those approved transactions or introducing customer frictions such as step-up verification/authentication

`NOT_EVALUATED`: if only logging the results without using them

<h2 id="tocS_SignalPaymentMethod">SignalPaymentMethod</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasignalpaymentmethod"></a>
<a id="schema_SignalPaymentMethod"></a>
<a id="tocSsignalpaymentmethod"></a>
<a id="tocssignalpaymentmethod"></a>

```json
"SAME_DAY_ACH"
```

The payment method to complete the transaction after the risk assessment. It may be different from the default payment method.

`SAME_DAY_ACH`: Same Day ACH by Nacha. The debit transaction is processed and settled on the same day.

`STANDARD_ACH`: Standard ACH by Nacha.

`MULTIPLE_PAYMENT_METHODS`: if there is no default debit rail or there are multiple payment methods.

The core attributes object contains additional data that can be used to assess the ACH return risk.

If using a Balance-only ruleset, only `available_balance` and `current_balance` will be returned as core attributes. If using a Signal Transaction Scores ruleset, over 80 core attributes will be returned. Examples of attributes include:

`available_balance` and `current_balance`: The balance in the ACH transaction funding account

`days_since_first_plaid_connection`: The number of days since the first time the Item was connected to an application via Plaid

`plaid_connections_count_7d`: The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid over the past 7 days

`plaid_connections_count_30d`: The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid over the past 30 days

`total_plaid_connections_count`: The number of times the Item has been connected to applications via Plaid

`is_savings_or_money_market_account`: Indicates whether the ACH transaction funding account is a savings/money market account

For the full list and detailed documentation of core attributes available, or to request that core attributes not be returned, contact sales or your Plaid account manager.

StatementsListRequest defines the request schema for `/statements/list`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_token|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|true|none|The access token associated with the Item for which data is being requested.|

Request object for `/protect/report/create`.
You must provide either `user_id`, or an `incident_event` with at least one supported identifier: `link_session_id`, `idv_session_id`, `protect_event_id`, `signal_client_transaction_id`, or `access_token`. Context fields such as `internal_reference`, `time`, `amount`, and `bank_account` do not satisfy this identifier requirement.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|user_id|string|false|none|The Plaid User ID associated with the report.|
|incident_event|[ProtectIncidentEvent](#schemaprotectincidentevent)|false|none|Details about the incident event.|
|report_confidence|[ProtectReportConfidence](#schemaprotectreportconfidence)|true|none|The confidence level of the incident report.<br>`CONFIRMED` indicates the incident has been verified and definitively occurred.<br><br>`SUSPECTED` indicates the incident is believed to have occurred but has not been fully verified.|
|report_type|[ProtectReportType](#schemaprotectreporttype)|true|none|The type of incident being reported.<br><br>`USER_ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER` - Indicates that a legitimate user's account was accessed or controlled by an unauthorized party.<br><br>`FALSE_IDENTITY` - Indicates that a user created an account using stolen or fabricated identity information.<br><br>`STOLEN_IDENTITY` - Indicates that a user created an account using identity information belonging to a real individual without their consent.<br><br>`SYNTHETIC_IDENTITY` - Indicates that a user created an account using a fake or partially fabricated identity (e.g., combining real and fake information to form a new persona).<br><br>`MULTIPLE_USER_ACCOUNTS` - Indicates that the same individual is operating multiple accounts in violation of policy.<br><br>`SCAM_VICTIM` - Indicates that the user was tricked into authorizing or sending funds as part of a scam.<br><br>`BANK_ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER` - Indicates that a user's linked bank account was accessed or misused by an unauthorized party.<br><br>`BANK_CONNECTION_REVOKED` - Indicates that a linked bank account connection was revoked by the financial institution, often due to suspected misuse, fraud, or security concerns.<br><br>`CARD_TESTING` - Indicates that a card was used in small or repeated transactions to test its validity.<br><br>`UNAUTHORIZED_TRANSACTION` - Indicates that a transaction was made without the user's consent or authorization.<br><br>`CARD_CHARGEBACK` - Indicates that a card transaction was reversed via a chargeback claim.<br><br>`ACH_RETURN` - Indicates that an ACH transaction was returned or reversed by the bank.<br><br>`DISPUTE` - Indicates that a user filed a dispute regarding a transaction or account activity.<br><br>`FIRST_PARTY_FRAUD` - Indicates that a user intentionally misrepresented themselves or their actions for financial gain.<br><br>`MISSED_PAYMENT` - Indicates that a user failed to make a required payment on time.<br><br>`LOAN_STACKING` - Indicates that a user applied for or took out multiple loans simultaneously beyond their ability to repay.<br><br>`MONEY_LAUNDERING` - Indicates that funds are being moved through accounts to obscure their illicit origin.<br><br>`NO_FRAUD` - Indicates that an investigation determined no fraudulent activity occurred on user/event (positive label).<br><br>`OTHER` - Indicates that the case involves fraud or financial risk not covered by other report types.|
|report_source|[ProtectReportSource](#schemaprotectreportsource)|true|none|The source that identified or reported the incident.<br><br>`INTERNAL_REVIEW` - Incident was identified through internal fraud investigations or review processes.<br><br>`USER_SELF_REPORTED` - Incident was reported directly by the affected user.<br><br>`BANK_FEEDBACK` - Incident was identified through bank feedback, including ACH returns and connection revocations.<br><br>`NETWORK_FEEDBACK` - Incident was identified through card network alerts or chargebacks.<br><br>`AUTOMATED_SYSTEM` - Incident was detected by automated systems such as fraud models or rule engines.<br><br>`THIRD_PARTY_ALERT` - Incident was identified through external vendor or consortium alerts.<br><br>`OTHER` - Incident was identified through a source not covered by other categories.|
|bank_account|[ProtectBankAccount](#schemaprotectbankaccount)|false|none|Bank account information associated with the incident.|
|ach_return_code|string \| null|false|none|Must be a valid ACH return code (e.g. `R01`), required if `report_type` is `ACH_RETURN`.|
|notes|string \| null|false|none|Additional context or details about the report.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|

|report_confidence|SUSPECTED|
|report_type|USER_ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER|

```json
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "user": {
    "user_id": "string",
    "client_user_id": "string"
  },
  "client_advance_id": "string",
  "advance_type": "FIRST",
  "previous_advance_count": 0,
  "decision_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "decision": "APPROVED",
  "is_taken": true,
  "cash_advance": {
    "amount_approved": {
      "iso_currency_code": "USD",
      "value": 0
    },
    "amount_due": {
      "iso_currency_code": "USD",
      "value": 0
    },
    "due_date": "1970-01-01"
  }
}
```

Request object for `/protect/cash_advance/decision/create`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|[APIClientID](#schemaapiclientid)|false|none|Your Plaid API `client_id`. The `client_id` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` header or as part of a request body.|
|secret|[APISecret](#schemaapisecret)|false|none|Your Plaid API `secret`. The `secret` is required and may be provided either in the `PLAID-SECRET` header or as part of a request body.|
|user|[ProtectUser](#schemaprotectuser)|true|none|Represents an end user for `/protect/compute` requests.|
|client_advance_id|string \| null|false|none|Your unique identifier for a cash-advance. Required when `is_taken` is `true`. This should be the same identifier provided when recording a repayment.|
|advance_type|[CashAdvanceType](#schemacashadvancetype)|false|none|Required when `is_taken` is `true`.<br>Indicates if this would be a user's first or repeat cash-advance.<br><br>`FIRST` - A user's first cash-advance.<br><br>`REPEAT` - A user has previously taken out a cash-advance.|
|previous_advance_count|integer \| null|false|none|The number of cash-advances a user has previously taken.|
|decision_time|string(date-time)|true|none|The time the decision was made, in ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`).|
|decision|[CashAdvanceDecisionOutcome](#schemacashadvancedecisionoutcome)|true|none|The outcome of a cash-advance decision.<br><br>`APPROVED` - The cash-advance was approved.<br><br>`DECLINED` - The cash-advance was declined.|
|is_taken|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the end user took the cash-advance. Required when `decision` is APPROVED. When `true`, `client_advance_id` and `cash_advance` are required.|
|cash_advance|[CashAdvanceInfo](#schemacashadvanceinfo)|false|none|The details of a cash-advance associated with the decision. Required when `is_taken` is `true`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|advance_type|FIRST|
|advance_type|REPEAT|
|decision|APPROVED|
|decision|DECLINED|

<h2 id="tocS_ProtectReport">ProtectReport</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaprotectreport"></a>
<a id="schema_ProtectReport"></a>
<a id="tocSprotectreport"></a>
<a id="tocsprotectreport"></a>

```json
{
  "report_id": "string",
  "incident_event": {
    "protect_event_id": "string",
    "link_session_id": "string",
    "idv_session_id": "string",
    "signal_client_transaction_id": "string",
    "internal_reference": "string",
    "time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "amount": {
      "iso_currency_code": "USD",
      "value": 0
    },
    "item_id": "string"
  },
  "report_confidence": "CONFIRMED",
  "report_type": "USER_ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER",
  "report_source": "INTERNAL_REVIEW",
  "bank_account": {
    "account_id": "string",
    "account_number": "string",
    "routing_number": "string"
  },
  "ach_return_code": "string",
  "notes": "string",
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

A Protect report associated with a user. Contains details about documented incidents, which may include fraud, investigation outcomes, or other risk events.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|report_id|string|true|none|A unique identifier representing the submitted report.|
|incident_event|[ProtectIncidentEventResponse](#schemaprotectincidenteventresponse)|true|none|Details about the incident event.|
|report_confidence|[ProtectReportConfidence](#schemaprotectreportconfidence)|true|none|The confidence level of the incident report.<br>`CONFIRMED` indicates the incident has been verified and definitively occurred.<br><br>`SUSPECTED` indicates the incident is believed to have occurred but has not been fully verified.|
|report_type|[ProtectReportType](#schemaprotectreporttype)|true|none|The type of incident being reported.<br><br>`USER_ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER` - Indicates that a legitimate user's account was accessed or controlled by an unauthorized party.<br><br>`FALSE_IDENTITY` - Indicates that a user created an account using stolen or fabricated identity information.<br><br>`STOLEN_IDENTITY` - Indicates that a user created an account using identity information belonging to a real individual without their consent.<br><br>`SYNTHETIC_IDENTITY` - Indicates that a user created an account using a fake or partially fabricated identity (e.g., combining real and fake information to form a new persona).<br><br>`MULTIPLE_USER_ACCOUNTS` - Indicates that the same individual is operating multiple accounts in violation of policy.<br><br>`SCAM_VICTIM` - Indicates that the user was tricked into authorizing or sending funds as part of a scam.<br><br>`BANK_ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER` - Indicates that a user's linked bank account was accessed or misused by an unauthorized party.<br><br>`BANK_CONNECTION_REVOKED` - Indicates that a linked bank account connection was revoked by the financial institution, often due to suspected misuse, fraud, or security concerns.<br><br>`CARD_TESTING` - Indicates that a card was used in small or repeated transactions to test its validity.<br><br>`UNAUTHORIZED_TRANSACTION` - Indicates that a transaction was made without the user's consent or authorization.<br><br>`CARD_CHARGEBACK` - Indicates that a card transaction was reversed via a chargeback claim.<br><br>`ACH_RETURN` - Indicates that an ACH transaction was returned or reversed by the bank.<br><br>`DISPUTE` - Indicates that a user filed a dispute regarding a transaction or account activity.<br><br>`FIRST_PARTY_FRAUD` - Indicates that a user intentionally misrepresented themselves or their actions for financial gain.<br><br>`MISSED_PAYMENT` - Indicates that a user failed to make a required payment on time.<br><br>`LOAN_STACKING` - Indicates that a user applied for or took out multiple loans simultaneously beyond their ability to repay.<br><br>`MONEY_LAUNDERING` - Indicates that funds are being moved through accounts to obscure their illicit origin.<br><br>`NO_FRAUD` - Indicates that an investigation determined no fraudulent activity occurred on user/event (positive label).<br><br>`OTHER` - Indicates that the case involves fraud or financial risk not covered by other report types.|
|report_source|[ProtectReportSource](#schemaprotectreportsource)|true|none|The source that identified or reported the incident.<br><br>`INTERNAL_REVIEW` - Incident was identified through internal fraud investigations or review processes.<br><br>`USER_SELF_REPORTED` - Incident was reported directly by the affected user.<br><br>`BANK_FEEDBACK` - Incident was identified through bank feedback, including ACH returns and connection revocations.<br><br>`NETWORK_FEEDBACK` - Incident was identified through card network alerts or chargebacks.<br><br>`AUTOMATED_SYSTEM` - Incident was detected by automated systems such as fraud models or rule engines.<br><br>`THIRD_PARTY_ALERT` - Incident was identified through external vendor or consortium alerts.<br><br>`OTHER` - Incident was identified through a source not covered by other categories.|
|bank_account|[ProtectBankAccount](#schemaprotectbankaccount)|true|none|Bank account information associated with the incident.|
|ach_return_code|string \| null|true|none|ACH return code if the report type is `ACH_RETURN` (e.g. `R01`).|
|notes|string \| null|true|none|Additional context or details about the report.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp when the report was created, in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2020-07-24T03:26:02Z').|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|report_confidence|CONFIRMED|
|report_confidence|SUSPECTED|
|report_type|USER_ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER|
|report_type|FALSE_IDENTITY|
|report_type|STOLEN_IDENTITY|
|report_type|SYNTHETIC_IDENTITY|
|report_type|MULTIPLE_USER_ACCOUNTS|
|report_type|SCAM_VICTIM|
|report_type|BANK_ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER|
|report_type|BANK_CONNECTION_REVOKED|
|report_type|CARD_TESTING|
|report_type|UNAUTHORIZED_TRANSACTION|
|report_type|CARD_CHARGEBACK|
|report_type|ACH_RETURN|
|report_type|DISPUTE|
|report_type|FIRST_PARTY_FRAUD|
|report_type|MISSED_PAYMENT|
|report_type|LOAN_STACKING|
|report_type|MONEY_LAUNDERING|
|report_type|NO_FRAUD|
|report_type|OTHER|
|report_source|INTERNAL_REVIEW|
|report_source|USER_SELF_REPORTED|
|report_source|BANK_FEEDBACK|
|report_source|NETWORK_FEEDBACK|
|report_source|AUTOMATED_SYSTEM|
|report_source|THIRD_PARTY_ALERT|
|report_source|OTHER|


The repayment status of a cash-advance.

`REPAID` - The cash-advance has been fully repaid.

`PARTIAL_PAYMENT` - A payment has been made on the cash-advance, but there is still an outstanding balance.

`UNPAID` - The cash-advance is past its due date and has not been repaid; the user is delinquent.


The confidence level of the incident report.
`CONFIRMED` indicates the incident has been verified and definitively occurred.

`SUSPECTED` indicates the incident is believed to have occurred but has not been fully verified.

<h2 id="tocS_ProtectReportType">ProtectReportType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaprotectreporttype"></a>
<a id="schema_ProtectReportType"></a>
<a id="tocSprotectreporttype"></a>
<a id="tocsprotectreporttype"></a>

```json
"USER_ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER"
```

The type of incident being reported.

`USER_ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER` - Indicates that a legitimate user's account was accessed or controlled by an unauthorized party.

`FALSE_IDENTITY` - Indicates that a user created an account using stolen or fabricated identity information.

`STOLEN_IDENTITY` - Indicates that a user created an account using identity information belonging to a real individual without their consent.

`SYNTHETIC_IDENTITY` - Indicates that a user created an account using a fake or partially fabricated identity (e.g., combining real and fake information to form a new persona).

`MULTIPLE_USER_ACCOUNTS` - Indicates that the same individual is operating multiple accounts in violation of policy.

`SCAM_VICTIM` - Indicates that the user was tricked into authorizing or sending funds as part of a scam.

`BANK_ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER` - Indicates that a user's linked bank account was accessed or misused by an unauthorized party.

`BANK_CONNECTION_REVOKED` - Indicates that a linked bank account connection was revoked by the financial institution, often due to suspected misuse, fraud, or security concerns.

`CARD_TESTING` - Indicates that a card was used in small or repeated transactions to test its validity.

`UNAUTHORIZED_TRANSACTION` - Indicates that a transaction was made without the user's consent or authorization.

`CARD_CHARGEBACK` - Indicates that a card transaction was reversed via a chargeback claim.

`ACH_RETURN` - Indicates that an ACH transaction was returned or reversed by the bank.

`DISPUTE` - Indicates that a user filed a dispute regarding a transaction or account activity.

`FIRST_PARTY_FRAUD` - Indicates that a user intentionally misrepresented themselves or their actions for financial gain.

`MISSED_PAYMENT` - Indicates that a user failed to make a required payment on time.

`LOAN_STACKING` - Indicates that a user applied for or took out multiple loans simultaneously beyond their ability to repay.

`MONEY_LAUNDERING` - Indicates that funds are being moved through accounts to obscure their illicit origin.

`NO_FRAUD` - Indicates that an investigation determined no fraudulent activity occurred on user/event (positive label).

`OTHER` - Indicates that the case involves fraud or financial risk not covered by other report types.

<h2 id="tocS_ProtectReportSource">ProtectReportSource</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaprotectreportsource"></a>
<a id="schema_ProtectReportSource"></a>
<a id="tocSprotectreportsource"></a>
<a id="tocsprotectreportsource"></a>

```json
"INTERNAL_REVIEW"
```

The source that identified or reported the incident.

`INTERNAL_REVIEW` - Incident was identified through internal fraud investigations or review processes.

`USER_SELF_REPORTED` - Incident was reported directly by the affected user.

`BANK_FEEDBACK` - Incident was identified through bank feedback, including ACH returns and connection revocations.

`NETWORK_FEEDBACK` - Incident was identified through card network alerts or chargebacks.

`AUTOMATED_SYSTEM` - Incident was detected by automated systems such as fraud models or rule engines.

`THIRD_PARTY_ALERT` - Incident was identified through external vendor or consortium alerts.

`OTHER` - Incident was identified through a source not covered by other categories.
